title: [bug] The PII guard has not been running: beads' core.hooksPath overrides .git/hooks
description:
FOUND 2026-09-02 while preparing the wordle-teams-4yt PR. THIS REPOSITORY IS PUBLIC and the guard that exists to stop third-party user data reaching it was silently disabled.

WHAT WAS WRONG. `scripts/check-no-pii.mjs` was wired into `.git/hooks/pre-commit`. beads sets `core.hooksPath` to `.beads/hooks`, and that setting OVERRIDES `.git/hooks` ENTIRELY — git does not run both. `.beads/hooks/pre-commit` contained only the beads integration block and had no reference to the guard, so from the moment beads installed its hooks the check stopped running. Nothing warned about it.

  git config --get core.hooksPath   ->   /home/cdub/projects/wordle-teams/.beads/hooks

VERIFIED BY PROBE, NOT BY INSPECTION. A file containing a third-party-shaped address was staged and committed: the commit SUCCEEDED with exit 0. The same file run through the script directly failed with exit 1, so the guard itself worked and simply was not being invoked. The probe commit was immediately reset and the file deleted.

THE PROJECT'S OWN DOCUMENTATION WAS WRONG BECAUSE OF THIS. CLAUDE.md says "DO NOT USE --no-verify - the hook chains to the PII guard". It did not chain to it. And check-no-pii.mjs's own header told the next person to install it into `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, which is the directory git is configured to ignore.

THIS IS THE SECOND WAY THE SAME GUARD HAS FAILED OPEN. A note already in check-no-pii.mjs records that every commit in Phase 4 was made with --no-verify "on the belief that this hook merely staged .beads/issues.jsonl". So the guard has now been bypassed once by a mistaken belief about what it did, and once by a config change that silently unhooked it.

FIXED IN THE SAME SESSION: the call was added to `.beads/hooks/pre-commit`, AFTER beads' own END marker, because beads rewrites only the region between its markers and would otherwise overwrite it on the next `bd hooks install`. Re-probed: the commit is now BLOCKED with exit 1. A full-tree scan is clean at 620 files, so nothing has actually leaked through the window.

WHAT IS STILL WORTH DOING, none of it done here:
  1. NOTHING PROVES THE WIRING. The fix is a line in a hook file that a future `bd hooks install`, a fresh clone with a different core.hooksPath, or a beads version bump could undo just as silently. A test that asserts the configured hooks directory's pre-commit actually invokes the guard would turn this from a thing someone noticed into a thing CI knows. That test cannot live in vitest alone - it has to read `git config core.hooksPath` - but it can.
  2. main's copy of check-no-pii.mjs is OLDER and lacks the reserved-TLD allowance that feat/v2-replatform has, so restoring the hook on a main-based branch fails on fixture addresses that are not real. The two versions should converge before the guard is relied on there.
  3. Worth confirming whether the older v1 branches ever had the guard running at all.

NO ADDRESSES IN THIS ISSUE, deliberately - the guard scans this file too, and quoting the probe address in a comment failed the check, which is its own small proof that it works.
close_reason: Guard re-wired into .beads/hooks/pre-commit after the END marker, and now ASSERTED by src/pii-guard-wiring.test.ts, which reads git config core.hooksPath rather than assuming a path and pins that the call sits outside beads' managed block. Three mutations killed. The first version of the test reproduced the very bug it guards - it matched the filename in the hook's own comment while the call was absent - which is recorded in the file.

title: Task 10: SPIKE S2 — does web-push run in a Convex 'use node' action?
description: THE HIGHEST-RISK UNKNOWN IN THE PHASE. Phase 5 shipped validateEvent through four green gates and it could not run on this runtime — Buffer is not defined — and only a live request found it. web-push needs Node crypto for VAPID JWT signing and AES128GCM. Gates tasks 11, 12 and 13; if it fails, STOP and re-plan rather than working around it. The VAPID private key must never reach this repo, a commit message, or an issue — this repository is public. Plan task 10.
acceptance_criteria: A 'use node' action on beta sends one real notification to a real device and returns statusCode 201. The outcome, success or failure mode, is pasted into this issue.
notes:
VAPID SETUP DONE 2026-08-28 by the owner. On beta (fabulous-goldfish-949):

  VAPID_SUBJECT     = mailto:reminders@wordleteams.com
  VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY  = BMw9W7iLyDb64MTd4J_T2SE8-K4bV3o8I0a-1rE3XromuPDjrX8a93sNEVcubfurRLmw3LAEJwg0KTaXVtopzVE
  VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY = set, 43 chars (32-byte scalar). Only copy is on the deployment.

Public key validated: 87 chars -> 65 bytes, first byte 0x04, url-safe, round-trips. Valid uncompressed P-256 point. The public key is not a secret — the browser needs it to subscribe, and convex/push.ts will serve it from a query.

Generated with node webcrypto rather than installing web-push, and piped straight into `convex env set` so the private key was never printed, filed, or put in shell history. Script kept out of the repo deliberately (public repo).

REMINDERS_ENABLED and REMINDERS_ALLOWLIST deliberately left UNSET — the spike does not go through sweep, and the kill switch stays off.

STILL NEEDED for this spike: a real push subscription from a browser on beta, and running the deployed probe from the Convex DASHBOARD — `convex run` cannot reach beta (deployment:functions:runTestQuery denied), though `convex env` can.
S2 ANSWERED 2026-08-28 — PASSES. web-push runs on Convex's Node runtime.

Probe result from the dashboard against fabulous-goldfish-949:

  { ok: true, stage: "sent", statusCode: 201,
    env: { hasBuffer: true, hasSubject: true, hasPublicKey: true, hasPrivateKey: true } }

THE DECISIVE LINE IS hasBuffer. Measured minutes earlier on the DEFAULT runtime, via convex run --inline-query:

  hasBuffer false   hasCrypto true   hasSubtle true

So WebCrypto exists everywhere but Node's Buffer only under 'use node' — and web-push needs it for VAPID JWT signing and AES128GCM payload encryption. The directive is load-bearing, not precautionary, and this is the exact shape of Phase 5's `Buffer is not defined`, which reached production-shaped code through four green gates.

201 means the push service ACCEPTED the encrypted payload — so signing and encryption both executed, which is the runtime question this spike existed to answer. It does not by itself prove the notification rendered on the device; that is the phase's done-when and is verified again in task 11.

Tasks 11, 12 and 13 proceed as planned. No redesign needed.

CLEANUP: convex/spikePush.ts and public/sw-spike.js both removed. The owner should unregister the throwaway worker in their browser (DevTools > Application > Service Workers > Unregister); task 13 registers the real one at /sw.js, same scope, which supersedes it anyway.
close_reason:
S2 PASSES. web-push runs in a Convex 'use node' action on beta.

  { ok: true, stage: "sent", statusCode: 201,
    env: { hasBuffer: true, hasSubject: true, hasPublicKey: true, hasPrivateKey: true } }

hasBuffer: true under 'use node' versus hasBuffer: false on the default runtime (measured the same afternoon via convex run --inline-query, which also showed hasCrypto/hasSubtle true). WebCrypto is present everywhere; Node's Buffer is not, and web-push needs it for VAPID JWT signing and AES128GCM payload encryption. The directive is load-bearing, not precautionary.

201 = the push service accepted the encrypted payload, so signing and encryption both executed. That is the runtime question this spike existed to answer. Whether the notification RENDERS on a device is re-verified in task 11 against the phase's done-when.

THE HIGHEST-RISK UNKNOWN IN THE PHASE IS CLOSED. Tasks 11, 12 and 13 proceed as designed — no redesign of the push half.

Artifacts removed and verified gone from beta: convex/spikePush.ts and public/sw-spike.js both 404. web-push and @types/web-push stay in package.json; task 11 needs them. All four gates green after removal (702 tests / 43 files); beta healthy (/ 307 -> /login 200).

Two process traps hit while running this, both recorded to memory: `gh run watch` on a run selected with --limit 1 straight after a push reports a false green because it grabs the PREVIOUS run (caught only because a curl 404'd); and running just `pnpm build` after adding a static asset missed a lint failure that CI then found, because build does not typecheck and lint reaches public/*.js.

description:

title: Server actions in me/actions.ts perform privileged writes without authorization
description:
src/app/me/actions.ts starts with 'use server', so every export is a Next.js Server Action — a public HTTP endpoint. Confirmed against .next/server/server-reference-manifest.json: all 21 registered action ids carry the action-browser layer, and 12 are reachable from the webhook route's module graph.

processWebhookEvent and storeWebhookEvent are among them. They accept a caller-supplied event argument, use createAdminClient (service role, bypasses RLS), write player_customer.membership_status, and invoke handle_upgrade_team_invites — with no session or authorization check. Sibling actions in the same file (createTeam) do call getSession and throw Unauthorized, so the omission is inconsistent rather than deliberate.

Next.js guidance is explicit that Server Actions are public endpoints and must verify authorization themselves; reachability of an action id is not a security boundary.

Present in production today under the Lemon Squeezy integration — not introduced by the Polar migration.

FIX IN PROGRESS: wordle-teams-c6v moves both functions into src/lib/polar/webhook.ts, a module without the 'use server' directive, so they stop being actions at all. That closes this specific path.

STILL TO AUDIT after that: the remaining exports of me/actions.ts. getCheckoutUrl(user: User) takes a caller-supplied User rather than deriving it from the session, which is the same class of problem at lower severity.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: no export of a 'use server' module performs a privileged write without deriving identity from the session, and getCheckoutUrl derives the player from the session rather than a caller-supplied argument.
notes:
FULLY FIXED as of ymy. getCheckoutUrl now takes NO arguments and derives the player from the session via getUserFromSession, as does the new getBillingPortalUrl; both live in src/lib/polar/actions.ts. The previous getCheckoutUrl(user: User) accepted caller-supplied identity on what Next.js treats as a public HTTP endpoint.

Registered server actions across the three commits: 21 (12 reachable from the webhook route) -> 19 -> 16. The reduction comes from deleting the two webhook handlers and the duplicate getCheckoutUrl copies.

Verified: 14 assertions covering both actions rejecting unauthenticated callers WITHOUT calling Polar at all, using the session id and email rather than any argument, and — asserted directly — having an arity of zero, so no caller-supplied identity is even expressible.
close_reason: Both webhook handlers and both billing actions no longer accept caller-supplied identity; action count 21 -> 16

title: Polar P2e: DB migration - auth hook, drop columns, webhook idempotency
description:
One migration file. THE INTERNAL ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING:

  1. create or replace public.custom_access_token_hook FIRST, dropping the user_customer_id and user_member_variant claims
  2. THEN alter table public.player_customer drop column customer_id, drop column membership_variant
  3. create unique index webhook_events_webhook_id_key on public.webhook_events (webhook_id)

If the columns are dropped while the old hook still selects them, custom_access_token_hook throws and EVERY LOGIN BREAKS. This project already has a login-lockout incident (wordle-teams-jvt) in its history. Base the new hook on supabase/migrations/20240325200437_add_customerid_back_into_auth_hook.sql, keeping user_member_status / user_first_name / user_last_name and removing the other two.

Then regenerate src/lib/database.types.ts via npm run gen-types.

P0 because this is the single riskiest step in the migration.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: migration applies cleanly on dev, login still works on dev afterward, player_customer has only (id, player_id, membership_status), and a duplicate webhook_id insert is rejected by the unique index.
notes:
Done. supabase/migrations/20260731120000_polar_migration_drop_lemonsqueezy_columns.sql, verified against a real local Postgres (not just written).

FOUND DURING VERIFICATION — webhook_id was uuid, not text. The spec and this issue both claimed it was already text and needed no change. It was uuid, because Lemon Squeezy's meta.webhook_id happened to be one and database.types.ts renders uuid as string, which hid it. Standard Webhooks explicitly does NOT require a UUID — the spec's own example id is msg_2KWPBgLlAfxdpx2AI54pPJ85f4W, which a uuid cast rejects. Left alone, the first non-UUID id from Polar would throw on insert, return 500, and put Polar into an infinite retry loop against an event that could never be stored. The migration now converts the column to text. Spec corrected; c6v updated.

SCOPE MOVED: gen-types moved to ymy. Regenerating database.types.ts here would break typecheck in utils.ts:107-108, me/page.tsx:41, and app-bar-server.tsx:31-33, which is ymy's type-ripple scope. This migration touches no TypeScript, so the repo stays green.

OTHER DECISIONS: unique index is PARTIAL (where webhook_id is not null) so legacy null rows stay exempt. Dedupe before indexing orders by processed desc, id asc, so a retry set containing one processed and one failed row keeps the processed one. 'immutable' volatility on the hook was deliberately preserved to keep this migration to one concern — filed separately as wordle-teams-wau.

VERIFIED LOCALLY (supabase db reset, then psql): player_customer is exactly (id, player_id, membership_status); both columns gone; no remaining function or RLS policy references either; the hook INVOKES without throwing for both an unknown user and a real pro player, returning the three expected claims — this is the login-safety proof; webhook_id is text; the partial unique index exists; a non-UUID Standard Webhooks id inserts fine; a duplicate raises a unique violation; two null webhook_ids are both allowed; member_status enum unchanged.
close_reason: Migration written and verified against a local Postgres; caught and fixed a uuid/text column bug that would have broken the webhook pipeline

title: P0: /login is completely unusable for anyone blocking lemonsqueezy.com — infinite error loop locks the page
description:
REPRODUCED AGAINST PRODUCTION 2026-07-30. If app.lemonsqueezy.com fails to load, the login page enters an infinite error loop, pegs the main thread, never renders, and the tab eventually crashes. Affected users cannot sign in or sign up AT ALL.

MEASURED (headless Chromium, prod https://wordleteams.com/login, fresh profile):
 - normal load: renders fine, createLemonSqueezy defined, 0 errors
 - lemon.js request aborted: 998 'createLemonSqueezy is not a function' errors within the first 500ms;
 document.body.innerText() times out after 3s (main thread locked);
 page never renders the sign-in UI; tab crashes shortly after
 - lemon.js delayed 0.5/1.5/3s: 0 errors, renders fine

So the trigger is FAILURE TO LOAD, not slowness. beforeInteractive defers hydration until the script resolves, so a slow network is safe; an aborted/blocked request is not.

THE LOOP (all four links confirmed in code):
 1. src/components/app-bar/app-bar-base.tsx:34-35 — useEffect calls window.createLemonSqueezy() unguarded, as its FIRST statement.
 2. src/app/login/layout.tsx renders <Welcome />, and src/components/welcome.tsx:21 renders <AppBar />. So AppBar lives in the LAYOUT of the /login segment.
 3. Next.js error.tsx does not catch errors thrown by the layout of its own segment, so src/app/login/error.tsx cannot catch it. There is no src/app/error.tsx. It bubbles all the way to src/app/global-error.tsx.
 4. src/app/global-error.tsx:15 renders <AppBar /> — the same component that just threw. It throws again. Loop.

SENTRY: issue 6834987895, 3380 events / 11 users, first seen 2025-08-25, still firing 2026-07-26. Sampled transactions: /login 447, /home 63, / 3, /terms 1 — never /me. ~63 events per session is the loop signature.

WHO IS BLOCKED: app.lemonsqueezy.com is a payments/tracking domain blocked by uBlock Origin + EasyPrivacy, Brave Shields, Safari content blockers, Pi-hole/NextDNS, and corporate/school DNS filtering. Note the churn data in wordle-teams-456: a large share of never-activated accounts are on school and corporate domains (multiple k12/university and enterprise domains) — exactly the networks most likely to filter that domain.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: the failure is 100% client-side, so Vercel/Axiom logs show nothing — which is why the earlier log-only pass found 163 visitors reaching /login with only ~12 completing auth and zero server errors. Sentry's 11-user count is an undercount: the /monitoring tunnel drops ~11% of events (306x 400, 87x 429), and an ad-blocker that blocks lemonsqueezy will usually block the Sentry tunnel too — the users most affected are the least able to report it.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Guard the call: if (typeof window.createLemonSqueezy === 'function') before invoking, and move the LemonSqueezy Setup into its own useEffect so a failure cannot block the PWA and time-zone logic that follow it in the same effect. 2) Move the <Script> out of the component into the root layout, or load it lazily only where checkout is actually used. 3) Remove <AppBar /> from src/app/global-error.tsx so the error fallback can never re-trigger the error it is displaying. 4) Add src/app/error.tsx so page-level errors stop escalating to global-error. 5) Re-run scripts/repro-login.mjs with lemon.js blocked and confirm the sign-in UI renders with 0 errors.
notes: SHIPPED TO PRODUCTION 2026-07-30. Merged dev (aeb3c00) then main (762cbda); Vercel production deploy Ready. Verified against live https://wordleteams.com/login with the regression script: lemon.js allowed PASS, lemon.js BLOCKED PASS (0 errors, page responsive, sign-in UI rendered). Was 998 errors in 500ms with an unresponsive page. Next: watch Sentry issue 6834987895 for new events — it should go quiet — then re-measure the login funnel in wordle-teams-390.
close_reason: Fixed in a5d91f1 on branch fix/login-lemonsqueezy-lockout. Verified on a local production build: with lemon.js blocked, 0 createLemonSqueezy errors and the sign-in UI renders (was 998 errors in 500ms with the page unresponsive). All 5 acceptance criteria met: guarded call driven by Script onReady, strategy corrected to afterInteractive, setup split out of the mount effect, AppBar removed from global-error.tsx, src/app/error.tsx added. Regression check at scripts/repro-login-lockout.mjs. Still needs a production deploy before the funnel can be re-measured.

title: [bug] e2e reuses whatever dev server holds port 3000, and it had been serving 2-day-old code
description:
FOUND 2026-09-02 while verifying wt-ksh.8.55's rendered output. THIS UNDERMINES EVERY e2e RESULT THIS PHASE HAS RELIED ON, which is why it is P1 despite being a test-harness issue.

WHAT HAPPENED. playwright.config.ts sets `reuseExistingServer: true` against http://localhost:3000. A `vite dev --port 3000` process had been running since **Aug 31 17:30** - two days, from an earlier session. Every e2e run since then attached to it instead of starting a fresh one, so the suite was exercising that process's view of the code rather than the working tree.

IT WAS DEMONSTRABLY STALE, not merely old. Measured side by side:
  - port 3000 (the 2-day-old process): GET /about carried `og:url = https://wordleteams.com` and NO rel=canonical - the pre-change behaviour.
  - port 3001 (a server started fresh from the same working tree, seconds earlier): `og:url = https://wordleteams.com/about` and the matching canonical.
Same files on disk, different output. So vite's HMR had NOT propagated the change into the long-lived SSR module graph.

HOW IT SURFACED, which is the part worth keeping. A new e2e asserting exactly one og:url per route reported TWO on /about. That number was impossible from either version of the code and is what forced the question "which server am I even talking to". A test asserting a COUNT caught what an assertion on a value would have missed - a stale server serving the old value looks like a straightforward failure, and the natural response is to doubt the change.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS TASK:
  - wt-ksh.8.40 (Task 17) had its blocker cleared on the premise that e2e was reliable enough to tell a regression from noise, citing six consecutive clean runs. Those runs cannot be assumed to have exercised the code that was current at the time.
  - Any "e2e is green" claim made in the last two days is suspect, INCLUDING the 65/65 runs recorded against the edge-cache work.
  - The failure is SILENT and biased toward false GREEN: a stale server passes tests for code that has since been broken.

AFTER KILLING IT, a genuinely clean full run gave 64 passed / 2 failed, both in invites.spec.ts, and the same spec passes 3/3 in isolation on a cold server. So the invites flakiness (wordle-teams-jtvx) is real and load-related rather than an artifact of this - but its severity was measured against runs that are now untrustworthy.

FIX SHAPE, not implemented here because it is a judgement call about developer ergonomics:
  1. `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI` is the Playwright default and is what most repos do - but this repo has no CI e2e at all (wt-ksh.8.49), so that expression is FALSE everywhere it runs and would simply disable reuse. That may be the right answer; it costs ~25s of startup per run.
  2. Keep reuse but make it verifiable: have the webServer probe assert a build identity (an endpoint or a header carrying the same deploy/commit id the Worker already has via CF_VERSION_METADATA) and refuse to reuse a mismatch.
  3. Keep reuse and document the hazard loudly in playwright.config.ts plus the Task 17 walk instructions.

Option 2 is the only one that keeps the ergonomics and removes the failure mode, but it needs a dev-only identity endpoint that does not exist.

IMMEDIATE MITIGATION FOR ANYONE RUNNING e2e BEFORE THIS IS FIXED: confirm nothing is already on 3000, or kill it first.

  ss -ltnp | grep :3000
close_reason: reuseExistingServer is now false, so an occupied port is a loud error naming both the port and the setting rather than a silent substitution - verified by starting a decoy server and watching the run refuse. Costs ~25s of startup per run, paid deliberately for the property that a green run means the code on disk is green. Re-enabling it requires a verifiable build identity, which nothing serves today; that condition is recorded in the config.

title: Phase 7.5 — the post-v2 roadmap, delivered WITH v2 rather than after it
description:
The seven post-v2 roadmap epics, moved INSIDE the v2 release rather than sitting behind it.

THE DECISION, and it is the owner's, taken 2026-09-02: Phase 7.5 lands BEFORE Phase 8's DNS cutover. v2 and all seven roadmap items go live in one flip, and the announcement email describes the whole thing at once.

WHY, because it changes how every item in here should be judged. v2 is a big, visible change and the owner is emailing every existing player about it - including people who hit early friction or confusion and gave up. That email is a re-engagement moment that only happens once. The explicit goal is that it does NOT say "and exciting new features are on the way": someone who comes back because of it should find enough new value in front of them to stay. So these items are not a roadmap any more; they are part of the launch.

WHAT MOVED. All seven post-v2 roadmap epics, in the owner's original priority order:
  #1 wordle-teams-qix  Team chat (free)
  #2 wordle-teams-418  Board import from a pasted screenshot (paid)
  #3 wordle-teams-4s0  Insights and analysis from global guess/answer data (paid)
  #4 wordle-teams-qt4  App onboarding tour
  #5 wordle-teams-0hx  SEO
  #6 wordle-teams-c0f  PWA launch screen and startup speed
  #7 wordle-teams-iht  Monetization and marketing for earlier, more consistent Pro conversions

WHAT CHANGED STRUCTURALLY: wordle-teams-qix was blocked by wt-ksh.9 (Phase 8 - Cutover), which is what made the whole chain post-v2. That edge is REMOVED and reversed - Phase 8 is now blocked by this phase instead. The serial chain between the seven is KEPT, because it encodes the owner's priority order.

READ THIS BEFORE PLANNING: the serial chain plus this phase gating cutover means the launch date is the sum of all seven epics, done one at a time. That is a real consequence of the sequencing decision and it should be checked against how long the owner is willing to hold v2 unlaunched. If it is too long, the honest options are to parallelise the chain, to cut items from the launch set, or to revisit the split (cut over quietly, land the rest, then email). Do not silently reorder or drop anything - surface it.

TWO OF THESE ARE NOT USER-VISIBLE VALUE, and the email cannot lean on them: #5 SEO and #7 monetization/marketing serve acquisition and conversion rather than the returning player. #6 PWA startup speed is felt but not announceable. The items that actually carry the email are #1 chat, #2 board import, #3 insights and #4 the onboarding tour - and #4 is the one aimed squarely at the population the email is trying to win back, since confusion is why they left.

ALSO IN SCOPE: brainstorming which further paid features are worth building, so the paid tier has a reason to exist beyond team count at relaunch.

title: Cloudflare serves a MANAGED robots.txt on beta; ours is never served
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-01 against https://beta.wordleteams.com/robots.txt. Beta does NOT serve the robots.txt in this repo. Cloudflare serves a MANAGED robots.txt instead - content-signals boilerplate, 'User-agent: * / Allow: /', and a block list of AI crawlers (Amazonbot, ClaudeBot, CCBot, Bytespider, Google-Extended and others). 64 lines, none of them ours.

WHAT IS MISSING AS A RESULT, on beta right now:
  Disallow: /app            -> the dashboard is crawlable
  Disallow: /me             -> the redirect to it is crawlable
  Disallow: /complete-profile
  Disallow: /api
  Sitemap: https://wordleteams.com/sitemap.xml   -> nothing points at the sitemap

WHY IT MATTERS FAR BEYOND BETA: at cutover the apex flips to this same Cloudflare zone. If the managed robots.txt feature is enabled there too, PRODUCTION's robots rules are silently replaced the moment the DNS changes, and v2's file is never served. The dashboard becomes crawlable on the real domain. Nothing in the repo, in any test, or in any gate can see this - our file is correct and is served correctly by the dev server and by the Workers assets layer; it is overridden at the zone edge.

This is precisely the class of defect a parity audit exists to find, and it is invisible to every automated check we have.

ALSO NOTE, SEPARATELY: v1's PRODUCTION robots.txt has a live bug. It says 'Disallow: /me/' with a trailing slash. robots.txt rules are prefix matches, so '/me/' does not match '/me' - v1's dashboard has been crawlable for the life of the project. Verified by fetching wordleteams.com/robots.txt on 2026-09-01. v2 fixes it by disallowing '/me' without the slash, pinned by a named test.

ACTIONS: find the Cloudflare setting (Managed robots.txt / content signals, zone level) and decide whether to disable it, merge our rules into it, or accept it. Then decide the same question for the production zone BEFORE the DNS flip. Task 13's parity harness will report prod and beta robots.txt as differing, and this is why - it is a real difference, not a harness bug.
acceptance_criteria: The robots.txt served at beta.wordleteams.com contains this repo's Disallow rules and Sitemap directive, or the override is a recorded, deliberate decision with the production zone's behaviour settled before cutover.
notes:
CORRECTED AND CLOSED 2026-09-01, SAME DAY IT WAS FILED. THE PREMISE WAS WRONG.

Cloudflare does NOT override this repo's robots.txt. It PREPENDS a managed block (content-signals preamble plus nine AI-crawler Disallow groups, delimited by 'BEGIN/END Cloudflare Managed content') and then serves OUR FILE IN FULL beneath it. Re-measured against beta on 2026-09-01: the served file is 108 lines; our content occupies lines 62-108 and is byte-identical to v2/public/robots.txt, including all four Disallow rules and the Sitemap directive.

  103: Disallow: /app
  104: Disallow: /me
  105: Disallow: /complete-profile
  106: Disallow: /api
  108: Sitemap: https://wordleteams.com/sitemap.xml

HOW THE WRONG CONCLUSION WAS REACHED, because it is the more useful half: the first fetch was piped through 'grep ... | head -20', which truncated the output before our section. Absence of evidence from a truncated view was read as evidence of absence. That is the same defect class this phase has now catalogued eleven times - an assertion or check scoped narrower than the claim drawn from it - committed while filing a P1 about a crawler policy.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, AND STILL WORTH A DECISION: the served file now contains TWO 'User-agent: *' groups - Cloudflare's (Allow: /, no disallows) at line 29, and ours (with the four disallows) at line 101. Google's parser merges groups sharing a user-agent, so our rules apply for Googlebot. Not every crawler merges; some take the first matching group only, and for those our disallows would be invisible. That is a real but much milder problem than 'our rules are never served', and it is what the follow-up issue tracks.

UNAFFECTED AND STILL TRUE: v1's production robots.txt says 'Disallow: /me/' with a trailing slash, and prefix matching means it does not cover '/me' - v1's dashboard has been crawlable for the life of the project. Verified independently by fetching wordleteams.com/robots.txt. v2 fixes it.
close_reason: Premise wrong: Cloudflare prepends its managed block and serves our file in full beneath it. Our rules ARE live on beta. Superseded by the duplicate-User-agent-group issue.

title: e2e flake: routes.spec.ts:146 stalls on /complete-profile after the profile submit
description:
e2e/routes.spec.ts:146 "a signed-in visitor to /home stays on /home" failed once during the review of Phase 7 Task 6 and passed on re-run in isolation. Lines 124-146 are untouched by that task's diff (e2f3d5f..498a313), so this is pre-existing rather than a regression.

SYMPTOM
The spec signs in, asserts /complete-profile, fills First Name and Last Name, clicks Submit, and then asserts toHaveURL('/app'). On the failing run the page was still on /complete-profile when that assertion timed out. Everything before the Submit had already passed, so the sign-in itself landed.

ISOLATION
pnpm exec playwright test e2e/routes.spec.ts:146 passes. The full suite passed on the next run too, so it is intermittent under load rather than deterministic.

LIKELY MECHANISM - the same family as wordle-teams-1cd, but a DIFFERENT navigation
1cd was the OTP sign-in hop: e2e/sign-in.ts returned as soon as Verify was clicked, so the caller's next assertion had to absorb a full document load on Playwright's 5s default. That was fixed by having sign-in.ts wait for the URL to leave /login (e2e/sign-in.ts:70-95), and the fix holds - this spec's toHaveURL('/complete-profile') is not what failed.

The unwaited hop here is the PROFILE SUBMIT, one step later and with no equivalent guard. src/routes/complete-profile.tsx handleSubmit awaits the completeProfile mutation and then awaits navigate({ to: '/app' }); /app's beforeLoad calls ensureQueryData for needsProfile and its loader awaits getMyTeams, amIPro and getMyPlayerId SEQUENTIALLY. All of that is billed to the caller's toHaveURL('/app'), which carries Playwright's 5s default. Under a full parallel suite against the local anonymous Convex backend that is the same shape of tail 1cd measured at 0.76-3.96s for the sign-in hop.

So: probably not a new root cause, but NOT covered by 1cd's fix either - 1cd guarded the /login exit, and nothing guards the /complete-profile exit. Leftover local e2e account or team state (1cd's original suspicion, teams scanned 1624 locally vs ~171 in production) remains a plausible aggravator for the loader half.

WHERE ELSE THE SAME HOP IS ASSERTED
e2e/complete-profile.spec.ts:24 and the two invites.spec.ts flows (201, 367) do the same submit-then-assert. invites.spec.ts:243 already carries a comment about Phase 4 losing a run in three to a related timeout and uses an explicit 20s there.

SUGGESTED DIRECTION - decide, do not just widen
Either a shared helper that completes the profile and waits for the /app landing the way sign-in.ts waits for the /login exit (preferred: it fixes every call site at once and keeps downstream assertions strict at 5s), or instrument the hop first and confirm the tail before choosing. Do NOT blanket-raise timeouts: 1cd's write-up is explicit that the fix was the helper's contract, not the ceiling.

FIRST STEP: instrument the submit-to-/app hop across a few full-suite runs the way 1cd instrumented sign-in, and confirm the measured tail before changing anything.

NOTE: e2e is not one of the four CI gates (wt-ksh.8.49), so this can only ever be caught by someone running pnpm e2e by hand - which is exactly how a spec once stayed red for three tasks.
notes:
Cross-referenced to wordle-teams-1cd (CLOSED, fixed in 10e4ce1): same failure shape - an unwaited navigation billed to a 5s default assertion - but a different hop. 1cd's fix guards the /login exit in e2e/sign-in.ts:70-95 and is still in place and working here; nothing guards the /complete-profile exit. Treat 1cd's write-up as the method to copy (instrument, measure the tail, fix the helper's contract rather than the ceiling), not as a duplicate.
OBSERVED AGAIN 2026-09-01, during Phase 7 Task 8's full `pnpm e2e`, and this time
BOTH halves of the prediction above failed in the same run:

  2 failed
    e2e/invites.spec.ts:119 - an invited address joins the team after completing a profile
    e2e/routes.spec.ts:124  - a signed-in visitor to /home stays on /home
  57 passed

Both passed on an immediate isolated re-run:
  pnpm exec playwright test e2e/invites.spec.ts:119 e2e/routes.spec.ts:124  -> 2 passed (10.7s)

So the "WHERE ELSE THE SAME HOP IS ASSERTED" section is no longer a prediction — the
invites flow flakes on the same unwaited /complete-profile -> /app hop under full-suite
load. That strengthens the preferred direction: a shared helper that waits for the /app
landing fixes both call sites at once, and widening a timeout on routes.spec.ts alone
would have left invites.spec.ts flaking.

Task 8 changed nothing on this path (its diff is robots.txt, a sitemap route,
lib/seo.ts, lib/sitemap.ts and __root.tsx meta), so this is still pre-existing.
OBSERVED AGAIN 2026-09-01, during the review of Phase 7 Task 9. TWO NEW MEMBERS OF THE SET, and the pattern behind all four is now visible.

  2 failed in the full run
    e2e/routes.spec.ts:124      - a signed-in visitor to /home stays on /home
    e2e/board-entry.spec.ts:27  - enter a board and see the score land
  57 passed

Both passed on an immediate isolated re-run: 4.9s and 6.8s respectively, against 14.4s and 20.8s when they timed out in the full run. That ~3x inflation under parallel load is the timing signature to look for - the tests are not doing anything different, they are waiting behind everything else.

Neither touches /about, and nothing in Task 9's diff (eight screenshots, a route, two test files, an addendum table) can reach them. Pre-existing, as with every prior sighting.

THE FOUR SPECS NOW KNOWN TO FLAKE, AND WHAT THEY HAVE IN COMMON:
  e2e/routes.spec.ts:146      - a signed-in visitor to /home stays on /home  (earlier line numbering)
  e2e/invites.spec.ts:119     - an invited address joins the team after completing a profile
  e2e/routes.spec.ts:124      - a signed-in visitor to /home stays on /home
  e2e/board-entry.spec.ts:27  - enter a board and see the score land

ALL FOUR ARE SHARED-AUTH-STATE TESTS. That is the pattern worth recording, and it is broader than the /complete-profile -> /app hop this issue was originally scoped to: board-entry.spec.ts:27 does not complete a profile at all. What it shares with the other three is that it depends on an authenticated session established outside the test body, so it is billed for whatever the sign-in path costs under load and has no guard of its own on that wait.

That does not overturn the preferred direction - a helper that waits for the landing rather than a widened ceiling - but it does widen where the helper has to live: the shared auth setup, not only the profile submit.

NOT REPRODUCED DELIBERATELY AND NOT INSTRUMENTED HERE. The FIRST STEP above still stands: measure the tail across several full-suite runs before changing anything.
AND ONCE MORE IN THE SAME SESSION, on the fix run for that review (pnpm e2e, 2026-09-01):

  2 failed
    e2e/invites.spec.ts:119 - an invited address joins the team after completing a profile
    e2e/routes.spec.ts:124  - a signed-in visitor to /home stays on /home
  57 passed (1.2m)

Isolated re-run of exactly those two: 2 passed (12.9s) - routes.spec.ts:124 in 4.9s, invites.spec.ts:119 in 12.2s. Same signature.

So across three consecutive full runs the failing pair is drawn from the same four specs and is never the same pair twice. That is the strongest evidence yet that the cause is contention on the shared authenticated state rather than anything in a particular spec, and it means "did the suite go green" is not a usable signal on this repo until it is fixed: a clean run proves nothing and a red one has to be re-run before it means anything.
NEW INSTANCE, DIFFERENT MECHANISM, SAME FAMILY — seen during Phase 7 Task 10's full
e2e run (2026-09-01, 60 tests, 57 passed):

  e2e/billing.spec.ts:81 "the billing link and the upgrade CTA each report their own failure"

failed NOT on a navigation timeout but on a Convex write conflict raised by its OWN seed,
before the page was touched:

  OptimisticConcurrencyControlFailure — Documents read from or written to the "teams" table
  changed while this mutation was being run and on every subsequent retry. Another call to
  this mutation changed the document with ID jx79bpqmkktj3thqbynnfpada58dj75c.

That is a different root cause from the submit-to-/app hop this issue describes: two
parallel workers' seed mutations contending on the SAME teams document. e2eSeed's
ensureTeamFor / ensureSharedTeamFor both do `ctx.db.query('teams').collect()` and then
write, so every concurrent seed reads every team row — the read set is the whole table,
and any other worker's insert invalidates it. With enough local teams accumulated (8.51
already notes 1624 locally vs ~171 in production) the retry window is wide enough to
exhaust Convex's retries.

Passed on re-run: `npx playwright test e2e/billing.spec.ts e2e/invites.spec.ts
e2e/routes.spec.ts --workers=1` — 42/42 green. So it is load/parallelism dependent, like
the rest of this family.

Two candidate fixes, both cheap, neither attempted here (out of Task 10's scope):
  1. Narrow the seeds' read set — an index on the team lookup instead of collect(),
     so a seed only conflicts with a seed touching the same team.
  2. Prune local e2e data (convex/e2ePrune.ts exists), which shrinks the collect().

Note for whoever picks this up: the collect()-then-write shape is deliberate at e2e scale
per e2eSeed.ts's own comment, so option 1 is a change of mind about that, not a bug fix.
OBSERVED AGAIN 2026-09-01, in the full `pnpm e2e` for the Phase 7 Task 10 review fixes.
A FIFTH AND SIXTH MEMBER OF THE SET, and a SECOND, INDEPENDENT PRESSURE SOURCE.

  2 failed of 60
    e2e/invites.spec.ts:119     - an invited address joins the team after completing a profile
    e2e/team-boards.spec.ts:28  - today's boards are concealed until you enter your own
  58 passed (1.0m)

Both passed on an immediate isolated re-run (6.6s and 11.8s together, against the
full-run timeouts). Same ~3x inflation signature recorded for the earlier four.

team-boards.spec.ts:28 is NEW - the spec landed with Task 10 - and its failure is not on
the /complete-profile -> /app hop at all: it timed out on `expect(entry).toBeHidden()`
after a board submit, waiting on the Convex subscription to push the new score. That is a
different navigation but the same shape: an unwaited async settle billed to a 5s default
under parallel load. e2e/board-entry.spec.ts:27, already in this set, is the same submit.

THE SECOND PRESSURE SOURCE - e2eSeed.ensureTeamFor's collect()-then-write, and OCC.
convex/e2eSeed.ts:69 does `await ctx.db.query('teams').collect()` and then inserts a team.
The collect() puts EVERY teams row in the transaction's read set, so any other concurrent
ensureTeamFor insert invalidates it and Convex retries the whole mutation. team-boards.spec.ts
takes the caller count from five to six - settings, teams, billing, board-entry, invites and
now team-boards - all running in parallel against the one local backend, every one of them
reading the whole table before writing to it. That is O(n^2) retry pressure on the seed
step, and it is billed to whatever assertion follows the seed.

Noted, deliberately NOT fixed here (Task 10 review scope was the component's coverage).
It is a separate lever from the /complete-profile helper this issue already prefers, and
worth weighing alongside it: a by_player index, or seeding through a single serialized
helper, would take the read set off the whole table. Compare convex/e2eSeed.ts:99's
ensureSharedTeamFor, which already exists precisely because two ensureTeamFor calls do not
compose.

Locally there are ~1624 teams rows against ~171 in production, which makes the collect()
both slower and far more likely to be invalidated here than it ever would be in prod.
OBSERVED AGAIN 2026-09-01, during Phase 7 Task 11's full `pnpm e2e` — and the
set is now WIDER than the six specs recorded so far. Six failed out of 60:

  e2e/board-entry.spec.ts:27   (already on the list)
  e2e/invites.spec.ts:119      (already on the list)
  e2e/team-boards.spec.ts:28   (already on the list)
  e2e/settings.spec.ts:28      NEW — "the hamburger opens the menu, and each item opens the dialog on its own tab"
  e2e/settings.spec.ts:95      NEW — "changing the reminder time and toggling Email each report success and persist"
  e2e/teams.spec.ts:35         NEW — "creating a team through the dropdown makes it the selected one"

All six pass in isolation. The three new ones were re-run together
(`pnpm e2e e2e/settings.spec.ts e2e/teams.spec.ts`) and all 8 tests in those
two files passed in 38s.

Task 11's diff cannot reach any of them: the only runtime change on a page an
e2e spec loads is the monthly-winner dialog on /app, which opens only when a
monthlyWinners row exists for the VIEWER'S PREVIOUS calendar month. Every e2e
account is created fresh per test, convex/e2eSeed.ts writes no dailyScores at
all, and board-entry.spec.ts enters boards dated TODAY — so no run of this
suite can produce a previous-month winner row, and the dialog is never mounted
open. Verified by the isolation runs above.

Point for whoever picks this up: the failure set is not a stable list of six
specs to memorise. It grows with parallel load, which supports the "unwaited
navigation billed to a 5s default assertion" mechanism over anything
spec-specific. The list quoted in the task briefs should say "any spec that
does a sign-in or profile-submit hop", not six line numbers.

THE FLAKE SET IS GROWING WITH LOAD, WHICH MEANS THE BASELINE IS NO LONGER A BASELINE. Trajectory across Phase 7: 2 known flakes -> 4 -> 5 -> 6, and Task 11's run failed SIX with three not previously on the list (settings.spec.ts:28, settings.spec.ts:95, teams.spec.ts:35). All pass in isolation; settings+teams re-ran 8/8.

The important read is that this is not a fixed set of six bad tests. It is a load-dependent failure rate across every spec that seeds shared auth state, and it climbs as the suite grows. Phase 7 has added specs steadily (routes, team-boards), so each task makes the next task's e2e run noisier, and 'known flake' is doing more and more work as an explanation.

TWO MECHANISMS ARE NOW IDENTIFIED, and they are independent:
  1. convex/e2eSeed.ts:69 does ctx.db.query('teams').collect() before inserting, so EVERY caller puts the whole table in its read set and any concurrent insert forces a retry - O(n^2) under parallel workers, and worse locally where the table holds ~1624 rows against production's ~171. Six specs now call ensureTeamFor.
  2. Unwaited settles after a navigation or submit - the /complete-profile -> /app hop this issue was originally scoped to, plus at least one more at a board submit.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ANNOYANCE: e2e is the ONLY place several protections in this codebase live, and CI does not run it (wt-ksh.8.49). A suite that fails six of sixty on a normal run cannot be used to tell a regression from noise - which is exactly the state that let the Phase 6 handoff's 'a watcher has been running since 2026-08-18' claim go unchallenged. Phase 7's own e2e-added protections are worth less every task this goes unfixed.

Raising to P1. Not a Phase 7 task, but it should be settled before Task 17's checklist walk leans on e2e output, and certainly before cutover.
FIXED. Five consecutive green full-suite runs, 60/60, plus a sixth after the wt-ksh.8.49 work. THREE causes, and the one this issue named was the second of them.

1. A READ-SET CONFLICT, WHICH NAMED ITSELF THE MOMENT THE SUITE WAS RUN. The first full run did not time out at all - it failed with OptimisticConcurrencyControlFailure on the "teams" table. convex/e2eSeed.ts's ensureTeamFor found the account's team with query('teams').collect(), which puts EVERY team in the mutation's read set, so any concurrent insert by another worker invalidated it and Convex exhausted its retries. Six specs call the seed, so the collision rate is quadratic in callers - which is exactly why the count climbed 2 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6 as the suite grew, and why everything passed in isolation. Now keyed on a deterministic id derived from the address (e2eTeamLegacyId, convex/lib/e2e.ts), so the lookup is an indexed by_legacyId point read and the read set is ONE document. ensureSharedTeamFor had the identical scan; fixing only the first would have left the flake alive via teams.spec.ts.

   IT IS ALSO A CORRECTNESS FIX. The old scan returned ANY team whose playerIds contained the account, which after an invite flow can be the INVITER's team - where the account is not owner, and e2e/invites.spec.ts:47 says being owner is what unlocks the controls.

2. THE UNWAITED PROFILE SUBMIT - this issue's prediction, and real, but only visible once the OCC failures stopped masking it. e2e/complete-profile.ts now waits for the app to leave /complete-profile, exactly as sign-in.ts waits for the /login exit; six call sites use it. The predicate is "left /complete-profile" rather than a destination, because a plain signup lands on /app and an invited address on /?team=. Board-entry submits are a different flow and are untouched.

3. ELEVEN PLAYWRIGHT WORKERS AGAINST ONE VITE DEV SERVER, which no one had looked at. Playwright defaults to cpus/2; on this box that is eleven. The product was never slow - the harness was oversubscribed. complete-profile.spec.ts:25 runs in 5.8s alone and was measured at 15.9s and 23.2s under eleven, so assertions on Playwright's 5s default failed on whichever spec happened to be landing a navigation while the others were.

   MEASURED BOTH WAYS, four full-suite runs each:
     11 workers, 5s ceiling   2-3 failures of 60, different specs each run
     11 workers, 20s ceiling  60/60, but the ceiling then hides a real stall
      4 workers, 5s ceiling   60/60, at the SAME 1.1-1.2m wall clock
   The wall clock decides it: the extra parallelism bought nothing, because these tests wait on the dev server rather than on CPU. So cutting workers removes the CAUSE where raising the ceiling would only accommodate it - which is the rule this issue set out, and it held. Pinned as a literal so the suite behaves the same on a 4-core CI runner as on a 22-core desktop; cpus/2 made the flake rate a property of the machine, which is a large part of why this was hard to pin down.

Commit eb1075d. Four gates green throughout.
close_reason: Closed

title: CI runs no e2e, so a whole class of route regressions deploys green
description:
deploy-v2.yml runs lint, typecheck, test:once, build, deploy, then smoke-tests /login only. It never runs Playwright. Phase 7 has been adding its real-response coverage - cache headers, redirect chains, route existence, link targets, page titles - to e2e/routes.spec.ts, and NONE of it runs in CI. Those protections exist only when a human remembers to run pnpm e2e.

DEMONSTRATED, not theorised. Task 5's review swapped the two legal pages' <title> elements AND mispointed the footer's 'Privacy Policy' link at /terms: all four CI gates passed and it would have deployed to beta green. Separately, deleting src/routes/me.tsx - the permanent redirect that exists because production PWA installs carry start_url: /me and can never be updated - also passed all four gates, which is why src/routes.test.ts was created in Task 1.

THE PATTERN THAT WORKS, and it is already in this repo: a source-reading unit test. src/routes.test.ts, src/lib/sw-push.test.ts, src/styles.test.ts and now src/legal-prose.test.ts all read files as strings under vitest and therefore ARE gates. Every task that adds an e2e-only protection should ask whether a source guard can cover the same invariant.

OPTIONS: run e2e in CI (needs a Convex backend in the workflow - the reason it is absent); or accept the split and adopt the source-guard convention explicitly, writing it into the plan so later tasks do not each rediscover it. The second is cheaper and is what the phase has converged on by accident; making it deliberate is the point of this issue.
acceptance_criteria: Either e2e runs in CI, or the source-guard convention is written into the plan and the phase's e2e-only protections have been reviewed for which ones need a gate-level twin.
notes:
DONE, by the second of the two options this issue offered: the source-guard convention is now written into the plan, and the phase's e2e-only protections have been reviewed.

THE CONVENTION is a new section in docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit.md, alongside the other "each line here cost this project real time" entries. It states the rule, ranks the three forms of twin (render under jsdom > parse with src/test-support/source-ast.ts > read as a string), and carries the two traps this phase paid for: strip comments before asserting over source, because the first textual occurrence of almost any code string here is prose about that code; and bound a slice at BOTH ends, because slice(indexOf(x)) runs to end-of-file and, on a miss, slice(-1) silently returns the last character.

THE REVIEW FOUND COVERAGE BETTER THAN THIS ISSUE ASSUMED. routes.test.ts, server.test.ts, cache-policy.test.ts, crawler-metadata.test.ts, legal-prose.test.ts, login-error.test.ts, maintenance-page.test.ts, styles.test.ts, about-screenshots.test.ts and feature-cards.test.ts already twin the route, cache-header, metadata, legal-prose and landing-content protections.

ONE REAL GAP, AND IT WAS HIDING BEHIND A FALSE CLAIM. The app bar's link targets and the Home link's active state were protected ONLY by e2e/routes.spec.ts:221,258,265. §7a row 19 asserted "plus the source guard in v2/src/routes.test.ts" - and that guard does not exist: routes.test.ts pins / and /home's ROUTE behaviour (their beforeLoad) and never reads Header.tsx's links. So the wordmark could have been repointed at /home with all four gates green, which is precisely this issue's thesis, sitting inside a row that claimed otherwise. Row 19 corrected.

THE TWIN is in src/components/Header.hook.test.ts, which already renders the real bar. It asserts the anchors EXHAUSTIVELY - ['/', '/', '/about'], so an added link is a change here too - and reads source for the activeProps the Link mock necessarily drops, comments stripped and the slice bounded at both ends. The exhaustive form earned its keep immediately: the first draft asserted ['/', '/'] and failed on the real component, which had a third link.

FOUR MUTATIONS, ALL KILLED: repointing the wordmark, repointing the Home link, deleting activeProps, renaming the active class. Worth recording that the first two attempts at the last two were NOT kills - the anchor matched twice, because there is a second nav link carrying the same activeProps - and reporting those as kills would have been wrong.

WHY NOT e2e IN CI, recorded in the plan rather than left implicit: the suite drives a local anonymous Convex backend with E2E_TEST_MODE=true, and that flag must never be set on the deployment CI deploys to (wordle-teams-7az). Standing up a second backend inside the deploy job is real work with a new failure surface and would gate every beta deploy on a browser suite. Revisit if the twin set stops keeping up.

Four gates green: 1247 tests / 78 files. e2e 60/60.
close_reason: Closed

title: Confirm s-maxage on a Worker response actually reaches Cloudflare's edge cache
description:
Phase 7 Task 3 set public, s-maxage=86400 on static documents to buy back wordle-teams-jcj's cost (28-41% of requests to v1's marketing pages missed the edge and cold-started a function at ~1.9s). THE HEADER MAY BE NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT. A response returned from a Worker's fetch handler is not written to Cloudflare's CDN cache by default. That needs one of: the Cache API (caches.default.put), cf: { cacheEverything: true } on an origin subrequest, or a Cache Rule. Review searched the repo on 2026-08-31 and found NONE of the three - no caches.default, no cacheEverything, no Cache Rule. wrangler.jsonc uses a Custom Domain route with main: src/server.ts.

So the header is correct and needed regardless (browsers and any downstream shared cache honour it), but the edge win this task exists to deliver may currently be zero.

ONE COMMAND SETTLES IT, once the change is on beta - and it must be run TWICE, because the first request is what would populate the cache:
  curl -sI https://beta.wordleteams.com/about | grep -i 'cf-cache-status|cache-control'
HIT on the second request means it works. DYNAMIC, or no cf-cache-status at all, means a Cache Rule for the static paths is still needed.

This also sets the severity of the sibling issue about stale-while-revalidate having no invalidation: if nothing is cached at the edge, neither problem bites yet.
acceptance_criteria: cf-cache-status is measured on beta for a static path across two consecutive requests, and either reports HIT, or a Cache Rule is added and then reports HIT.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-09-02 ON BETA. THE ANSWER IS NO, AND THE ISSUE'S OWN REMEDY DOES NOT APPLY.

Three consecutive GETs to https://beta.wordleteams.com/about (real GETs, not HEAD — a HEAD can be treated differently by the cache, so the first HEAD run was discarded and redone):

  cache-control: public, max-age=0, s-maxage=86400, stale-while-revalidate=604800
  cf-cache-status: (ABSENT on all three)

Not DYNAMIC, not MISS, not BYPASS — the header is not present at all. Same for GET /. So the SSR document never enters Cloudflare's CDN cache and Task 3's edge win is currently ZERO, exactly as the review predicted. The header is still correct and still earns the browser and any downstream shared cache, so nothing shipped is wrong; it is just not buying the thing it was added to buy.

THE EDGE CACHE ITSELF IS WORKING ON THIS ZONE — so this is not a zone-level misconfiguration. Same two-request test against the Workers Assets paths:

  /opengraph-image.png  -> cf-cache-status: HIT
  /favicon.ico          -> cf-cache-status: HIT

Assets are served by the assets layer without entering the Worker's fetch handler, so they are cached normally. Only the Worker-GENERATED documents are absent from the cache. (Side note for wordle-teams-82zq: those two are an edge HIT despite carrying `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`, so 82zq costs a browser revalidation round-trip, not an origin hit. That lowers its severity; it does not remove it.)

A CACHE RULE WILL NOT FIX THIS, so the "or a Cache Rule is added and then reports HIT" branch of the acceptance criterion is not an available option. Verified against Cloudflare's docs rather than assumed:

  - developers.cloudflare.com/workers/reference/how-the-cache-works/ — "For projects where there is no backend (that is, the entire project is on Workers), the Cache API is the only option to customize caching."
  - developers.cloudflare.com/cache/concepts/cache-responses/ — when a Worker generates a response without sending any subrequests, the response did not come from cache, so the cache status is none/unknown. Matches the measurement exactly.
  - Workers and Response Header Transform Rules execute AFTER the caching decision is made and cannot influence whether a response is cached.

wrangler.jsonc uses a Custom Domain with main: src/server.ts, and src/server.ts renders the document itself — there is no origin subrequest anywhere in the path for a Cache Rule to act on.

SO THE ONLY MECHANISM THAT WORKS IS THE CACHE API (caches.default.match / .put) inside src/server.ts. That is a larger change than this issue was scoped for and it is NOT being made unilaterally, because it interacts with two things already on the board:

  1. It makes wt-ksh.8.46 (stale-while-revalidate with no invalidation) go from theoretical to live. Today nothing is at the edge, so a stale document cannot be served and `wrangler deploy` purging nothing costs nothing. The moment we put() ourselves, a deploy leaves a day of fresh + a week of SWR of the OLD marketing pages at the edge with no eviction path. An explicit purge step, or a deploy-versioned cache key, has to land WITH the put — not after it.
  2. cache-policy.ts's session reasoning has to be re-applied to the WRITE side, not just the header. Reading `caches.default.match` before the session check would serve a shared document to a signed-in visitor; writing without the check would store a token-bearing one. The existing policy computes what the header says; it does not currently gate what we store.

FILED SEPARATELY rather than absorbed here — see the follow-up issue linked from this one. This issue's measurement half is complete and is what it was actually asking.
close_reason: Measured on beta 2026-09-02: no cf-cache-status at all on Worker-rendered documents across three consecutive GETs, so the edge win is currently zero. The 'or a Cache Rule' branch of the acceptance criterion is not an available remedy - verified against Cloudflare docs that Cache Rules run before the Worker and a Worker-generated response with no origin subrequest is not cache-eligible. The Cache API remedy is split out to wordle-teams-fqeq, which carries the HIT goal and is parented to wt-ksh.8.

title: A NUL byte makes sw-push.test.ts invisible to every recursive grep
description:
v2/src/lib/sw-push.test.ts contains one literal NUL byte, in a malformed-URL fixture around line 148. GNU grep classifies the file as binary, so a recursive search does NOT list it - measured 2026-08-31, both with and without -I:

  grep -rl REMINDER_FALLBACK src/   ->   src/sw.ts, src/lib/sw-push.ts   (the test file is absent)

git diff also renders it as 'Bin 8175 -> 8811 bytes' rather than a readable diff, so a change to it is unreviewable by eye in a normal diff.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS: Phase 7 is an audit phase and a great deal of it is grep-driven - finding every URL-bearing consumer, every stale comment, every delete site. This file is a silent hole in every one of those sweeps. Phase 7 Task 1's implementer nearly missed its three dashboard-URL references for exactly this reason, and found them only by reading the file directly.

FIX: replace the literal NUL in the fixture with a JavaScript escape sequence, which preserves the test's intent (a URL containing a NUL) while making the file text again.

Found during Phase 7 Task 1 (wt-ksh.8.24).
acceptance_criteria: A recursive grep for a string that appears in sw-push.test.ts lists the file, and git diff renders changes to it as text.
notes:
SCOPE IS MUCH WIDER THAN ONE TEST FILE. Measured 2026-08-31: EVERY SSR DOCUMENT THIS APP SERVES CONTAINS NUL BYTES. A fetched GET / holds 5 of them - TanStack serializes route ids as i:"__root__\u0000" into the dehydrated payload, so the NUL is structural, not incidental, and it is present on every rendered route.

CONSEQUENCE: any grep-based inspection of a fetched page SILENTLY FINDS NOTHING. Not an error, not a warning - grep classifies the response as binary and reports no matches. `file` calls it 'data'. This bit the Phase 7 controller directly while verifying Task 4: greps for the h1, for 'Compete with friends', and for the feature-card copy all came back empty against a page that was in fact fully server-rendered, and the natural reading of that evidence was 'the landing page is client-rendered only, so crawlers see nothing' - a serious and completely false conclusion about the exact property the page exists to provide.

WHO NEEDS TO KNOW:
  - wt-ksh.8.36 (Task 13, scripts/parity-routes.mjs) fetches every route on prod and beta and inspects title / canonical / OG tags. If it matches with anything grep-like, or shells out to grep, it will report every beta route as missing every tag. Use a real parser or strip NULs first.
  - wt-ksh.8.40 (Task 17, the written checklist walk) - same hazard for any spot-check by curl+grep.
  - Anyone debugging a page by curl+grep, ever.

WORKAROUNDS: grep -a treats the input as text and works. python/node string handling is unaffected. tr -d '\000' before piping also works.

The original finding - v2/src/lib/sw-push.test.ts carrying a literal NUL, making it invisible to recursive source greps and rendering its git diff as 'Bin 8175 -> 8811 bytes' - still stands and is separately fixable. The SSR-document half is NOT fixable here; it is how TanStack serializes, so the answer is that tooling must not assume text.
close_reason: Literal NUL replaced with an escape in v2/src/lib/sw-push.test.ts (a32b08f). Both acceptance criteria verified: a recursive grep for REMINDER_FALLBACK now lists the file, and git diff renders it as text. Test intent preserved - the shipped source line was evaluated and element 4 is still a one-char string with charCodeAt(0)===0. The SSR-document half is unfixable by design (TanStack serialises route ids with a NUL) and is captured in the notes for wt-ksh.8.36 / wt-ksh.8.40 to consume.

notes:
CUTOVER-RELEVANT, from Phase 7 Task 5: wordle-teams-4yt records that the privacy policy and terms both name Apple and Facebook as sign-in providers. Neither has EVER been offered - v1 had google, twitter, azure, github, slack, discord; v2 has google, microsoft, github, discord (verified in v2/convex/auth.ts:32-35). So a published privacy policy names two companies as recipients of user data that receive none, and omits Microsoft and Discord, which do. The privacy policy also says a username is collected; no username field exists in either codebase.

This was ALREADY WRONG IN v1 and is not a re-platform regression, so it does not block cutover - but the cutover is when these pages start being served from the new stack under the same domain, and it is the natural moment to correct a document that has been inaccurate the whole time. The owner should decide before the flip whether to correct it, since amending legal copy is their call and not a task outcome.
MAINTENANCE MODE IS TWO STEPS, NOT ONE (from Phase 7 Task 7 review; full detail in wt-ksh.8.52).

The runbook must not say "set MAINTENANCE=true" and stop. `/` is the one path that is both gated (v2/src/lib/maintenance.ts GATED_PATHS) and edge-cacheable (v2/src/lib/cache-policy.ts STATIC_DOCUMENTS), so while the flag is off the landing page goes out `public, s-maxage=86400, stale-while-revalidate=604800`. A shared cache still holding that pre-outage copy keeps serving it for up to 24h fresh + 7 days stale, and the gate never sees those requests because the Worker is not invoked on a cache hit. `wrangler deploy` purges nothing.

  1. Set MAINTENANCE to 'true' (Cloudflare dashboard var; no deploy needed).
  2. Purge the Cloudflare cache, at minimum `/`.

Turning maintenance OFF has the mirror consideration only in that the maintenance response itself is `private, no-store`, so nothing to purge on the way back up.

Cross-reference wt-ksh.8.45: whether s-maxage reaches Cloudflare's edge at all is still unmeasured. If it turns out nothing is cached, step 2 is a no-op and can be dropped from the runbook — measure before writing it as a hard requirement.
BLOCKER-CLASS ITEM FOR THE RUNBOOK, from Phase 7 Task 8: Cloudflare serves a MANAGED robots.txt on beta and this repo's file is never served (measured 2026-09-01). At cutover the apex joins the same zone. Before the DNS flip, settle whether the production zone does the same - if it does, v2's robots rules never take effect and the dashboard is crawlable on the real domain. See the dedicated issue. Nothing in CI can detect this; it must be checked by fetching robots.txt from the live hostname.
CORRECTION 2026-09-01 to the note above about a Cloudflare managed robots.txt override: THE OVERRIDE CLAIM WAS WRONG. Cloudflare prepends its managed block and serves this repo's robots.txt in full beneath it; our disallows and the Sitemap directive are live on beta. The remaining, milder question is the duplicate 'User-agent: *' group and whether every crawler merges them - see the dedicated issue. Still worth confirming the production zone's behaviour before the flip, but it is not the blocker the earlier note described.
RUNBOOK REQUIREMENTS BANKED BY TASK 14 (2026-09-01). Three open issues now close on THIS task rather than on their own measurement, because each one's done-when is a checklist step, not a state. All three were measured green on beta today; that is explicitly not sufficient.

1. wordle-teams-7az - E2E_TEST_MODE must be UNSET on the Convex deployment at cutover, and RE-CONFIRMED AFTER THE FINAL DATA COPY. Currently not set on fabulous-goldfish-949. The risk is the gap: someone sets it to run e2e against beta between now and cutover and nobody clears it. If it survives, two public mutations (testOtps.takeFor, e2eSeed.ensureTeamFor) become live unauthenticated write paths, AND isE2eTraffic silently suppresses sign-in codes and team invites for every e2e+*@wordleteams.com address with no error raised anywhere. Closing 7az is also what makes convex/lib/e2e.ts's comment true on its production half.

2. wordle-teams-3bl - the checklist must name ALL FIVE POLAR_* variables AS A SET THAT MOVES TOGETHER: POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN, POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET, POLAR_PRO_MONTHLY_PRODUCT_ID, POLAR_PRO_ANNUAL_PRODUCT_ID, POLAR_SERVER. Polar's sandbox is a wholly separate instance with its own accounts, products and tokens, so flipping POLAR_SERVER to 'production' without the token and both product ids sends real subscribers to an instance holding none of their data. Currently POLAR_SERVER='sandbox' on beta, correct for Task 18 and WRONG the moment the domain flips.

3. THE MEASUREMENT RULE ITSELF BELONGS IN THE RUNBOOK, because every check above is run under time pressure with DNS waiting. Two ways to read the wrong machine, both silent:
   - A bare 'convex env --prod' from v2/ resolves to the LOCAL anonymous backend and reports success. It returned SITE_URL=http://localhost:3000 today. Read a beta-only sentinel FIRST, in every shell: SITE_URL must be https://beta.wordleteams.com.
   - 'convex env get' EXITS 0 whether or not the variable exists. Verified: E2E_TEST_MODE absent, exit 0. Match the 'not found' TEXT, never the exit code.

ALSO FOR THE RUNBOOK, from Task 13's parity run and wt-ksh.8.52: maintenance mode is TWO STEPS, not one. '/' is edge-cacheable and a cached landing page outlives the MAINTENANCE flag, so the Worker is never invoked.

AND: wrangler var ENVIRONMENT is currently 'beta' and MUST become 'production' at cutover, or every LogSnag funnel event is mistagged.

IT SUPERSEDES wt-ksh.9's runbook prose, and says so at the top, because two of that text's bullets are factually wrong. Section 7 records five claims that were believed, written down and acted on: nothing in v2 deletes from players/playerMembership (false since e2ePrune); cascadeDeleteTeam has two callers (four); the db.delete count is a constant (14 -> 21 -> 26); nothing in v2 writes playerMembership/webhookEvents (false since Phase 5's billing.ts); and v1's one-hour passcode claim against this deployment's OTP_EXPIRY_SEC = 300.

The runbook states what actually happens if it survives, including the silent half: isE2eTraffic suppresses sign-in codes and invitations for e2e+*@wordleteams.com with no error raised anywhere.
  wordle-teams-3bl - all five POLAR_* named as a set that moves together, with the reason (sandbox is a wholly separate instance) and the four token scopes with their call sites.
  wordle-teams-c68 - the corrected delete-site facts are in section 7, and the runbook tells the operator to RUN the grep rather than trust a figure, including the one it prints itself.

ALSO IN IT, from this phase's measurements rather than from the plan's list: the measurement rule as section 0 (both silent ways to read the wrong machine, with the sentinel); maintenance mode as TWO steps because / is edge-cacheable and a cached landing outlives the flag (wt-ksh.8.52), with the caveat that wt-ksh.8.45 may make the whole section moot and one curl settles it; the copy's --with-reminders restoration (wt-ksh.7.32) with the banner that states its mode in both directions; the supabase.co DNS trap with its two misleading symptoms; ENVIRONMENT -> production or every funnel event is mistagged; and a rollback section, which the plan's required-lines list did not ask for but wt-ksh.9's acceptance criteria requires ('rollback path documented and live').

Section 8 lists the nine known open items at cutover, including wordle-teams-4yt, which is the owner's call and not a task outcome: the privacy policy and terms name Apple and Facebook as sign-in providers and claim a username is collected, none of which is true in either codebase.

description:

The interactive half is walked by hand with the owner: sign-in by OTP and each social provider, the whole dashboard including TeamBoards and the celebration dialog, teams create/rename/invite/cancel/remove/leave/delete, billing and the portal, every settings control, the error states, maintenance mode on and off, and the PWA installed from beta. HAZARD FROM wt-ksh.8.44, RAISED TO P1: every SSR document this app serves contains NUL bytes (TanStack serializes route ids as __root__\u0000), so grep treats a fetched page as BINARY and silently reports no matches. It is not an error and not a warning - it looks exactly like the content being absent. title: Task 15: a fresh copy run and verify-parity
description:

DIAGNOSED 2026-09-01. supabase.co is blocked by DNS FILTERING ON THE NETWORK. The decisive test, against the SAME resolver over UDP 53:

  dig @8.8.8.8 github.com    NOERROR
  dig @8.8.8.8 supabase.com  NOERROR
  dig @8.8.8.8 convex.dev    NOERROR
  dig @8.8.8.8 supabase.co   NO RESPONSE AT ALL

title: Task 14: env and secret hygiene (cd8, 7az, 3bl, 5il)
description:
THE MEASUREMENT RULE FOR THIS WHOLE TASK: convex env --prod and convex run --prod silently fall back to the local backend at 127.0.0.1:3210. A bare convex env list --prod on 2026-08-31 returned the LOCAL backend's variables including SITE_URL=http://localhost:3000. And convex env get exits 0 whether or not the variable exists. So establish a beta sentinel first and match on the not-found text, never the exit code. Any step whose evidence is a bare command's exit status is not evidence. For 5il, if .dev.vars reached a deployment the secrets must be ROTATED, not merely excluded going forward.

## Context

THE SENTINEL DID EXACTLY WHAT THE PLAN WARNED IT WOULD. From v2/, 'npx convex env get SITE_URL --prod' returned http://localhost:3000: v2/.env.local sets CONVEX_DEPLOYMENT=anonymous:anonymous-v2, so --prod resolves to the LOCAL backend and reports success. Extracting that key inline on a command line was refused by the sandbox classifier, correctly - it is indistinguishable from credential exfiltration. It needs the owner to export CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY for the beta deployment into the session, or to run the reads themselves.

THE READS, once the sentinel says https://beta.wordleteams.com:
  npx convex env get SITE_URL --prod        expect https://beta.wordleteams.com
  npx convex env get E2E_TEST_MODE --prod   expect the NOT FOUND text, and match on that text, never on the exit code - 'convex env get' exits 0 either way
  npx convex env list --prod                for the five POLAR_* vars (wordle-teams-3bl)

STEP 1-2 (wordle-teams-cd8) - CLOSED. SITE_URL = https://beta.wordleteams.com, E2E_TEST_MODE not found. title: Task 13: scripts/parity-routes.mjs
description:
Compares both origins route by route: status, Cache-Control, Content-Type, title, canonical, OG tags, and whether the route exists at all. Verdict logic goes in scripts/lib/ per the rule recorded in vitest.config.ts's comment, so a test can reach it; the fetching cannot be tested and stays in the script. TWO THINGS TO GET RIGHT: do not follow redirects silently, since /me returning a 301 to /app is the interesting answer - use redirect: manual and report the Location; and send no cookies, because the anonymous rendering is what a crawler and a first-time visitor get and it is the case the cache policy makes cacheable. /branding goes in the list and is EXPECTED to be absent on beta.

## Context
Phase 7 of the v2 re-platform (T13). Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit-design.md  Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit.md
acceptance_criteria: The report classifies match, missing-on-beta, differs and expected, with a test proving that identical bodies with different cache headers still count as a difference; and it has been run against both origins with the output saved.
notes:
HAZARD FROM wt-ksh.8.44, RAISED TO P1: every SSR document this app serves contains NUL bytes (TanStack serializes route ids as __root__\u0000), so grep treats a fetched page as BINARY and silently reports no matches. It is not an error and not a warning - it looks exactly like the content being absent. This already produced a false conclusion once during Phase 7, that the landing page was client-rendered and invisible to crawlers, when it was fully server-rendered.

So: do not inspect a fetched document with grep, or by shelling out to it. Parse the HTML, or strip NULs first (tr -d '\000'), or use grep -a. A harness that gets this wrong reports every route on beta as missing every meta tag, which reads as a catastrophic parity failure and is not one.
DONE. scripts/parity-routes.mjs (fetching) + scripts/lib/parity-routes-report.mjs (verdicts) + 34 tests. Run against both origins; output saved to docs/superpowers/audits/2026-09-01-parity-routes.md. Four gates green: lint 0, tsc 0, 1230 tests / 77 files, build 0.

THE FIRST DRAFT LIED, AND IT LIED IN THE HAZARD-ADJACENT WAY. Not the NUL bytes - those were handled from the start - but the HEAD BOUND. The reader scanned only up to </head>, which is correct HTML and wrong for this measurement: React streams metadata into the BODY on dynamically rendered routes and hoists it into the head only once the client runs. Measured on prod 2026-09-01: /about closes </head> at byte 2960 and emits its <title> at 9787. Prerendered routes like /privacy put it in the head as expected, so HALF the routes looked right. The report claimed prod's /, /about and /login had no title and no OpenGraph tags at all, and rendered twelve phantom og:* divergence rows per route - "beta invented twelve tags production never had". Fixed by bounding on foreign content and serialized text (svg/math/script/template) instead of on the head. Pinned by a regression test carrying the byte offsets.

MUTATION PASS: 15 mutations, all 15 killed, but only after two rounds. Two survived round one and both were the test's fault, not the code's:
- The script-payload test quoted its markup the way a JS string literal would, so the backslashes alone defeated the attribute parser and deleting the script stripper changed nothing. Rewritten with raw markup.
- "First title wins" was claimed by the code and exercised by nothing. Pinned.
Three more round-one mutations were NO-OPS whose perl anchors never matched - counted as no-ops, not kills, and redone as exact string swaps.

RESULT: 15 routes - 13 differs, 1 missing-on-prod (/app, correct), 1 expected (/branding). Every row is a real difference. Note prod's /branding is a 307 to /login, not a public page - it was never crawlable, which makes its absence on beta cheaper than assumed.

FILED FROM THE OUTPUT: wordle-teams-82zq (P2, /opengraph-image.png went from immutable/1yr on prod to max-age=0/must-revalidate on beta - cache-policy.ts only reaches text/html so no policy covers static assets at all), wordle-teams-d2oc (P3, beta's 307s carry no Cache-Control - the exact gap server.ts's maintenance comment warns about), wordle-teams-cog5 (P3, /me is 307 while the route file and the handoff both say permanent), wordle-teams-woe0 (P3, Task 16 §7a row for /about's title).

CONFIRMS wt-ksh.8.55 mechanically: og:url is https://wordleteams.com on every beta route including /about and /home. relativize() is written so that a URL pointing at the OTHER origin stays absolute, which is what makes it visible - reducing every URL to its pathname would have rendered it as "/" on both sides and filed it as a match.

description:

It goes in Header.tsx, which already renders a Billing button and already computes isPro === false at :106 with a comment on why it is not !isPro. Phase 7 of the v2 re-platform (T12). Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit-design.md  Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit.md

Note the comped-pro OWNER still sees Billing rather than Upgrade - that is correct behaviour, not a residue, so the sandbox pass still wants a fresh non-pro account, which can now be made with ZERO teams instead of two.

REVIEW FOUND A CRITICAL THIS TASK INTRODUCED, and it is the most consequential defect of the phase. The implementer made the Billing/Upgrade slot a SWAP on the stated grounds that v1 does the same. IT DOES NOT. v1's user-dropdown.tsx:55-59 has TWO INDEPENDENT GATES THAT OVERLAP ON PURPOSE - proMember is 'pro', hasBillingAccount is ['pro','cancelled','expired'] - with a comment three lines above saying exactly why: 'A lapsed player sees both entries: Billing to manage past invoices or payment details, Upgrade to start again.'
