And they arrive in that state at cutover: migrate.ts:495-501 copies both statuses out of Supabase, and polarEvents.ts:60-63 maps every subscription.revoked to 'expired'.

WHAT MAKES IT INSTRUCTIVE IS HOW IT GOT IN. The implementer DID check v1 before deciding, found both predicates, and read them as a swap. The evidence was read; the conclusion was still wrong, and then propagated into five places including two beads issues. Third time this phase a confidently-stated claim about v1 has failed independent check - after the OTP expiry ('1 hour' vs a real 300 seconds) and the contrast figures. title: Task 11: the monthly-winner celebration dialog (wordle-teams-k7w)
description:
v2 has the backend and no way to call it: winners.ts exports only internal helpers, so there is no public query for last month's winner and no mutation marking a celebration seen. Divergence 3 in 7a is a careful argument about hasSeenCelebration's rewrite semantics for a dialog that has never existed. THIS TASK BUILDS THREE THINGS: the query, the mutation and the UI. V1 HAS A BUG HERE: when someone else won, it renders the CURRENT user's name, so the dialog tells you that you won and then says better luck next time. Recommendation is to fix it and record a divergence. Two more decisions: react-confetti-explosion is a v1 dependency v2 does not have (CSS is the smaller answer, and respect prefers-reduced-motion, which v1 does not); and do the hasSeenCelebration append INSIDE the mutation rather than porting v1's read-modify-write, which is the pattern wordle-teams-069 is open against.

## Context
Phase 7 of the v2 re-platform (T11). Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit-design.md  Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit.md
acceptance_criteria: The dialog renders for a seeded winner row, the append is transactional and idempotent, both halves of divergence 3 are pinned by tests, and the v1 naming bug is either fixed and recorded or deliberately ported with a comment saying so.
notes:
CLOSED 2026-09-01. Commits 58963bd (the feature), 49205ee, 4383c81 (review fixes).

The second of the two v1 dashboard features with NO OWNING PHASE. v2 had the whole write side and no way to read it: winners.ts exported only internal helpers, so 7a divergence 3 - a careful, evidence-cited argument about hasSeenCelebration's rewrite semantics - had been sitting in the divergence list since Phase 2 protecting a field NOTHING HAD EVER READ. This task built the reader, so those semantics finally got exercised. Both halves already had tests; review confirmed each pins its own direction and neither was duplicated.

v1's MISNAMED-WINNER BUG IS FIXED, NOT PORTED. v1 interpolates the CURRENT VIEWER's name into the 'somebody else won' branch, so every member of a team where they did not win is told their own name won and then 'better luck next time' - the two halves of the dialog contradicting each other. 7a row 35.

REVIEW CORRECTED THE CLAIM ABOUT THAT FIX, and the correction is the useful part: the implementer said the mistake was made UNREPRESENTABLE. It is not. Reintroducing it one layer down - ctx.db.get(row.playerId) -> ctx.db.get(playerId) in the Convex query - carries the viewer's name with no type error. Three tests catch it, so it is FIXED AND PINNED, not impossible. Row 35 reworded to the property that is actually true: the viewer's name is never in scope where the copy is built. The fixer then found the same overclaim in two code comments the review had not scoped and corrected those too.

INSTANCE SIXTEEN, AND A NEW KIND. The confetti's positive branch was asserted only in an environment production never has. Mutating window.matchMedia?.(Q).matches ?? false to window.matchMedia?.(Q) ?? false - a truthy MediaQueryList - left ALL 1171 TESTS PASSING while the winner got zero confetti in production, forever, silently. Every test asserting confetti renders ran under jsdom, where matchMedia is undefined, so the ?? false was what let pieces through; the one test that stubbed it returned matches: true. No test ever exercised 'matchMedia exists and reports false' - the configuration of every real browser. The assertion was bounded and the set was right; the ENVIRONMENT was not production's. Generalised in the test's comment to any matchMedia / navigator.* / window.* capability check pinned only under jsdom. Controller verified the mutant now dies.

ALSO CAUGHT BY THE IMPLEMENTER ITSELF, before review: the remount key was pinned nowhere, so dismissing one team's dialog silently suppressed the next team's forever. And its own 'the server renders nothing' test passed with the hydration gate DELETED, because a closed Radix Dialog is not a DOM node either way - it changed the test to assert the queryKeys and rewrote the doc comment to say what the gate actually prevents, rather than adjusting the score.

CSS confetti, no dependency - the fourth time this phase has refused a runtime dep on the same reasoning (rows 20, 25, 31). It also gained something the dependency does not have: prefers-reduced-motion, which v1 ignores. Asked via matchMedia rather than an @media block deliberately, because an @media rule would still mount 24 nodes and leave a static pile of paper pinned to the dialog - the honest reduced version is ABSENCE, not stillness.

Every caller-visible failure is a ConvexError via accessError - review walked every reachable path in both new functions and confirmed zero plain Errors. That is the check no test can make, since plain messages are redacted in production while convex-test never redacts.

Two decisions verified against v1 and upheld: marked seen on OPEN not dismiss (v1's timing, and the better behaviour - getLastMonthWinner is a reactive subscription, so a dialog marked only on dismiss reappears on every dashboard load until someone completes the gesture); and month as a CLIENT argument, which leaks nothing because requireTeamMemberFor runs first and an arbitrary month can only self-suppress.

IT GATES THE APP ROUTES ONLY: v1's matcher deliberately excluded /home, /about, /privacy and /terms, arguing they are static and render fine while the app is down, and that is the better behaviour. Built v1's way (rewrite, URL preserved), every curl check passed: GET /app returned 200 with the maintenance document, /privacy still rendered. A real browser against the real Worker told a different story: the document is SSR'd for /maintenance while window.location still says /app, so the client router re-matches /app, runs the anonymous bounce, and lands on /login with the app FULLY ALIVE underneath. title: Task 3: per-route cache headers
description:
server.ts sets private, no-store on every text/html response. Amendment A4 on wt-ksh.8 predicted exactly this would reproduce wordle-teams-jcj on a new platform: 28-41% of requests to v1's /home, /privacy and /terms missed the edge and cold-started a function at ~1.9s. THE RULE IS TWO-DIMENSIONAL. __root.tsx's beforeLoad returns the auth token into router context and TanStack serializes context into the SSR document, so a signed-in user's /privacy embeds their JWT too. Public caching requires a static route AND no session cookie. An unrecognised path defaults to no-store, so a route nobody has written yet is slow rather than shared. VERIFY THE COOKIE NAME against a real session before shipping: if the regex is wrong, hasSessionCookie returns false for every signed-in user and the policy caches their tokens publicly.

## Context
Phase 7 of the v2 re-platform (T3). Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit-design.md  Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit.md
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover the policy including the fail-safe default; an e2e asserts real response headers for anonymous static, anonymous dashboard and signed-in static; and deleting the wiring in server.ts leaves the unit suite green while turning the e2e red.
notes:
CLOSED 2026-08-31. Commits cc11b1b (the policy), c048daa (review fixes).

THE PREMISE WAS VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED, AND IT HOLDS. A signed-in GET /about really does embed the auth JWT in the SSR document - measured twice independently, byte-identical to the request's better-auth.convex_jwt cookie, and absent entirely when anonymous. So public caching genuinely requires BOTH a static route AND no session cookie; the second dimension is load-bearing, not belt-and-braces.

REAL SESSION COOKIE NAMES, established empirically rather than from docs: better-auth.session_token and better-auth.convex_jwt. Neither convex/auth.ts nor src/lib/auth-client.ts sets cookiePrefix or useSecureCookies. hasSessionCookie matches BOTH, anchored to a name position, because the failure mode of a miss is publishing a token-bearing document to a shared cache. An e2e test pins the cookie name itself with a message naming the function to fix, so an upstream rename fails loudly instead of silently disabling the check.

REVIEW FOUND ONE CRITICAL, AND THE PLAN CAUSED IT. The header was applied regardless of response status, and six of the seven listed routes are built by LATER tasks - so /, /home, /privacy, /terms, /maintenance and /login-error each served a 404 with 24h public freshness and a 7-day stale tail, the site root included. wrangler deploy does not purge Cloudflare's cache, so nothing would have evicted those 404s when the real routes landed. Now gated on status === 200; verified live across all eight paths. The plan's claim that 'listing early is safe' was false and is corrected, along with a second false claim that 'deploys invalidate' - true on Vercel, false here.

MUTATION COVERAGE IS THE BEST OF THE PHASE SO FAR: 17 of 17 policy mutations killed by unit tests, including s-maxage->max-age, which is the exact bug class jcj was. Deleting the server.ts wiring leaves 935 unit tests green and turns e2e red - the extraction trap anticipated and gated up front rather than found by review, which is a first for this phase.

ALSO FIXED: the content-type guard was untested (deleting it left everything green); the cookie separator missed an HTTP/2 comma-join, which is the dangerous direction; max-age=0 added so a browser does not fall back to heuristic freshness; and a test named for /app actually asserted /login's headers - the fourth instance this phase of an assertion scoped wider than its own name.

STILL OPEN AND IMPORTANT: wt-ksh.8.45 - a Worker response is not written to Cloudflare's edge cache without a Cache Rule or caches.default.put, and none exists in the repo, so this task's edge win may currently be ZERO until measured on beta. wt-ksh.8.46 - stale-while-revalidate has no invalidation behind it on deploy.

title: Task 0: restore the local Convex backend (lvv)
description:
The local Convex backend has silently refused every push since the creator->owner rename. e2e drives that backend and several protections in this codebase live ONLY in e2e, so every e2e result is meaningless until this is fixed. Do not reach for --typecheck=disable or a schema v.any(): either pushes a lie to a backend Playwright then trusts. convex codegen needs Node 20/22/24; this box defaults to v25.2.1. Use: mise exec node@22 -- npx convex dev

## Context
Phase 7 of the v2 re-platform (T0). Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit-design.md  Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit.md
acceptance_criteria: A push succeeds against 127.0.0.1:3210 and pnpm e2e reports 22 passed, the Phase 6 close-out figure. If it is not 22, stop and find out why before touching anything else.
notes:
PREMISE WAS STALE. The local backend was NOT refusing pushes. wordle-teams-lvv records the outage as RESOLVED on 2026-08-26 16:56, after migrate.backfillTeamOwner then migrate.clearTeamCreator were run against local (1348 rows each). Nothing has regressed since.

EVIDENCE. A convex dev watcher started 2026-08-28 was still alive at the start of this task (CLI pid 580974, local-backend binary pid 581421 on port 3210). Its log, /tmp/convexdev.log, holds 21 "Convex functions ready!" lines and ZERO "Schema validation failed" lines. The most recent push was 10:28:56 today, two seconds after the newest write under convex/ (migrate.ts, 10:28:54), so the deployment was already current with the working tree.

THE ONLY ERROR OBSERVED. The first "npx convex dev --once" failed with exit 1 and:

  A local backend is still running on port 3210. Please stop it and run this command again.

That is a port-ownership refusal from the already-running watcher, not a schema error, and it is the likely source of the plan's belief that pushes were being refused. Stopping the watcher (SIGTERM to the CLI, then to the orphaned convex-local-backend binary, which does not exit with its parent) and rerunning gave exit 0, "Convex functions ready! (2.05s)".

BASELINE ESTABLISHED. Watcher restarted, then pnpm e2e: 22 passed (1.2m), exit 0. Matches the Phase 6 close-out figure exactly. No test was touched.

NO PRODUCTION CODE CHANGED. convex/schema.ts and convex/teams.ts contain no occurrence of "creator".

ONE COSMETIC WARNING, left alone: "Found multiple VITE_CONVEX_URL environment variables in .env.local so cannot update automatically." Only one VITE_CONVEX_URL line exists; the CLI appears to also count the separate CONVEX_URL line. It only means the CLI will not rewrite the URL for you, and the URL is already correct.

OPERATIONAL NOTE FOR LATER TASKS. Killing the convex dev CLI leaves the convex-local-backend binary holding ports 3210/3211. Any later task that restarts the watcher must SIGTERM that orphan too, or the next --once will fail with the port message above and look like a backend fault.

CORRECTION ON WATCHER DURABILITY. The watcher I reported as running at the end of this task was reaped roughly an hour later, at 17:36. Both the CLI and the convex-local-backend binary died and ports 3210/3211 went quiet. It was a background job of an agent session, so it is session-bound, not a standing service. Restarted at 17:37:14 (CLI pid 1244919, backend pid 1245006, "Convex functions ready! (3.36s)", both ports listening again) but the same fragility applies to that one.

CONSEQUENCE FOR LATER TASKS: do not assume a watcher is up because Task 0 said so. Check first, with all three of: pgrep -af "convex/bin/main.js dev", pgrep -af convex-local-backend, and ss -ltn for 3210/3211. Ports alone are NOT proof the watcher is alive, because the backend binary can outlive its CLI (see below). Anyone needing a durable watcher should start it in a real shell outside an agent session.

REFINEMENT TO THE ORPHAN NOTE ABOVE: whether the backend binary is orphaned depends on how the CLI dies. A SIGTERM aimed only at the CLI leaves the binary alive holding the ports, which is the case that produces the misleading "A local backend is still running on port 3210" on the next --once. A kill that takes the whole process group, which is what the harness did at 17:36, takes both and leaves nothing behind. Both outcomes are normal; check for the orphan rather than assuming either.

description:
CORRECTION to what was recorded on wt-ksh.7.26 and wt-ksh.7.31 on 2026-08-28. Those notes say the copy carries neither reminder_delivery_methods nor time_zone. IT CARRIES BOTH, plus three more — scripts/copy-from-supabase.mjs:151-155:

  hasPwa:                  !!p.has_pwa
  timeZone:                opt(p.time_zone)
  reminderDeliveryMethods: p.reminder_delivery_methods || []
  reminderDeliveryTime:    p.reminder_delivery_time
  lastBoardEntryReminder:  ms(p.last_board_entry_reminder)

and convex/migrate.ts's playerInput validator accepts all five, so they land.

The wrong claim came from measuring the LOCAL backend and reporting it as beta — 0 players with a timeZone there — after convex run --prod silently fell back to 127.0.0.1. Beta's actual state is still unmeasured.

WHY IT MATTERS: the owner's decision was that reminder settings arrive at CUTOVER, not before, so that a Phase 7 re-copy cannot switch reminders on for someone who does not know this beta exists and who already gets real reminders from v1. As written, the copy does exactly what that decision forbids.

RISK RANKING of the five, so the fix is targeted rather than broad:
  reminderDeliveryMethods  DANGEROUS — this is what turns reminders on
  timeZone                 DANGEROUS — the sweep skips anyone without one, so it is the second half of eligibility
  lastBoardEntryReminder   PROTECTIVE — copied forward it SUPPRESSES a same-day send; keep it
  reminderDeliveryTime     harmless alone (inert without the two above)
  hasPwa                   harmless (display only until push ships)

Do not simply delete the lines: Phase 7's parity audit compares beta against production, so removing a field makes it an EXPECTED divergence that has to be recorded, and the cutover runbook has to put it back. Prefer a single explicit flag or a documented omission with both halves written down.

Note the env kill switch (REMINDERS_ENABLED / REMINDERS_ALLOWLIST, wt-ksh.7.26) protects regardless, and is now the ONLY thing protecting rather than a second layer.

THE CODE HALF IS DONE AND SHIPPED (commit d95796a, 2026-09-02). DO NOT RE-IMPLEMENT IT.

scripts/lib/copy-reminder-policy.mjs now withholds the two fields that decide eligibility - timeZone and reminderDeliveryMethods - and copy-from-supabase.mjs restores them with a single --with-reminders flag, which the cutover runbook passes to the final copy. Ten tests; nine mutations, all killed. The run banner states the mode in both directions on every run.

Landed BEFORE any Task 15 copy run rather than after it, which is a deliberate departure from the plan's step order: the plan sequences this run-then-check at Task 15 Step 5, but the script carried all five reminder fields, so running first would have written the exact thing the owner's decision forbids and a later correction does not unwrite it.

Both other acceptance clauses are met: 7a row 41 records the omission as an expected Phase 7 divergence, and docs/runbooks/2026-cutover.md section 4.2 carries the restoring line.

STAYS OPEN ON ONE CLAUSE ONLY: 'verified by measuring beta after a run'. That needs a copy run, which is blocked because supabase.co does not resolve on this machine - network DNS filtering, not a Supabase outage. See wt-ksh.8.38. When the copy runs, measure beta for any player left holding a non-empty reminderDeliveryMethods and close this.
STILL OPEN AFTER THE 2026-09-02 COPY RUN, and the reason is worth being precise about rather than closing on inference.

WHAT THE RUN SHOWS. The copy wrote all 392 copyable players (374 inserted, 18 updated) with the policy's output, and the overwrite report lists reminderDeliveryMethods as CHANGED ON 14 ROWS - so the explicit empty array reached the deployment and cleared values an earlier copy had written. reminderFieldsFor's withholding path is unit-tested and its nine mutations are all killed, and the run banner confirmed 'held back'.

WHY THAT IS NOT YET THE DONE-WHEN. The criterion is 'verified by MEASURING beta after a run', and the above is inference from the write path, not a measurement of the stored state. The distinction is exactly the one this phase keeps being caught by.

WHAT IS MISSING IS ONE FUNCTION, not access. The migration key works fine against beta through ConvexHttpClient - internal.migrate.parityProbe was called successfully this session - but NO internal query exposes reminderDeliveryMethods. parityProbe returns legacyId and email only; playerScoreFingerprint and countTable do not touch it. The deploy key in v2/.env.local is separately refused deployment:data:view, so `npx convex data players --prod` is not a route either.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER MEASURES: beta holds ONE v2-born player (no legacyId). If that account set its own reminder preferences, a non-zero count is not the copy's doing. title: SITE_URL on the beta Convex deployment is http://localhost:3000
description:
Measured 2026-08-28 via: cd v2 && pnpm exec convex run --prod --inline-query 'return { siteUrl: process.env.SITE_URL ?? null }' -> 'http://localhost:3000'.

That deployment (the prod Convex one, which serves beta.wordleteams.com and BECOMES production at cutover) uses SITE_URL in three places:

  convex/auth.ts:17     Better Auth base URL, fail-fast if unset
  convex/polar.ts:269   checkout and customer-portal return URLs
  convex/teams.ts:685   the sign-in link inside every team-invite email

So an invite email sent from beta right now carries a localhost link that will not work for the recipient, and a Polar checkout return would bounce to localhost. Neither fails loudly — the code only guards against SITE_URL being UNSET, never against it being wrong, so all three paths run happily and produce dead URLs.

Not found by any gate, and could not be: lint/typecheck/test/build never read a deployment's env.

Phase 6 makes it worse if left: the board-entry reminder email builds every image URL from SITE_URL, so reminders would ship with broken images pointing at localhost.

Suspected cause: set during local development against this deployment and never restored. Worth checking whether the same is true of any other var on that deployment while fixing.

Fix: set SITE_URL to https://beta.wordleteams.com on the prod Convex deployment, and to the real domain at cutover. Consider whether the three call sites should validate the shape rather than just presence — an https origin check would have caught this.
acceptance_criteria: SITE_URL on the prod Convex deployment is an https origin matching the domain that deployment actually serves; an invite email sent from beta contains a working link.
close_reason:
MEASURED 2026-08-28 against fabulous-goldfish-949, via `convex env get` with the prod deploy key — which DOES reach beta, unlike `convex run`.

  SITE_URL       = https://beta.wordleteams.com   CORRECT
  E2E_TEST_MODE  = not set                        CORRECT per wordle-teams-7az

So SITE_URL was never misconfigured. The earlier localhost:3000 reading came from the LOCAL backend, because `convex run --prod` silently falls back to 127.0.0.1:3210 when v2/.env.local names an anonymous deployment.

ONE CONSEQUENCE WORTH CARRYING FORWARD, because it was also reported wrong: E2E_TEST_MODE being unset means convex/email.ts's realRecipients does NOT suppress e2e+ addresses on beta. That is correct for a deployment that becomes production, but it removes a layer people may assume is there — if beta holds e2e-debris players with e2e+ emails and reminder methods set, a sweep would send real mail to mailboxes that never existed, from the production sending domain. That is the wordle-teams-96l failure mode.

The REMINDERS_ENABLED kill switch is what actually prevents this, and it is correctly unset. See wt-ksh.7.26.

TRAP FOUND WHILE MEASURING: `convex env get` exits 0 whether or not the variable exists. An exit-code check reports everything as set — it briefly made the unset kill switch look configured. Match on the "not found" text instead.

title: Task 13: the real service worker — precache, NetworkOnly, offline, push, cache purge
description: Replaces the task 2 stub. Navigations are NetworkOnly with a static public/offline.html fallback — NOT a route, because injectManifest precaches build output and a server-rendered /offline has no build-time artifact, so it would look configured and be absent exactly when needed. The activate handler's cache purge IS the serwist kill switch. Also links the manifest in __root.tsx, which is what makes v2 installable at all. Blocked on tasks 2 and 11. Plan task 13.

notes:
THE PLAN'S SHAPE FOR THIS TASK IS DEAD. Do not follow it. S3 (wt-ksh.7.19) proved vite-plugin-pwa 1.3.0 silently emits nothing under the Environment API multi-environment build @cloudflare/vite-plugin drives, it is already the latest published version, and client-scoping does not help.

OWNER-APPROVED REPLACEMENT, 2026-08-29: bundle src/sw.ts with esbuild, then inject the precache manifest with workbox-build's injectManifest, as a step the build script runs AFTER vite build, writing dist/client/sw.js. Keeps Workbox and puts the worker at root scope by construction — a worker can only control the scope it is served from, so a hashed path under assets/ would collapse the whole design.

ALREADY IN PLACE from the spike (d73b846): src/sw.ts as a starting stub, plus workbox-build and workbox-precaching. vite-plugin-pwa and workbox-window were removed.

TWO GOTCHAS MEASURED DURING THE SPIKE:
1. Any file under src/ naming ServiceWorkerGlobalScope gets CLOUDFLARE's Workers-flavoured ambient interface, from worker-configuration.d.ts included project-wide via tsconfig's types array. This tsconfig has no "webworker" lib. The stub carries an explicit intersection to get __WB_MANIFEST. Decide deliberately whether to keep riding Cloudflare's ambient type or add the webworker lib for this file.
2. workbox-build's injectManifest does string replacement only — it does NOT bundle or transpile. So src/sw.ts must be bundled to JS first; that is why the approach is esbuild-then-injectManifest and not injectManifest alone.

VERIFY THE RESULT OVER THE WIRE, not just in dist: beta currently returns 404 for /sw.js (confirmed 2026-08-29). After this task, check the status, the content-type, AND the cache-control — a long max-age on a service worker delays every future update and would need a header rule.
IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE — commit f71d183. NOT closed: bd refuses because this issue is blocked by wt-ksh.7.28 (Task 11, still in_progress). Close it once Task 11 closes; nothing here is outstanding.

What shipped:
- v2/scripts/build-sw.mjs — esbuild bundles src/sw.ts, workbox-build injectManifest injects the precache manifest, output at dist/client/sw.js (root scope). vite-plugin-pwa is gone for good; the header comment records the S3 measurement.
- The build step fails loudly on all four conditions (file missing, placeholder survived, zero entries, wrong path). Each proven to exit 1.
- src/sw.ts — precache, NetworkOnly navigations with a matchPrecache offline fallback, push + notificationclick matched to convex/pushSend.ts, and an activate-time cache purge whose keep-set is read from workbox-core cacheNames.
- public/offline.html, src/lib/register-sw.ts, manifest + theme-color linked in __root.tsx (which also closes wt-ksh.7.1).

Findings: the plan's cache-name predicate would have SPARED serwist's precache — serwist 9.2.1 names it serwist-precache-v2-SCOPE, so a !name.includes('precache') filter is false for it and the largest cache the eviction exists to remove would survive forever. Also: the dev server never serves dist/client/sw.js, so the Playwright suite cannot exercise the worker at all; beta verification is the only path.

IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE AND VERIFIED ON BETA. Not closed: bd blocks this on wt-ksh.7.28 (Task 11), whose own done-when needs a real device. Close both together.

Done in f71d183 + 643a0cb + 13a2f1a, deployed via run 33253650550 (success). VERIFIED IN A REAL BROWSER AGAINST BETA, not just in dist:

  /sw.js            200, content-type text/javascript, cache-control "public, max-age=0, must-revalidate"
                    — the long-max-age hazard the plan warned about does NOT exist here; no header rule needed.
  /manifest.json    200, and the document links it at last — that is what makes the app installable.
  theme-color       #0a0a0a present.
  registrations     EXACTLY ONE, scope https://beta.wordleteams.com/ (root), script /sw.js.
  caches.keys()     exactly ["workbox-precache-v2-https://beta.wordleteams.com/"].
  offline page      precached as offline.html?__WB_REVISION__=c45b981f..., 3779 bytes, correct content.
  documents cached  NONE — wordle-teams-bpt's acceptance criterion.
  offline navigate  setOffline(true) then navigate -> "Offline · Wordle Teams" and the real copy.

NOTE ON /offline.html OVER THE WIRE: it 307s to /offline (Cloudflare static-asset html_handling strips .html). That does NOT break precaching — the browser check above confirms the correct 3779-byte page is in the precache under the revisioned key.

THE PLAN'S BUILD APPROACH WAS DEAD (wt-ksh.7.19). Replaced with esbuild + workbox-build injectManifest after vite build, and the script FAILS LOUDLY on five conditions (not written / placeholder survived / zero entries / offline.html absent from the manifest / wrong path), removing the artifact on every failure path. That answers S3's real lesson: not "the plugin is broken" but "it broke in total silence".

FOUR DEFECTS THE REVIEW LOOP CAUGHT, all reproduced by me:
1. The plan's cache-purge predicate would have SPARED serwist's precache — serwist names it serwist-precache-v2-<scope>, so !name.includes('precache') is FALSE for it. The kill switch would have silently failed to kill the largest cache it exists to remove.
2. The plan's caches.match('/offline.html') cannot work; workbox stores under a revisioned key, as the live key above shows. Now matchPrecache.
3. registerServiceWorker could throw synchronously and blank the app — 'serviceWorker' in navigator is [[HasProperty]] and never invokes the accessor, but the next line's read does, and that getter throws SecurityError when site data is blocked. Outside any try, in the ROOT component's effect. v1 had it inside a try; the port lost it.
4. sw-caches.test.ts was a FALSE GREEN on the module's one claim — hardcoding the literals passed 7/7, because under vitest there is no registration so cacheNames.suffix is '' and the derived names collapse to the literals. The live cache name above proves the divergence. Now pinned; the mutant fails 8/10.

Plus a bypass the implementer's own test found and I confirmed: blob: URLs INHERIT their inner URL's origin, so new URL('blob:https://beta.wordleteams.com/abc').origin is ours and an origin-only check passes it. The notification URL clamp now requires http(s) too.

829 tests / 54 files, up from 776/50. Four gates green, and green under TZ=UTC.

KNOWN LIMITATION, recorded not fixed: the e2e suite CANNOT exercise this worker. pnpm dev is plain vite serving src/, so dist/client/sw.js does not exist there, and playwright.config.ts's webServer is pnpm dev. Registration is gated on import.meta.env.PROD. Beta is the only place it can be verified.

CARRIED FORWARD FROM S2 — an unverified link, worth designing around.

The S2 probe returned statusCode 201 and NO notification rendered on the owner's machine. Separately, DevTools' own "Push" test button DID render one.

Those test different things. The DevTools button delivers a payload straight to the service worker, bypassing the push service AND the encryption path — so it proves the SW's push handler works. 201 proves the push service accepted the request. Neither proves the middle link: real encrypted payload -> push service -> browser decrypts -> SW push event fires.

WHY THIS IS NOT PEDANTRY: a push service returns 201 WITHOUT decrypting. If the payload was encrypted against the wrong p256dh/auth, the service still says 201 and the browser silently drops the undecryptable message. That failure mode is invisible from the server side — it looks exactly like success. It is equally consistent with ordinary FCM latency, or the notification appearing and being missed.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TASK: do not treat a 2xx from webpush.sendNotification as proof of delivery, in code comments or in the acceptance check. This task's done-when requires a notification actually RENDERING on a real device from a real sweep — not a status code. If it does not render, suspect the subscription keys round-tripping through savePushSubscription (base64url encoding of p256dh/auth is the likely culprit) before suspecting the runtime, which S2 has already cleared.

INVALID_REMINDER_METHOD fires for unknown methods AND duplicates but described only the first, so ['email','email'] got a message stating a rule the input already satisfied. INVALID_TIME_ZONE read as a rejected user choice when the zone is auto-detected from the browser and the user cannot act on it.

Also: mySettings held its field mapping in the wrapper, violating the module's own stated invariant (two mutants survived there) — extracted to mySettingsFor. Method case-sensitivity is now pinned ('Email' rejected). markPwaInstalledFor documented as SET-ONLY: nothing clears hasPwa, so a player who uninstalls the PWA keeps it true and the sweep will believe push is deliverable.

description: Pure functions: localParts, isDueThisHour, alreadyRemindedToday, hasRecentActivity, enteredOn, needsWeekendOptIn. Ports v1's get_players_for_reminder minus two timezone bugs — the weekend check and the ten-day window both resolve against the server's CURRENT_DATE. convex/lib/reminders.ts + tests at ecd6f8e, deployed to beta green. 28 tests in the module, 655 total across 38 files; lint/tsc/test/build all verified 0 by the controller independently, not taken on report.

Two review rounds. Spec review: compliant, no test weakened. Code-quality review ran a mutation battery — the -10/-11, >=/>, and dropped-hourCycle mutants were all killed, so the tests constrain rather than decorate — and found three things worth having:

1. The hourCycle rationale was BACKWARDS in the plan and shipped comment. hour12:false resolves to h23 and gives '00', identical to what we use; only explicit 'h24' gives '24'. The real hazard is OMITTING the option, where en-US defaults to h12 and 14:00 formats as '02'. The test claiming to pin this passed under hour12:false, so it pinned nothing. Both fixed; the test now contrasts an h24 formatter against ours.
2. Two documented decisions had no test: >= over === in alreadyRemindedToday (the === mutant survived), and the copied-row alias path pinned only one of five Postgres spellings. Both now covered.
3. MEASURED AND CARRIED INTO TASK 9: both window bounds are inclusive and the cron ticks on the hour, so an on-the-hour reminder matches TWO consecutive ticks in any whole-hour-offset zone — 7182 double-matches over 399 days in Chicago/Sydney/London/Honolulu, zero in half-hour zones, nobody ever missed including across DST. The once-per-day stamp is therefore the only thing between us and two emails a day for most players, which makes claim-before-send load-bearing rather than preferred. Written into the plan's task 9 so the sweep implementer cannot reasonably stamp after a successful send.

title: Task 2: SPIKE S3 — does vite-plugin-pwa build here, and is /sw.js served at root?
description: wrangler.jsonc:101 has the assets binding commented out, so public/ is served by @cloudflare/vite-plugin's own build-time config, and how that interacts with a plugin emitting a root-scope service worker has never been measured. A SW served from the wrong path, with the wrong content type, or with a long cache lifetime fails three different quiet ways. Plan task 2.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm build exits 0; dist/client/sw.js exists at the root and not under assets/; curl -I against beta returns 200 with a JS content-type; the cache-control value is recorded.
notes:
PARTIALLY ANSWERED 2026-08-28, incidentally, while setting up the S2 push spike.

Deployed public/sw-spike.js (a throwaway worker) and measured against beta:

  dist/client/sw-spike.js          <- public/ files land at the ROOT of the client output
  GET https://beta.wordleteams.com/sw-spike.js
    HTTP/2 200
    content-type: text/javascript
    cache-control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate

So: root scope is available, the content type is correct, and the cache-control is ideal for a service worker — no long max-age to delay an update.

STILL UNANSWERED, which is the harder half: whether vite-plugin-pwa's injectManifest strategy BUILDS alongside @cloudflare/vite-plugin and tanstackStart(), and whether it emits its worker to that same root location. A hand-written file in public/ proves the serving path, not the plugin's build path.
S3 ANSWERED 2026-08-28. NEGATIVE RESULT, and a precise one.

vite-plugin-pwa 1.3.0 emits NOTHING in this repo. pnpm build exits 0, dist contains no sw.js and no workbox file anywhere, and the build log contains zero mentions of pwa/workbox/service worker. No error, no warning, not even the plugin's usual banner. Total silence at every layer — exactly the quiet-failure mode this spike existed to catch.

ROOT CAUSE, verified in the plugin's own source rather than inferred:
  - node_modules/.pnpm/vite-plugin-pwa@1.3.0/.../dist/index.js:986 — configResolved(config) does `ctx.viteConfig = config` unconditionally, with no per-environment awareness.
  - same file:422 — closeBundle guards on `if (!ctx.viteConfig.build.ssr)`.
vite build here runs Vite's Environment API multi-environment build driven by @cloudflare/vite-plugin, which resolves root, then client (build.ssr=false), then ssr (build.ssr=true). The ssr config lands LAST and pins build.ssr=true forever, so the closeBundle guard never passes and _generateSW never runs.

NO UPGRADE PATH: `npm view vite-plugin-pwa version` returns 1.3.0 — the installed version IS the latest published.

WORKAROUND TRIED AND FAILED: scoping the returned plugins with applyToEnvironment: e => e.name === 'client'. Still no sw.js. applyToEnvironment gates the build hooks, but configResolved is a global hook that still fires for every environment config, so ctx.viteConfig is pinned regardless.

CONSEQUENCE: Task 13 CANNOT be the plan's shape. The plan's whole PWA design assumed this plugin. Task 12 is also still blocked, because it needs a registered service worker and v2 has none.

SEPARATE FINDING FOR TASK 13, independent of the plugin: any file under src/ that names ServiceWorkerGlobalScope gets CLOUDFLARE's Workers-flavoured ambient interface (from worker-configuration.d.ts, included project-wide via tsconfig's `types`), NOT the browser one. tsconfig has no "webworker" lib. The stub needed `declare const self: ServiceWorkerGlobalScope & { __WB_MANIFEST: Array<PrecacheEntry | string> }` to typecheck. Also workbox-precaching is a transitive dep that pnpm does not hoist, so it needs its own explicit install.
close_reason:
S3 answered 2026-08-29 in d73b846, deployed to beta (run 33236138838, success). The answer is NO.

vite-plugin-pwa 1.3.0 cannot work in this repo. Build exits 0 and emits no service worker at all, silently. Root cause verified in the plugin's source: configResolved pins ctx.viteConfig to the LAST resolved environment config (ssr) and closeBundle guards on !ctx.viteConfig.build.ssr, so _generateSW never runs under the Environment API multi-environment build @cloudflare/vite-plugin drives. 1.3.0 is the latest published version, and scoping the plugins to the client environment does not help either — measured.

OVER-THE-WIRE CHECK (step 7): https://beta.wordleteams.com/sw.js returns 404 after the deploy, as expected — nothing is emitted, so nothing is served. Content-type and cache-control questions are moot until a worker actually ships.

DECISION, owner-approved 2026-08-29: Task 13 drops the plugin and instead bundles src/sw.ts with esbuild and injects the precache manifest with workbox-build's injectManifest, run as a step after vite build. Keeps Workbox and puts sw.js at root scope by construction. src/sw.ts, workbox-build and workbox-precaching are kept for it; vite-plugin-pwa and workbox-window were removed rather than left as dead config.

title: A Polar misconfiguration is indistinguishable from an outage in the UI
description:
FOUND 2026-08-27 by the owner, on the first real beta attempt: clicking Billing gives 'Could not open the billing portal'.

THE DEFECT IS DIAGNOSABILITY, NOT THE PORTAL. polar() calls assertPolarEnv() at polar.ts:503, INSIDE the try. The throw is caught at :508, is not isMissingCustomer, and falls through to the generic { reason: 'error' } at :514. So a missing env var, a POLAR_SERVER typo, a token/server mismatch and a genuine Polar outage all present as the same toast.

THE CONTROLLER ASSERTED THE OPPOSITE and was wrong: 'assertPolarEnv validates all five together and throws, so the first checkout click is a complete and LOUD test of the remaining four.' It throws, but nothing loud reaches anyone - the catch swallows it. Recorded because the reasoning error is the interesting part: validating as a set was the right call, and it was defeated by a catch two frames away that was written for a different purpose.

THE SAME DEFECT IS ON THE CHECKOUT PATH: createProCheckout returns bare null (polar.ts:346-348) for every failure mode alike.

WORSE THAN A BAD MESSAGE: retrying can NEVER fix a misconfiguration, so 'try again later' is untrue in exactly the way the three-way PortalResult was designed to prevent for no-customer. We fixed that distinction for the expected state and left it broken for the operator one.

DONE WHEN: a configuration failure is distinguishable from an operational one on both the portal and checkout paths; the user-facing copy for it does not tell anyone to retry; no env var VALUE or NAME reaches the browser; and the specific cause is still logged server-side.
notes:
FIXED 2026-08-27, commit f03b8fe. 627 tests / 37 files; four gates exit 0; e2e 17 passed.

THE REAL CAUSE, from the owner's log, and it was NONE of the four causes the controller ranked:

  403 {"error": "insufficient_scope", "error_description": "The request requires higher privileges than provided by the access token."}
  www-authenticate: Bearer realm="polar", scope="customer_sessions:write"
  x-polar-sandbox: 1   url: https://sandbox-api.polar.sh/v1/customer-sessions/

A VALID, AUTHENTICATING TOKEN MISSING ONE SCOPE. Not a missing var, not a POLAR_SERVER typo, not a token/server mismatch, not an expired token - POLAR_SERVER was correct (the sandbox header and URL prove it) and the token authenticated fine.

THE FOUR SCOPES THE INTEGRATION NEEDS, one per SDK call in convex/polar.ts:
  checkouts:write         polar.ts:425  checkouts.create
  customer_sessions:write polar.ts:657  customerSessions.create   <- the one that failed
  checkouts:read          polar.ts:739  checkouts.get
  customers:write         polar.ts:798  customers.update
Only the second is reachable from the portal button, so a token short of the others fails later and in rarer paths - customers.update runs only for an email-matched customer, which is the hardest case to reproduce deliberately.

THE FIX CLASSIFIES THIS CORRECTLY, AND THE IMPLEMENTER'S JUDGMENT CALL IS NOW VINDICATED BY DATA. isCredentialProblem groups 403 with 401 as 'not-configured', which the implementer wrote 'BY JUDGMENT, NOT BY MEASUREMENT... nothing in this repo has seen Polar send one'. Polar then sent one, first thing, and the case it was guessing about is the one that actually happened. The comment now carries the real response instead of the guess.

THE UNDERLYING DEFECT, for the record: polar() calls assertPolarEnv() INSIDE the try, so a config failure was caught by a catch written for Polar's HTTP responses and returned as the generic retryable error. The fix hoists the env gate out of every try, before the identity lookup and before any network call. Mutation-tested: collapsing not-configured into error fails 5 tests; un-hoisting the gate fails 5; reverting the copy to the retry sentence fails 2; leaking POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN into the copy fails 1.
close_reason: Closed

title: Nothing in the Phase 5 plan sets the POLAR_* env vars on the Convex deployment - and there are five, not four
description:
Found while building Task 9 (wordle-teams-l1v).

The spec's operational note and every plan task name four variables: POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN, POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET, POLAR_PRO_MONTHLY_PRODUCT_ID, POLAR_PRO_ANNUAL_PRODUCT_ID. NO TASK IN THE PLAN ACTUALLY SETS THEM on any Convex deployment; Task 13's sandbox pass assumes they are already there.

There are now FIVE. v1's client.ts picked the Polar server with ENVIRONMENT === 'prod' ? 'production' : 'sandbox'. v2 HAS NO SUCH VARIABLE IN CONVEX - the only ENVIRONMENT in the tree is wrangler.jsonc's, set on the Cloudflare worker that serves the front end, invisible to a Convex function. So convex/polar.ts requires POLAR_SERVER, validated in the same set as the other four and checked to be exactly 'production' or 'sandbox' (v1's ternary silently defaulted anything unrecognised to sandbox, so a typo would send real subscribers to an instance holding none of their data).

Polar's sandbox is a wholly separate instance from production - separate accounts, organizations, products and tokens - so server and credentials must move together. Phase 5 verifies on sandbox against beta (decision C); the SAME deployment flips to production at cutover by changing POLAR_SERVER plus the token and both product ids together.

NO VALUES IN THIS REPO OR IN BEADS - this repo is public. Names only.

DONE WHEN: all five are set on the deployment beta runs on, before Task 13's sandbox pass, and the cutover checklist names all five as a set that moves together.
notes:
PARTIALLY VERIFIED LIVE 2026-08-27, after the owner set the five vars on the PROD Convex deployment (which beta uses).

PROBED THE DEPLOYED ENDPOINT: https://fabulous-goldfish-949.convex.site/polar/webhook
(Convex serves httpActions on .convex.site, NOT .convex.cloud - that is the URL to register in Polar.)

  POST, no webhook-id header  -> 400
  POST, bogus signature       -> 403, body 'Invalid signature'

THE 400 IS THE PROOF. convex/http.ts checks POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET at :121, BEFORE the webhook-id header at :144. With the secret missing that request returned 500; it now returns 400. So POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set on the deployment AND is reaching the code. The 403 confirms the standardwebhooks verifier is live and rejects an unsigned request without leaking anything.

THE OTHER FOUR ARE NOT YET VERIFIED, and deliberately were not: POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN, POLAR_PRO_MONTHLY_PRODUCT_ID, POLAR_PRO_ANNUAL_PRODUCT_ID and POLAR_SERVER are read only by assertPolarEnv on the ACTION paths (checkout, portal, the checkout fallback), and every one of those requires either an authenticated session or a validly signed delivery. Listing them would mean extracting a production deploy key into a temp file; the marginal value did not justify it.

THAT IS SAFE BY DESIGN. assertPolarEnv validates ALL FIVE TOGETHER and throws naming every missing one, so the FIRST checkout or portal click in the sandbox pass is a complete test of the remaining four and fails loudly rather than silently. That was the point of validating them as a set rather than one per call site.

POLAR_SERVER must be exactly 'production' or 'sandbox' - it is NOT a ternary with a default, precisely so a typo cannot silently resolve to sandbox. For the sandbox pass it must be 'sandbox', and it must move to 'production' at cutover together with the credentials, since Polar's sandbox is a separate instance with its own accounts, products and tokens.
ENV-VAR HALF VERIFIED LIVE 2026-09-01 on fabulous-goldfish-949, sentinel confirmed first. All FIVE are set, which is what this issue was filed to establish:

  POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN, POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET, POLAR_PRO_MONTHLY_PRODUCT_ID,
  POLAR_PRO_ANNUAL_PRODUCT_ID, POLAR_SERVER

POLAR_SERVER = 'sandbox' - read explicitly, not inferred. That is one of the two legal values and the correct one for Task 18's pass. No value of any other variable was read or recorded; this repo is public.

SCOPE HALF STILL UNVERIFIED, and it cannot be verified from here. Cross-checked the call sites instead: convex/polar.ts has exactly FOUR SDK calls, matching this issue's enumeration, though every line number has drifted one down since it was written -
  checkouts.create        :426  -> checkouts:write
  customerSessions.create :658  -> customer_sessions:write
  checkouts.get           :740  -> checkouts:read
  customers.update        :799  -> customers:write
Whether the token actually carries those four scopes can only be answered by exercising it, which is Task 18. As this issue already records, assertPolarEnv validates all five together and names every missing one, so the first checkout in the sandbox pass is a complete test that fails loudly.

STILL OPEN ON ITS SECOND CLAUSE: 'the cutover checklist names all five as a set that moves together'. Carried to wt-ksh.8.43 (Task 20). Polar's sandbox is a separate instance, so POLAR_SERVER, the token and both product ids must move as one at cutover.
CLOSED BY THE RUNBOOK. docs/runbooks/2026-cutover.md now carries this issue's checklist requirement in full, which was the clause it was left open on when Phase 7 measured it green. See wt-ksh.8.43's note for what landed where.
close_reason: Closed

title: getCustomerPortalUrl resolves in one namespace; a migrated subscriber gets 'no-customer'
description:
Found while building Task 9 (wordle-teams-l1v). NOT a defect ported from v1 - v1 had only one namespace.

convex/polar.ts's getCustomerPortalUrl calls customerSessions.create({ externalCustomerId: <convex player id> }). Inbound identity resolves across BOTH namespaces (decision F, resolvePlayerIdFor: Convex id then by_legacyId), because after cutover a migrated subscriber's Polar customer carries their v1 uuid as external_id - v1's checkout.ts:22 set it to the v1 player id. The OUTBOUND direction does not.

CONSEQUENCE: between cutover and that subscriber's next subscription webhook, the portal answers { url: null, reason: 'no-customer' } to a PAYING subscriber - the exact 'say something untrue' failure the three-way result exists to prevent. repairCustomerExternalId closes it, but only on their next event, which for an annual plan can be months away.

OPTIONS: (a) on no-customer, retry once with player.legacyId when present, and schedule repairCustomerExternalId on success; (b) a pre-cutover backfill over the Polar API stamping Convex ids onto every migrated customer - which spec decision F rules out as a SOLE mechanism, but not as a supplement; (c) accept and make the UI copy honest.

NOT DONE IN TASK 9 deliberately: it is a second Polar call plus a change to which identities the portal accepts, which is a design question rather than a port. The gap is written into getCustomerPortalUrl's doc comment, which cites this issue id.

DONE WHEN: a migrated subscriber whose Polar customer still holds a v1 uuid can open the portal, or the phase records a decision not to and the UI copy says something true.
notes:
FIXED in the follow-up to Task 9. Option (a), as suggested by the coordinator.

WHY IT WAS NOT A NEW DECISION: decision F already establishes 'accept both namespaces'. Only the inbound direction had been written down; the portal resolving one was an inconsistency, not an open question.

WHAT SHIPPED, in convex/polar.ts:
- checkoutIdentity now also returns legacyId (null for a v2-native player).
- externalIdsFor({ playerId, legacyId }) -> the ordered names to try. Convex id first, v1 uuid second, empties and duplicates dropped. A player with NO legacyId gets a one-element list, so nobody who signed up after cutover pays for a second call, and the cost decays to zero as customers heal.
- lookupPortal(candidates, attempt) walks them. ONLY no-customer advances: a 500 or an auth failure stops the walk and stays an error, because retrying it as the next identity would report an outage as 'you have no subscription' - to everyone, not just migrated users. Exhausting every identity is still no-customer, which stays truthful for the genuinely new user.
- getCustomerPortalUrl wires the two and, when the winning identity was NOT the Convex id, schedules repairCustomerExternalId with the customer id the session returned (CustomerSession.customerId). Fire-and-forget via ctx.scheduler.runAfter(0, ...), wrapped, so tidying up can never take away a session the player is entitled to. The portal is now the FIRST live caller of repairCustomerExternalId; the webhook's is still Task 10.

TESTABILITY: the attempt is an injected parameter, so the sequencing is real logic under test rather than a stub-and-assert-called test. 11 new tests (524 -> 535). Mutation-checked: dropping the legacy fallback and letting any failure advance the walk each turn tests red.

NOT TESTED: the SDK calls themselves and the scheduler wiring - network and ctx. Covered by Task 13's sandbox pass, whose checklist item 'a non-subscriber is told they have no billing account' should gain a sibling: a MIGRATED subscriber can open the portal.

Comments corrected that this made false: assertPolarEnv's list of what is unit tested (written in the previous commit), the portal's 'resolved by the Convex id' line, repairCustomerExternalId's 'nothing calls this yet', the module docblock's 'the single exception is checkoutIdentity', and polarIdentity.ts's customerId note.
close_reason: Closed

title: The db.delete site inventories are stale — 14 hits is now 21, and downgradeTeamRemovalFor is a new path in
description:
Filed by Task 7 (wordle-teams-stf), which was told to REPORT this rather than fix it. Parent is wt-ksh.6 (Phase 5) — link it with `bd dep`, since --parent could not mint a child id under that prefix.

Two documents enumerate v2's delete sites and both are now wrong.

1. wt-ksh.9's runbook, step 2, the 'players, playerMembership' bullet. It says: git grep -n "db\.delete(" convex/ printed FOURTEEN hits on 2026-08-25, and only three matter (winners.ts, scores.ts, teams.ts), the rest being testOtps.ts (three), migrate.ts and four *.test.ts files.

MEASURED 2026-08-26, same command, same directory: TWENTY-ONE hits. The breakdown is teams.ts 4, e2ePrune.ts 4, testOtps.ts 3, teams.test.ts 2, e2ePrune.test.ts 2, and one each in migrate.ts, scores.ts, winners.ts, access.test.ts, scores.test.ts, winners.test.ts.

The drift is NOT Task 7's. convex/billing.ts contains no db.delete call at all; it reaches deletion only through cascadeDeleteTeam. The seven extra hits are e2ePrune.ts and e2ePrune.test.ts, which landed with the e2e prune (wordle-teams-1cd) after the runbook line was written. So the runbook has been stale since before Phase 5 started, and an operator following it at cutover would find seven hits the text does not account for and no way to tell which are new.

2. Same runbook, the 'teams. STOP AND READ.' bullet. It names cascadeDeleteTeam's reachable callers as 'the creator deletes a team, or the last member leaves one'. There are now four: deleteTeamFor, leaveTeamFor's last-member case, e2ePrune.ts, and since Phase 5 billing.ts's downgradeTeamRemovalFor. It also still says 'creator', which the Phase 5 rename made a stale field name.

The downgrade one matters at cutover for a reason the others do not: a team it deletes carries a legacyId, so a later copy re-inserts it — exactly the resurrection wt-ksh.13.10 describes — and it is triggered by a Polar webhook rather than by a person, so it can fire during a dual-running window with nobody watching.

3. scripts/lib/copy-tallies.mjs:286 says 'Confirmed for teams (cascadeDeleteTeam, convex/teams.ts) and for boards (upsertBoardFor, convex/scores.ts)'. This one is arguably still TRUE as written — it names the deleting function, not its callers, and cascadeDeleteTeam is still the function. Check it rather than assuming it needs an edit.

DONE WHEN: the runbook's hit count is a measured number with a dated command beside it, its caller list for cascadeDeleteTeam names all four, the 'creator' wording is gone, and copy-tallies.mjs has been read and either updated or explicitly confirmed accurate.
notes:
MEASURED AND PART-FIXED 2026-09-01 (Phase 7 Task 16). One of the four sites is fixed in code; three are beads prose that Task 20's runbook supersedes.

THE COUNT DRIFTED AGAIN WHILE THIS ISSUE WAS OPEN: fourteen on 2026-08-25, twenty-one when this was filed on 2026-08-26, TWENTY-SIX on 2026-09-01 - sixteen production, ten in *.test.ts. New since the filing: push.ts (1), billing.test.ts (2), and e2ePrune.ts and winners.test.ts one each. That is the actual lesson and it is now written into the fix: the number is dated, the command is named as the source of truth, and the prose says do not trust the figure.

1. scripts/lib/copy-tallies.mjs - FIXED. And it needed more than a number. The old text said the three deletes touching a COPIED table are winners.ts, scores.ts and teams.ts, and that "none of the three touches players, playerMembership or webhookEvents". convex/e2ePrune.ts has since landed and deletes from BOTH of the first two - dailyScores :338, monthlyWinners :351, playerMembership :361, pushSubscriptions :372, players :378. So it is FOUR production sites, not three. webhookEvents is still touched by no delete anywhere. title: Local Convex backend silently refused every push after the creator->owner rename
description:
FOUND 2026-08-26 while working wordle-teams-1cd. RESOLVED during that work, filed so the failure mode is recorded.

The local anonymous backend rejected EVERY 'convex dev' push from the moment the creator->owner rename landed until 2026-08-26 16:56. 47 consecutive failures in the watcher log, all identical:

  Schema validation failed. Document ... in table 'teams' does not match the schema:
  Object contains extra field 'creator' that is not in the validator.

1348 of 1680 local teams still carried the dropped 'creator' field, and none of them had 'owner' set. Convex validates the schema against every existing document on push and refuses a narrowing any row violates, so one stale field froze the whole deployment.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED: the watcher process stayed alive and kept retrying, codegen kept succeeding (api.d.ts is only rewritten when the API SHAPE changes, and it did not), and the vite dev server kept serving current frontend code. So tsc, vitest and build were all green while the backend served pre-rename functions. Nothing in the quality gates looks at what is actually deployed locally - the same blind spot recorded for e2e.

The runbook step existed and was run on beta (see the Task 2b closure) but was never run against local, and migrate.clearTeamCreator refuses a team with creator and no owner, so it needed migrate.backfillTeamOwner first. Both were still deployed in the stale code; running backfillTeamOwner then clearTeamCreator (1348 rows each) unblocked the push immediately.

FOLLOW-UP WORTH CONSIDERING: a cheap check that the local deployment's function set matches the working tree, so 'the backend is running code from four days ago' cannot be invisible again.
notes:
TITLE CORRECTED: said '4 days', but the description is right - pushes failed from the moment the rename's schema drop landed (2247b25, 2026-08-26) until 16:56 the same day. The 4-day figure was the watcher's uptime, not the outage.

THIS IS THE EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION OF A DESIGN PREMISE THAT WAS UNVERIFIED WHEN THE PHASE 5 PLAN WAS WRITTEN. The five-step rename (add owner / backfill / switch readers / clear creator / drop creator) was designed around the belief that Convex rejects a schema push when existing documents carry a field the schema no longer declares. That could not be tested locally at design time - validation happens server-side, not in the installed package - so the safe ordering was adopted on the grounds that it is correct under either reading.

It is now MEASURED, and the belief was right:
  Schema validation failed. Document ... in table 'teams' does not match the schema:
  Object contains extra field 'creator' that is not in the validator.

Had the rename been done in fewer steps, the Task 2c deploy would have failed against BETA exactly as it failed locally. Beta survived only because steps 2 and 4 (backfill, then clear) were run against it. The local backend never had them run - that is the entire difference, and it is why local broke while beta did not.

THE REAL LESSON, and it is bigger than this bug: lint, typecheck, vitest and build were ALL GREEN throughout, because none of them talks to the backend. convex-test builds its own schema in memory. So a deployment can be frozen for an arbitrary period while every gate reports success. The only signal was e2e, which is not in the gates.
close_reason: Fixed 2026-08-26 16:56 by migrate.backfillTeamOwner then migrate.clearTeamCreator against local (1348 rows each). Re-verified 2026-08-31 during Phase 7 Task 0: convex dev --once exits 0, functions ready in 2.05s, no 'creator' remains in schema.ts or teams.ts, and pnpm e2e is 22 passed. Left open for five days after it was fixed, which caused Phase 7's Task 0 to be written against a failure that no longer existed - see wt-ksh.8.23.

title: Task 10: the webhook endpoint - verify, store, process, retry on failure
description:
Phase 5, wt-ksh.6. Port src/lib/polar/webhook.ts into a Convex httpAction registered in convex/http.ts (which today only registers Better Auth routes).

THE ORDER MATTERS AND IS THE WHOLE DESIGN: verify the Standard Webhooks signature -> resolve the player (Task 4) -> STORE the event -> process it -> return. A failure AFTER storing must return non-2xx so Polar retries. Anything that auto-acknowledges before the handler resolves destroys this - see Task 0.

IDEMPOTENCY KEYS ON A STRING FROM THE HEADER. Polar follows Standard Webhooks; ids look like msg_2KWPBgLlAfxdpx2AI54pPJ85f4W. Read it from the webhook-id HEADER, not the body. v1 lost a day to a uuid column that rejected them, returned 500, and put Polar into an infinite retry loop against an event that could never be stored. The v2 schema comment on webhookEvents already says all of this.

CONVEX HAS NO UNIQUE CONSTRAINTS, so the replay guard is an explicit by_webhookId lookup at the top of the mutation, returning early if the row exists. v1 got this free from a partial unique index; v2 does not.

FOUR OUTCOMES, all distinct, following v1's WebhookOutcome:
  processed  - stored and applied
  duplicate  - already handled; return 2xx WITHOUT reprocessing
  ignored    - accepted but not actionable and retrying will never help (unknown player)
  failed     - return non-2xx so Polar retries

Recognised-but-inert events (canceled, past_due) still STORE the row for the audit trail and still return processed; they simply apply no transition.

Mark the row processed after the membership change succeeds or fails on its own terms - and do NOT make marking-processed fatal, or a 500 there makes Polar redeliver an event that was in fact applied.

DONE WHEN: a duplicate webhook-id returns success without reprocessing (parent acceptance criterion 3); an unknown player is ignored rather than retried forever; a mid-processing failure returns non-2xx; a bad signature is rejected before any write; and all of it is pinned by convex-test.
notes:
COMPLETE 2026-08-27. Commits 5c949d0 + a35e035 + 968a3dd. 566 tests / 35 files; four gates exit 0. ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 3 PINNED, BOTH HALVES.

THE FINDING THAT MATTERED MOST IN THE PHASE: @polar-sh/sdk's validateEvent CANNOT RUN ON CONVEX'S DEFAULT RUNTIME. dist/esm/webhooks.js:126 calls Buffer.from(secret,'utf-8'); Buffer is a Node global the default runtime does not provide. EVERY DELIVERY WOULD HAVE FAILED VERIFICATION.

NO GATE IN THIS REPO COULD SEE IT. vitest's edge-runtime environment DOES define Buffer, and npx convex codegen analyses modules without serving a request. lint/typecheck/test/build were all green over code that could not process a single real delivery. Only issuing a live request found it.

Fixed by verifying through standardwebhooks@1.0.0 directly - the library the SDK itself verifies through - which never calls the Buffer global. BYTE-IDENTITY PROVEN, not assumed: the reviewer traced both key derivations to source (SDK: base64.decode(base64(utf8(secret))) == utf8(secret); shipped: TextEncoder().encode(secret) == utf8(secret)) and then signed a delivery under the SDK-DERIVED key and verified it under the SHIPPED key, across 8 secrets including non-ASCII, CJK and emoji. That cross-test is the operation real Polar bytes perform.

The latin-1 trap was avoided: passing the STRING with format:'raw' takes Uint8Array.from(s, c => c.charCodeAt(0)), which diverges on any non-ASCII secret.

CONSEQUENCE: a verified delivery is the RAW WIRE JSON, so polarIdentity.ts reads customer.external_id / customer_id / checkout_id. metadata.player_id is unchanged, being our own key. Decision F is untouched; only the field names in the spec were wrong, and the spec now carries the correction.

SECOND BUG, FOUND IN REVIEW: a transient failure of the checkout fallback became a permanent unretryable 202. fetchCheckoutExternalId caught EVERYTHING - Polar 5xx, 429, network, assertPolarEnv's throw - and returned null, which fell to the 202 path. 202 tells Polar never to redeliver AND stores no audit row, so the delivery vanished. It bit exactly the shape the fallback exists for, and a deployment with the webhook secret set but POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN missing would silently drop those upgrades. Now isMissingCheckout returns true only for 404/422 (the two client errors checkoutsGet declares, measured at dist/esm/funcs/checkoutsGet.js:87); everything else rethrows and answers 500.

MUTATION VERDICTS (exit codes): restore-the-swallow 1 | guard-on-row-existence 1 (exactly one test, the divergence-13 one; the duplicate test correctly stays green) | canceled-as-revoked 1 (4 tests) | sanity 0.

convex/http.test.ts now drives the whole protocol through t.fetch with REAL Standard Webhooks signatures - 500 no secret, 400 no webhook-id, 403 bad signature, 403 body swapped after signing, 202 nobody, 500 fallback unaskable, 200 across all three identity namespaces, redelivery changing nothing, canceled inert.

title: Task 5: identity - candidate extraction + dual-namespace resolution
description:
Phase 5, wt-ksh.6. Port src/lib/polar/identity.ts. THIS IS A CUTOVER PREREQUISITE, NOT HARDENING.

THE BUG IT EXISTS FOR: Polar does NOT reliably stamp external_customer_id onto a customer. When a checkout matches an EXISTING customer by email, the value stays on the checkout and the customer keeps its own null external id. The webhook is delivered, logged succeeded=true http=202, and NOBODY IS UPGRADED. Silent, because 202 is not an error. Observed on dev 2026-08-03 against a real subscription.

WORSE IN V2 THAN IN V1: at cutover every migrated user already exists as a Polar customer under their email - which is exactly the failing case. Every single upgrade would hit it.

RESOLVE IN THREE STEPS, cheapest first:
  1. customer.externalId                      - the happy path, no API call
  2. metadata.player_id from the checkout      - we set it ourselves, no API call
  3. checkouts.get(checkoutId).externalCustomerId - one API call, last resort
Then REPAIR: stamp the id onto the Polar customer so later events for the same person take path 1. Best-effort, never awaited by the caller, never fatal - failing to tidy up must not turn a successful webhook into a retry.

v1 validates the resolved value against a UUID regex before trusting it. In v2 the external id is the player's Convex id, which is NOT a uuid - decide what the validation becomes and state it. Do not simply drop the check.

Needs network, so this is a Convex ACTION, not a mutation.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 2 OF THE PARENT LANDS HERE, and the design requires it be pinned by a UNIT TEST before any sandbox run: customer.externalId null + metadata.player_id present -> resolution succeeds. The owner chose to build everything before verifying, so this test is what stops the identity bug surfacing late.

DONE WHEN: all three paths are pinned by test including the null-externalId case; the repair is pinned as best-effort - a repair failure does not fail the resolution; and a resolution that finds nothing returns null rather than throwing.
notes:
COMPLETE 2026-08-27 for the RESOLUTION half. Commits 2c15986 + 4d7e9a9. 483 tests / 32 files; four gates exit 0, verified independently by the controller.

SPLIT: this issue's DONE-WHEN spanned all three resolution paths AND the customer repair. The repair and the checkouts.get fallback both need the Polar SDK and belong to Task 9 (wordle-teams-l1v), where they are now recorded. This issue covers convex/lib/polarIdentity.ts (pure candidate extraction) and resolvePlayerIdFor (dual-namespace DB resolution).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 2 IS NOW PINNED - both release-gate cases, before any sandbox run, as decision C requires.

MUTATION VERDICTS (exit codes, isolated extraction, re-run after the review amendments rather than assumed inert):
  by_legacyId fallback deleted     -> 1 (3 failed)
  existence check dropped          -> 1 (1 failed)
  metadata-ignoring extractor      -> 1 (3 failed)
  sanity rename                    -> 0

THE PLAN'S RELEASE-GATE TEST WAS VACUOUS AND THIS IS THE MOST SERIOUS PLAN DEFECT SO FAR. 'RELEASE GATE, case 1' was a BYTE-FOR-BYTE duplicate of the plain 'resolves a native Convex player id' test above it - same body, different name - so it asserted nothing about metadata.player_id. The owner had designated exactly this case a gate that must pass BEFORE the sandbox run, so a vacuous test there would have manufactured the false confidence the gate exists to prevent.

PROVEN BY COUNTER-MUTANT, not by inspection: against a metadata-ignoring extractor the shipped test exits 1 and the plan's exits 0. Same technique proved the plan's single-direction ordering test is passed by a resolver that ignores order entirely.

NO UUID REGEX. v1 validated every candidate against a uuid pattern; that cannot be ported (v2 player ids are Convex Ids) and would be actively wrong, since the uuids that DO arrive are legacyId values. The check that replaces it is 'does this name a live player' - normalizeId for shape, then ctx.db.get for existence, then by_legacyId.

title: Task 7: downgradeTeamRemovalFor - SOFTENED, never deletes an occupied team
description:
Phase 5, wt-ksh.6. The Convex port of v1's handle_downgrade_team_removal - DELIBERATELY NOT FAITHFUL. See design decision A.

WHAT V1 DOES (20240501191728): keeps the first 2 teams the player belongs to, ordered creator-owned first then oldest; removes the player from the rest; then DELETES the teams they created that are not in the keep list - taking every other member's scores and monthly-winner history with them.

WHAT V2 DOES INSTEAD. Owner's decision 2026-08-25: a billing event on one account must not destroy a third party's data.
  1. Keep 2 teams. Same ordering rule as v1: teams the player created first, then oldest.
  2. Remove the player from every other team they belong to.
  3. For a team they CREATED and have now left: reassign creator to the earliest-joined remaining member.
  4. ONLY if no members remain: delete the team. Nobody loses anything, and copy-filters.mjs already establishes that a team with nobody on it is not a team.

RULED OUT - leaving the team creator-less. V2-ADDENDUM already records that a creator-less team cannot be edited by anyone; manufacturing that state deliberately is worse than reassigning.

THE ORDERING RULE IS SUBTLE AND V1'S SQL IS HARD TO READ. Establish what it actually does before porting - the keep query does 'group by creator, created_at ... order by case when creator = player then 0 else 1 end, created_at limit 2'. Verify the intended semantics rather than transliterating the SQL.

INTERACTION WORTH KNOWING: a team deleted here carries a legacyId, so a later copy re-inserts it - that is wt-ksh.13.10, already detected by the copy's insert report, not this task's problem. But step 4 above is a NEW delete site, so wt-ksh.13.10's runbook step 2 and the 'db.delete' inventory in scripts/lib/copy-tallies.mjs both name delete sites and may need updating. Check.

DONE WHEN: a downgrade with 5 teams keeps exactly 2; a team the player created and left survives with a reassigned creator; a team with no members left is deleted; no team containing another member is EVER deleted; and all four are pinned by convex-test.
notes:
COMPLETE 2026-08-26. Commits e405d8b (implementation) + 5e8fd58 (pin the copy). DIVERGENCE 12.

MEASURED independently by the controller: lint/typecheck/build exit 0; 454 tests / 30 files; e2e 15 passed (38.6s).

MUTATION-TESTED, verdicts from EXIT CODES, in an isolated git-archive extraction:
  ordering CONTROL (drop the owned term)  -> exit 1
  ordering SANITY  (rename a local)       -> exit 0
Both reproduced independently by the spec reviewer.

THE COPY FIX IS PINNED BY A PROPERTY TEST, not an exact string. src/lib/convex-error.test.ts is the FIRST test file for that module. It asserts no /creat/i and a present /\bowner\b/i over both codes, plus a length guard so an empty string cannot satisfy 'does not mention creation'. Two controls (one per code) both exit 1; a SANITY rewrite to DIFFERENT owner-based sentences still passes - so it pins the property, not the wording.

WHY THAT MATTERED: the review noticed the rewording was itself guarded by nothing, which is the exact blind spot that let the original strings go stale. Fixing the sentence without fixing the mechanism would have left the next drift equally invisible.

TWO PLAN SNIPPETS WERE WRONG AND WERE CAUGHT (both reproduced verbatim by the reviewer):
- The 5-team ordering test used all-solo teams, so the three dropped ones are correctly DELETED and the test's own (await ctx.db.get(id))!.playerIds then dereferences null. Real TypeError.
- The cascade test used a nonexistent monthlyWinners.score field and omitted the REQUIRED hasSeenCelebration.
Neither rewrite weakened the pin; the cascade test is now stronger, asserting the scoringSystems row is gone too.

BEHAVIOURAL TENSION WORTH KNOWING: teams.ts:382 refuses to let an owner leave their own team (OWNER_NOT_REMOVABLE), yet this helper removes an owner from theirs. The user-facing copy stays true only because the owner reassignment happens in the SAME ctx.db.patch. A future refactor that splits that patch has the copy downstream of it.

title: Task 6: upgradeTeamInvitesFor + the derived pending-invite count
description:
Phase 5, wt-ksh.6. The Convex port of v1's handle_upgrade_team_invites RPC.

v1 (20240426190809): for the upgrading player, on every team whose invited array holds their email - remove the email from invited, append their id to player_ids - then zero invites_pending_upgrade.

v2: the same, as a ...For helper. Move the player from team.invited to team.playerIds on every team that invited them, and reset their pending-upgrade count to 0.

KEYS OFF teams.invited, NOT OFF THE COUNTER. This is what makes design decision D safe: v1's counter lives in auth.users.raw_app_meta_data, which the copy script does not read and will not start reading. The actual parking is in teams.invited, which IS copied - so a migrated v1 user with parked invites is released correctly in v2 even though their counter arrives as 0.

Addresses in invited are lowercased on write since Phase 4; compare normalised.

RULE: the logic goes in the ...For helper, never in the mutation wrapper - convex-test cannot stand up a Better Auth session (wordle-teams-obw). Throw ConvexError via accessError, never a plain Error.

DONE WHEN: a player invited to three teams while free is on all three after upgrading; a player with no parked invites upgrades without error; the count reaches 0; and every case is pinned by convex-test.
notes:
COMPLETE 2026-08-27. Commits 22bc65c + 03d8fbb. 492 tests / 32 files; four gates exit 0, verified independently.

REAL USER-VISIBLE BUG CAUGHT IN REVIEW: pendingInviteCountFor counted teams the player is ALREADY A MEMBER OF. A copied team can list someone in both playerIds and invited - v1 never removed an invite it could not match, and billing.ts's own docblock calls that 'exactly what the copy brings over'. So a migrated non-pro user would have seen 'N Invites Pending' for a team they are already in, with nothing to accept and nothing to click. We would have replaced a counter that can DRIFT (decision G's reason) with a derivation that OVER-COUNTS - the same user-visible wrongness, differently caused. Fixed in pendingInviteCountFor only; parkedInvitesFor still selects those teams so the release keeps clearing the stale address.

MUTATION VERDICTS (exit codes, isolated extraction):
  A drop address, no roster add       -> 1 (2 failed)
  B case-sensitive matchKey           -> 1 (4 failed)
  C remove already-member exclusion   -> 1 (1 failed, the new test)
  D exclusion inside parkedInvitesFor -> 1 (2 failed, the stranding bug)
  SANITY rename                       -> 0

CONTROL D IS THE CONTROLLER'S OWN SNIPPET. The review instruction's prose said 'fix in pendingInviteCountFor, NOT parkedInvitesFor' and the code block pasted underneath it was parkedInvitesFor's body. The implementer followed the prose, then measured the snippet: it strands exactly the addresses the release exists to clear. Tenth plan/instruction snippet to be wrong; the prose has been right throughout and the pasted code has not.

IMPORT CYCLE RETIRED. teams.ts -> billing.ts was the first cycle in convex/, bought solely to feed a six-line query wrapper, while billing.ts -> teams.ts (cascadeDeleteTeam) is a real dependency with three importers. myPendingInviteCount moved into billing.ts; client path is now api.billing.myPendingInviteCount. Verified by Tarjan over all 31 non-generated modules: no SCC > 1, no self-loop, ACYCLIC. Note the cycle DID deploy green to beta first, so Convex's analyzer accepts cycles - this was a design call, not a correctness fix.

INVARIANT TO PRESERVE: parkedInvitesFor is one SELECTION with two callers. The count NARROWS that set and can never widen it, so no team can be counted that the upgrade would not clear.
