title: Task 12 — month-scoped Scoring System card and editor
description:
Plan task 12.

The card shows the system that governed the month currently in the URL - the same resolved system the scores table computes with, so the two can never disagree. A badge reads "In effect from Mon YYYY" when the month resolved to a version rather than the team's original values.

Customize is hidden when viewing a past month (a past month's rules are settled), when the viewer is not pro, and when they did not create the team. The first is a correctness rule; the other two are v1's gates, and like v1's they are UI-only.

Editor is Dialog on desktop, Sheet on mobile, as v1's CustomizeButton. Values are held as strings so a half-typed minus sign does not become 0.

The missed-day row is labelled "Missed day", NOT v1's "0". The schema field nA is a misnomer - v1's own card files it under "0 attempts" and it has nothing to do with the N/A shown for weekends. The schema field name is unchanged.

Files: v2/src/components/scoring-system-card.tsx (new), scoring-system-editor.tsx (new), v2/src/routes/index.tsx.

Step 5 of the plan is the acceptance walk and is the actual proof of wordle-teams-1j3.
acceptance_criteria: Editing the system in the current month leaves the previous month's displayed totals, row order and card values unchanged; the badge appears only on a historical month; Customize is absent on a past month, for non-pro and for non-creators; both themes screenshotted.
close_reason:
Done in 6af1865 (card + editor) and bdbf442 (review fixes). wordle-teams-1j3 is now visible to a user.

ACCEPTANCE WALK PASSED: July 2026 read Casey 5 / Robin 3. The system was then changed drastically in August — nA from 0 to -50, fail to -100 — and August recomputed to -900 each. July re-read UNCHANGED at Casey 5 / Robin 3, same order, no badge, no Customize button. Had versioning regressed, July's 28 unplayed days would each have shifted by -50.

CRITICAL BUG CAUGHT IN REVIEW: the plan specified inputMode='numeric' on the eight point inputs, which renders a digits-only keypad with no minus sign on iOS. Negative values are the entire feature — the DEFAULT system contains sixGuesses -1 and failed -3 — and the mobile Sheet exists specifically for phone users. v1 uses plain type='text' with no inputMode. Removed, with a comment so it is not re-added as an obvious mobile improvement. Not directly observable in headless chromium; verified that '-' and '-50' are accepted, round-trip through the server range check, and that out-of-range sets aria-invalid.

Also: the two eight-row label lists are now one exhaustiveness-checked Record<keyof ScoringSystem,string>, the [-100,100] bound is shared with requireValues, Save explains itself via aria-invalid plus a role=alert message, and the as-unknown-as cast is gone.

209 tests, tsc + build clean, e2e 5/5.

title: Task 11 — MyTeams card with creator-only team deletion
description:
Plan task 11.

Ports v1's my-teams.tsx: every team you are on with its members, and a delete popover for the ones you created.

THE PATH NO TEST COVERS: deleting the team you are currently viewing leaves the team search param pointing at a dead id, which surfaces as the route error boundary rather than a toast. The card clears localStorage and navigates with empty search so the sync hook picks the first remaining team. Exercise it by hand.

Files: v2/src/components/teams/my-teams-card.tsx (new), v2/src/routes/index.tsx.

pnpm e2e AND screenshots in both themes on a touch viewport.
acceptance_criteria: Every team renders with its members, delete works and cascades, deleting the SELECTED team falls back to another rather than hitting the error boundary, and both themes are screenshotted.
close_reason:
Done in 033d23c (card + two bugs found by the screenshot pass) and e3a1e15 (ConfirmPopover extracted, fixing the twin bug in current-team-card).

TWO RENDERING BUGS THE SCREENSHOT GATE CAUGHT, both invisible to tsc/vitest/build:
1. <main> had no grid-cols-1 at the base breakpoint, so its single implicit column sized to max-content and a long team name blew out the whole page width on a phone. PREDATES Task 11 — reachable via CurrentTeamCard's heading since Task 10. A reviewer reproduced it empirically: scrollWidth 840 vs clientWidth 390 without the class, 390 vs 390 with it.
2. PopoverContent's w-auto sized to an un-wrappable long team name and ran the confirm popover off-screen. current-team-card.tsx had the identical unfixed bug; the implementer flagged it rather than silently fixing shipped code, and the ConfirmPopover extraction fixed it by construction — the cap now lives in one place and cannot regress by omission a third time.

Delete-the-selected-team path driven by hand twice: success toast, fallback to another team, error boundary never appeared.

209 tests, tsc + build clean, e2e 5/5.

title: Task 10 — CurrentTeam card, member removal, team settings dialog
description:
Plan task 10.

The settings dialog ships in the SAME task as the Settings button that opens it. tsconfig has noUnusedLocals, so splitting them would leave this task with an unused settingsOpen local and a failing tsc.

Ports v1's current-team-client.tsx minus the Invite button (Phase 4). Settings and per-member remove are creator-only in the UI, and now also in the mutation. The creator's own row is filtered at the CALL SITE, so the card needs no knowledge of who the creator is.

Files: v2/src/components/teams/current-team-card.tsx (new), update-team-dialog.tsx (new), v2/src/routes/index.tsx.

pnpm e2e AND screenshots in both themes on a touch viewport - a zero-height Separator and an invisible Switch are the two documented radix-nova symptoms and neither is visible to the toolchain.
acceptance_criteria: Members render, Settings and remove appear only for the creator and not on their own row, the settings dialog round-trips, and both themes are screenshotted with visible Separator and Switch tracks.
close_reason:
Done in b3c6f67 (card + settings dialog) and 806a3f3 (review fixes: controlled popover closed explicitly on success, TeamFields extracted and shared by both dialogs). Spec review reasoned the member-filter expression through both branches and confirmed equivalence with v1's inline canInvite check.

Finding worth keeping: relying on the row unmounting to close the popover was safe in v1 because it mutated local state synchronously; v2 waits on a Convex subscription push, so the popover stayed open and interactive over an already-removed member. Fixed. NOTE the implementer measured the real window at single-digit to ~20ms even under CDP throttling, because Convex pushes over an already-open websocket rather than paying a fresh round trip — so the review's 'visible on a slow connection' framing was overstated. The fix removes the race regardless.

209 tests, tsc + build clean, e2e 5/5. Screenshotted both dialogs in both themes after the extraction.

title: Task 9 — team dropdown with create-team, and the upgrade swap
description:
Plan task 9.

team-picker.tsx is rewritten from Select to v1's DropdownMenu radio group, because "New Team" and "Upgrade for more" live INSIDE the dropdown in prod - a Select would need a second button beside it, a shape prod does not have.

Past two teams a free account sees "Upgrade for more" instead of "New Team". UI-only, exactly as in v1. Checkout is Phase 5, so the item says so rather than doing nothing - a dead menu item is indistinguishable from a broken one.

mutationErrorMessage lands FIRST in this task; every dialog in Tasks 9-12 imports it, and typedCodeMessage is module-private to convex-error.ts.

Files: v2/src/components/team-picker.tsx (rewrite), teams/create-team-dialog.tsx (new), v2/src/lib/convex-error.ts, v2/src/routes/index.tsx.

pnpm e2e AND screenshots in both themes on a touch viewport.
acceptance_criteria: The dropdown switches and creates teams, the free-tier swap shows at two teams, and both themes are screenshotted with a visible separator and a touch-sized New Team item.
close_reason:
Done in 2b21167 (dropdown, create dialog, mutationErrorMessage) plus three review rounds: da30714 (dynamic aria-label announcing the selected team, reset-on-open so a cancelled draft does not return, product wording on the upgrade toast, FREE_TEAM_LIMIT moved to convex/lib so Phase 5's server check can import it) and fe0e670 (inset the dialog on mobile, matching v1).

Verified visually on an iPhone 13 viewport in both themes, by the implementer and by the controller reading the screenshots: opaque popover, visible separators and switch tracks, truncated trigger, live New Team -> Upgrade for more swap after creating a second team, clean form on reopen-after-cancel, preserved draft on failed submit.

209 tests, tsc + build clean, e2e 5/5.

title: Task 8 — resolve the scoring version per month, and setScoringSystem
description:
Plan task 8. The load-bearing task for wordle-teams-1j3.

TWO HALVES, AND HALF OF IT IS WORSE THAN NONE.

The read half: getTeamMonthFor returns systemFor(team, versions, month) plus systemEffectiveFrom for the badge, instead of the team's live values - without it the scores table computes a past month's totals under today's rules.

The write half: winners.ts resolves the version for each month it recomputes, and setScoringSystem upserts the row for the current month then recomputes that month and every later month with a winner row.

The submitter's local today is client-supplied and bounded to +/-1 day of the server's date, reusing upsertBoard's guard - it decides which month a version governs for the WHOLE TEAM, so an unbounded value is shared-state corruption, not a personal view quirk. See wordle-teams-04r: that Convex's clock is UTC is currently an inference, not an observation.

No pro check in the mutation, matching v1's save action.

Files: v2/convex/winners.ts, scores.ts, scores.test.ts, teams.ts, teams.test.ts.

Blocked by Tasks 1, 3, 4. THIS IS THE TASK MOST LIKELY TO GO WRONG - it looks correct until someone views a past month.
acceptance_criteria: Inverting the scoring system in the current month leaves the previous month's winner, its hasSeenCelebration and its resolved system unchanged, while the current month recomputes — proven by test, not by inspection.
close_reason:
Done in feca88a (both halves + 4 added tests) and 654e986 (review fixes: OCC overclaim corrected to match upsertBoardFor, SYSTEM_FIELDS derived from DEFAULT_SYSTEM so a new field cannot skip validation, accepted-bounds test, vacuous-assertion comment corrected, bandwidth-guard enumeration updated, loadTeamMonthSystem rename). 209 tests, tsc + build clean.

TWO FINDINGS WORTH KEEPING:
1. The plan's flagship test did NOT pin the write half. Reverting to 'system: team' left all 204 tests green — the test targets a current-month edit, so the previous month was protected by the month filter, not by version resolution. Reproduced by the controller. Only the implementer's added tests catch it; a second reviewer confirmed they also catch a hoisted-resolution failure mode.
2. The plan told the implementer to return the resolved system directly. systemFor returns the TEAM DOC on fallback, so that would have put invited (real emails, public repo) and creator on the wire for every team with no version rows. The implementer refused the instruction and kept the explicit eight-field pick.

title: Task 7 — removeMember recomputes every affected month
description:
Plan task 7. Divergence 5.

Removing a member recomputes EVERY month the team has a winner row for. v1's update_monthly_winners is a trigger on daily_scores and removing a player touches teams, so it never fires - a removed player stays named as the winner of months they are no longer in, and production is carrying stale rows today.

The creator cannot be removed, matching v1's UI which hides the button on your own row. Since only the creator can reach the mutation at all, that makes "remove yourself" unreachable rather than merely hidden - v1 has no leave-team affordance and neither does this.

The removed player's boards are untouched.

Files: v2/convex/teams.ts, teams.test.ts.

Blocked by Tasks 1, 4.
acceptance_criteria: The member is gone, the creator cannot be removed, every affected month's winner row is recomputed, and the removed player's boards survive — all by test.
close_reason: Done in 71b56d7 (mutation + tests) and e78d4fc (review fixes: silent no-op for a non-member, winnerOf docstring + test). Spec review constructed the partial-recompute failure case independently and confirmed the rewritten test goes red for the right reason. 197 tests, tsc + build clean. Note: the plan's original test premise was wrong — winnerOf returns null only for an empty candidate list, not an all-zero one.

title: Task 6 — createTeam, updateTeam, deleteTeam with a hand-written cascade
description:
Plan task 6.

createTeam writes DEFAULT_SYSTEM's eight values, creator, playerIds of just the caller, empty invited, createdAt, and NO legacyId. No server-side team cap - v1's is UI-only.

updateTeam recomputes every month with a winner row WHEN playWeekends FLIPS, and nothing otherwise. playWeekends is an input to monthTotal, so flipping it re-scores every month; a rename changes no total.

deleteTeam CASCADES BY HAND. Postgres has ON DELETE CASCADE on monthly_winners.team_id; Convex has nothing, so the monthlyWinners and scoringSystems rows go explicitly. dailyScores are NOT deleted - a board belongs to a player and is shared across every team they are on.

Files: v2/convex/teams.ts, teams.test.ts.

Blocked by Tasks 0, 3, 4.
acceptance_criteria: Create, update and delete proven; delete removes the team's winner and scoring-version rows and leaves its boards; a playWeekends flip recomputes; a non-creator member is refused on all three.
close_reason:
Done in 2d0eb51 (three mutations + cascade) and f023c77 (review fixes: no-recompute branch pinned by a stale-winner test, today bound extracted to isPlausibleToday in lib/puzzleDay.ts, empty-cascade test). Spec review confirmed the stale-team-doc test would genuinely catch a regression, the cascade's prefix index queries match every row, and cross-team isolation holds. 190 tests, tsc + build clean.

Side effect worth recording: sharing the today bound exposed that upsertBoard threw INVALID_BOARD for clock skew, rendering 'That board is not complete. Check the answer and your guesses.' to a user whose board was fine and whose clock was wrong. Shipped Phase 2 code; now throws INVALID_DATE.

title: Task 5 — convex/teams.ts, one widened getMyTeams
description:
Plan task 5.

getMyTeams moves out of scores.ts and grows members, creator flag and settings, so ONE subscription drives the picker, the CurrentTeam card and the MyTeams card. Plus amIPro for the two UI gates.

Splitting into a thin picker query and a scoped detail query would NOT be cheaper: the read set is the whole teams table either way, because Convex cannot index array membership.

Members exclude profile-incomplete players, matching getTeamMonthFor and the winner recomputation. Fields are picked explicitly so the wire payload cannot carry the invite list, which holds real email addresses.

Files: v2/convex/teams.ts (new), teams.test.ts (new), v2/convex/scores.ts, v2/src/routes/index.tsx.

Changes the dashboard loader, so pnpm e2e is mandatory.
acceptance_criteria: One query returns members, creator flag and settings for the caller's teams only; a non-member's team is absent; the invite list does not reach the wire; pnpm e2e green.
close_reason: Done in 206c32f (widened query) and e30d038 (review fixes: undefined-creator and zero-teams tests, hasCompleteProfile extracted to convex/lib/player.ts as a type predicate, three stale comments repointed). Spec review verified the invited-array never reaches the wire, the profile filter agrees across all three sites, and no api.scores.getMyTeams reference survives. 176 tests, tsc + build clean, e2e 5/5.

title: Task 4 — requireTeamCreator, isPro, and three typed error codes
description:
Plan task 4.

requireTeamCreatorFor throws NOT_A_MEMBER for a non-member (so a probe cannot distinguish "no such team" from "not yours" from "yours but not yours to edit") and NOT_TEAM_CREATOR for a member who is not the creator. isProFor reads playerMembership and is never enforced.

AccessCode gains NOT_TEAM_CREATOR, INVALID_TEAM and INVALID_SYSTEM, which BREAKS the exhaustive switch in src/lib/convex-error.ts until each has copy. That failure is the check doing its job - do not route around it.

Includes the edge case worth asserting rather than discovering: teams.creator is optional because a scoped copy may not include it, so a team whose creator was not copied has NOBODY who can edit it.

Files: v2/convex/access.ts, access.test.ts, v2/src/lib/convex-error.ts.

BLOCKS Tasks 6, 7, 8.
acceptance_criteria: A non-creator member is refused, a non-member is refused with a different code, and an uncopied-creator team is refused to everyone — all by test; tsc clean again.
close_reason: Done in 11a11b6 (helpers + codes) and 74a5b1c (review fixes: INVALID_TEAM split into INVALID_TEAM/INVALID_DATE/CREATOR_NOT_REMOVABLE, fixtures consolidated onto convex/fixtures.ts, typed-code assertions). Spec review verified all four authorization semantics: NOT_A_MEMBER for non-members with no information leak, undefined creator refused to everyone, accessError still throwing internally, isProFor true only for 'pro'. Guard and exhaustive switch both cover 9 codes. 168 tests, tsc + build clean.

title: Task 3 — scoringSystems table and lib/scoringSystem.ts
description:
Plan task 3. Part of wordle-teams-1j3.

New table keyed on (teamId, effectiveFrom). New dependency-free module exporting systemFor, effectiveFromOf and DEFAULT_SYSTEM.

Resolution is "the version with the greatest effectiveFrom <= month, else the base". The base is the team doc's own eight fields, which is what makes this need no backfill and no change to the copy script.

NO legacyId on the table, and that is not an oversight: it has no Supabase counterpart, so nothing is ever copied into it.

pointsFor, monthTotal and winnerOf are UNTOUCHED - they already take the system as a parameter.

Files: v2/convex/schema.ts, v2/convex/lib/scoringSystem.ts (new), scoringSystem.test.ts (new).

BLOCKS Task 6 (which writes DEFAULT_SYSTEM) and Task 8.
acceptance_criteria: Resolution, base fallback, month boundaries and year-boundary ordering are green, and convex deploy accepts the table.
close_reason: Done in b05f173 (module + table) and c51069e (review fixes: total comparator, tie-break test, as-const DEFAULT_SYSTEM). Spec review verified resolution semantics, boundary inclusivity, year rollover, non-mutation of the caller's array, and systemFor/effectiveFromOf agreement. 162 tests, tsc + build clean. Note: the mid-task convex dev push was dropped from the plan — CONVEX_DEPLOYMENT is a local sqlite backend and convex-test is the real schema gate.

title: Task 2 — extract the dashboard search-param sync into a tested hook
description:
Plan task 2. Closes wordle-teams-lb9.

The effect in index.tsx navigates to fill in URL state while racing hydration - the classic infinite-redirect shape, and the highest-risk code in the Phase 2 UI. Phase 3 adds three cards to the same file.

The decomposition is the point: the DECISION comes out as a pure resolveDashboardSearch that needs no router, and the hook becomes a thin effect around it. The termination property then becomes a test rather than a comment - feed the function its own output and it must return null.

Files: v2/src/lib/dashboard-search.ts (new), dashboard-search.test.ts (new), use-dashboard-search-sync.ts (new), v2/src/routes/index.tsx.

Touches a route, so pnpm e2e is mandatory.

BLOCKS Tasks 9-13.
acceptance_criteria: index.tsx holds the route and layout; the decision lives in a pure tested function including an idempotency assertion; pnpm e2e green.
close_reason: Done in d67e29b (extraction) and 44a20ab (review fixes: stale cross-file comment, STORAGE_KEY consolidation, null-return doc, idempotency assertion). Spec review verified behaviour equivalence field by field and could not construct a looping input. 151 tests, tsc + build clean, e2e 5/5.

title: Task 1 — extract recomputeWinners into convex/winners.ts
description:
Plan task 1. Closes wordle-teams-4gj.

recomputeWinners is an unexported function inside scores.ts, reachable only by constructing a valid board submission and passing it through the whole validity and upsert machinery. Phase 3 calls it from three more mutations, so it moves out FIRST.

Four entry points: recomputeTeamMonth (the unit of work), recomputeTeamMonths, recomputePlayerMonth (what upsertBoard calls, behaviour unchanged), monthsWithWinners (what bounds the blast radius of a membership or scoring change).

THIS IS A PURE REFACTOR. The proof is that scores.test.ts passes untouched - if an assertion there needed editing, behaviour changed and the extraction is wrong.

Files: v2/convex/winners.ts (new), v2/convex/winners.test.ts (new), v2/convex/scores.ts.

BLOCKS Tasks 6, 7, 8.
acceptance_criteria: The five winner behaviours are proven by tests that never construct a board submission, and scores.test.ts passes unmodified.
close_reason: Done in 273196b (extraction) and 4816483 (review fixes: shared fixtures module, restored cost comment, WriterCtx export rationale, two test gaps). Spec review confirmed the extraction is behaviour-identical statement-by-statement and scores.test.ts assertions are untouched. 144 tests, tsc + build clean.

title: Task 0 — teams.legacyId optional so a native team can be created
description:
Plan task 0. teams.legacyId is a required v.number(), and a team created natively in v2 has no Supabase primary key to carry, so createTeam cannot insert as the schema stands.

Same fix and same rationale as Phase 2's widening of dailyScores and monthlyWinners: the copy is unaffected because idempotency runs through by_legacyId and native rows correctly never match, and legacyId === undefined becomes the marker Phase 7's row-count reconciliation against Supabase needs.

Files: v2/convex/schema.ts, v2/convex/schema.test.ts.

BLOCKS Task 6.
acceptance_criteria: convex deploy accepts the schema and an insert without legacyId succeeds; a copied team carrying legacyId still inserts.
close_reason: Done in dea05fb (schema + tests) and 2c1649e (fixture reuse after code review). NOTE: dea05fb's trailer says wt-ksh.4.2, an id invented in the plan before beads minted the real ones — not amended, since it is a shared branch and the trailer is cosmetic. Plan corrected in cee7727.

title: Verify live cross-player scoreboard update on beta (deferred from Phase 2)
description:
DEFERRED FROM PHASE 2 by owner decision, 2026-08-19. The only acceptance criterion of wt-ksh.3 not verified on beta.

Criterion 5 of the Phase 2 design: "A board entered in one browser updates another viewer's table WITHOUT a refresh." This is one of only two sanctioned departures from strict 1:1 parity with v1 (Convex reactivity making scoreboards live), so it is a headline feature rather than a nicety.

What IS verified on beta, by the owner:
 - a board entered on a copied account lands in the right cell with no refresh (single browser)
 - monthlyWinners rows are present and correct per team
 - month totals and row ordering match expectations

What is NOT verified: propagation to a DIFFERENT signed-in player's browser. The single-browser check proves the local mutation-to-query path; it does not prove the subscription pushes to other connected clients.

Deferred because it needs a second team with a second player to log in as, which Phase 2 cannot create — team creation is Phase 3 (wt-ksh.4) and invites are Phase 4 (wt-ksh.5). Attempting it in Phase 2 would have meant hand-seeding data on the deployment that becomes production.

DO THIS AT THE END OF PHASE 3, or Phase 4 if adding a second player to a team turns out to need the invite flow. Two browsers, two different signed-in players on one team: enter a board as A, confirm B's table updates with no refresh and no interaction.

Nothing in the repo covers this and nothing can — it needs two authenticated sessions against a real deployment.
acceptance_criteria: Two browsers, two different players, one team: a board entered by one appears in the other's table with no refresh.
close_reason:
AUTOMATED rather than observed once. v2/e2e/teams.spec.ts drives two independent Playwright browser contexts — separate storage state, two different signed-in players, one shared team seeded profile-complete via ensureSharedTeamFor. Player A enters a board; the assertion watches PLAYER A's cell as rendered on PLAYER B's page, with no page.reload() anywhere in B's path and no interaction with B between sign-in and the assertion.

Proven load-bearing rather than assumed: the implementer's first draft watched B's OWN row, which stays empty because B never plays — caught because the assertion timed out. Then, with the fixed version passing, they temporarily set B's context offline before A submits and confirmed the test fails identically. So it fails when reactivity is broken, not merely when something else changes.

Runs on every pnpm e2e. 8/8 green locally and in the deploy workflow.

Remaining for the owner: the same check against beta with two real browsers, as part of wt-ksh.4's side-by-side done-when.

title: Pinned columns drift while scrolling and row borders double — sticky vs border-collapse
description:
Two symptoms reported on beta, almost certainly ONE root cause.

SYMPTOM A: the pinned Player and Score columns move while scrolling horizontally and only settle into their sticky position after the gesture ends. They should never move at all.

SYMPTOM B: each player row appears to have both a top and a bottom border, so the line between rows is visibly thicker than the table's outer border.

HYPOTHESIS — position: sticky on table cells combined with border-collapse: collapse. Tailwind's preflight sets border-collapse: collapse on every table, and nothing here overrides it. That combination is long-broken across browsers: collapsed borders belong to the table's grid rather than to individual cells, so a sticky cell is repainted outside the normal flow and its borders escape the collapsed model. That produces exactly these two symptoms — late/jittery repositioning of the sticky cell, and a border rendered by the sticky cell IN ADDITION to the collapsed grid line, reading as a doubled row separator.

Compounding it: the pinned cells carry no z-index. scores-table.tsx sets `sticky left-0 bg-background` and `sticky right-0 bg-background` with no stacking context, so nothing guarantees they paint above the scrolling day cells.

PROPOSED FIX, to be verified rather than assumed:
 - border-separate + border-spacing-0 on the scores table
 - move the row border off <tr> and onto the cells, because a border on <tr> is ignored under border-collapse: separate — Tailwind's TableRow puts it on the row, so it will silently vanish otherwise
 - give the pinned cells an explicit z-index above the scrolling cells

Note this interacts with the earlier finding that the doubling was "entirely the currentColor border" (wt-ksh.3.12). That measurement was taken on DESKTOP chromium against a reproduction; the owner is reporting from a real device. Both can be true — the currentColor border made it far more visible, and a real doubling remains underneath.

VERIFY ON A REAL TOUCH VIEWPORT, and confirm both symptoms are gone, not just one.
acceptance_criteria: Pinned columns are stationary throughout a horizontal scroll, and the line between rows matches the table's outer border.
close_reason: Closed

title: Scores table still captures vertical touch scroll on mobile
description:
Reported on beta after the wt-ksh.3.13 fix: on mobile, dragging vertically with a finger inside the scores table scrolls the TABLE, not the page. No part of the table should scroll vertically.

wt-ksh.3.13 changed the Table primitive's wrapper from overflow-auto to overflow-x-auto, which was necessary but NOT sufficient, and the reason was already written down at the time. CSS refuses to pair a non-visible overflow-x with a visible overflow-y: setting overflow-x: auto silently coerces the COMPUTED overflow-y from visible to auto. That caveat is in the comment on ui/table.tsx. It was reasoned to be inert because nothing constrains the wrapper's height — which is true for LAYOUT, but not for TOUCH. A touch-capable element whose computed overflow-y is auto is still a scroll container as far as gesture handling is concerned, so it swallows the vertical drag instead of chaining it to the page.

FIX: set overflow-y explicitly to hidden rather than leaving it coerced. overflow-x: auto with overflow-y: hidden is a legal pair and stops the element being a vertical scroll target. Nothing gets clipped: the wrapper's height is auto and exactly matches the table's, so there is no vertical overflow to hide.

Consider overscroll-behavior-y: contain as belt-and-braces only if hidden proves insufficient — do not reach for it first, it treats the symptom.

Verify by actually dragging vertically at a mobile viewport with a touch-emulating context, not by reading computed styles: the computed value is the thing that misled the previous fix.
acceptance_criteria: A vertical drag starting inside the scores table scrolls the page, at a touch-emulating mobile viewport.
close_reason: Closed

title: E2E_TEST_MODE must be unset on the deployment that becomes production
description:
CUTOVER RISK. Same class as the wrangler.jsonc ENVIRONMENT issue.

Two public Convex mutations exist solely for e2e: testOtps.takeFor (pre-existing, Phase 0/1) and e2eSeed.ensureTeamFor (added Phase 2 task 9). Both are double-gated: process.env.E2E_TEST_MODE === 'true' AND the address matching /^e2e\+[^@]+@wordleteams\.com$/i. Neither can do anything without both.

The gating is sound. The risk is the deployment lifecycle around it.

E2E_TEST_MODE has to be set on whatever deployment the e2e suite runs against. The v2 design says the BETA Convex deployment BECOMES production at cutover — same project, same environment variables, DNS just flips. So if the variable is set on beta and nobody clears it, it is set on production the moment the domain moves.

With it set, anyone who can reach the deployment can mint an OTP for any e2e+*@wordleteams.com address and create a player and team. Bounded by the address pattern, so it cannot touch a real user's data — but it is a live unauthenticated write path in production.

Cutover checklist needs an explicit step: confirm E2E_TEST_MODE is UNSET on the production Convex deployment, and re-confirm after the final data copy. Consider also whether these two functions should be stripped at cutover rather than merely disabled.
acceptance_criteria: The Phase 8 cutover runbook has a step confirming E2E_TEST_MODE is unset on the production Convex deployment.
notes:
SHARPENED 2026-08-22 by the wordle-teams-96l fix. E2E_TEST_MODE surviving onto production now has a NEW and silent failure mode beyond the ones already recorded here.

convex/lib/e2e.ts's isE2eTraffic suppresses real mail for e2e+*@wordleteams.com addresses whenever the flag is 'true'. It guards BOTH senders: sign-in codes (auth.ts) and team invites (teams.ts). So if the flag survives cutover, then on production any address matching e2e+*@wordleteams.com:
  - never receives a sign-in code, and
  - never receives a team invitation,
with NO error raised anywhere - the invite is still parked in teams.invited and invitePlayer still reports success. The person simply never hears anything.

That domain is the product's own, so the population is small, but the failure is silent and indistinguishable from 'they ignored the email'.

The code comment in convex/lib/e2e.ts deliberately does NOT claim the flag is unset on production - an earlier draft did, citing this issue, which says the opposite. It now states the dependency and points here. Closing 7az is what makes that comment's production half true.
MEASURED 2026-09-01: E2E_TEST_MODE is NOT SET on fabulous-goldfish-949 today. See wordle-teams-cd8 for the reading and for why the exit code cannot be used to establish it.

THIS ISSUE DOES NOT CLOSE ON THAT MEASUREMENT, and deliberately not. Its done-when is a CHECKLIST STEP, not a state: 'confirm E2E_TEST_MODE is UNSET on the production Convex deployment, and re-confirm AFTER the final data copy'. Today's reading has no bearing on what the variable is at cutover - the whole risk this issue describes is that someone sets it to run e2e against beta between now and then and nobody clears it. A green reading in September is exactly the evidence that would make that feel unnecessary.

CARRIED TO wt-ksh.8.43 (Task 20, the runbook). Closing this needs the runbook to contain the re-confirm step, which is also what makes convex/lib/e2e.ts's comment true on its production half.
CLOSED BY THE RUNBOOK. docs/runbooks/2026-cutover.md now carries this issue's checklist requirement in full, which was the clause it was left open on when Phase 7 measured it green. See wt-ksh.8.43's note for what landed where.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 2: e2e smoke, beta verification and phase close
description:
One Playwright smoke test, not a suite, per the parent design. Extract the existing sign-in helper out of login.spec.ts into e2e/sign-in.ts so there is one definition, then login, enter a board, and assert the score lands. The dialog closing only on success means its disappearance is itself the assertion that the write landed. Then the full verification sweep, the beta deploy, and the phase done-when: enter board, live score updates in a second browser without a refresh, correct monthly winner row per team.

title: Phase 2: board entry with the keyboard-aware mobile sheet
description:
Ports v1's board entry AS IT STANDS ON dev, per amendment A3, not the version the 2026-07-16 design was written against. The three a335ae8 behaviours: handleSubmit wrapped in try/catch, setSubmitting(false) in finally so the form can never be left stuck, and the sheet closing ONLY on success (it used to close unconditionally and discard everything typed). The fourth, a warning toast when the winner update failed, is designed out rather than dropped, because the winner write now shares the mutation's transaction. Desktop Dialog and mobile top Sheet bound to the visual viewport, per the 2026-07-15 keyboard-aware sheet design: iOS Safari does not reflow a fixed panel when the keyboard opens and Radix locks body scroll, so without it the lower rows and Submit are unreachable. Adds shadcn popover and calendar for the date picker, which the design system does not cover; run the CLI from inside v2/.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop-design.md
acceptance_criteria: Six guess rows reachable by finger-scroll at an iOS viewport with Submit pinned above the keyboard, and a failed submit leaves the sheet open with the typed board intact and the form not stuck submitting. Screenshotted.
notes: Implemented per plan Task 8, commit b7b0359. Screenshot-verified (real Better Auth OTP login + temporary Convex seed, both cleaned up): desktop Dialog and mobile top Sheet, light+dark, board typed and colored correctly, forced-failure path confirmed sheet stays open / board intact / Submit re-enabled. Found and fixed two real bugs the toolchain missed: (1) form.tsx's scrollActiveRowIntoView used querySelector('#1-1') which throws (CSS ID selectors can't start with a digit) — crashed on every keystroke; (2) ui/sonner.tsx's <Toaster> was built but never mounted anywhere, so all toast calls app-wide were silent no-ops — mounted in __root.tsx. tsc/tests(118)/build all clean.

title: Phase 2: the month scores table
description:
The month grid. DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 8 'Leaderboard table': horizontally scrolling grid in a rounded-md border, Player column pinned left and Score pinned right, both painted bg-background so rows slide underneath, rows sorted by month total descending, score bold and right-aligned. Hand-rolled on the shadcn table primitive rather than @tanstack/react-table, which v1 uses: this table never sorts, filters or paginates, and the pinning is plain sticky CSS that react-table plays no part in. Cell rules come from the existing scoreCell helper, already unit tested. Ports v1's player-name disambiguation: first name alone, 'First L' when two players share one, initials on mobile. Rendering only the days the month has means v1's getDayVisibility has no equivalent to port. No component test: the spec rules out a component-test suite for a 1:1 port.

title: Phase 2: dashboard shell, day formatting, error mapping, team and month pickers
description:
Team and month live in the URL as search params, validated by the route. v1 kept them in a React context backed by localStorage and needed three separate hydration guards to stop the server and client disagreeing, and still shipped wordle-teams-uc5; search params cannot mismatch because both sides read the same URL. The current month is resolved from the browser clock in an effect after hydration, never during render, which is the 45e3cd6 lesson. localStorage still supplies the default team, applied post-mount via a replace navigation. Also: format-day.ts (Intl plus an ordinal helper, matching v1's 'EE do' and 'MMM yyyy' without adding date-fns), convex-error.ts mapping the typed ConvexError codes to user-facing copy, the read-only team picker, and the three-month picker. The pro expansion of the month window ships with the rest of the pro gate, not here.

title: Phase 2: recompute monthly winners inside the score mutation
description:
The relocation of the update_monthly_winners Postgres trigger into the score mutation, in the same transaction as the board write. Recomputes for every team the submitting player belongs to, for that puzzleDay's month only. Two deliberate differences from the SQL: it derives the winner server-side rather than trusting a client-computed array, and hasSeenCelebration survives an unchanged winner instead of being wiped by the SQL's delete-and-reinsert, which would re-fire the confetti at someone who already dismissed it. No winner means any existing row is deleted, matching the SQL. Profile-incomplete players cannot win, matching their exclusion from the table. Blocked on the legacyId schema change.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop-design.md
acceptance_criteria: convex-test proves a winner row per team, the highest total winning, ties broken as v1 breaks them, hasSeenCelebration preserved on an unchanged winner and reset on a changed one, and other months left alone.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 2: upsertBoard keyed on (player, puzzleDay) so duplicates cannot recur
description:
upsertBoard keyed on (playerId, puzzleDay), which is what makes a duplicate row impossible. v1 keyed on a client-held score id and inserted whenever the client had none, so a double submit created a second row for the same day; it has already done so 5 times in production (wordle-teams-rac). The 5 copied pairs are left untouched and read first-wins, as v1 renders them. Empty answer and guesses with an existing row deletes. The mutation re-validates with the shared boardIsValid and throws INVALID_BOARD: unreachable through the UI, which disables submit on the same predicate, but v1 had no server-side validation at all. Blocked on the legacyId schema change.

Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop.md Task 4
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop-design.md
acceptance_criteria: Create, update and delete all proven, and a double submit yields exactly one row. An incomplete board and an empty board with no existing score are both refused.
close_reason: Closed

title: Phase 2: team-and-month scoped read queries
description:
getTeamMonth scoped to one team and one month via a by_player_and_puzzleDay range query per member. v1 loaded every team, player and score ever into a client context; Convex re-pushes a query's whole result to every subscriber on every write, and wordle-teams-dcu flags database bandwidth, not function calls, as the binding free-tier limit. Also getMyTeams for the selector and getMyPlayerId so board entry can find the caller's own row without joining on name. Players without a completed profile are excluded, matching v1's getTeams, because a just-accepted invitee has no name and v1's fromDbPlayer throws on one.

acceptance_criteria: A scoped month returns only that month's rows and only for team members, proven by convex-test. Team settings and the scoring system ride along for the table.

title: Phase 2: access-check helpers replacing the RLS policies
description:
convex/access.ts replaces the Supabase RLS policies, per the parent design's logic-relocation table. requirePlayer resolves the signed-in user's copied player by lowercased email, the same join me.ts uses. requireTeamMemberFor takes an explicit playerId and is what the tests exercise, so the negative cases can be proven against real documents without standing up a Better Auth session in convex-test; requireTeamMember is the thin wrapper the functions call. A missing team throws NOT_A_MEMBER too, so a probe cannot tell 'no such team' from 'not yours'.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop-design.md
acceptance_criteria: convex-test proves a non-member is refused, an unauthenticated caller throws, and a deleted team is indistinguishable from a forbidden one.

title: Phase 2: pure day-string, board and scoring core shared by client and server
description:
Three dependency-free modules under v2/convex/lib/, imported by BOTH the browser and the Convex mutation so the scores table and the stored winner cannot disagree. puzzleDay.ts is arithmetic on YYYY-MM-DD strings. board.ts holds toRows, normalizeGuesses, attemptsFor and boardIsValid, ported from v1 utils.ts and the DailyScore class. scoring.ts holds pointsFor, monthTotal and winnerOf, ported from aggregateScoreByMonth and thisMonthsCurrentWinner. Two rules are load-bearing: attemptsFor must filter empty guesses because copied rows can carry v1's trailing sentinel, and winnerOf must compare with a strict > so the first player at the maximum wins a tie, as v1 does. pointsFor must be total and never throw, because it runs inside the board-entry transaction. src/lib/wordle.ts re-exports toRows rather than keeping its own copy.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-18-v2-phase2-core-loop-design.md
acceptance_criteria: vitest covers attempts including the trailing-sentinel case, points, month totals with missed days before today, weekends excluded when playWeekends is off, future days ignored, and tie-breaking. Suite green, tsc clean.

title: Phase 2: allow natively-created scores and winners to omit legacyId
description:
Schema prerequisite. dailyScores.legacyId and monthlyWinners.legacyId are required v.number(), because the schema was written for the Supabase copy where every row carries a primary key. Phase 2 is the first phase that creates rows natively and a board entered on beta has no Supabase identity, so upsertBoard cannot insert at all as things stand.

Widen both to v.optional(v.number()). Absence becomes meaningful: no legacyId means "born in v2, not copied", which is what Phase 7 row-count reconciliation needs. Leave the other four tables required.

title: DECISION: where do v2's login funnel events go?
description:
Owner decision. wt-ksh.12.7 built the instrumentation but deliberately did not choose a destination, because v2 has NO analytics dependency at all today (verified 2026-08-18: no logsnag, posthog or analytics anywhere in v2/src or v2/convex) and wiring one needs a credential and a vendor call that are not mine to make.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS: v2/src/lib/funnel.ts emits four typed events — login_view, login_provider_click (with provider), login_code_requested, login_callback_arrived (oauth|otp). All four call sites are wired and verified firing. The module is destination-agnostic: shipping them somewhere is a change to the single send() function and nothing else. Today send() logs to console in dev and no-ops in production, so NOTHING IS BEING COLLECTED YET and wordle-teams-390 still cannot be attributed.

OPTIONS:
 (a) LogSnag. The v2 design says 'keep LogSnag', v1 already emits to it, and one destination is what makes the v1-vs-v2 funnel directly comparable — which is the whole point of measuring. Needs an API token in the Worker env. CAUTION: v1's handleLogsnagEvent awaits logsnag.track() with no try/catch so an outage blocks sign-in (wordle-teams-4ov); funnel.ts is already written fire-and-forget, so do not reintroduce that shape.
 (b) A Convex table. Zero new vendors, queryable with the tools already in the project, and at ~200 login views a month the volume is negligible. Weigh against wordle-teams-dcu (database bandwidth, not function calls, is the binding free-tier limit) — though at this volume that is noise.
 (c) Cloudflare Web Analytics. Already in the v2 design, but it is page-level and cannot see a provider-button click, so it does not answer wordle-teams-390 on its own.

RECOMMENDATION: (a) LogSnag, precisely because comparability with v1's existing funnel is the thing that makes the number actionable.

DO NOT PUT EMAIL ADDRESSES IN THESE EVENTS. The repo is public and the payload may reach a third party; funnel.ts documents this rule and currently carries provider ids and step names only.
acceptance_criteria: A destination is chosen, funnel.ts's send() ships to it fire-and-forget, and a real login on beta produces a visible login_view and login_callback_arrived pair.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-18. LogSnag chosen and wired end to end, verified on beta.

SHAPE. The token is a secret and cannot ship to the browser, so the client beacons to a new /api/funnel route and the Worker forwards to LogSnag. Project 'wordle-teams' (same as v1, which is what keeps the two funnels comparable) on its own channel 'login-funnel' with notify:false, so it does not drown v1's signup notifications on 'users'. Delivered by fetch rather than the logsnag package — one less dependency, a few lines on a Worker.

VERIFIED ON BETA, not locally. An x-funnel response header reports sent | skipped | dropped:
  login_view                -> sent
  login_provider_click      -> sent
  login_callback_arrived    -> sent
  unknown event name        -> dropped
  malformed body            -> dropped
Also confirmed the browser actually beacons: loading beta's /login produced POST /api/funnel {"name":"login_view"} and clicking Google produced the provider_click. And the exact payload shape was accepted directly by api.logsnag.com with HTTP 200.

WHY THE HEADER EXISTS. A 204 alone cannot distinguish 'delivered' from 'quietly dropped because LOGSNAG_TOKEN is unset on the Worker' — the unconfigured path returns early and reports nowhere, so it was the one silent failure mode in the design. The header makes it curl-checkable without changing the beacon contract, since clients ignore response headers. That is how I proved the Worker can actually read the secret.

keepalive ON THE CLIENT FETCH. login_provider_click fires immediately before the document navigates away to the provider, so a normal fetch would be cancelled — precisely the event that tells us someone chose a provider would be the one most likely lost.

SECURITY. /api/funnel is public and unauthenticated. Event names, providers and methods are allowlisted and tags are BUILT rather than passed through, so nothing from the request body reaches LogSnag verbatim and no PII is carried (these events are pre-auth anyway). The mapping is a pure function with 7 unit tests — which is how a real bug got caught: with an object literal, EVENTS['__proto__'] resolves up the prototype chain to Object.prototype, which is truthy, so the allowlist passed for a name that was never allowed and emitted an event with an undefined name. It is a Map now.

NEVER BLOCKS AUTH. The route always answers 204 and never throws; an unset token is a silent no-op; LogSnag failures go to Sentry. wordle-teams-4ov is exactly the opposite shape in v1 — an awaited logsnag.track() with no try/catch, where a vendor outage blocks sign-in.

CONFIG. LOGSNAG_TOKEN pushed with 'wrangler secret put' to the wordle-teams-v2 Worker (verified present via 'wrangler secret list'); the value came from the repo root .env.local and is not in git. ENVIRONMENT is now a declared wrangler var set to 'beta' — CHANGE IT TO 'production' AT CUTOVER (Phase 8) or every prod event will be tagged beta.

NOTE: the verification above wrote a handful of synthetic events into the login-funnel channel today, plus one 'Funnel wiring check'. Ignore them when reading early numbers.

STILL OPEN, and this is the point of the whole exercise: wordle-teams-390 cannot be attributed until real traffic flows through beta. The events exist now; the data does not yet.
close_reason: Closed

title: Login surface: labeled provider buttons + funnel events (A7 exception)
description:
Spend the A7 parity exception: the login/onboarding surface.

This is the one surface where this phase may change behaviour, not just appearance. Amendment
A7 (2026-08-18) granted it because wordle-teams-390 is the product's largest measured leak —
~93% of people who reach /login never complete an auth round-trip, with ZERO server-side auth
failures in either measurement window, and the leak did not move when Lemon Squeezy was removed.

Two deliverables, both from wordle-teams-390's acceptance criteria:

1. LABELED PROVIDER BUTTONS. v1 renders a 3x2 grid of icon-only buttons whose labels exist only
   as sr-only text plus a hover Tooltip (src/app/login/oauth/oauth-provider.tsx:50-67). Tooltips
   do not appear on tap, and the heaviest login traffic is iPhone. v2 ships visible text labels.

2. CLIENT-SIDE FUNNEL EVENTS: login-page view, provider-button click, callback arrival — enough
   to attribute where abandonment happens rather than inferring it from server logs.

title: Build the presentational Wordle board component
description:
Build the presentational Wordle board component in v2 against the design system.

SCOPE BOUNDARY: this task is the board as a DISPLAY component — given a set of guesses, render
it. The entry interaction (keyboard, mobile viewport-aware sheet, submit handling) is Phase 2
work and stays there. Splitting it this way is deliberate: the board is the design system's
signature component, so it belongs to the system, while entry is core-loop behaviour.

Spec, DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 6: 5-column grid, 6 rows, gap-1 (4px), fixed 320px width on
desktop. Letters uppercase, text-3xl md:text-4xl.

TILES ARE SQUARE — radius 0. The doc is emphatic twice ('Don't round them', 'the sharp corner is
the game's visual signature'). This is the one place the radius vocabulary does not apply.

States read tokens, never inline accents: correct -> --wordle-correct (white-ish text), present
-> --wordle-present paired with --warning-foreground, absent -> --wordle-absent, empty -> no
fill, border only via --wordle-tile-border.

Also port the display rules: 7 attempts renders X, a missed day before today scores 0, non-play
weekends render N/A in muted text, and boards can be hidden per team until the viewing player
has submitted their own for that day.
acceptance_criteria: All four tile states plus X, 0 and N/A render from tokens with square corners in both themes; grep for green-|yellow- utilities in the component returns nothing.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-18.

SHIPPED: src/lib/wordle.ts (pure logic), src/lib/wordle.test.ts (18 tests), src/components/wordle-board.tsx, src/components/score-cell.tsx. vitest.config.ts now also includes src/**/*.test.ts — it was convex-only, so any src test would silently never have run.

Logic was split out of the component so the duplicate-letter rules can be tested without a DOM. That is where the value was: two of my own first-draft test expectations were wrong, and working them out by hand is what surfaced the bug below.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: grid is exactly 320px at md, tiles compute to border-radius 0px, font-size 36px (text-4xl), and the four states resolve to the right tokens in both themes. Score cells render 4 / X / 0 / blank / N-A, covering all five v1 rules.

TWO DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS FROM v1, both contrast:
 1. Tile foregrounds now travel with their background instead of inheriting the page foreground. v1's PRESENT tile inherits, so in DARK mode it is near-white on #eab308 — 1.84:1, below even the 3:1 large-text floor, on the signature component. Pairing it with --warning-foreground gives 9.83:1. This is a live v1 bug that the design system's own token pairing fixes.
 2. CORRECT tiles take --success-foreground (white-ish) per DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 6, rather than inheriting. Worth being honest that this is slightly LOWER contrast than v1 in light mode — 3.30:1 vs v1's inherited 6.00:1 — but tiles are text-3xl/4xl, so the 3:1 large-text threshold applies and it clears. Chose it because the doc explicitly says white-ish text and because an inherited foreground flips colour between themes, which is what styles.css rule 2 warns against. Easy to revert to inherit if you would rather have the higher number.

A REAL v1 BUG FOUND AND FILED, NOT FIXED: wt-ksh.12.10. v1's pass 2 demotes the EARLIER duplicate 'present' rather than the later surplus one, so a legitimate yellow is lost. Answer SPEED, guess GEESE: real Wordle gives -YGY- (two E's shown, matching the answer), v1 and this port give --GY- (one E). The player is told a correct letter is wrong. NOT fixed here because the board is squarely inside the strict-parity scope — A7's exception covers login/onboarding only, and silently changing scoring feedback during a re-skin is exactly the drift the parity rule exists to prevent. Pinned by a deliberately-named test so it cannot change by accident.

SCOPE HELD: presentational only. Entry interaction (keyboard, mobile viewport-aware sheet, submit handling) stays in Phase 2. v1's team-context dependency became showLetters/boardEntry props. v1's padArray MUTATED its input; toRows does not.

title: Add the Phase 2 shadcn component set with the documented fixes
description:
Add the shadcn components Phase 2 consumes, with the design system's documented fixes applied.

Set: button, card, badge, table, dialog, sheet, tabs, select, switch, input, skeleton, sonner,
input-otp, avatar, dropdown-menu, separator. Anything beyond this defers to the phase that needs
it. Do NOT bring over aceternity or magicui — border-beam is the only magicui piece
DESIGN_SYSTEM.md references and it is marketing-only decoration.

Fixes to apply while adding, from DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 10 and MIGRATION.md:
 1. Badge `success` variant must be bg-success + text-success-foreground. v1 pairs bg-green-600
    with text-secondary-foreground = ~2.1:1, a live WCAG AA failure. Add a matching `warning`.
 2. Card padding: v1 forked the primitive to px-4 py-6 md:p-6. Pick ONE default and let
    consumers override; do not fork the primitive again.
 3. Radius: bind each component to a single step off --radius. v1 has md, lg, xl and a one-off
    rounded-[6px] at the same hierarchy level.
 4. Toast severity: v1's sonner success and error render identically. Give each an accent edge
    or icon.
 5. Font as a token: font-display vs font-sans, rather than v1's per-element className.

Card titles are text-2xl font-semibold with a right-aligned action row on the same line.
DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 7 calls this deliberate and characteristic, not a mistake. Keep it.
acceptance_criteria: Every listed component renders in both themes on a scratch route; the success badge measures at least 4.5:1 in light mode; no aceternity or magicui dependency was added.
notes:
CORRECTION 2026-08-18 from wt-ksh.12.3 — fix #1 in this task's description is WRONG AS WRITTEN. Do not apply it verbatim.

This task says the Badge success variant 'must be bg-success + text-success-foreground' because v1 pairs bg-green-600 with text-secondary-foreground at '~2.1:1, a live WCAG AA failure'. That came from DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 10. Recomputed against a checker validated on six published WCAG reference pairs: v1's actual pair, near-black #111113 on green-600 #16a34a, is 5.72:1 and PASSES AA. The bundle's prescribed replacement, white on #16a34a, is 3.30:1 and FAILS. v1's badge was never broken.

WHAT TO DO INSTEAD: bg-success + text-success-foreground is still the right shape — the point stands that the accent should be a token rather than an inline green-600 — but it is a TOKENIZATION change, not a contrast fix, and the win is smaller than advertised. It is now safe on contrast only because wt-ksh.12.3 darkened --success (light) from #16a34a to #15803d, which puts white-on-success at 5.02:1. With the bundle's original value it would have shipped a regression.

Knock-on for this task: there is no live accessibility bug to cite as justification, so if the badge work is ever descoped, nothing is being left broken. Also note --accent-foreground no longer exists as the brand pair; it is --accent-solid-foreground (see wt-ksh.12.3 for why). And v1's success badge behaviour is a legitimate parity target after all.

Separately, wordle-correct light stays #16a34a while success light is now #15803d, so the badge green and the correct-tile green differ slightly in light mode. That is deliberate: tiles carry text-3xl/4xl where 3.30:1 clears the large-text bar, and the tile is the game's colour.
DONE 2026-08-18. All 16 components in, all five fixes resolved — but the style choice from wt-ksh.12.2 had to be reversed, for a real reason.

STYLE CHANGED radix-nova -> default. THE radix-nova REGISTRY VARIANT IS BROKEN UPSTREAM: it imports Radix primitives but styles on BASE UI data attributes. Confirmed by fetching the registry directly — ui.shadcn.com/r/styles/radix-nova/switch.json imports 'radix-ui' yet contains 4 occurrences of data-checked: and zero of data-[state=, identical selectors to base-nova. Radix emits data-state="checked" and data-orientation="horizontal"; Base UI emits data-checked and data-horizontal. Blast radius before the fix: ~80 mismatched selectors across 8 components (dialog, dropdown-menu, select, separator, sheet, switch, tabs, table).

CAUGHT VISUALLY, NOT BY THE TOOLCHAIN. Build, tsc and tests were all green with it broken — Tailwind simply never generated the rules. It showed up in a screenshot as an invisible Switch: the track computed to rgba(0,0,0,0) with a white thumb on a near-white page, and the Separator measured 96x0. This is the argument for the screenshot step being part of the gate, not decoration.

default IS radix-native (data-[state=) and internally consistent, and it is what v1's own components.json uses, so it is also the parity-correct choice. It matches DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 7 metrics out of the box far better than nova did: badge rounded-full px-2.5 py-0.5 text-xs font-semibold, switch 44x24 track with a 20px thumb, solid destructive rather than nova's tinted one. This retires my earlier claim on wt-ksh.12.2 that the New York/Default prompt was 'moot' — it is the legacy axis, but the legacy styles are the ones that actually work with Radix.

THE FIVE FIXES:
 1. Badge success + warning variants added, tokenised (bg-success/text-success-foreground). Measured live in both themes: 5.02:1 light, 4.79:1 dark, both clearing AA. The task's original contrast justification was wrong (see the correction note above); this is a tokenisation change and is documented as such in the component.
 2. Card padding — NO CHANGE NEEDED. Nothing forks the primitive; consumers override normally.
 3. Radius vocabulary — NO CHANGE NEEDED under default. Audited all 16: button/input md, card/dialog lg, badge/avatar/switch full, skeleton md-overridable. That is exactly DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 4, unsurprisingly, since the doc describes v1 and v1 uses this style. Drift #8 was about v1's CONSUMERS, not its primitives.
 4. Toast severity — sonner ships distinct per-severity icon shapes; success and error additionally take their semantic colour (5.02:1 and 4.83:1 on the toast surface). warning and info deliberately inherit: --warning is #facc15 at 1.7:1 there, so colouring it would read as broken. Verified an error toast renders with the red octagon-X.
 5. Font as a token — DONE HERE rather than deferred. Google Fonts import swapped Fraunces+Manrope -> Inter+Geist; --font-sans: Inter and a new --font-display: Geist; the .display-title CSS class deleted in favour of the font-display utility. Verified computed body font is Inter.

A DEFECT I WOULD HAVE INTRODUCED: shadcn's stock sonner.tsx imports useTheme from next-themes, which v2 does not use — it would have been a second theme source of truth disagreeing with ThemeToggle whenever a user picks a mode explicitly. Added src/lib/use-resolved-theme.ts, which reads the authoritative .dark class via MutationObserver, and removed next-themes from the dependency set.

VERIFIED: build, tsc --noEmit, 15/15 tests. A scratch /gallery route rendered all 16 in both themes at 1100px; dialog, sheet and dropdown all mount and Escape-close; two toasts render. Zero Base-UI attribute selectors remain. No aceternity, magicui or framer dependency. Scratch route deleted and the build re-run clean afterwards.

description:
Initialize shadcn/ui inside v2/ so the component set has somewhere to land.

MUST BE RUN FROM INSIDE v2/. Running `shadcn` at the repo root misdetects the project as v1
(Next.js 15.4.10, Tailwind v3, rsc true) and — verified 2026-08-18 — even resolves tailwindCss
to docs/design-system/globals.v2.css, the handoff file we just committed. Initializing from the
root would write config against the wrong app.

Settings: Tailwind v4 (so @theme inline, not tailwind.config.ts), TypeScript, rsc FALSE
(TanStack Start, not RSC), iconLibrary lucide (already a v2 dep), base RADIX to match v1's
component APIs — parity means matching v1's vocabulary, and v1 is Radix-backed.
CLI templates include `start` for TanStack Start. Package manager is pnpm@11.20.0, so
`pnpm dlx shadcn@latest`.
acceptance_criteria: v2/components.json exists and points at v2/src/styles.css; the @/ alias resolves; one added component renders under vite dev and vite build passes.
notes:
DONE 2026-08-18. Verified: vite build passes, tsc --noEmit clean, 15/15 vitest pass, and a Button rendered server-side under vite dev on /about (smoke test reverted afterwards). Compiled CSS confirms the mapping works, not just that it compiled: dist has .bg-primary{background-color:var(--primary)} plus --primary defined in both light and dark, and the existing teal tokens are untouched.

THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE TASK AS WRITTEN:

1. The alias is #/, NOT @/. v2's tsconfig maps '#/*' -> './src/*' and every existing import uses it. The task's done-when said @/ because I assumed shadcn's default; kept the codebase's convention instead of introducing a second alias. components.json aliases are all #/-prefixed.

2. There is no 'base' field in components.json. The published schema (ui.shadcn.com/schema.json) has required [style, tailwind, rsc, aliases] and NO base property — the base is encoded into style, e.g. 'radix-nova'. Writing base:'radix' produces 'Invalid configuration found'. So the radix-base decision is expressed as style:'radix-nova'. This also means the interactive 'New York vs Default' prompt is the legacy style axis, not the base choice, and my earlier plan to pick 'Default' for v1 parity was moot.

3. shadcn init is INTERACTIVE even with --yes, and its prompts need a real TTY — piped stdin and piped arrow-key escape sequences are both ignored, and a pty via script(1) hung. Bypassed by hand-authoring components.json against the schema, then 'pnpm dlx shadcn@latest add button --yes', which is fully non-interactive and correct. That is the path for wt-ksh.12.5's 16 components.

WHAT init WOULD HAVE DONE THAT I DID BY HAND: created src/lib/utils.ts with cn(); installed class-variance-authority, clsx, tailwind-merge, radix-ui, tw-animate-css; added @import 'tw-animate-css', @custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *)), an @theme inline color/radius mapping and a :root/.dark value block to src/styles.css.

TWO THINGS FOR DOWNSTREAM TASKS:
 - The :root/.dark VALUES currently in styles.css are the stock neutral baseline and are marked in-file as a placeholder for wt-ksh.12.3 to replace from tokens.json. The @theme inline MAPPING above them is permanent and should survive.
 - Nova's button differs from v1: rounded-lg rather than radius md, and a TINTED destructive (bg-destructive/10 text-destructive) where v1 is solid. wt-ksh.12.5 conforms components to DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 7 metrics.

title: Phase 1.5 — Design system foundation (import Claude Design system into v2)
description:
Import the design system built in Claude Design (derived from v1, then improved) into v2, and
build the component vocabulary Phase 2 needs, BEFORE Phase 2 builds board entry and scoreboard.

## Why this phase exists, and why here

v2's UI is effectively greenfield: v2/src/components holds three files (Header, Footer,
ThemeToggle), there is no shadcn install and no components.json, and the entire visual system
is a hand-rolled 464-line v2/src/styles.css — the sea/lagoon/palm/sand token set with light,
dark and prefers-color-scheme variants.

Phase 2 is the first phase that builds substantial UI. Landing the design system after Phase 2
means restyling the board and scoreboard; landing it before means building them once. The
window for this being cheap closes when Phase 2 starts.

## What the artifacts are

CSS / Tailwind theme tokens, plus static HTML/CSS mockups. No React components — translating
mockups to TSX is part of the work. As of 2026-08-18 the artifacts are NOT in the repo and not
in ~/Downloads; exporting them out of Claude Design is task one and is an owner action.

## Relationship to the parity rule

Amendment A7 (2026-08-18) added the login/onboarding surface as a third sanctioned exception to
strict-1:1 parity, alongside reactivity and passkeys. This phase is where that exception gets
spent: login/onboarding is the one surface where the design system may change behaviour, not
just appearance, because wordle-teams-390's fix (labeled provider buttons instead of an
icon-only tooltip grid) is design work on the product's largest known leak.

Everywhere else, the design system changes how screens look, not what they do. A3 still governs
which version of v1 behaviour ports.

## Scope boundaries

IN: token import/reconciliation, the component vocabulary Phase 2 consumes, the login/onboarding
surface, light+dark parity, mobile-first verification.

OUT: redesigning screens that do not exist yet (teams, invites, payments, reminders) — those get
built on the system in their own phases, not retrofitted in this one. Out too: any behaviour
change outside login/onboarding.

## Open questions — resolve when the export lands, before the task breakdown is final

1. Do the Claude Design tokens SUPERSEDE the existing styles.css sea/lagoon palette, or extend
   it? Determines whether Header/Footer/ThemeToggle and the existing static pages get restyled.
2. Does v2 adopt shadcn (matching v1's vocabulary: button, card, dialog, drawer, sheet, tabs,
   input-otp, sonner, table...) or stay hand-rolled on Tailwind v4? v1 also pulls aceternity and
   magicui, which are almost certainly not worth carrying over.
3. How much of the mockups' component surface does Phase 2 actually need, versus what defers to
   the phase that consumes it?
4. Dark mode: the existing styles.css supports data-theme plus prefers-color-scheme. Do the
   Claude Design tokens cover dark, or is that ours to derive?

## Done when

The design system's tokens are the single source of truth in v2, every component Phase 2 needs
exists and renders correctly in light and dark on a phone, and the login screen on beta uses
labeled provider buttons rather than the icon-only tooltip grid.
acceptance_criteria: Design system tokens are the single source of truth in v2/src/styles.css; every component Phase 2 needs exists and renders correctly in light and dark on a phone; beta's login screen uses labeled provider buttons instead of the icon-only tooltip grid.
notes:
ARTIFACTS REVIEWED 2026-08-18. All four open questions are now answered, and one finding changes this phase's shape.

THE BUNDLE TARGETS v1, NOT v2. The README says it proposes tokens 'for the v2 replatform', but every concrete artifact is aimed at the existing Next.js app. 'v1 -> v2' in this bundle means token-set version 1 -> version 2, applied in place to main. Evidence:
 - globals.v2.css is described as 'a drop-in replacement for src/app/globals.css' — v1's path — and is Tailwind 3 syntax: @tailwind base/components/utilities, @layer base, @apply border-border, .dark class.
 - tailwind.tokens.ts expects a tailwind.config.ts theme.extend.colors block consuming hsl(var(--token)). v2 has no tailwind.config.ts; it is Tailwind v4 via @tailwindcss/vite with an @theme block.
 - The whole Layer 3 alias block exists so src/components/ui/* compiles unchanged. That is v1's ~30 shadcn components. v2 has three components and no shadcn.
 - MIGRATION.md phases 2-4 name v1 files exclusively: wordle-board.tsx, ui/badge.tsx, app-bar/app-bar-base.tsx, home/feature-cards.tsx, magicui/border-beam.tsx.
 - tokens.json meta: stack 'Next.js + Tailwind + shadcn/ui', themeMechanism '.dark class on <html> via next-themes', branch main, captured 2026-08-03.
DO NOT run MIGRATION.md as written against v2. Use DESIGN_SYSTEM.md sections 1-11 as the spec and tokens.json's v2 block as the value source, translated to Tailwind v4.

WHY THIS IS STILL THE RIGHT INPUT: the bundle is a source-derived capture of v1's design plus a normalization pass. Adopting it in v2 does not violate strict-1:1 parity — it ENCODES parity, minus the nine catalogued drift items. That is a better fit for this project than a fresh design would have been.

Q1 SUPERSEDE OR EXTEND — SUPERSEDE, and this is a real cost. The design system is neutral + green + yellow and states 'No rebrand... the green->yellow accent stays'. v2's current styles.css is an unrelated teal palette (sea-ink, lagoon, palm, sand, foam). They are incompatible; one must win, and it should be the design system, because v1 is what users know and parity is the rule. Blast radius is small NOW and grows: the teal tokens are used by src/routes/about.tsx, Header.tsx, Footer.tsx, ThemeToggle.tsx and 51 hand-rolled classes in styles.css, across 5 routes total. This is the argument for doing the phase before Phase 2, quantified.

Q2 SHADCN OR HAND-ROLLED — ADOPT SHADCN in v2. Three reasons: the bundle's entire compat layer presumes it; v1's component vocabulary IS shadcn and parity means matching it; and Phase 2 needs table, dialog, sheet, tabs, select, switch, input, badge, card, skeleton, toast and input-otp, which is a lot to hand-roll. Do NOT carry over aceternity or magicui — border-beam is the only magicui piece the design doc references and it is marketing-only.

Q3 COMPONENT SURFACE PHASE 2 NEEDS — the Wordle board (signature: 5x6 grid, gap-1, 320px desktop, SQUARE tiles, radius 0), the leaderboard table (pinned Player column left, Score column right, both painted bg-background so rows slide under), dialog-on-desktop / sheet-on-mobile as one content component with two presentations, plus button, card, badge, select, skeleton, toast. Everything else defers to the phase that consumes it.

Q4 DARK MODE — COVERED. tokens.json v2 and globals.v2.css both carry full light+dark, with a verified contrast table in MIGRATION.md. Better than expected: v2's ThemeToggle.tsx already adds a light/dark CLASS to <html> alongside data-theme, so the bundle's .dark selectors work in v2 unchanged.

BUGS THE BUNDLE FIXES THAT v2 MUST NOT INHERIT: the success badge pairs bg-green-600 with text-secondary-foreground, ~2.1:1, fails WCAG AA. Also nine catalogued drift items in DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 10.

NOT COVERED BY THE BUNDLE: the A7 login exception. DESIGN_SYSTEM.md documents the OTP input but gives no guidance on the provider-button grid, so wordle-teams-390's labeled-button fix is additive work in this phase, not something the bundle hands us.
PHASE COMPLETE 2026-08-18. All seven planned tasks (wt-ksh.12.2 .. .12.8) closed, plus the .12.1 export.

DONE-WHEN VERIFIED ON BETA, NOT JUST LOCALLY. Six deploy-v2 workflow runs succeeded on feat/v2-replatform; the latest is live. Measured on https://beta.wordleteams.com/login at 390x844 in both themes: body background rgb(250,250,250) light and rgb(10,10,10) dark, body font Inter, a real <h1> 'Sign in', --accent-solid resolving to #15803d light and #22c55e dark (the AA-corrected values from wt-ksh.12.3), and all four provider buttons carrying visible text labels. Zero teal identifiers in the served HTML.

Gate at close: vite build clean, tsc --noEmit clean, 33/33 unit tests, 2/2 e2e.

WHAT CHANGED VERSUS THE PLAN, and why:
 - Style went radix-nova -> default. The radix-nova registry variant is broken upstream (Radix imports, Base UI selectors). default is radix-native and is what v1 uses, so it is also the parity-correct answer.
 - Fonts were done here rather than deferred, since the base layer was already being rewritten.
 - Fixes 2 and 3 (card padding, radius vocabulary) turned out to be no-ops under default — nothing forks the primitive and the radii already match DESIGN_SYSTEM.md section 4.

FOUR DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED that the bundle did not flag: the --surface collision that meant the design-system surface token was never in effect; the --accent-foreground double-declaration; shadcn CardTitle rendering a plain div so a Card-wrapped page has no h1; and sonner importing next-themes as a second theme source of truth.

THE BUNDLE'S CONTRAST TABLE IS UNRELIABLE and its headline badge fix is inverted — v1's pair is 5.72:1 and passes, the prescribed replacement is 3.30:1 and fails. Four token values deviate deliberately as a result. All of this is written up in docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md.

THREE ISSUES REMAIN OPEN under this phase, none blocking Phase 2:
 - wt-ksh.12.11 (P1, owner): funnel events have no destination, so wordle-teams-390 still cannot be attributed. Recommended LogSnag.
 - wt-ksh.12.9 (P2): header/footer/about still carry TanStack starter content. Must not reach cutover.
 - wt-ksh.12.10 (P2): v1 board over-demotes duplicate letters; reproduced faithfully and pinned by test, to be fixed deliberately.

Phase 2 (wt-ksh.3) is now unblocked and will be built on the design system rather than restyled afterwards, which was the whole point of sequencing this phase here.
