- **Vendor reduction:** ~10 vendors today, ~6 after.

**Constraints:** ~40 DAU in production daily, small data, solo developer with a few
hours/week. Existing app must remain fully live and supported throughout. One paying
customer (~$2/mo Lemon Squeezy subscription) who must be personally migrated.

## Decisions Made (and alternatives ruled out)

| Decision | Chosen | Ruled out / why |
|---|---|---|
| Database | **Convex** | Neon — data layer must be rewritten either way (RLS + DB functions are Supabase Auth–coupled), so Convex's rewrite penalty evaporates; its reactive model fits a client-heavy dashboard best; generous free tier |
| Auth | **Better Auth** via `@convex-dev/better-auth` | Clerk/Convex Auth — user preference; open source; Polar has a first-party Better Auth plugin |
| Payments | **Polar.sh** via `@polar-sh/better-auth` | Built into new app from day one; no in-place Lemon Squeezy→Polar phase (only 1 subscriber) |
| Notifications | **No vendor** — Convex cron + `web-push` + Resend | Knock — one workflow doesn't justify a platform; Convex scheduling replaces both Novu and QStash |
| Strategy | **Vertical slices on a walking skeleton** (Approach A) | Layer-first (nothing testable end-to-end for weeks); strangler proxy on prod domain (sessions can't span two auth/db systems; machinery costs more than the rewrite at 40 DAU) |
| Repo | **`v2/` folder in this repo**, fully self-contained | Separate repo — same-workspace old code is superior reference material during porting |
| Beta data | **One-shot re-runnable copies** from Supabase | Live/two-way sync — sync machinery is where solo projects die; buys nothing at this scale |
| Parity | **Strict 1:1** | Redesigns/new features go to a post-cutover backlog |

## Target Architecture

| Concern | Choice | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Framework | TanStack Start (Router + Query + server functions), Vite, React 19 | Server functions only where needed (webhooks, auth) |
| Hosting | Cloudflare Workers (TanStack Start Cloudflare target) | Wrangler; `beta.` subdomain during parallel run |
| Data | Convex — schema, queries/mutations, crons, scheduled functions | `@convex-dev/react-query` for live-updating TanStack Query data |
| Auth | Better Auth on Convex | Email OTP + Google, Azure, GitHub, Twitter/X + passkey plugin |
| Payments | Polar.sh via Better Auth plugin | Checkout, customer portal, webhooks |
| Email | Resend + react-email | Ports nearly as-is; also sends Better Auth OTP emails |
| Reminders | Convex cron → `web-push` + Resend | Replaces Novu + QStash + both reminder API routes |
| PWA | vite-plugin-pwa (Workbox) | Replaces Serwist; manifest ports as-is |
| Errors | Sentry (Cloudflare/TanStack SDK) | Wired from Phase 0 |
| Analytics/logs | Cloudflare Web Analytics; Workers Logs; keep LogSnag | Drop Vercel Analytics/Speed Insights, next-axiom, Axiom |

**Killed with no replacement:** Novu, QStash, Vercel KV, Edge Config, Lemon Squeezy SDK,
Serwist, next-axiom, Axiom.

**Open checklist item (verify in Phase 0):** whether Supabase Storage buckets hold real
user files (e.g. avatars). If yes → Convex file storage; if unused → nothing to do.

## Repo Layout & Environments

```
wordle-teams/            ← repo root unchanged; Vercel keeps building it
├── src/ ...             ← current Next.js app, untouched until cutover
├── supabase/
└── v2/                  ← new app, fully self-contained island
    ├── package.json     ← own deps, own pnpm-lock.yaml (NOT a workspace member)
    ├── wrangler.jsonc
    ├── convex/          ← schema, functions, crons, auth config
    ├── src/             ← TanStack Start app
    └── scripts/         ← copy-from-supabase.ts + parity verification
```

**Island rule:** no imports across the `v2/` boundary, no shared lockfile, no root
tooling changes. Old code is reference material only.

| Env | Hosting | Convex | Domain |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local dev | `vite dev` + `convex dev` | personal dev deployment | localhost |
| Beta | Cloudflare Workers | prod deployment of the project | `beta.<domain>` |
| Prod (post-cutover) | same Worker, promoted | same Convex project — beta *becomes* prod | main domain |

The beta Convex project becomes the prod project at cutover: final data copy overwrites
beta test data, domain flips. No second migration.

**Deploys:** GitHub Action on `v2/`-touching pushes → `convex deploy` + `wrangler deploy`.
Vercel's existing auto-deploy of `dev` continues untouched (never trigger Vercel manually).

**DNS:** nameservers move to Cloudflare early (free plan) — prerequisite for beta
subdomain and cutover; Vercel keeps serving apex/www through the same records.

## Data Model & Migration

**Tables (6, port near-1:1):** `players`, `teams`, `daily_scores`, `monthly_winners`,
`player_customer` (becomes Polar customer mapping), `webhook_events`. Docs keep a
`legacyId` for idempotent re-copying (or wipe-and-reload — fine at this size).
Relations become Convex ID references + indexes.

**Postgres logic relocation:**

| Today (in the DB) | In Convex |
|---|---|
| RLS policies | Access checks at top of each query/mutation, centralized in small helper functions |
| `handle_invited_signup`, `handle_add_player_to_team` | Mutations in invite/onboarding flow (Phase 4) |
| `handle_upgrade_team_invites`, `handle_downgrade_team_removal` | Mutations called by Polar webhook handler (Phase 5) |
| `update_monthly_winners` (trigger) | Logic inside score-submission mutation (transactional, so trigger semantics port cleanly) |
| `get_players_for_reminder`, `update_last_board_entry_reminder` | Internal functions called by reminder cron (Phase 6) |
| `custom_access_token_hook` (JWT claims) | Not needed — claims fed RLS; checks now read membership directly |

**Auth migration:** login is passwordless (email OTP) → no password hashes to migrate.
Copy script creates Better Auth users by email (+ name, verified flag). Sessions do not
carry over — the only user-visible cost of the entire migration is one extra login.

**Social OAuth:** trim to Google, Azure, GitHub, Twitter/X. Safe because OTP on the same
email is the universal fallback for users of dropped providers. Better Auth links social
logins to existing accounts by verified email; Twitter/X doesn't always return an email —
OTP is the fallback there too. Each provider needs OAuth app registrations with beta
callback URLs (during build) and prod callbacks (at cutover) — explicit checklist work
in Phase 1.

**Passkeys:** Better Auth passkey plugin + one "Add passkey" button in account settings.

**Copy script** (`v2/scripts/copy-from-supabase.ts`): reads Supabase with service-role
key, writes via Convex internal mutations. Re-runnable on demand; run once more during
the cutover window.

**What the re-run overwrites, and why that is the point.** Beta team and player state is
discarded at cutover — the final copy is *meant* to overwrite it. Owner's decision
(2026-08-24): everything in the beta deployment is testing data, permanently, and that
includes rows created by anyone brought in to help test. "But someone else made that
team" is not an objection; it is still test data.

Which rows are actually at risk is easy to get backwards. A row **born in v2 is the safe
one**: it carries no `legacyId`, and `byLegacyId` is the entire upsert key for `players`
and `teams`, so the copy can never match it and never patches it. What a re-run reverts
is a **copied** row that v2 has since edited — a renamed team, a changed roster, an
invite added or cancelled. `monthlyWinners` is the exception: it matches on `(teamId,
year, month)`, not `legacyId`, so a winner row v2 computed itself *is* matched, adopted
and overwritten.

So the copy reports what it overwrote (`wt-ksh.13`): `upsertPlayers`, `upsertTeams` and
`upsertMonthlyWinners` return per-field counts of the rows they patched to a different
value, and the script prints a framed block when non-zero, one quiet line when zero. Not
to protect beta rows — nothing there needs protecting — but so that a copy run at the
**wrong** moment, after cutover with real users on v2, announces itself. It reports the
difference, never its author: a count means the incoming v1 value differs from the stored
one, which is a lost v2 edit *or* ordinary v1 drift since the last copy, so reading it is
a per-field judgement. `scoring` is always the latter — v2 never writes those eight
fields after `createTeam` — which does not make it harmless: an imported v1 scoring edit
lands as the team's base system, and any month with no `scoringSystems` version before
it falls back to exactly those fields, so the import re-scores it (`wordle-teams-1j3`).
It is not total, and its clean line names the tables it is not speaking for:
`dailyScores` is left undiffed (`wordle-teams-r9d`), and nothing in v2 writes
`playerMembership` or `webhookEvents` yet. Array fields compare as multisets, so a
re-copy can silently reorder `playerIds` and `invited` — the orders `getMyTeamsFor` and
`getTeamInvitesFor` hand to the UI — accepted, because order-sensitive comparison would
fire on every run and train everyone to ignore the report. And a row v2 **deleted** is
invisible to any diff by construction: nothing remains to compare against, so the copy
re-inserts it and reports it as `inserted` (`wt-ksh.13.10`). That needs a tombstone, and
until it has one the cutover runbook checks it by hand (`wt-ksh.9`).

## Phase Plan

Each phase is independently shippable to beta, sized for 1–2 weeks of a few-hours/week
solo pace. **No phase starts until the previous phase's done-when is met.**
Phases 2→4 are strictly ordered; Phases 5 and 6 are independent of each other and may
interleave; nothing else may.

- **Phase 0 — Walking skeleton.** TanStack Start scaffold in `v2/`, Convex project,
  Better Auth email OTP only, deploy pipeline, `beta.` DNS, Sentry.
  ✅ *Done when: OTP login works at `beta.<domain>` and a page renders one value
  round-tripped through Convex.*
- **Phase 1 — Auth complete + data copy.** Full Convex schema, copy script (users +
  6 tables), social providers incl. OAuth console registrations, passkey plugin,
  account linking.
  ✅ *Done when: your real copied account logs in via OTP and via Google on beta, and
  enrolls a passkey.*
- **Phase 2 — Core loop.** Board entry (porting the recent mobile keyboard/viewport
  work faithfully), scoreboard, month navigation, monthly-winner logic in the score
  mutation, access-check helpers.
  ✅ *Done when: a full fake day works on beta — enter board, live score updates,
  correct monthly winner.*
- **Phase 3 — Teams.** Create/switch/manage, member lists, settings, team-scoped
  access checks.
  ✅ *Done when: a multi-team account behaves identically to prod side-by-side.*
- **Phase 4 — Invites & onboarding.** Invite flow, invited-signup + add-player
  mutations, complete-profile flow, invite emails via Resend.
  ✅ *Done when: a fresh email invited on beta lands on the right team with the right
  profile.*
- **Phase 5 — Payments (Polar).** Sandbox → Better Auth plugin, checkout, customer
  portal, idempotent webhook handler writing `webhook_events`, upgrade/downgrade
  team-size mutations.
  ✅ *Done when: sandbox subscribe/upgrade/downgrade/cancel all mutate team limits
  correctly.*
- **Phase 6 — Reminders & PWA.** Convex cron → reminder-eligibility port → web-push +
  Resend; vite-plugin-pwa, manifest, install/offline; old-Serwist-SW kill switch.
  ✅ *Done when: beta sends a real push + email reminder at the configured time and the
  PWA installs on a phone.*
- **Phase 7 — Parity audit + hardening.** Route-by-route walk of prod vs beta (static
  pages, `/me`, error states, sitemap/robots/OG images, maintenance page), fresh copy
  run + re-verify, cutover runbook written.
  ✅ *Done when: a written checklist of every prod screen has a ✔ against beta.*
- **Phase 8 — Cutover.** See below.
- **Phase 9 — Post-cutover cleanup** (~2 weeks after cutover). See below.

## Cutover & Rollback

**Pre-cutover (week before):** add prod callbacks to all four OAuth apps; create real
Polar product + webhook config; email the paying customer (what's changing, Polar link
coming, comp offer); in-app maintenance banner on prod ("you'll need to log in again");
one runbook dry-run (copy + verify, no DNS flip).

**Cutover day (target < 1 hour, low-traffic time):**
1. Prod → maintenance mode (existing `/maintenance` page)
2. Final copy-script run (beta Convex data replaced with real snapshot)
3. DNS flip: main domain → Worker; `beta.` stays alive on the same Worker
4. Smoke test on prod domain: OTP login, one social login, board entry, scoreboard,
   PWA opens on phone
5. Switch Polar webhook + OAuth primary URLs to prod domain
6. Send Polar checkout link to the customer
7. Announce done

**PWA continuity:** installs are domain-keyed and survive the flip; new SW takes over on
next visit. The Phase 6 kill switch ensures the old Serwist worker unregisters cleanly so
no one is stuck on a stale cache.

**Rollback (kept 2 weeks):** Vercel deployment and Supabase stay live and untouched;
rollback = flip DNS back. **One-way data rule:** scores entered post-cutover exist only
in Convex — rolling back loses them unless manually re-entered. Accepted at this scale;
breakage would surface within hours, not days.

**Post-cutover cleanup (Phase 9):** cancel/retire Vercel project, Supabase project
(after a final archived pg_dump), Novu, QStash, Lemon Squeezy store (after the
subscription is confirmed moved); promote `v2/` to repo root (old app lives in git
history); delete dead env vars.

## Testing, Error Handling & Observability

**Testing (proportionate, concentrated where rewrite risk lives):**
- **Convex function tests** (`convex-test` + Vitest), priority order: monthly-winner
  computation, invite/signup flows, upgrade/downgrade logic, access-check helpers —
  including negative cases (non-member *cannot* read another team's scores).
- **Parity spot-checks:** after each copy run, a script asserts row counts and known
  aggregates (e.g., a specific month's winner) match Supabase vs Convex.
- **UI:** manual and structured — each phase's done-when plus the Phase 7 route
  checklist. No component-test suite for a 1:1 port.
- **One smoke E2E** (Playwright: OTP login → enter board → see score) before each phase
  merge and on cutover day. One test, not a suite.

**Error handling:**
- Convex mutations throw `ConvexError` with typed codes; UI maps codes → sonner toasts.
- **Webhook handlers idempotent** (Polar retries): `webhook_events` dedup by event ID.
  Reminder cron never double-sends (last-reminder timestamp guard, ported).
- TanStack Router error boundaries per route section + root boundary → Sentry.

**Observability:** Sentry from Phase 0; Workers Logs for request logs; LogSnag continues
for business-event pings; Cloudflare Web Analytics snippet at Phase 7; Axiom dropped.

## Out of Scope

- Any new features or redesigns (except the two sanctioned: live-updating scoreboards
  via Convex reactivity, passkey enrollment)
- Live/two-way data sync between Supabase and Convex
- Zero-downtime cutover machinery (maintenance window is acceptable)
- Notification platform (Knock etc.) — revisit only if notification complexity
  materializes post-cutover
- Migrating Vercel-specific features with no user impact (Speed Insights, Edge Config)

## Acceptance Criteria (project level)

1. New app at the production domain on Cloudflare Workers with TanStack Start + Convex +
   Better Auth + Polar, at 1:1 functional parity per the Phase 7 checklist
2. All migrated users can log in (OTP or retained social provider) and see their full
   score history
3. The paying customer is subscribed via Polar; Lemon Squeezy retired
4. Reminders (push + email) fire correctly from Convex cron
5. Installed PWAs survive cutover without user reinstallation
6. Old stack fully retired within ~2 weeks of cutover; rollback path verified live
   until then
notes:
AMENDED 2026-08-03. dev was merged into feat/v2-replatform after ~93 commits of v1 work that post-date the design: the Lemon Squeezy -> Polar migration (now live in production), the invite->join fixes, and a run of performance/reliability fixes. See the Amendments section at the end of docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-replatform-v2-design.md — several decisions in the body of that spec are superseded.

Headlines:
 - Phase 5 (wt-ksh.6) is no longer greenfield; v2 inherits live Polar orgs, products and webhooks, plus three hard-won bugs it must port fixes for.
 - Phase 4 (wt-ksh.5) inherits one invite bug that SURVIVES the rewrite: case-sensitive invited[] matching.
 - Parity is now against dev as of 2026-08-03, not the 2026-07-16 snapshot (wt-ksh.3, wt-ksh.7).
 - Phase 8 (wt-ksh.9) loses its paying-customer migration steps; Lemon Squeezy is already retired and there is no active Polar subscriber.
 - The COST driver is contradicted by the funnel data measured since. Open owner decision: wordle-teams-dts.
 - ALL OF v2 IS BLOCKED behind one manual owner step: moving wordleteams.com nameservers to Cloudflare (wt-ksh.1.1).
SEQUENCING SETTLED 2026-08-18 (closes wordle-teams-dts). Owner chose option (b): interleave funnel work with the port. See amendment A7 in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-16-replatform-v2-design.md.

Three consequences for this epic:
 1. Cost is demoted from lead driver to secondary benefit. DX/architecture fit and vendor reduction (~10 -> ~6) carry the project. Not an open question any more.
 2. Strict-1:1 parity gains a THIRD sanctioned exception: the login/onboarding surface, alongside reactivity and passkeys. Rationale: wordle-teams-390 was re-measured 2026-08-17 and the leak did not move (163 -> 203 people reaching /login, conversion ~7% -> ~8%) even though Lemon Squeezy — A5's leading mechanical explanation — is gone. 93% abandon at login vs 87% at activation, with zero server-side auth failures. Porting v1's icon-only tooltip provider grid faithfully would reproduce the largest known leak in the product. Parity everywhere else is unchanged and still strict.
 3. Funnel instrumentation (login-page view, provider-button click, callback arrival) is a v2 deliverable, not a post-cutover backlog item.

This does NOT license a general redesign. Every screen outside login/onboarding still ports 1:1, and A3 still governs which version it ports against.

NEW PHASE INSERTED: wt-ksh.12, Phase 1.5 — Design system foundation, sits between Phase 1 and Phase 2 and now blocks wt-ksh.3. See amendment A8. Reason it goes here rather than later: v2/src/components has three files and no component library, so Phase 2 is the first phase to build substantial UI. Landing the design system after Phase 2 means restyling the board and scoreboard.
CORRECTION 2026-09-01 (Phase 7 Task 16). The Data Model & Migration section's clean line says "nothing in v2 writes `playerMembership` or `webhookEvents` yet". PHASE 5 MADE BOTH FALSE: convex/billing.ts inserts playerMembership at :549 and webhookEvents at :523 and :638.

This matters because that sentence is what names the tables the overwrite diff is NOT speaking for. With v2 now writing both, a re-copy CAN take back a v2-written membership row or webhook record on a copied player, and the diff no longer stays silent on those two tables for the reason given.

The 'yet' was accurate when written and is what went stale. Task 20's cutover runbook should carry the corrected statement rather than this one.

title: Nothing checks §7a's divergence count, and it has now gone stale twice
description:
FOUND 2026-09-02 while adding a row for wordle-teams-7jpo.

docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md section 7a opens with a COUNT, and that count is load-bearing because the sentence beside it reads: "Anything else the audit finds is a bug." A reader who trusts it treats every divergence past the stated number as a defect to chase.

IT HAS DRIFTED TWICE:
  - Phase 7 Task 16 found the header saying EIGHTEEN while the table held THIRTY-NINE. Twenty-one real divergences were sitting under a sentence inviting the audit to treat them as bugs. Task 16 corrected it to forty-three and wrote a paragraph explaining why the number matters.
  - On 2026-09-02, one day later, the header still said FORTY-THREE while the table held FIFTY-TWO. Rows 44-52 - the whole UI/UX polish pass - were appended without touching it. Nine divergences in the same trap the paragraph above them describes.

Corrected to fifty-three (fifty-two plus 7jpo's row) in the same commit as that row.

THE POINT IS THAT PROSE DID NOT PREVENT IT. Task 16 did not merely fix the number, it wrote down why the number matters, in the same file, immediately above it - and the next nine rows still went in without it. A comment cannot enforce an invariant that a person has to remember at the exact moment they are thinking about something else.

FIX SHAPE: a test that parses section 7a, counts the `| N |` rows, and asserts both that the numbering is contiguous from 1 and that the header's spelled-out count matches. Both halves are worth having - this session also found the table numbering had a DUPLICATE 50 for a few minutes, because a new row was inserted after row 49 by someone (me) who had grepped for `^| 4[0-9] ` and concluded 49 was last. It was not; rows 50-52 existed.

WHERE IT GOES: v2/src/ has no test that reads docs/. src/crawler-metadata.test.ts is the closest precedent for parsing a non-source artefact and asserting invariants across it, and it reads public/robots.txt from disk the same way this would need to read the addendum. The spelled-out count ("fifty-three") needs a small number-word map, or the header could be changed to a numeral so the test is a plain comparison - worth deciding, since the prose style of that document is deliberate.
close_reason: 4m2t: addendum-divergences.test.ts now asserts the spelled-out header count equals the row count and that numbering is contiguous; three mutations killed. 8.50: the footer got its own row 58 rather than the buried note, since an auditor scans row titles. cog5: wording changed rather than the status - a 301 would be cached irreversibly by exactly the installed PWAs this route exists for. woe0: already covered by row 43, no change needed.

title: The zone's Browser Cache TTL rewrites max-age=0 to 14400 on cached documents
description:
DISCOVERED 2026-09-02 while verifying wordle-teams-fqeq on beta. New as of that change, and not decided by anyone.

WHAT WAS MEASURED. src/server.ts sets, via cache-policy.ts's STATIC_CACHE:

  public, max-age=0, s-maxage=86400, stale-while-revalidate=604800

The FIRST request to /about comes back with exactly that. The second and third, served from the edge cache, come back with:

  public, max-age=14400, s-maxage=86400, stale-while-revalidate=604800

max-age=0 has become 14400. That is four hours, and it is the zone's Browser Cache TTL setting rewriting max-age on responses Cloudflare caches. It did NOT apply before wordle-teams-fqeq, because these documents were never in the cache to be rewritten.

WHY IT MATTERS. `max-age=0` is a deliberate value, not an oversight: it means a browser revalidates every time, so the shared copy at the edge is the only cache with a long life and the version-keyed invalidation fully controls what anyone sees after a deploy. With max-age=14400, a returning visitor's own browser may hold a marketing page for up to four hours across a deploy, and NOTHING in the deploy reaches it - not the version key, not a purge. The invalidation story that made fqeq safe stops at the edge.

The exposure is small today (marketing copy, changed rarely) and it is a real gap in a story that was otherwise complete, which is why it is written down rather than absorbed.

WORTH KNOWING BEFORE DECIDING: this is a ZONE-WIDE dashboard setting (Caching -> Configuration -> Browser Cache TTL), so it is not visible in this repository and a reader of server.ts cannot discover it. Whatever is decided, the value should be named in cache-policy.ts's comment so the next person does not spend the same hour finding it.

OPTIONS, no recommendation yet:
  1. Set Browser Cache TTL to "Respect Existing Headers", so max-age=0 survives and the code means what it says. Zone-wide, so it also affects the asset paths - check what /favicon.ico and /opengraph-image.png currently rely on first (both are `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` at origin and DO edge-HIT, per wt-ksh.8.45, so they may be relying on the same rewrite).
  2. Add a Cache Rule scoped to the static document paths that sets browser TTL to respect origin, leaving the rest of the zone alone.
  3. Accept four hours and document it. Defensible for /about, /privacy and /terms; less so for `/`, which is the apex and the one page a returning player is most likely to hit right after the relaunch email.

RELATED: wordle-teams-82zq covers the static ASSET cache policy and is the sibling question for the same zone setting.
notes:
MECHANISM CONFIRMED AND A FOURTH OPTION FOUND, 2026-09-02.

THE RULE, from Cloudflare's docs rather than inferred: the Browser Cache TTL setting overrides the origin's max-age ONLY WHEN the origin's value is LOWER than the setting, and the DEFAULT on every plan is 4 hours. 4h = 14400. So nobody configured this — it is the zone default acting on a value we deliberately set to 0.

That single rule explains every observation on this zone:
  /terms (document)          origin max-age=0,     no must-revalidate  -> rewritten to 14400
  /assets/index-*.js         origin max-age=31536000 > 14400           -> untouched
  /sw.js, /favicon.ico,
  /manifest.json             origin max-age=0, WITH must-revalidate    -> untouched

THE THIRD ROW IS THE INTERESTING ONE. Those three are edge HITs with max-age=0 and are NOT rewritten, while the documents are. The only difference in the header is `must-revalidate`, which forbids serving stale and so contradicts extending the browser's freshness window. Cloudflare honours it.

SO A FOURTH OPTION EXISTS, and it needs no dashboard access at all: add `must-revalidate` to STATIC_CACHE in v2/src/lib/cache-policy.ts. One line, in the repo, tested, and demonstrated to work by three files on this very zone.

IT IS PROBABLY NOT THE RIGHT ONE, AND THE REASON IS WORTH RECORDING. `must-revalidate` and `stale-while-revalidate` are contradictory: SWR permits serving stale while revalidating, must-revalidate forbids serving stale at all, and must-revalidate wins. Adding it would buy back the browser-cache correctness by discarding the stale-while-revalidate week at the edge — which is a larger thing than the problem it fixes. Worth measuring before dismissing, since it is unclear whether Cloudflare's edge applies must-revalidate to its own shared copy or only passes it to the browser.

REVISED OPTION ORDER:
  1. Browser Cache TTL -> "Respect Existing Headers" (zone-wide, dashboard). NOW SAFER THAN WHEN THIS WAS FILED: wordle-teams-82zq gave every asset an explicit, deliberate Cache-Control via public/_headers, so "respect existing headers" respects real decisions rather than Workers Assets defaults. Before that change it would have exposed the assets.
  2. A Cache Rule scoped to the static document paths. Surgical, but more config living outside the repo.
  3. `must-revalidate` on STATIC_CACHE. In-repo and testable, but see the SWR conflict above.
  4. Accept four hours and document it.

SEVERITY, STATED HONESTLY: a visitor only holds a stale copy if they loaded the page within the previous four hours, and these are marketing pages that change rarely. The sharp case is `/` in the hours after the relaunch email, when the most people will load it and a fix shipped that day would not reach them.
close_reason: Owner set Browser Cache TTL to 'Respect Existing Headers' on 2026-09-02. Verified: all five static documents return max-age=0 with s-maxage and SWR intact on a second request that is still an edge HIT; every asset class unchanged; signed-in still private/no-store. cache-policy.ts's comment corrected (it had become false) and runbook 3.5 added, since dashboard state cannot be asserted from the repository and the apex inherits it.

title: [flake] invites.spec.ts 'adds them to the team directly' failed once in a full run, passes in isolation
description:
OBSERVED 2026-09-02 during the e2e run for wordle-teams-fqeq.

e2e/invites.spec.ts:340 "inviting someone who already has an account adds them to the team directly" failed on the FULL suite:

  waiting for locator('[data-sonner-toast]').filter({ hasText: /Ada was added to E2E Team/ })
  Expect "toBeVisible" with timeout 5000ms
  at e2e/invites.spec.ts:389

Result that run: 1 failed, 64 passed.

NOT REPRODUCIBLE, and both directions were checked rather than one:
  - the spec alone: 3/3 passed (26.6s)
  - the full suite re-run immediately after, unchanged code: 65/65 passed (1.6m)

NOT CAUSED BY THE CHANGE IT WAS FOUND UNDER. wordle-teams-fqeq adds Cache API storage for anonymous STATIC_DOCUMENTS only; /app is not one, and the invite toast is client-side. The re-run that went green was on the same working tree, so the change was present for the passing runs too.

WHY IT IS WORTH A TICKET RATHER THAN A SHRUG. wt-ksh.8.40 (Task 17, the written checklist walk) had its blocker cleared specifically on the grounds that e2e was reliable enough to tell a regression from noise - six consecutive clean runs at the time. This is the first observed exception, so the premise is now "reliable but not perfect", and whoever runs Task 17 should know that a single red invites case is not automatically a regression. Re-run before believing it.

LIKELY SHAPE, not investigated: a 5s toast timeout on the one spec that does a cross-account invite, under full-suite load with workers pinned to 4. The toast is transient, so a slow render can miss the window entirely rather than merely arrive late. If it recurs, the cheap first move is asserting the SERVER outcome (membership) before the toast rather than after - line 392 already does exactly that check, so the ordering is the only change.

DO NOT RAISE THE PLAYWRIGHT WORKER COUNT as a fix; it is pinned at 4 deliberately.
notes:
BETTER EVIDENCE 2026-09-02, and the earlier measurement was taken against an untrustworthy server.

wordle-teams-9mjm found that every e2e run for the last two days reused a `vite dev` process started on Aug 31 which was serving stale code. The runs recorded on this issue - one failure, then a clean 65/65 re-run - were both against that process.

MEASURED AGAIN AFTER KILLING IT, on a genuinely fresh server:
  - full suite: 64 passed, 2 FAILED, both in invites.spec.ts (:120 "an invited address joins the team after completing a profile" and :340 "adds them to the team directly")
  - invites.spec.ts alone, also on a cold fresh server: 3/3 passed in 40.3s

So it is worse than one intermittent case: TWO of the three invite tests fail under full-suite load and both pass in isolation. That is a load/contention signature rather than a cold-start one, since the isolated run was also cold.

THE SHAPE THIS POINTS AT is still the toast assertion. Both failures are `expect(toastWith(...)).toBeVisible()` with a 5s timeout, and a toast is transient - under four parallel workers a slow render misses the window entirely rather than arriving late. Line 392 already asserts the SERVER outcome (membership) straight afterwards, so reordering to check that first, then the toast, would make the test assert the thing that matters and stop depending on catching a disappearing element.

DO NOT RAISE THE WORKER COUNT. Still pinned at 4 deliberately.
close_reason: Root cause was the worker count, invalidated by wordle-teams-9mjm's own fix: workers:4 was measured while reuseExistingServer shared one warm dev server and its Convex connections, and the suite has since grown to 66 tests. At 4 workers it failed 2 of 3 full runs; at 2 workers, 66/66 three times for 12s more wall clock. The expect ceiling was deliberately not raised - the config already records that a 20s ceiling hides real stalls. A globalSetup warming Vite routes was written, measured at 643ms with no effect, and deleted: the bottleneck is the Convex backend, not first-paint compiles.

title: Put SSR documents in the edge cache with the Cache API — the s-maxage header alone reaches nothing
description:
SPLIT OUT OF wt-ksh.8.45, which measured the problem and proved the Cache Rule remedy unavailable. Read 8.45's notes first; the measurement is there and is not repeated here.

THE STATE: /about and / carry `public, max-age=0, s-maxage=86400, stale-while-revalidate=604800` and have NO cf-cache-status header at all across three consecutive GETs on beta (2026-09-02). A Worker that renders its own response, with no origin subrequest, is not eligible for the CDN cache, and Cache Rules run before the Worker and cannot reach it. The Cache API (caches.default) inside src/server.ts is the only mechanism.

Until this lands, Task 3's edge win is zero and wordle-teams-jcj is only half-fixed on v2: browsers and downstream shared caches honour the header, but every anonymous marketing request still wakes the Worker.

TWO THINGS THAT MUST LAND IN THE SAME CHANGE, not after it:

1. INVALIDATION. Today `wrangler deploy` purging nothing is harmless because nothing is at the edge. The moment we put() ourselves, a deploy leaves a day of fresh plus a week of stale-while-revalidate of the OLD marketing pages, with no eviction path. This is wt-ksh.8.46 going from theoretical to live. Either the cache key carries a deploy identifier (so a new deploy simply misses and the old entries age out unread), or the deploy runs an explicit purge. The key-versioning option is preferable because it needs nothing remembered at deploy time. Note that a purge API call needs a zone token this repo does not currently hold.

2. THE SESSION CHECK MOVES TO THE WRITE AND READ SIDES. cache-policy.ts today decides what the HEADER says. It does not gate what is STORED or what is SERVED FROM STORE, because nothing was stored. Both new directions are dangerous in the way that module's comments already describe:
   - reading caches.default.match BEFORE the session check would serve one visitor's shared document to a signed-in visitor;
   - writing without the session check would store a document whose dehydrated router state embeds a bearer JWT (cache-policy.ts documents this as verified empirically, not assumed).
   The safe shape is: compute the policy first, and only consult or populate the cache when the computed policy is STATIC_CACHE. That reuses the existing tested predicate rather than restating it, which is the whole reason it is a module.

ALSO IN SCOPE: only a 200 may be stored, mirroring the existing guard in server.ts; the put must go through ctx.waitUntil so it does not delay the response; and the maintenance gate must stay in front of the cache exactly as it is in front of the policy today, for the reason its comment gives.

DONE WHEN: two consecutive GETs to a static path on beta report cf-cache-status: HIT on the second; a signed-in request to the same path still reports `private, no-store` and is neither served from nor written to the cache; a redeploy does not serve the previous build's document; and the four gates plus e2e are green.
notes:
TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ISSUE'S OWN BODY, both established before writing any code.

1. THE DONE-WHEN IS NOT SATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN. I specified "cf-cache-status: HIT on the second request". That header is NOT emitted for a Cache API hit. cf-cache-status is added by the CDN cache layer that fetch() goes through; a response the Worker returns out of caches.default is returned by the Worker, and Cloudflare does not annotate it. Cloudflare's own debugging page covers Workers Caching and pointedly does not document the header for the Cache API, and the community reports agree.

   REPLACEMENT OBSERVABLE: the Worker sets its own header. The stored copy carries `x-doc-cache: HIT` and the freshly rendered copy carries `x-doc-cache: MISS`, so two consecutive GETs to a static path report MISS then HIT. That is a stronger check than cf-cache-status anyway, because it can only be produced by our own put/match round-trip.

2. PRERENDERING THE MARKETING ROUTES TO STATIC ASSETS IS NOT AN OPTION, and it is worth writing down because it is the obvious alternative and it looks better than it is. The measurement on wt-ksh.8.45 shows Workers Assets paths DO edge-cache (/favicon.ico and /opengraph-image.png both HIT), so serving these documents as build-time assets would get a real CDN hit with no Worker code at all.

   IT BREAKS `/`. routes/index.tsx has a beforeLoad redirect that bounces a SIGNED-IN visitor to /app — it ports v1's `welcomePaths` rule and exists for a real production behaviour (an iOS PWA relaunching onto the last page rather than the manifest start_url). Assets are served ahead of the Worker, so a prerendered `/` would hand a signed-in visitor the anonymous landing page and leave the redirect to happen client-side after hydration. That is precisely the hydration-mismatch failure the maintenance gate's comment documents having already measured once on this platform: the page is visible for a frame and then replaced, which is worse than not doing it.

   So the Cache API inside server.ts stands as the only viable mechanism, for the reason this issue already gives plus this one.

3. IMPLEMENTATION NOTE FOR WHOEVER WRITES IT: `caches` is UNDEFINED under plain vitest — the test script is `vitest`, not @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers, and src/server.test.ts composes the real Worker against a mocked server entry with a no-op ctx.waitUntil. The code must tolerate `caches` being absent (guard, do not assume), and the tests should inject a fake caches global to prove the four gated behaviours: anonymous static path is stored and served; signed-in request is neither read from nor written to; non-200 is not stored; non-GET is not stored.
IMPLEMENTED AND COMMITTED 2026-09-02 (dfa6c41). Pushed. NOT YET VERIFIED ON BETA - the deploy is the one step left and it needs the owner.

WHAT LANDED:
  - src/server.ts: Cache API read/write around the existing document handler. One predicate (cachePolicyFor returning STATIC_CACHE) gates reading AND writing, so the session rule is not restated anywhere. GET only, no query string, 200 only, fails open on a throwing cache or env.
  - wrangler.jsonc: version_metadata binding. The key is `${origin}/__doc-cache/${CF_VERSION_METADATA.id}${pathname}`, which is the invalidation mechanism - a new deploy misses and the orphans age out unread. Without a version the code declines to cache at all.
  - src/server.test.ts: 10 tests against a real Map-backed fake `caches` (a spy would let everything pass against a handler that caches nothing, since `caches` is undefined under plain vitest).

VERIFIED SO FAR:
  - Four gates green: 1345 tests / 81 files, lint, typecheck, build.
  - e2e 65/65. One flake on the first run, filed as wordle-teams-jtvx; the re-run on identical code was clean and the spec passes in isolation.
  - All six mutations killed: session check, static-path gate, query guard, 200 gate, version requirement, cache read. (A seventh attempt was a NO-OP - appending a comment - and was redone as a real deletion before being counted. Recording it because that is the exact trap the handoff warns about.)
  - The version_metadata binding SURVIVES THE BUILD. `vite build` redirects wrangler to a generated dist/server/wrangler.json, so this was worth checking rather than assuming: that file contains {"binding": "CF_VERSION_METADATA"}.

BLOCKED ON THE DEPLOY. `pnpm --dir v2 deploy` fails in a non-interactive shell with "it's necessary to set a CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN environment variable"; there is no token in .env.local and no wrangler OAuth config on this machine. The owner needs to run the deploy.

THEN THIS ONE COMMAND SETTLES THE DONE-WHEN, run twice against a static path:

  curl -s -o /dev/null -D - https://beta.wordleteams.com/about | grep -ia 'x-doc-cache|cache-control'

  First request:  x-doc-cache: MISS
  Second request: x-doc-cache: HIT

REMEMBER cf-cache-status WILL STILL BE ABSENT and that is expected, not a failure - see the correction note above. x-doc-cache is the observable now.

ALSO WORTH CHECKING IN THE SAME SITTING, because it is the dangerous direction and a unit test is not a deployment:
  - a signed-in request to /about must return `private, no-store` and NO x-doc-cache header at all;
  - /app must return `private, no-store` and no x-doc-cache;
  - a third request after a REDEPLOY must report MISS again, proving the version key.
VERIFIED ON BETA 2026-09-02, after CI deployed dfa6c41 ("Deploy v2 (beta)" green: lint, typecheck, unit tests, Convex, Worker, smoke test).

THE POSITIVE CASE, three consecutive GETs to /about:
  1: x-doc-cache: MISS   (no cf-cache-status)
  2: x-doc-cache: HIT    cf-cache-status: HIT
  3: x-doc-cache: HIT    cf-cache-status: HIT
/home behaves identically (MISS then HIT), so it is not a property of one route.

THE NEGATIVE CASES, which are the ones that mattered:
  - /about WITH a session cookie -> `private, no-store` and NO x-doc-cache header at all. Neither served from nor written to the cache. This is the direction that would have published a bearer JWT, and it is correct on the live deployment rather than only in a unit test.
  - /about?utm_source=x -> the s-maxage header is still set, but NO x-doc-cache. Not cached, so a bare /about cannot be poisoned by it.
  - /app -> 307 to /login with no content-type, so it never reaches the document handler. Not cached.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN EARLIER NOTE ON THIS ISSUE. I wrote that cf-cache-status is NOT emitted for a Cache API hit, based on Cloudflare's docs and community reports. THE MEASUREMENT CONTRADICTS THAT: cf-cache-status: HIT appears on every cached response here, alongside x-doc-cache. So the original acceptance criterion was satisfiable after all and I was wrong to replace it.

x-doc-cache STAYS ANYWAY, and is still the better signal. cf-cache-status: HIT proves only that Cloudflare's cache served something; x-doc-cache proves OUR put/match round-trip is what put it there, which is the thing under test and the thing a future regression would break silently. Both now agree, which is the strongest evidence available.

ONE UNDECIDED SIDE EFFECT, FILED SEPARATELY. The cached response comes back as `public, max-age=14400, ...` although the Worker sets `max-age=0`. That is the zone's Browser Cache TTL (4h) rewriting max-age on responses Cloudflare caches, and it did not apply before because these documents were never cached. Consequence: a returning browser may hold a marketing page for up to four hours across a deploy, which the version-keyed edge invalidation does not reach. See the follow-up issue.

DONE-WHEN SATISFIED on every clause: HIT on the second request; signed-in still private/no-store and uncached; and the version key is exercised by the deploy itself, since this deployment MISSED on its first request against a cache that held the previous version's entries.
THE VERSION KEY IS PROVEN ON A REAL REDEPLOY, 2026-09-02 — the one DONE-WHEN clause the earlier measurement could not settle.

3a61ec8 was deployed to beta (after one re-run, see below). Immediately afterwards:

  GET 1: x-doc-cache: MISS
  GET 2: x-doc-cache: HIT, cf-cache-status: HIT

The cache was warm with the PREVIOUS deployment's entries and the new version missed anyway, then repopulated under its own key. That is the invalidation mechanism working end to end against a live cache, not a unit test standing in for one.

INCIDENTAL, AND WORTH RECORDING FOR THE CUTOVER RUNBOOK: the first attempt at that deploy FAILED, and not because of the change (a comment-only commit). Convex returned a 500 finalizing the push:

  Error fetching POST https://fabulous-goldfish-949.convex.cloud/api/deploy2/finish_push
  500 Internal Server Error: InternalServerError: Hit an error while pushing:
  Your request couldn't be completed. Try again later.

The build, the schema validation and "No indexes are deleted by this push" all succeeded first; it failed at finish_push. `gh run rerun --failed` was clean. So this is a transient Convex-side fault with a retry as the remedy — worth knowing before someone hits it mid-cutover and starts diagnosing their own change.
close_reason: Implemented in dfa6c41, deployed to beta by CI, and verified live: /about and /home both report MISS then HIT on x-doc-cache and cf-cache-status; a signed-in request stays private/no-store with no cache involvement; query strings and non-static paths are not cached. Task 3's edge win is now real rather than zero.

title: Brainstorm which further paid features are worth building for the relaunch
description:
A brainstorm, not a build ticket. Come back with candidates and the reasoning, not with one answer already chosen.

THE QUESTION: beyond what is already planned, what should Pro actually BE at relaunch? Today the paid tier's only real substance is the team cap - v1's rule, ported. Two paid items are already in Phase 7.5 (#2 board import from a pasted screenshot, #3 insights from global guess/answer data), and this asks whether those plus a cap are a tier worth paying for, or whether something is missing.

WHY NOW, AND WHY IT IS NOT PREMATURE. The owner is emailing every existing player at the v2 launch, including people who bounced off the app early. That is the one moment when the largest number of people will look at the product with fresh eyes, and it is also when the most people will encounter the paywall for the first time. Deciding the paid surface AFTER that moment wastes it.

WHAT A GOOD ANSWER LOOKS LIKE:
  - Candidates grouped by what they are actually selling: capacity, insight, convenience, or status.
  - For each, the honest case AGAINST it, including whether it would feel like something taken away from the free tier. A free product that gets worse is how you lose the people this email is trying to win back.
  - Which candidates are cheap given what v2 already has - Convex subscriptions, the boards data, the scoring system, push - and which need real new infrastructure.
  - An explicit "do not build" list, with reasons, so the same ideas do not get re-proposed.

READ FIRST, because these are the numbers the answer has to respect:
  - wordle-teams-456: 87% of production signups never enter a single board. A paid tier is not the problem that number describes, and no feature in here should be justified as fixing it.
  - wordle-teams-390: ~7% of visitors who reach /login complete auth.
  - wordle-teams-iht (roadmap #7) is the monetization and marketing epic and is the natural home for whatever this decides. Do not duplicate its scope; this feeds it.
  - wordle-teams-g3k: there is currently NO active paying subscriber - the one paying customer is on an unbounded comped grace period. So there is no revenue baseline to compare against, and no existing subscriber to disrupt. That cuts both ways and should be said plainly in the answer.

CONSTRAINTS: Polar is the billing surface and the two Pro products (monthly + annual) already exist. Anything requiring a third product or a usage-metered price is a materially bigger change - say so where it applies rather than costing it as equal.

Filed 2026-09-02 at the owner's request, alongside Phase 7.5.

title: The copy's droppedMembers note calls an expected outcome a real problem under --scope=all
description:
scripts/copy-from-supabase.mjs:397-401 prints, unconditionally, whenever teams.droppedMembers > 0:

  note: N team membership(s) referenced a player outside the copied scope and were dropped.
  Expected with --scope=mine. It would be a real problem with --scope=all.

OBSERVED 2026-09-02 on a real --scope=all run against beta: droppedMembers=6, so the operator was told a normal outcome is "a real problem" - at cutover, under time pressure, which is the worst possible moment to be sent chasing a non-issue.

THE NOTE PREDATES THE PHASE 4 SKIP FILTERS. Under --scope=all, readScoped reads every player, but selectCopyable (scripts/lib/copy-filters.mjs) then removes the NAMELESS ones - 151 of 543 on this data. upsertTeams resolves each team's playerLegacyIds against the players actually copied and drops what it cannot resolve, so those 151 are "outside the copied scope" by construction. The drops are therefore expected under --scope=all too, exactly as they are under --scope=mine, and for a reason the note does not know about.

The same run reported playerMembership skipped=151, which is the sibling of this and IS correctly accounted for - verify-filters.mjs narrows memberships by player and documents the 1:1 relationship. Only the teams note was left behind.

DONE WHEN: the note distinguishes drops explained by the skip filters from drops that are genuinely unexpected. The copy already knows both numbers - copyable.skippedPlayers is in scope at the call site - so the honest version can say how many of the dropped references pointed at a skipped player, and only alarm on the remainder.

A stronger version worth considering: compute the remainder and print nothing at all when it is zero, since a note that fires on every --scope=all run is a note operators learn to skip.
close_reason: The note now predicts drops from the two rules that cause them (nameless filter, scope) and phrases only the unexplained remainder as a problem. explainTeamMemberDrops is a pure function in lib/copy-filters.mjs with seven tests; three mutations killed and a fourth recorded as unexpressible rather than claimed as covered.

title: The header's pending-invite badge is not visible when testing with a real account
description:
Reported 2026-09-02: the owner cannot see the "N Invites Pending" badge anywhere in the header while testing with a real signed-in account on beta.

THREE INDEPENDENT REASONS IT CAN BE INVISIBLE. Check in this order - the first is by far the most likely, and it is not a bug:

1. THE PRO GATE. Header.tsx computes:

     const showInviteBadge = isPro === false && (pendingInvites ?? 0) > 0

   A PRO player is deliberately never shown it, because accepting an invite IS the upgrade and there is nothing to click. So if the test account is pro - or is riding the unbounded grace period, see wordle-teams-g3k - the badge is correctly hidden and the test needs a non-pro account.

   Note the gate is an explicit comparison against false rather than a plain negation, on purpose: the pro flag is undefined while its query is in flight, and negating undefined is true, so the loose form would flash the badge at a pro player on every cold load. That is the one person the badge is not for.

2. WHAT COUNTS AS PENDING. pendingInviteCountFor (convex/billing.ts) takes parkedInvitesFor(...).teams and filters to those whose playerIds do NOT already contain this player. An invite the account has ALREADY ACCEPTED therefore counts zero, and an invite parked against an address that resolved to no player may not park where expected.

3. ADDRESS NORMALISATION. invitePlayer lowercases before writing to teams.invited, and Phase 4 measured mixed-case invites in production that never matched anything. If the invite was created by hand or pasted, confirm the stored string is lowercase.

DONE WHEN: the badge is shown to render for a non-pro account holding a real parked invite, or a defect is found and fixed.

If it turns out to be reason 1, close this and consider whether the pro gate deserves a row in the 7a divergence table. It IS v1's behaviour - v1 gates the same badge on the player not being a pro member - so it is not a divergence, but it is entirely non-obvious to someone testing, which is how this issue got filed.

TESTING NOTE: e2e/invites.spec.ts drives the parked-invite flows end to end and the suite is green, so the mechanism works. This is about one real account's state rather than a broken code path.

NO ADDRESSES IN THIS ISSUE, deliberately - this repository is public and .beads/issues.jsonl is tracked.
notes:
SETTLED 2026-09-02 AGAINST THE OWNER'S OWN TEST. NOT A DEFECT, and not reason 1 either — the handoff's prediction that this was the comped-pro account was WRONG, and the owner disproved it directly.

NEW EVIDENCE FROM THE OWNER: they tested with a genuinely non-pro account, reached the billing portal from the Upgrade button with it (so `isPro === false` is confirmed by the Upgrade CTA rendering at all — that button is gated on the same flag), invited a player, and still saw no badge.

THE ANSWER IS A FOURTH REASON THIS ISSUE DOES NOT LIST, and it is the one that actually applies:

THE BADGE IS FOR THE INVITEE, NEVER THE INVITER. parkedInvitesFor (convex/billing.ts:199) resolves the CALLER'S OWN address — `matchKey(player.email)` off their own player row — and finds teams whose `invited` array holds THAT. So it counts invites the signed-in player has RECEIVED. Sending one changes the sender's count by exactly zero, by construction. The owner was watching their own header after inviting someone else, which can never move.

AND FOR THE RECIPIENT, MOST INVITES PARK NOTHING AT ALL. teams.ts's invitePlayerFor has three outcomes for an address that already has a player row:
  - already on the team            -> `already_member`, writes nothing
  - non-pro AND already on FREE_TEAM_LIMIT teams -> `parked_at_cap`, address goes into `teams.invited`
  - anything else                  -> `added`: ONE PATCH, TWO FIELDS, straight onto playerIds, and the address is filtered OUT of `invited` in the same write
The third is the common case, and it is why nothing was pending for anyone: an under-cap invitee with an account is simply made a member immediately. There is correctly nothing to show a badge about. `teams.invited` only ever holds an address with NO account, one parked at the cap, or one copied from v1.

TWO EXACT REPRODUCTIONS, either of which will show it:

  A. Take a non-pro account that is ALREADY ON TWO TEAMS (FREE_TEAM_LIMIT). From a different account, invite it to a THIRD team — invitePlayerFor returns `parked_at_cap`. Sign in AS THAT ACCOUNT. The header shows "1 Invite Pending".

  B. Invite a brand-new address with no account to THREE teams, then sign up at that address. completeProfileFor claims at most FREE_TEAM_LIMIT of them and leaves the surplus parked (documented in upgradeTeamInvitesFor's note, and measured by players.test.ts's "the invites the cap held back are released by the upgrade path"). Signing in shows "1 Invite Pending".

The render site itself is fine: Header.tsx:206 puts the Badge in the header's right-hand cluster unconditionally on `showInviteBadge`, not behind a menu, so there is nothing hiding it once the count is non-zero.

WHAT THIS SUGGESTS IS WORTH DOING, none of it a fix to the badge:
  - The issue's DONE-WHEN is satisfiable by repro A without any code change. Recommend confirming A on beta, then closing.
  - The pro gate is v1's behaviour and is NOT a 7a divergence, as this issue already says. Still true.
  - THE REAL FINDING IS DISCOVERABILITY, and it is a candidate for Phase 7.5 rather than here: the only feedback the INVITER gets that an invite was parked rather than accepted is invitePlayerFor's `parked_at_cap` status. Whether the UI says anything useful with it is worth a look during Task 17's walk, because "I invited someone and nothing visibly happened" is exactly what the owner just experienced, and a returning player in the relaunch will experience it the same way.
CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS NOTE'S LAST BULLET, checked rather than left as a guess.

I wrote that the only feedback the inviter gets about a parked invite is the raw `parked_at_cap` status and suggested Task 17 look at whether the UI says anything useful with it. THAT IS WRONG. invite-player-dialog.tsx:108 already handles it, deliberately and well:

  toast.info(`<address> is already on the maximum number of teams for a free
             account. They'll join <team> automatically if they upgrade.`)

Chosen as `info` rather than `success` on purpose — the file's comment says calling it a success is "the exact lie divergence 9 exists to stop" — and it prints the server-normalised address rather than the typed one, because that is the string the owner will see in their pending list. All five outcomes are handled, with a `never` assignment forcing a message to exist for each. There is no discoverability gap here and nothing for Phase 7.5 to pick up.

WHICH MAKES THE OWNER'S REPORT FULLY EXPLAINED. Whatever the invitee's state, the owner DID get a toast naming the outcome — "X was added to TEAM" if the invitee had an account and was under the cap, "Invite sent to X" if they had no account. The only thing that did not appear is the badge, and the badge was never going to: it counts what the SIGNED-IN player has been invited to, and the owner was the one doing the inviting.

RECOMMENDATION UNCHANGED: run repro A on beta to satisfy the DONE-WHEN, then close. No code change.
STILL NOT VISIBLE FOR THE OWNER 2026-09-02, on a real phone, with a non-pro account. Screenshot supplied. TWO CANDIDATE CAUSES REMAIN AND THEY NEED DIFFERENT FIXES.

WHAT THE SCREENSHOT ESTABLISHES:
  - The account is non-pro. The Upgrade sparkle renders in the header, and that button is gated on the SAME `isPro === false` the badge is. So reason 1 in this issue's description is now definitively excluded.
  - The account IS A MEMBER of the team it was invited to ("Test Invite Bad...", visible as a player row in the scores table). pendingInviteCountFor EXCLUDES teams the player is already on, so that invite contributes 0 whether or not the address is still parked.

CANDIDATE A - THE COUNT IS GENUINELY 0. The likely one. For an address to park at all, invitePlayerFor needs the invitee to be at FREE_TEAM_LIMIT (2 teams) already, or to have no account yet. An invitee on 0 or 1 teams is added to the roster directly and nothing is parked. If this account holds fewer than 2 teams, no invite it receives can ever park, so the badge cannot appear no matter how many are sent.

CANDIDATE B - THE BADGE RENDERS BUT DOES NOT FIT. NOT YET TESTED, and it has apparently never been seen on a phone. Header.tsx puts the badge in the right-hand cluster with `whitespace-nowrap`, and the wordmark beside it is `flex-shrink-0` at text-2xl. On a ~390px viewport the wordmark, the badge ("1 Invite Pending" plus a Mails icon), the Upgrade button, the hamburger and the avatar are competing for the width, and neither of the two largest items can shrink or wrap. Rough arithmetic says it overflows; that is an ESTIMATE from the class names, not a measurement.

THE ONE-STEP DISCRIMINATOR: load beta on a DESKTOP browser with the same account.
  - badge appears on desktop, not on the phone  -> Candidate B, a real layout defect, and the fix belongs in Header.tsx (icon-only below `sm`, the way the Upgrade button already handles exactly this).
  - badge appears on neither                     -> Candidate A, the count is 0, and the data needs setting up per repro A above.

TO SETTLE CANDIDATE A WITH DATA RATHER THAN INFERENCE, v2/probe-invites.mjs (untracked scratch file) prints every team's `invited` array and what myPendingInviteCount would return for each player, with addresses masked:

  cd v2 && node --env-file=.env.local probe-invites.mjs

I could not run it myself - the auto-mode classifier blocks reading CONVEX_MIGRATION_KEY out of .env.local, which is reasonable and was not worked around.
SETTLED WITH DATA 2026-09-02. NOT A DEFECT. The owner ran the probe against beta and the answer is unambiguous.

THE OWNER'S OWN ROW: parked on 0 teams. The team under test: members=1, with ONE address parked in `invited` - the address the invite was SENT to, which has no account in beta.

So the invite parked exactly as designed, under the RECIPIENT's address. parkedInvitesFor resolves the CALLER's own email, so the sender's count is 0 by construction and no amount of inviting will move it. The recipient has no account to sign in with, so nobody was ever going to see a badge from this setup. Candidate A confirmed.

CANDIDATE B (the badge renders but overflows on a narrow header) IS DISPROVEN, not merely unconfirmed: the owner also checked a desktop browser and saw nothing there either. With a count of 0 there is nothing to render at any width, so the layout question never arose. It remains UNTESTED rather than known-good - no one has yet seen this badge on a real viewport - and that is worth one glance during wt-ksh.8.40's walk, since Header.tsx gives the badge `whitespace-nowrap` beside a `flex-shrink-0` wordmark and the Upgrade button next to it already goes icon-only below `sm`.

THE INVITER-SIDE SURFACE ALREADY EXISTS and is probably what was being looked for: current-team-card.tsx:277 lists pending invites to the team owner. The header badge is the INVITEE's view; the team card is the inviter's.

RECIPE THAT WILL ACTUALLY SHOW IT, given the two accounts in play:
  1. Sign up at the invited address. It claims the parked invite and joins the team under test (that team goes to 2 members).
  2. Get the first account to exactly FREE_TEAM_LIMIT teams.
  3. From the new account, create a third team and invite the first account to it. It is at the cap, so invitePlayerFor returns parked_at_cap and shows the "already on the maximum number of teams for a free account" toast.
  4. Sign in as the first account. The header shows "1 Invite Pending".

THE FINDING THAT OUTLASTS THIS TICKET. Of 393 players on beta, only SEVEN have any address parked at all - and that is an UPPER BOUND, because parityProbe returns playerCount rather than playerIds, so the probe could not apply pendingInviteCountFor's "already a member" exclusion. Several of those seven are copied v1 rows where the person is listed in BOTH playerIds and invited, which upgradeTeamInvitesFor's note says is exactly what the copy brings over, so the true number is lower still.

The badge is an upgrade driver that almost nobody will ever see, and constructing the state took the person who built it three attempts and a database query. That is not a defect - v1 gates it identically, and the narrowness is deliberate, since accepting an invite IS the upgrade. It is worth raising against wordle-teams-iht (monetization, Phase 7.5), because this is one of the very few places the free-tier cap ever speaks to a user, and the relaunch is when the most people will meet that cap for the first time.

LEFT OPEN pending the owner running the recipe above, since the DONE-WHEN asks for the badge to be SHOWN to render rather than merely explained.
CLOSED 2026-09-03 BY OBSERVING IT RENDER, which is what this issue's DONE-WHEN actually asked for.

The badge appeared during Phase 5's sandbox pass, in exactly the state the recipe on this issue described: the account was non-pro and already on FREE_TEAM_LIMIT teams (having just been downgraded by subscription.revoked), a second account invited it to a third team, the inviter saw the "already on the maximum number of teams for a free account" toast, and the capped account's header showed "1 Invite Pending".

Re-subscribing then released the parked invite automatically and the badge cleared, which exercises the other end of the same mechanism.

SO IT WAS NEVER A DEFECT, and the two earlier notes on this issue stand: the badge is the INVITEE's view, not the inviter's, and most invites park nothing at all because an under-cap invitee with an account is added to the roster immediately. What was missing was never code — it was an account in the one state that makes the badge meaningful, and constructing that state turned out to need a full downgrade.

WORTH KEEPING FOR wordle-teams-iht: this is now a measured statement rather than an estimate. Reaching the badge required a paid subscription, a revocation, five teams and a second account. Of 393 players on beta, seven have any address parked at all. It is an upgrade prompt that almost nobody will ever see.
close_reason: Shown to render, which is what the DONE-WHEN asked. Appeared during Phase 5's sandbox pass on a non-pro account at the 2-team cap invited to a third team, and cleared automatically when re-subscribing released the parked invite. Not a defect - the badge is the invitee's view and most invites park nothing, both established earlier; what was missing was an account in the state that makes it meaningful.

title: Step back on the dashboard cards: brainstorm the UI/UX against modern practice
description:
Not a bug list and not a polish pass over what is there. The ask is to STOP and reconsider the dashboard's card surface as a whole, from a current UX-best-practice lens, and come back with OPTIONS rather than a single opinion.

WHAT TO LOOK AT: the team card / scores table / TeamBoards panel grouping, the information hierarchy inside a card, what a player is actually trying to answer when they open the dashboard (did I play today, how did I do, how am I doing against the team, who has not entered yet), and whether the current carving serves that or just mirrors v1's.

WHAT A GOOD ANSWER LOOKS LIKE: two or three genuinely different directions with the tradeoff named for each - not one recommendation dressed up as a survey. Include what each costs to build against what already exists, and say plainly which parts of the current design are already right, so the brainstorm does not churn them.

CONSTRAINTS THAT ARE NOT UP FOR GRABS: docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md is the token and component vocabulary, and its 7a section records forty-three deliberate divergences from v1 - read it first so a proposal does not 'fix' something that was decided on purpose. Parity with v1 is NOT a constraint here; this is explicit permission to diverge, which means anything adopted becomes a new 7a row.

Filed 2026-09-02 at the owner's request, after a round of UI/UX polish on feat/v2-replatform.

title: Wide-screen layout, board-entry ring, and scroll reset on month navigation
description:
Four owner-reported items, all measured before planning.

## 1. MONTH NAVIGATION FROM TEAM BOARDS SCROLLS TO THE TOP (mobile)

Picking a day in another month from the Team Boards picker — or stepping across
a month boundary with the arrows — moves `?month=`, and the router resets scroll
on navigation. On a phone the panel is far down the page, so the viewer is
thrown to the top and has to scroll back to see the board they asked for.

FIX: `resetScroll: false` on that one navigate call. @tanstack/router-core
1.171.15 supports it (link.d.ts:62).

NOT applied to the TeamPicker/MonthPicker navigations at the top of the grid:
those controls are only usable when already scrolled to them, so the default is
harmless there and changing it is unrequested.

## 2. THE BOARD-ENTRY FOCUS RING IS TOO BIG AND IS CLIPPED

board-input.tsx:121 puts `focus:ring-2 focus:ring-offset-4` on a `w-full`
contentEditable div that merely CENTRES the board inside it. So the ring is
drawn around the full width of the sheet rather than around the board, and
board-entry/form.tsx:195's `overflow-y-auto` scroll container clips it at both
edges — overflow-y also computes overflow-x to auto, the same CSS rule
wordle-teams-iv09 turned on.

FIX: make the focusable element hug the board (`w-fit mx-auto`) instead of
spanning the row. The ring then sits just outside the tiles, is visible all the
way round, and has slack inside the scroll container.

## 3. THE DASHBOARD IS UNCAPPED WHILE THE HEADER AND FOOTER ARE NOT

MEASURED at 1920x1080: header nav and footer are 1080px wide, centred at
420-1500. `<main>` on /app is 0-1920 and its content spans 48-1872. So the
chrome sits in a narrow strip while the dashboard sprawls 744px wider than it.

Owner's decision 2026-09-02: raise the shared cap to 1440px and apply it to the
body of every page, not just the header, footer and marketing routes.

## 4. THE SCORES TABLE AND TEAM BOARDS CARD FALL SHORT ON THE RIGHT

Both carry `max-w-[96vw]`. Every sibling is bounded by the grid cell instead, so
above about 2400px viewport width the two disagree. MEASURED:

  1920   picker row right 1872   frame right 1872   aligned
  2560   picker row right 2512   frame right 2506   6px short
  3440   picker row right 3392   frame right 3350   42px short

The owner reported the scores table; the Team Boards card has the identical bug
and is fixed with it.

FIX: `max-w-full` — bounded by the parent, which is what every sibling already
uses. 96vw was a belt against the table widening the page, and the grid's own
`grid-cols-1` (routes/app.tsx's load-bearing note) is what actually prevents
that.

## OUT OF SCOPE

- The horizontal scroll INSIDE the scores table, which is intended.
- Any change to the card grid's column counts.

## DONE WHEN

- Crossing a month from the Team Boards picker or arrows leaves scroll where it
  was.
- The board-entry ring is fully visible and hugs the board.
- Header, footer and dashboard all stop at the same 1440px, at every width.
- The scores table and Team Boards card align with the Board Entry button and
  the picker row at 1920, 2560 and 3440.
close_reason: Page cap 1440 via --page-max token; 96vw removed; board-entry ring hugs the board; resetScroll:false verified at the mechanism.

title: Team Boards day arrows stop at the month boundary
description:
Follow-up to wordle-teams-5vv3, owner-approved 2026-09-02.

The Previous/Next day arrows step through `navigableDays`, which is the LOADED month, so they disable at its edges — at July 1st "Previous day" is dead while the picker beside it happily offers June 30th. Same friction the picker fix removed, through the other control.

SCOPE
- The arrows cross into an adjacent month when the current one is exhausted, moving `?month=` the same way the picker does.
- Bounded by the same window: `months`, i.e. monthOptions' output. An arrow must not reach a month the dropdown does not offer.
- Previous from the first day lands on the LAST navigable day of the earlier month; Next from the last day lands on the FIRST navigable day of the later one.
- Disabled only when there is genuinely nowhere left to go.

OUT OF SCOPE
- The picker's own bounds, done in wordle-teams-5vv3.
- The pro month expansion.

DONE WHEN
- At the first day of a month, Previous day moves to the previous month's last playable day and the dropdown follows.
- At the last day, Next day moves forward the same way, never past today.
- Both are disabled at the ends of the window and nowhere else.
- The stepping logic is a pure function with its own tests, like navigableDays and resolveDay beside it.
close_reason: Arrows cross months via a pure stepDay, bounded by the same monthOptions window as the picker.

title: [bug] Team Boards picker opens on today's month and cannot reach a previous one
description:
Owner-reported, two related complaints about the Team Boards day picker.

## 1. THE CALENDAR OPENS ON TODAY'S MONTH, WHATEVER DAY IS SELECTED

Select July in the month dropdown and the boards panel correctly shows a July
day — resolveDay already re-defaults to the last navigable day of the selected
month — but OPENING the picker shows September, and the viewer has to page back
two months to reach the day they are already looking at.

MEASURED CAUSE, in react-day-picker 10:

  node_modules/react-day-picker/dist/esm/helpers/getInitialMonth.js:14
    let initialMonth = month || defaultMonth || today;

`selected` is NOT consulted. src/components/date-picker.tsx passes neither
`month` nor `defaultMonth`, so the calendar always opens on today's month.

THIS IS NOT ONLY A TEAM BOARDS BUG. The same component is board entry's picker,
so editing a board for an older day opens the calendar on today there too. One
fix in date-picker.tsx covers both surfaces.

## 2. THE PICKER CANNOT REACH A PREVIOUS MONTH

team-boards.tsx bounds the picker to the selected month with minDay/maxDay. The
reason is real and is written down in date-picker.tsx: getTeamMonth loads ONE
month, so a day outside it has no boards to show. But the effect is that
viewing an earlier day means going up to the month dropdown first, which the
owner calls unintuitive — and board entry's picker, the same component, has no
such restriction.

## DECISION (owner, 2026-09-02)

The picker reaches exactly the months the MONTH DROPDOWN offers — today three,
and whatever the pro expansion later widens monthOptions to. Picking a day in
another month moves the dropdown with it, by navigating ?month=.

RULED OUT: unbounded back-navigation like board entry's. v2 has no pro month
gate yet — monthOptions returns three months for everyone — so unbounded would
hand every player unlimited history now and the pro expansion would later have
to take it away. Tying the picker to monthOptions means both widen together
when that lands, and the two controls can never disagree.

RULED OUT: bounding by the team's earliest score. Honest, but that date is not
loaded on the dashboard and would need a new query, and it has the same effect
on the unbuilt pro gate as unbounded.

## SCOPE

- date-picker.tsx: open on the selected day's month (defaultMonth), falling
  back sensibly when nothing is selected.
- team-boards.tsx: widen minDay to the first day of the earliest month the
  dropdown offers; drop the maxDay clamp so the existing no-future-days rule is
  the only upper bound; call back to the parent when a picked day leaves the
  current month.
- app.tsx: pass the month window down, and navigate ?month= on that callback.

## EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE

- The Previous/Next DAY ARROWS still stop at the month boundary. They step
  through `navigableDays`, which is the loaded month, and making them cross
  months is a second navigation path with its own questions. Worth raising
  separately; not silently absorbed here.
- The pro month expansion itself.
- Board entry's own bounds, which are already unrestricted and correct.

## DONE WHEN

- Selecting July in the dropdown and opening the boards picker shows JULY.
- A day in an earlier month can be picked from the boards picker, and doing so
  moves the month dropdown to match and shows that day's boards.
- The picker offers no month the dropdown does not.
- Board entry's picker opens on the day being edited, not on today.
close_reason: defaultMonth added; picker bounded to monthOptions with an onMonthChange navigation. p5mw was the defaultMonth half, open since the Task 10 review.

title: Dashboard blanks on team/month switch: no Suspense boundaries, no skeletons
description:
Owner-reported: switching team or month blanks most of the dashboard while the
new data loads. v1 had pulsing skeletons for this; v2 has none.

## MEASURED CAUSE

Three components on the dashboard call useSuspenseQuery on the SAME query,
api.scores.getTeamMonth, keyed by (teamId, month):

  src/components/scores-table.tsx:36
  src/components/teams/team-boards.tsx:50
  src/components/scoring-system-card.tsx:53

Changing team or month changes that key, so all three suspend at once. There is
NO Suspense boundary anywhere on the dashboard, and src/router.tsx sets no
defaultPendingComponent either, so the suspension bubbles past the route and
the whole grid unmounts.

The route's own loader does NOT re-run on that change — it prefetches
getMyTeams, amIPro and getMyPlayerId, none of which depend on team or month —
so this is purely component-level suspension, not a navigation.

## WHAT v1 DID

  src/app/me/page.tsx:60      <Suspense fallback={<SkeletonTable classes='md:col-span-3'/>}>
  src/components/app-grid-items/scores-table/skeleton-table.tsx
  src/components/app-grid-items/scores-table/skeleton-rows.tsx
  src/app/me/loading.tsx      route-level skeleton mirroring the whole grid

Note v1 wrapped ONLY the scores table. Its Team Boards panel and Scoring System
card blanked on a switch too — the same defect, just less noticeable. Owner's
decision 2026-09-02: cover all three, and add the full-grid skeleton for the
cold load as well.

## SCOPE

1. ScoresTableSkeleton — the real table's shape: sticky first and last columns,
   one column per day of the SELECTED month, a few body rows.
2. TeamBoardsSkeleton — the card, its title and day-nav row, and a block the
   height of a slide.
3. ScoringSystemCardSkeleton — the card, title, and one row per SYSTEM_FIELDS
   entry.
4. DashboardSkeleton — the full grid, wired as the /app route's
   pendingComponent, mirroring v1's me/loading.tsx.
5. A Suspense boundary around each of the three suspending components in
   src/routes/app.tsx, with the matching skeleton as its fallback.

## OUT OF SCOPE

- Keeping the previous team's data on screen while loading (placeholderData /
  keepPreviousData). It is a real alternative and it is NOT what was asked for;
  it also shows one month's numbers under another month's label.
- CurrentTeamCard and MyTeamsCard, which use plain useQuery and do not suspend.
- Changing any of the three components' own queries or loading logic.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Skeletons must carry the SAME grid classes as the components they replace
  (md:col-span-3, md:row-span-3) or the layout jumps on every switch, which is
  the problem restated.
- Day-column count comes from daysOfMonth(month), not v1's hardcoded 30.
- Scoring row count comes from SYSTEM_FIELDS so it cannot drift from the card.
- Reuse the existing ui/skeleton.tsx (animate-pulse bg-muted). Do not add a
  second pulse implementation.

## DONE WHEN

- Switching team or month leaves the grid in place, with pulsing placeholders
  where the three panels are, and no layout shift.
- A cold client-side navigation to /app shows the full-grid skeleton.
- A test pins that each of the three has a Suspense boundary with the right
  fallback, since none of this is visible to tsc, lint or the build.
close_reason: Suspense boundaries + skeletons for all three getTeamMonth panels, plus pendingComponent. 18 blank frames -> 0, verified by rAF sampler against the pre-fix file.

title: [bug] Menu items that are links render green; avatar initials touch the circle
description:
Two things the owner spotted on beta after wordle-teams-lyab shipped.

## 1. FOUR MENU ITEMS RENDER GREEN, THE OTHER FIVE DO NOT

Dashboard, Home, About and Feedback are green; Notifications, Theme, Billing,
Install Guide and Log out are not. The split is not arbitrary and not a theme
bug: those four are exactly the items that are ANCHORS.

MEASURED CAUSE. src/styles.css:282-286 sets, in the base layer:

    a { color: var(--accent-solid); ... }

which is right for prose. But a DropdownMenuItem written as
`<DropdownMenuItem asChild><Link/></DropdownMenuItem>` renders a real <a> —
Radix's asChild merges its props onto the child rather than wrapping it — so a
NAVIGATION CONTROL picks up the CONTENT link colour. The lucide icons go green
with the text because they are stroke="currentColor".

This is a general trap rather than a one-off: any anchor used as a UI control
in this app inherits the prose link colour. It will recur.

FIX AT THE BASE RULE, NOT THE CALL SITE, and use :where() to do it:

    a:where(:not([role])) { color: var(--accent-solid); ... }

A control anchor carries a widget role (role="menuitem" here) and is excluded;
a prose link has no role and is unaffected.

:where() IS LOAD-BEARING AND NOT A STYLE PREFERENCE. A bare
`a:not([role])` is specificity (0,1,1), which would start BEATING single-class
Tailwind utilities at (0,1,0) — so any anchor styled with a text-colour
utility would silently lose it, the wordmark's gradient among the things in
range. :where() contributes zero, keeping the whole selector at (0,0,1) exactly
as the current rule is.

## 2. THE AVATAR'S INITIALS TOUCH THE CIRCLE

src/components/app-menu.tsx renders `<Avatar className="h-8 w-8">` — 32px —
and the AvatarFallback sets NO font size, so the initials inherit the ambient
16px. Two 16px capitals in a 32px circle leaves almost no ring of space, which
is what the owner is seeing.
