Give the fallback an explicit smaller size. This lands before
wordle-teams-x3m9 puts a rotating gradient ring around the same circle, where
crowded letters would read worse still.

## DONE WHEN

- No item in the app bar menu renders in the accent colour; all nine share one
  colour, icons included.
- Prose links (/about, /privacy, /terms, the footer) are STILL green.
- The wordmark still renders its gradient.
- The avatar's initials have visible space between them and the circle's edge.
- A test covers the anchor-vs-div colour split, since it is invisible to tsc,
  lint and the build, and the four green items shipped through all of them.
close_reason: Base anchor rule scoped with :where(:not([role])); avatar initials at text-xs. Mutation-verified test in styles.test.ts. 1a2e9b8

title: [bug] Team boards carousel captures vertical drags and traps page scroll
description:
Owner-reported: dragging vertically inside the team boards carousel scrolls the
carousel instead of the page, so a mistouch in that area traps the page scroll.

## TWO COMPOUNDING CAUSES, BOTH IN src/components/teams/team-boards.tsx

1. THE TRACK IS A VERTICAL SCROLL CONTAINER BY ACCIDENT (line 170).
   The className sets overflow-x-auto and nothing for the y axis. Per the CSS
   overflow spec, when one axis is not visible the other computes from visible
   to AUTO - so overflow-y is auto, not visible, and the track will happily
   scroll vertically.

2. EVERY SLIDE OVERFLOWS ITS OWN HEIGHT BY 32px, ON EVERY SCREEN SIZE
   (lines 181-183). The slide is h-[450px]. Inside it:
     a name row      mb-2 h-[24px]   ->  24 + 8 margin
     the board wrap  flex h-full     ->  450, because h-full resolves against
                                         the 450px slide, NOT against what is
                                         left after the name row
   Total content 482px in a 450px box. So there is always something to scroll,
   independent of viewport or board contents.

Cause 2 creates the overflow and cause 1 lets the touch consume it. Fix both:
the height maths is the actual defect, and the explicit overflow-y is the belt
that stops it recurring.

## DO NOT REACH FOR touch-action: pan-x

It looks like the obvious fix and it is wrong. touch-action is intersected from
the hit-test element up through its ancestors, so pan-x on the track disables
VERTICAL panning for the ancestors too - the page would stop scrolling from
inside that region, which is the exact bug being fixed, arrived at from the
other direction.

## KEEP INTACT

The horizontal carousel is native scroll plus snap-x snap-mandatory, and the
onScroll handler derives the slide index from scrollLeft / clientWidth, which
is exact only because each slide is basis-full. None of that should change.

## DONE WHEN

- A vertical drag starting anywhere inside the carousel scrolls the page.
- Horizontal swipe, snapping and the arrow buttons all still work.
- No slide overflows its own box.
- Verified on a touch-emulating phone viewport, not a narrow desktop window.
close_reason: Slide overflow (measured 32px) and the accidental y-axis scroll container both fixed; pinned in hook test + browser measurement.

title: Billing portal is unreachable for comped and never-subscribed players
description:
Owner-reported: the Billing button reports no billing account for the owner's
comped account. Expected: a comped player should still have a billing customer
and reach the portal.

## CAUSE - NOT A BUG IN THE BUTTON

The comp is a membershipStatus of 'pro' carried across by convex/migrate.ts
from Supabase. That account never went through checkout, so Polar holds NO
customer with a matching externalCustomerId. getCustomerPortalUrl tries each
candidate from externalIdsFor, every one misses, lookupPortal exhausts the list
and correctly returns { url: null, reason: 'no-customer' }, and the UI shows the
honest info toast. Everything behaves as designed; the design has a gap.

The same gap hits every never-subscribed player, not just comped ones -
Header.tsx made Billing unconditional for any authenticated player precisely so
the no-customer branch could answer them.

## FIX

When lookupPortal exhausts every identity with no-customer, CREATE the Polar
customer keyed to externalId = playerId, using the email and name already
assembled by checkoutIdentity, then open a portal session against it.

## CONSTRAINTS THIS MUST RESPECT

- ONLY the no-customer exhaustion path may create. A 500 or a rejected
  credential must still stop and report itself. lookupPortal's doc comment is
  explicit that turning an outage into "you have no subscription" is the exact
  lie the multi-way result exists to prevent - do not let creation-on-miss
  become a way to relaunder a failure into a success.
- Creation is triggered by an explicit Billing click, never speculatively.
- Still no stored Polar customer id. The v2 schema comment at line 237 says not
  to reintroduce the columns v1 dropped; resolution stays by externalCustomerId.
- A creation that races another creation for the same externalId must not
  surface as an error. Treat an already-exists response as a hit and continue.
- polarEnvProblem() is checked before any of this, as it is today.

## OPEN, DECIDE DURING IMPLEMENTATION

Whether PortalResult gains a branch for "customer created, portal is empty" so
the UI can say something more useful than dropping the player into a portal
with no invoices. Not required for the acceptance criteria.

## DONE WHEN

- The owner's comped account opens a real Polar portal from the header.
- A never-subscribed account does too.
- An outage or a bad credential still reports as itself, and this is covered by
  a test - convex/polar.ts's existing tests inject the attempt, so the
  sequencing is testable without a network.
close_reason: ensurePortal creates the Polar customer after an exhausted no-customer sweep; outage/credential guard moved inside the tested function after a mutation check found it unpinned.

title: [bug] Five dead Tailwind-v3 CSS-var utilities in select, dropdown and popover
description:
Six Tailwind-v3-era CSS-variable utilities outside calendar.tsx compile to
invalid CSS under Tailwind v4 and are silently dropped. Found while diagnosing
the date picker; same class of bug, different components.

In Tailwind v3, an arbitrary value of the form h-[--foo] was interpreted as
var(--foo). In v4 it is NOT: it emits the literal token, so the declaration is
invalid and every browser discards it. v4 spells it h-(--foo) or h-[var(--foo)].

## THE DEAD ONES

  src/components/ui/select.tsx:78
    max-h-[--radix-select-content-available-height]
    origin-[--radix-select-content-transform-origin]

  src/components/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx:50
    origin-[--radix-dropdown-menu-content-transform-origin]

  src/components/ui/dropdown-menu.tsx:68
    origin-[--radix-dropdown-menu-content-transform-origin]

  src/components/ui/popover.tsx:20
    origin-[--radix-popover-content-transform-origin]

## OBSERVABLE CONSEQUENCES

- The select, dropdown and popover open/close zoom animations scale from the
  element's default origin rather than from the side Radix positioned them on.
  Cosmetic but wrong on every menu in the app.
- The select content has NO max-height, so a long select can run past the
  bottom of the viewport instead of scrolling inside itself. Not cosmetic.

## THE FILE PROVES THE PATTERN IS AN OVERSIGHT

dropdown-menu.tsx:68 already uses the CORRECT form for its sibling declaration:
max-h-[var(--radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-height)]. So one line in the
same className string is right and the one next to it is wrong.

## WORTH DOING WHILE HERE

Add a gate. src/styles.test.ts already asserts against compiled CSS for the
contrast tokens; an assertion that no compiled rule contains a property value
starting with two dashes would catch the next one of these at test time instead
of at a screenshot. That is the durable half of this issue.

## DONE WHEN

- All six use the v4 spelling.
- The select has a working max-height.
- A test fails if a dead CSS-variable utility is reintroduced.
notes: CORRECTION: five, not six. The description counted dropdown-menu.tsx:68's max-h-[var(--radix-dropdown-menu-content-available-height)] as an offender; it is the CORRECT v4 spelling and was always fine — which is precisely the tell that the broken ones beside it were an oversight. The five real ones: select.tsx (max-height + transform-origin), dropdown-menu.tsx x2 (transform-origin), popover.tsx (transform-origin).
close_reason: 5 utilities fixed; source-scan gate added to styles.test.ts. Compiled CSS now has 0 dead declarations.

title: [bug] Social profile image never populates unless the provider created the account
description:
The header avatar falls back to initials for an account that signs in with
GitHub or Discord. Owner-reported.

## MEASURED CAUSE

better-auth writes the user's image ONLY when it creates the user.

  node_modules/better-auth/dist/oauth2/link-account.mjs:99
    createOAuthUser({ name, image, ... })   <- new user, image written

  node_modules/better-auth/dist/oauth2/link-account.mjs:67-77
    if (overrideUserInfo) { updateUser(..., { name, image, ... }) }
                                           <- existing user, GATED

overrideUserInfo comes from the provider option overrideUserInfoOnSignIn:

  node_modules/better-auth/dist/api/routes/callback.mjs:151
    overrideUserInfo: provider.options?.overrideUserInfoOnSignIn

convex/auth.ts never sets it, so it is undefined and the update never runs.

CONSEQUENCE: any account CREATED by email OTP - which is the whole migration
path, since migrate.ts creates players rows keyed by email and never creates
Better Auth users - keeps image: null permanently, no matter how many social
providers it later links. The screenshot showing initials rather than a broken
image icon is consistent: user?.image is falsy, so AvatarImage never renders.

## FIX

Set overrideUserInfoOnSignIn: true per provider in the PROVIDER_OPTIONS map in
convex/auth.ts, which already exists for exactly this kind of per-provider
option.

## TWO THINGS TO FLAG IN THE IMPLEMENTATION, NOT DISCOVER LATER

1. IT IS WIDER THAN THE IMAGE. The same branch also rewrites name and email on
   every social sign-in. Low risk here - initials come from the players row and
   not from Better Auth's name (see lib/initials.ts), and account linking
   already requires a verified email match on both sides - but it should be
   stated in the code comment rather than left as a surprise.

2. MICROSOFT IS DIFFERENT AND MUST NOT BE "FIXED". convex/auth.ts deliberately
   drops the User.Read scope, and its comment states that scope "buys exactly
   one thing: the profile photo", dropped because it triggers an admin-consent
   gate for the 15 work/school users. Microsoft users legitimately have no
   image. Do not add the scope back.

## DONE WHEN

- An account created by OTP that later signs in with GitHub or Discord shows
  the provider's avatar in the header.
- Microsoft's scope list is unchanged.
- Existing null-image accounts are NOT backfilled; the fix takes effect on the
  next social sign-in and that is accepted.
close_reason: overrideUserInfoOnSignIn defaulted on, microsoft opted out; auth.ts gains its first tests (8).

title: Header: avatar moves right of the menu and regains the brand ring
description:
Two changes to the avatar, both owner-requested.

## POSITION

The avatar moves to the RIGHT of the hamburger. Today user-menu.tsx renders
them avatar-then-trigger inside one flex row; the order flips.

## THE RING

v1 wraps the avatar in a spinning gradient ring and v2 dropped it. Port it:

  v1 src/components/app-bar/user-dropdown.tsx:119
  an absolutely positioned -inset-0.5 rounded-full div behind the avatar,
  animate-spin-super-slow, bg-gradient-to-r from green through green to yellow

  v1 tailwind.config.ts:100
  'spin-super-slow': 'spin 5s linear infinite'

TWO DEVIATIONS FROM v1, BOTH DELIBERATE:

1. TOKENS, NOT HARDCODED GREENS. v1 hardcodes green-600/green-500/yellow-400
   plus a dark: variant pair. Use --brand-from / --brand-via / --brand-to, which
   already fork by theme, so the gradient has one definition instead of two.
   This is the same tokenisation Header.tsx's wordmark comment describes.
   Rule 1 of styles.css: a raw Tailwind colour utility in a component is a
   missing token.

2. NO SPIN UNDER prefers-reduced-motion. The ring stays, the rotation stops.
   This repo already sets that precedent - monthly-winner-celebration.tsx asks
   matchMedia rather than relying on a CSS media query, specifically so a
   vitest gate can observe the rule. Prefer that shape here too.

Tailwind v4 has no tailwind.config.ts on v2 - the keyframe/animation belongs in
src/styles.css alongside the confetti-fall block.

## THE AVATAR STAYS DECORATIVE

No click handler, no role=button, no cursor-pointer. The hamburger beside it is
the control. This preserves the reasoning in user-menu.tsx's doc comment - v1's
ringed avatar "reads as a badge, not a control" and users were not finding it -
while giving the ring back now that a real, separate control exists next to it.
Update that doc comment: it currently says "No spinning ring is ported", which
this issue makes false.

## DONE WHEN

- Avatar renders to the right of the hamburger.
- The ring is visible in both light and dark and derives from brand tokens.
- The ring does not rotate under prefers-reduced-motion, and a test observes it.
- The avatar is still not interactive.
close_reason: Avatar right of the trigger, ringed with brand tokens, static under reduced motion, gated on a session. 4 mutants verified dead.

title: Header: collapse nav, billing and theme into the account menu
description:
The bar currently carries a Billing button, the avatar, a hamburger and an
"Auto" theme pill, with a Home/About link row wrapping onto its own line below
them on a phone. Five controls plus a nav row is too much for the surface.

## TARGET

Bar, left to right: wordmark (Link to /) - spacer - invite badge - Upgrade
button (non-pro only) - hamburger - avatar.

Menu contents, signed OUT (the menu must now render for signed-out visitors,
which it does not today - UserMenu only mounts inside Header's isAuthenticated
block):
  Home, About, Theme submenu, Log in

Menu contents, signed IN:
  label: display name + Pro/Free badge
  Dashboard (/me), Notifications, Theme submenu, Billing,
  Home, About, Feedback (feedback.wordleteams.com),
  Install Guide, Log out

Theme becomes a Light/Dark/System submenu matching v1's user-dropdown.tsx,
replacing the cycling pill.

## NOTES

LOG OUT IS A PARITY GAP THIS CLOSES, not new polish. v1's user-dropdown.tsx has
a Log out item; v2's user-menu.tsx has only Notifications and Install Guide, so
there is currently NO way to sign out from the v2 header at all.

THE THEME STATE MODEL DOES NOT CHANGE. The localStorage 'theme' key and the
FOUC-preventing THEME_INIT_SCRIPT in routes/__root.tsx:18 stay exactly as they
are. applyThemeMode should be lifted out of ThemeToggle into something the menu
items can call; this is presentation only.

UPGRADE STAYS A VISIBLE BUTTON. Deliberate - see the epic's out-of-scope note.

## TESTS THAT WILL BREAK AND MUST BE REWRITTEN, NOT DELETED

- src/components/Header.hook.test.ts, 451 lines. The Billing/Upgrade button-set
  assertions (lines 177-253) and both app-bar link tests (407-451). The
  behaviours are all still real, they have just moved into a menu.
- src/routes.test.ts asserts on the nav links.
- e2e/billing.spec.ts and e2e/settings.spec.ts drive these controls.

E2E SITS OUTSIDE THE QUALITY GATES on this project - test, tsc and build never
run Playwright. Run it explicitly.

## DONE WHEN

- The bar holds at most wordmark, invite badge, Upgrade, hamburger, avatar.
- A signed-out visitor can open the menu and reach Home, About, Theme, Log in.
- A signed-in player can reach Log out, Dashboard and Feedback from the menu.
- Theme switching still works and still does not flash on load.
- All four gates pass and Playwright passes.
close_reason: Header restructured; nav/billing/theme in the menu, log-out gap closed. All 4 gates + 59 e2e green. 574f63c

title: Phase 7 UI/UX polish: header, date picker, boards carousel
description:
Owner-reported UI/UX refinement pass on the v2 replatform branch, gathered from
two phone screenshots and a description of the carousel drag behaviour. Three
surfaces, plus two root causes found while investigating them that are wider
than the surfaces that surfaced them.

## WHAT WE ARE BUILDING AND WHY

The v2 header has accumulated five controls in one bar (billing, avatar, menu,
theme pill, plus a Home/About link row on its own line) and reads as clutter on
a phone. The date picker is unusable at its rendered size. The team boards
carousel captures vertical drags, so a mistouch there stops the page scrolling.
And the billing button reports "no billing account" for the owner, who is
comped and therefore has no Polar customer record at all.

## SCOPE

1. HEADER RESTRUCTURE. Bar becomes: wordmark (links to /) - spacer - invite
   badge - Upgrade button - hamburger - avatar. The Home/About row, the Billing
   button and the Auto theme pill all move into the account menu. The menu now
   renders for signed-out visitors too, holding Home, About, Theme and Log in;
   signed in it additionally holds the name and Pro/Free badge, Dashboard,
   Notifications, Theme, Billing, Feedback, Install Guide and Log out.
   Theme becomes a Light/Dark/System submenu, matching v1.

2. AVATAR. Moves to the RIGHT of the hamburger and regains v1's rotating
   gradient ring (v1 user-dropdown.tsx:119, animate-spin-super-slow). Stays
   decorative - no click handler, no role=button - which preserves the reason
   v2 split identity from the control in the first place. Ring uses the
   brand-from/via/to tokens rather than v1's hardcoded greens, and does not
   spin under prefers-reduced-motion.

3. SOCIAL PROFILE IMAGE. Never populates for an account that was not CREATED
   by that social provider. See the child issue for the measured cause.

4. DATE PICKER. Calendar sizing is entirely dead under Tailwind v4. Corrects
   and completes wordle-teams-5p9, which named the wrong cause.

5. TEAM BOARDS CAROUSEL. Vertical drags inside the track scroll the track
   instead of the page.

6. BILLING FOR NON-CHECKOUT ACCOUNTS. Create the Polar customer on demand when
   no external id resolves, so comped and never-subscribed players reach a real
   portal.

## EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE

- Moving Upgrade into the menu. It stays a visible button. wordle-teams-456
  says 87% of prod signups never enter a board; burying the only
  always-reachable conversion CTA behind a hamburger works against that.
- Backfilling the image column for accounts already holding a null one. The
  fix takes effect on the next social sign-in and that is accepted.
- Restyling the scores table, the month picker, or anything else visible in the
  screenshots but not named by the owner.
- v1 parity as a constraint. This epic DELIBERATELY DIVERGES from v1 on the
  header layout and the calendar sizing. Record both in
  docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md section 7a so the Phase 7 route-by-route
  audit expects the divergence rather than flagging it.

## KEY DECISIONS AND RULED-OUT ALTERNATIVES

- Signed-out visitors keep the same hamburger with fewer items, rather than
  losing nav entirely. Ruled out: no menu when signed out, which would strand
  /about and /login with no way back to the landing.
- The avatar does NOT become a second menu trigger. Ruled out because two
  adjacent controls doing the identical thing is its own problem, and because
  v2's existing comment argues the ringed avatar reads as a badge rather than a
  control.
- Date picker stays a popover on mobile rather than becoming a sheet. Ruled out
  the sheet because it is a second code path and a nested sheet inside the
  board-entry sheet, with focus-trap sharp edges, for a problem that correct
  sizing already solves.
- Billing is fixed by creating the Polar customer on demand, not by hand-adding
  one customer in the Polar dashboard and not by issuing the owner a
  100%-discount subscription. On-demand generalises to every comped and
  never-subscribed player and needs no manual step.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- The header bar holds at most: wordmark, invite badge, Upgrade, hamburger,
  avatar. No nav row, no Billing button, no theme pill.
- The account menu opens for a signed-out visitor and offers Home, About, Theme
  and Log in.
- A signed-in player can reach Log out from the header. v2 currently has no
  logout affordance there at all.
- The avatar sits right of the hamburger, is ringed, and the ring is static
  under prefers-reduced-motion.
- A social sign-in updates the stored profile image on an account that already
  existed.
- Calendar day cells are at least 44px on mobile and the month caption does not
  collide with the nav chevrons.
- A vertical drag starting inside the boards carousel scrolls the PAGE.
- The billing portal opens for the owner's comped account.
- All four gates pass (test, lint, typecheck, build) AND Playwright is run
  explicitly, since e2e sits outside the gates.
close_reason: All 7 children closed. Header, date picker and carousel all done, plus 2 follow-ups found on beta.

title: /opengraph-image.png lost its immutable one-year cache on beta
description: Measured by scripts/parity-routes.mjs on 2026-09-01. Production serves the OpenGraph image with 'public, immutable, no-transform, max-age=31536000'; beta serves it with 'public, max-age=0, must-revalidate'. It is a content-hashed-by-nothing static asset fetched by every social card render and every crawler, and beta now revalidates it on every request. cache-policy.ts only reaches text/html documents, so no route policy covers static assets at all - this is Cloudflare Workers Assets' default, not a decision. Decide the intended value before cutover and pin it, because the apex domain inherits whatever beta has.
notes:
FIXED AND VERIFIED ON BETA 2026-09-02 (82c8fec), via a public/_headers file — Workers Assets honours it, which was worth confirming rather than assuming.

MEASURED WIDER THAN THIS ISSUE DESCRIBED. It was not only the OpenGraph image: EVERY asset was on Workers Assets' `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate` default, including the content-hashed bundles. /assets/index-*.js — the JS every visitor fetches, with a content hash in its filename — was revalidating on every request. That was the larger half of the cost and it is fixed by the same file.

AFTER (measured on beta):
  /assets/index-MYgn8UW1.js   public, max-age=31536000, immutable
  /opengraph-image.png        public, immutable, no-transform, max-age=31536000   <- byte-identical to production
  /sw.js                      public, max-age=0, must-revalidate                  <- deliberately untouched
  /manifest.json              public, max-age=0, must-revalidate                  <- see the follow-up
  /favicon.ico                public, max-age=0, must-revalidate                  <- production also serves this on the default

/sw.js IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST AND IT IS NOT COVERED, deliberately. The service worker controls every future update; a browser holding a year-old copy cannot be reached by shipping a new one. src/asset-headers.test.ts asserts it has no rule AND that no rule is a bare `/*`, because that single edit is what would silently catch it.

The test parses the file rather than substring-matching it, for the reason crawler-metadata.test.ts gives about robots.txt — and because the assertion that matters here is a negative one, which a substring check cannot express at all.
close_reason: public/_headers now sets the policy Workers Assets was defaulting for. Verified live on beta: hashed bundles immutable for a year, /opengraph-image.png byte-identical to production, /sw.js deliberately left on revalidate-always and pinned by a negative assertion. The regression was wider than filed - every asset was on max-age=0, including the content-hashed JS.

title: e2e can no longer reach the billing portal: PORTAL_NOT_CONFIGURED loses its end-to-end proof
description:
FOUND 2026-09-01 while implementing Phase 7 Task 12 (wordle-teams-6tp).

Header.tsx now renders Billing only when isPro === true and Upgrade when isPro === false — a swap, matching v1's user-dropdown.tsx (Billing behind hasBillingAccount, Upgrade behind !proMember). Every account e2e/billing.spec.ts can mint is FREE, so the Billing button is no longer present in any e2e run and the portal's not-configured branch is no longer exercised end to end.

WHAT STILL COVERS IT (all at gate level, which e2e is not):
- src/lib/billing-copy.test.ts pins PORTAL_NOT_CONFIGURED's three properties (no retry wording, no variable name, says whose problem it is)
- convex/polar.test.ts pins lookupPortal's classification
- src/components/Header.hook.test.ts (new) pins that the Billing button reaches api.polar.getCustomerPortalUrl and surfaces PORTAL_NOT_CONFIGURED

WHAT IS LOST: the join between the REAL action answering a REAL unconfigured deployment and the toast the player sees, for the portal specifically. The checkout's identical branch is still proven end to end in the same file.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN TASK 12: reaching the button needs a pro account, which means a second OTP sign-in plus a comp-pro seed mutation convex/e2eSeed.ts does not have. billing.spec.ts's own header documents the sign-in budget and the measured flake it caused (15 tests passed 3/3; 19 failed 5/5). Adding both was out of Task 12's scope.

OPTIONS WHEN PICKED UP:
1. Add a comp-pro argument to convex/e2eSeed.ts's ensureTeamFor and a second signed-in context. Costs one OTP sign-in — weigh against wt-ksh.8.51.
2. Accept it: Task 18 (wordle-teams-02c) runs the Polar sandbox pass against a deployment that IS configured, which exercises the portal for real with a real customer.
3. Decide the portal only ever mattered for subscribers and that gate-level coverage is enough.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-09-01 by the Task 12 review (finding C1), and NOT by any of the three options above. The premise dissolved.

This issue existed because Header.tsx gated Billing on isPro === true, so no e2e account - all of them free - could reach the button. That gate was itself the bug: it was justified by a false reading of v1. v1's src/components/app-bar/user-dropdown.tsx:55-59 gates Billing on hasBillingAccount = ['pro','cancelled','expired'].includes(memberStatus) and Upgrade on !proMember, and for 'cancelled' and 'expired' BOTH render, deliberately - v1's comment: "Anyone who has ever subscribed has a Polar customer record worth linking to, even once the subscription has lapsed." Since amIPro is false for both statuses and Header.tsx holds v2's only getCustomerPortalUrl call site, the gate had taken the customer portal away from every lapsed subscriber - and convex/migrate.ts copies both statuses out of Supabase, so those are real users at cutover.

Billing is now unconditional for an authenticated player, so e2e/billing.spec.ts reaches it with the free account it already mints: no second OTP sign-in and no comp-pro seed mutation. The portal block is restored in that spec - Billing clicked, "Billing is unavailable." asserted against a deployment that genuinely has no POLAR_* set, plus the wordle-teams-9fm guard that the not-configured reason is not reported as "You do not have a billing account yet." The join between the real action and the real toast, which is the only thing this issue said was lost, is back.

Option 1 (a comp-pro seed argument and a second signed-in context) was NOT taken and is not needed for this; the sign-in budget in that spec's header is untouched. Task 18 (wordle-teams-02c) still runs the sandbox pass against a configured deployment, which is the only place a REAL Polar customer reaches a REAL portal.
close_reason: Dissolved by the Task 12 review's C1 fix: Billing is unconditional again, so e2e reaches the portal with the free account it already mints. See notes.

title: The footer's Source Code link 404s: cdub615/wordleteams does not exist
description:
v2/src/components/Footer.tsx links "Source Code" at https://github.com/cdub615/wordleteams, which returns 404. The repository is https://github.com/cdub615/wordle-teams (with the hyphen), which returns 200. Verified 2026-09-01 with curl -o /dev/null -w %{http_code} against both.

Found while doing Phase 7 Task 9 (the About screenshots), which ports v1's own GitHub link — v1's src/components/about.tsx uses the hyphenated, working URL, so the two links in v2 now disagree with each other and one of them is dead. The About one is correct.

Footer renders under EVERY route in the app (src/routes/__root.tsx), so this is a broken link on every page of the site.

One-character fix. Not taken in Task 9 to keep that commit to its own scope.

DONE WHEN: Footer.tsx points at https://github.com/cdub615/wordle-teams, and something pins it — Footer has no test of its own today, which is why the wrong URL has survived.
notes:
Discovered during wt-ksh.8.32 (Phase 7 Task 9).
VERIFIED AND COMPOUNDED 2026-09-01. Measured: github.com/cdub615/wordleteams returns 404; github.com/cdub615/wordle-teams returns 200.

BOTH VERSIONS HAVE THE BUG, AND BOTH ABOUT PAGES ARE CORRECT:
  v1 src/components/home/footer.tsx  -> cdub615/wordleteams   (404)
  v1 src/components/about.tsx        -> cdub615/wordle-teams  (200)
  v2 src/components/Footer.tsx       -> cdub615/wordleteams   (404)
  v2 src/routes/about.tsx            -> cdub615/wordle-teams  (200)

So v1 has shipped a dead Source Code link for the life of the project and v2 ported it faithfully.

IT IS WORSE IN v2, VIA wt-ksh.8.50. v1 imports its footer only from the home component, so the dead link appears on ONE page. v2's __root.tsx renders Footer under every route, so the same dead link is now on every page of the site - the landing, both legal pages, /about, /login, /login-error and the dashboard.

Footer.tsx has NO TEST AT ALL, which is why a one-character error survived a full parity phase that has otherwise pinned page titles, link targets, meta attribute forms and legal prose. Worth fixing WITH a link-target test rather than alone.
close_reason:
FIXED AND CLOSED 2026-09-01, by the Phase 7 Task 9 review.

THE DELIVERABLE WAS THE COVERAGE, NOT THE TYPO. The character change is one line in v2/src/components/Footer.tsx (cdub615/wordleteams -> cdub615/wordle-teams). What made this worth a task is the reason a one-character error survived a whole parity phase inside a file that already had a test.

src/routes.test.ts's footer test matched <Link to= only. It was bounded, parsed and genuinely exhaustive - over the three internal router links, which is a set the defect could not appear in. All five <a href> links, the class containing the dead URL, were invisible to it, and its name ("the footer sends each label to the page it names") read as covering the whole footer.

WHAT LANDED:
  - Footer.tsx points at the repository that exists.
  - The test now pins BOTH sets of label/target pairs exhaustively, and is renamed to "the footer sends each label to the destination it names".
  - It also asserts the opening-tag counts (3 Links, 5 anchors), so a link the pattern cannot read - one wrapped across lines by a formatter, or carrying a className - is a failure rather than a silent absence. That is the same blindness one layer down.
  - The reader had to change too: codeOf strips // to end of line, so read through it every https:// href was truncated to "https:" and four of the five anchors were not in the source at all. The footer is now read with a comment stripper that leaves URLs alone.
  - Footer.tsx's header records the divergence, and V2-ADDENDUM.md gets 7a row 30, since the audit reads that table and v1 still ships the dead link.

MUTATION-VERIFIED at gate level (pnpm test:once): repointing Changelog at the feedback board fails; restoring the original wordleteams spelling fails.

title: og:url is the apex on every route, and / and /home are duplicate content with no canonical
description:
The site declares no canonical URL anywhere, and two things depend on one.

Both are v1 behaviours ported unchanged by Phase 7 Task 8, which was a parity port
of robots.txt/sitemap.xml/OG. Neither is a regression; both are worth fixing before
the apex flips to v2 and the URLs start being crawled fresh.

1. og:url IS THE APEX ON EVERY ROUTE.
   v1 sets openGraph.url in the root layout's metadata and no page overrides it, so
   production emits `<meta property="og:url" content="https://wordleteams.com">` on
   /privacy, /terms, /about and everything else. Verified by curl against
   wordleteams.com/home. v2 reproduces it exactly: src/lib/seo.ts's socialMetaTags is
   spread into __root.tsx's head() and nothing varies by route.

   og:url is meant to name the canonical URL of the page being shared. Sharing
   /privacy today announces itself as the home page, so a scraper that dedupes on
   og:url treats every page on the site as the same page.

   FIX SHAPE: per-route head() overrides. TanStack merges a child route's meta over
   the root's, so each route that matters adds one tag. src/lib/seo.ts already has
   SITE_ORIGIN to build it from.

2. / AND /home ARE THE SAME PAGE, BOTH ADVERTISED, WITH NO rel=canonical.
   src/routes/index.tsx and src/routes/home.tsx render the same component —
   src/components/Header.tsx:123 says so — and src/lib/sitemap.ts lists both, at 1.0
   and 0.9, because v1's sitemap does. That is duplicate content submitted twice, and
   the sitemap's priorities are the only hint about which one is meant to win.
   Google ignores priority.

   /home cannot simply be dropped: routes.test.ts and src/routes/home.tsx both record
   that it exists for inbound links and for v1's sitemap, and it is deliberately
   exempt from the signed-in bounce that / has.

   FIX SHAPE: `<link rel="canonical" href="https://wordleteams.com">` on /home (and,
   for consistency, a self-referential canonical on every route), which is the same
   per-route head() machinery as (1). Keep both in the sitemap.

DO THESE TOGETHER — they are one mechanism. src/crawler-metadata.test.ts already
imports socialMetaTags and parses __root.tsx's head(), so the per-route version has
a place to be asserted; extend that file rather than starting a new one, and pin
each route's canonical against the sitemap's <loc> for that path so the two cannot
disagree.
acceptance_criteria: Every public route emits a self-referential og:url and rel=canonical, asserted in src/crawler-metadata.test.ts against the sitemap's <loc> for that path.
close_reason: Per-route og:url and rel=canonical implemented via a table keyed on the route's own path, with /home canonicalising to the apex. og:url removed from the root rather than overridden there, so a merge rule cannot produce two tags. Verified in a rendered document by a new e2e that walks all seven advertised routes asserting exactly one of each, agreeing. Six mutations killed.

title: beta has no noindex, and Cloudflare does not supply one the way Vercel did
description:
beta.wordleteams.com is fully crawlable and now carries a real robots.txt.

Phase 7 Task 8 replaced v2's Vite-default robots.txt with a real one. The file is a
static asset, identical on every deployment, and it says "Allow: /" plus a
Sitemap: directive naming https://wordleteams.com/sitemap.xml. That is the correct
content for the production host and it is deliberate (a Sitemap: directive names the
canonical host, which is what v1 does).

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO is stop beta itself from being indexed. Nothing on
beta.wordleteams.com is noindexed today:
  - Vercel used to supply this for free. Every preview deployment gets an automatic
    `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` header from Vercel. Cloudflare Workers supply no
    equivalent, and wrangler.jsonc sets no headers.
  - grep for noindex in v2 finds exactly one hit, public/offline.html.
  - beta is a Custom Domain on a real hostname, not an obscure preview URL.

The exposure got materially larger this phase: before Task 4 beta had no marketing
surface at all (the apex WAS the dashboard and bounced anonymous visitors). It now
serves the landing page, /home, /about, /privacy and /terms — the same copy as
production, on a second hostname, with no canonical link between them.

OPTIONS, none of them taken here because all of them are cutover decisions:
  - `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` on every response from src/server.ts when
    wrangler.jsonc's ENVIRONMENT var is not "production". Cheap, reversible, and
    the var already exists and is already flagged "CHANGE THIS TO production AT
    CUTOVER". Must be removed/flipped in the same step as ENVIRONMENT, or it takes
    production out of the index.
  - Cloudflare Access in front of beta. Heavier, and breaks the e2e/smoke path.
  - Do nothing and accept it. Defensible while beta is unlinked from anywhere.

Decide before Phase 8, and put whichever it is in the cutover runbook (wt-ksh.8.43),
because the failure mode of the first option is the one that matters: shipping
noindex to production.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded and, if it is the header, it is implemented AND named as a step in the cutover runbook.
close_reason: Decision recorded and implemented: X-Robots-Tag noindex keyed on the REQUEST HOSTNAME (deny-list), not the ENVIRONMENT var, because beta and production are the same deployment and a var cannot tell two hostnames apart at cutover. Fails safe - an unrecognised host is indexable, so production can never be accidentally noindexed. Wired as the outermost Worker layer so the maintenance redirect, edge-cache hits and non-HTML responses are covered. Runbook 3.4 rewritten as a two-direction verification with no step to remember. Static assets remain uncovered and the runbook says so.

title: Flipping MAINTENANCE on is not sufficient for / — it needs a Cloudflare cache purge
description:
`/` is the single path that is BOTH in v2/src/lib/maintenance.ts's GATED_PATHS and in v2/src/lib/cache-policy.ts's STATIC_DOCUMENTS.

While maintenance is OFF, `/` goes out with `public, max-age=0, s-maxage=86400, stale-while-revalidate=604800`. When the flag is flipped ON, a shared cache still holding the pre-outage landing page can keep serving it for up to 24h fresh plus 7 days stale — and the maintenance gate NEVER SEES THOSE REQUESTS, because the Worker is not invoked for a cache hit. `wrangler deploy` purges nothing.

v2/src/server.ts reasons carefully about the OUTBOUND direction (the gate runs in front of the cache policy, so a maintenance response is never published with shared freshness) and gets it right. The INBOUND direction — a cached 200 that outlives the flag — is not addressable in code from inside the Worker.

## The mitigation is procedural, not a code change
Turning maintenance mode on is TWO steps, not one:
  1. Set the MAINTENANCE var to 'true' (Cloudflare dashboard, no deploy needed).
  2. Purge the Cloudflare cache — at minimum the apex `/` — or the landing page keeps serving to anyone whose request is answered from the edge.

## Explicitly NOT the fix
- Do NOT remove `/` from STATIC_DOCUMENTS. That costs the landing page the edge cache wordle-teams-jcj exists to buy back, on the apex, which is the highest-traffic anonymous route.
- Do NOT ungate `/`. Letting the landing page render during an outage is arguably fine but is a behaviour change nobody asked for.

The interaction is recorded in a comment on GATED_PATHS in v2/src/lib/maintenance.ts.

## Severity depends on wt-ksh.8.45
wt-ksh.8.45 has not yet established that `s-maxage` on a Worker response reaches Cloudflare's edge cache at all (no caches.default, no cacheEverything, no Cache Rule found in the repo). IF NOTHING IS CACHED AT THE EDGE, THE SEVERITY HERE IS NIL. Measure wt-ksh.8.45 first; do not build a mitigation for a problem that may not exist yet. The browser-cache half is real either way but affects only the individual visitor who already loaded the page, which is a much smaller blast radius.
acceptance_criteria: The cutover runbook (wt-ksh.8.43) records maintenance mode as a two-step procedure — set the var, then purge the Cloudflare cache for / — OR wt-ksh.8.45 establishes that nothing reaches Cloudflare's edge cache, in which case this closes as not-applicable with that finding recorded.
notes:
THIS IS NO LONGER THEORETICAL, AS OF 2026-09-02. RAISE ITS WEIGHT ACCORDINGLY.

When this was filed, wt-ksh.8.45 had not established that `s-maxage` on a Worker response reached Cloudflare's edge cache at all — and it then measured that it did NOT. So for a day this issue described a hazard that could not fire: nothing was cached, so no cached 200 could outlive the flag, and the purge step was a no-op.

wordle-teams-fqeq changed that deliberately. Documents are now stored in the Cache API and `/` returns `x-doc-cache: HIT` and `cf-cache-status: HIT` on beta. So the inbound direction this issue describes is live: flipping MAINTENANCE on without a purge leaves the pre-outage landing page being served for up to a day fresh and a week stale, to exactly the visitors the outage notice exists for.

TWO THINGS THAT MAKE THE PURGE MORE TRACTABLE THAN WHEN THIS WAS WRITTEN:
  - The cache key carries CF_VERSION_METADATA.id, so a REDEPLOY is now an alternative to a purge: a new version misses on every key and renders fresh. Slower than a purge but it needs no zone token, and the runbook can name it as the fallback.
  - The zone's Browser Cache TTL is now "Respect Existing Headers" (wordle-teams-g1cd), so `max-age=0` reaches the browser intact. Before that change a visitor's OWN browser held the page for four hours and no server-side purge could reach it at all — which would have made this issue only half-fixable.

The stale caveat inside v2/src/lib/maintenance.ts saying the purge "costs nothing today" has been corrected in the same commit as this note.

title: Legal copy names Apple and Facebook as sign-in providers, and a username that does not exist
description:
Found while porting v1's legal pages to v2 (Phase 7 Task 5, commit 176eb48).
The prose was copied verbatim on purpose — these are published documents and
amending them is an owner decision, not a port's — so both inaccuracies shipped
forward unchanged and are recorded in the header comments of
v2/src/routes/privacy.tsx and v2/src/routes/terms.tsx.

1. PROVIDER LIST NAMES TWO COMPANIES THAT RECEIVE NOTHING.

   privacy: "your profile image if provided by the third-party sign-in provider
   you use (e.g., Google, Apple, Facebook, etc.)"
   terms:   "sign in via online accounts from third-party service providers
   (e.g. Google, Apple, Facebook, etc)"

   Apple and Facebook have never been sign-in providers. v1 offered google,
   twitter, azure, github, slack and discord (src/app/login/oauth/oauth-signin
   .tsx). v2 offers google, microsoft, github and discord (v2/convex/auth.ts,
   which records that slack had zero users and X was dropped once it stopped
   being free). So the list is wrong in both directions and was already wrong
   in v1 — this is not a v2 regression.

   Both are hedged with "e.g." and "etc", which is what keeps this a P2 rather
   than a P1: the list reads as illustrative. It still names two companies as
   recipients of user data when they are not.

2. NO USERNAME IS COLLECTED.

   privacy: "we collect your name, username, email address"

   There is no username field in either codebase. v2's players table is
   firstName/lastName (v2/convex/schema.ts); v1 had none either — the only
   other hit for the word in v1 is marketing copy on the landing page saying
   you do NOT need to manage another username.

WHAT IS NOT AFFECTED, checked deliberately: no vendor, platform or datastore is
named anywhere in either document, so the Supabase/Vercel -> Convex/Cloudflare
re-platform contradicts nothing. The profile-image claim is still true (v2
stores and renders user.image from the OAuth provider). The contact addresses
are still ours. Governing law, liability and termination are
architecture-independent.

DONE WHEN: the owner has decided either (a) to reissue both documents with a
corrected provider list and the username clause removed, bumping the Effective
Date / Last Updated line from May 21 2024 and deciding whether users need
notice under the Changes clauses, or (b) to leave the text as published, in
which case close this and leave the header comments in place as the record.
Whichever way it goes, v1's src/app/{privacy,terms}/page.tsx should be changed
in step if v1 is still serving traffic at cutover.

title: text-subtle can now reach WCAG AA and no longer needs to be the documented exception
description:
Discovered while fixing the Phase 7 Task 4 review finding C1.

WHAT CHANGED. C1 moved light --text-muted from #71717a to #6b6b74, because
#71717a is 4.63:1 on --background #fafafa but only 4.40:1 on --surface-sunken
#f4f4f5, which is where the marketing landing's six feature-card paragraphs
sit. The token now measures 4.80 on --surface-sunken, 5.05 on --background and
5.28 on --surface. (v2/src/styles.css, v2/src/styles.test.ts.)

WHY THAT MATTERS HERE. styles.css and V2-ADDENDUM.md section 2 both used to
justify --text-subtle staying below AA with: it "cannot reach 4.5 and still
read as a rank below text-muted, which is itself only 4.63" - three text ranks
do not fit above the line. With text-muted at 5.05 that argument no longer
holds. There is now room to darken --text-subtle (light #767680, 4.31:1; dark
#737373, 4.18:1) to clear AA while staying a visible rank below text-muted.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE IN THE C1 FIX. --text-subtle moves N/A cells, timestamps
and placeholders app-wide, which is a wider blast radius than a contrast fix on
one band, and the "use text-muted for anything normal-sized that must be
legible" workaround in styles.css was written for the old constraint and would
need revisiting with it.

DONE WHEN: either --text-subtle is darkened to clear 4.5:1 in both themes, the
exception test in v2/src/styles.test.ts ("--text-subtle is still the documented
exception") is deleted and --text-subtle is added to TEXT_SURFACES there; or a
reason to keep it below AA that does not rest on the old rank argument is
recorded in V2-ADDENDUM.md section 2. Both stale justifications are already
corrected in that section and in v2/src/styles.css.
close_reason: 8.48: resolved by the second branch of its DONE-WHEN. The premise that there was room to lift text-subtle rested on text-muted's --background figure (5.05); the binding surface is --surface-sunken at 4.80, so the band is 4.50-4.80 and the best AA-clearing grey sits 1.06:1 from text-muted against a shipped 1.174:1. Reason recorded in V2-ADDENDUM section 2 and styles.css, and pinned by a search in styles.test.ts that flags the exception for revisiting if text-muted ever moves. Dark-only lift split to wordle-teams-51zk. 721e: comment corrected.

title: stale-while-revalidate has no invalidation behind it on a Worker deploy
description:
Phase 7 Task 3 ships public, s-maxage=86400, stale-while-revalidate=604800 on static documents.

v1 got away with the equivalent because Vercel purged its ISR cache on deploy. A wrangler deploy does NOT purge Cloudflare's cache. So a copy change to /about or /privacy can be invisible at the edge for up to 24h, then served stale for up to 7 more days - a worst case of eight days between shipping a fix and every visitor seeing it.

Note the plan originally carried a comment asserting 'Deploys invalidate, so the window only bounds how stale a between-deploy edge can get.' That is TRUE ON VERCEL AND FALSE ON CLOUDFLARE. Task 3's implementer spotted it and dropped the sentence rather than copying it; this issue exists so the underlying problem is not dropped with it.

OPTIONS: purge the cache as a deploy step; shorten s-maxage (the win over no-store is already enormous at 300s); or accept it and write the staleness window into the cutover runbook so nobody debugs a 'fix that did not ship' for a week. Blocked in practice on the sibling issue - if nothing reaches the edge, this does not bite yet.
acceptance_criteria: Either a purge step exists in the deploy, or s-maxage is shortened deliberately, or the staleness window is recorded in the cutover runbook as accepted.
close_reason: Edge half solved by construction: fqeq's version-keyed cache means a deploy misses rather than needing a purge, verified against a real redeploy. Browser half recorded as accepted in runbook 8b - max-age=0 plus stale-while-revalidate=604800 lets a browser serve up to 7 days stale and no purge reaches a private cache; worst case is one stale view per visitor per change. The open-items row saying 'no purge on deploy' was corrected, since it would send an operator looking for a step that is neither present nor needed.

title: Task 9: About's missing half, the eight screenshots
description:
about.tsx says in a comment that it is the SUBSTANCE of v1's About page and that porting the marketing surface belongs to Phase 7. The eight: board-entry, install-button, create-team, upgrade-button, feedback-page, changelog-page, twitter-acct, github-repo. The carousel is NOT ported; wt-ksh.12.5 ruled the aceternity InfiniteMovingCards dependency out, so the community images become a plain responsive grid. Every image needs explicit width/height or an aspect-ratio container, since v2 has no next/image to get that from.

## Context
Phase 7 of the v2 re-platform (T9). Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit-design.md  Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit.md
acceptance_criteria: The screenshots render with v1's alt text verbatim, and the comment claiming the page is only the substance is gone.
notes:
CLOSED 2026-09-01. Commits 73f8e56 (the screenshots), a2ce268 (beads), 40a30f9 (review fixes).

Eight product screenshots ported byte-identical to v1 (462.4 KiB), the aceternity carousel replaced by a plain responsive grid per wt-ksh.12.5, and every declared width/height verified against the file's real PNG IHDR chunk rather than a copied number. Precache confirmed unchanged at 36 files - measured both ways, and the manifest enumerated rather than counted, because 7a divergence 18 exists precisely because a precache silently swallowed documents once.

REVIEW FOUND A CRITICAL THE IMPLEMENTER'S OWN 24 MUTATIONS MISSED. The carousel guarantee - the one thing wt-ksh.12.5 actually asks for - rested on importedModulesOf, a helper with one call site and NO contract test. One plausible refinement to it ('only report package imports, skip relative paths') makes an aceternity import invisible with the whole suite green - and relative is exactly v1's import form, './ui/aceternity/infinite-moving-cards'. The test file spent seven tests pinning its OTHER extractor under the banner 'everything below is only as good as the extractor', then leaned the guarantee that matters on a second extractor it pinned zero times. Now has an eight-case contract block.

INSTANCE THIRTEEN OF THE PHASE'S RECURRING DEFECT, AND THE SUBTLEST YET. The controller asserted Footer.tsx had no test; review checked and found one - whose regex matched '<Link to=' only, making it structurally blind to all five '<a href>' links, which is the class containing the live 404. Its name read as covering the whole footer. Every prior instance was an assertion too LOOSE; this one was bounded, parsed AND exhaustive - over a set chosen so the defect could not appear in it. The lesson 'bounded and parsed' is necessary and not sufficient; the set has to be right too.

A REQUIRED SIDE-FIX FOUND WHILE WRITING THAT TEST: codeOf strips '//' to end of line, so read through it every https:// href truncated to 'https:' and FOUR OF FIVE ANCHORS DID NOT EXIST in the source as the test saw them. The footer is now read with a comment stripper that leaves URLs alone. A test written without noticing would have been exhaustive over an empty set.

THE DEAD LINK IS FIXED. Both v1's and v2's footers pointed at github.com/cdub615/wordleteams, which 404s; both About pages had the hyphenated spelling right. v1 has shipped it for the life of the project, and because v2 renders the footer on every route where v1 renders it only on home (wt-ksh.8.50), v2 turned a one-page dead link into a site-wide one. Verified by the controller: the mutation now fails a gate. wordle-teams-xmk closed with the deliverable recorded as the COVERAGE, not the character.

A GENUINE IRONY, AND IT WAS THREE RULES NOT ONE: Tailwind v4 scans source text INCLUDING COMMENTS, so the comment explaining why v2 does not use raw outline-green-600 shipped .outline-green-600 into production CSS - along with .md:rotate-3 and .md:-rotate-6 from the comment explaining the dropped tilts. The documentation of a rule emitting the three utilities it rules out. Confirmed gone: 0 hits each.

7a ROWS 25-30 ADDED, none of which Task 9 had recorded: the carousel becoming a grid, the DOM reorder (v1's flex-col-reverse puts two images ahead of their own annotations - a WCAG 1.3.2 meaningful-sequence problem), the dropped tilts, the dropped '(button below)' parenthetical, the outline halving 4px -> 2px which was documented NOWHERE, and the footer URL fix - which is itself now a divergence from production.

On the 462 KiB: review upheld the decision but replaced the reasoning. 'Lazy and below the fold' is weak - lazy defers rather than reduces, and anyone who scrolls an About page pulls all of it. The real justification is that byte-identity to v1 is what makes the port verifiable, and re-encoding in the same commit would have destroyed the md5 check proving faithfulness. Two files (github-repo.png 155 KiB, twitter-acct.png 105 KiB) are ~900px screenshots drawn at ~370 CSS px - 56% of the payload at ~2x the needed pixels. Named on wordle-teams-jcj with measured figures.

Tests 1083 / 69 files (was 1055/68). e2e 59 with known flakes. All four gates green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Task 8: robots.txt, sitemap.xml, and the OpenGraph image
description:
v2's robots.txt is the Vite starter default: it allows everything and names no sitemap, so /complete-profile and /api are crawlable and nothing points at a sitemap that does not exist. Port from v1's robots.ts and sitemap.ts, excluding both /me and /app and dropping /branding and /novu since neither exists in v2. v1's sitemap sets lastModified to new Date() on every request, which tells a crawler nothing; use the build date or drop lastmod and say which in a comment.

## Context
Phase 7 of the v2 re-platform (T8). Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit-design.md  Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit.md
acceptance_criteria: robots.txt disallows /app, /me, /complete-profile and /api and names the sitemap; the sitemap lists the public routes and not the private ones; the OG image is served and the meta tags match v1's.
notes:
CLOSED 2026-09-01. Commits c4254f9 (the artefacts), 04e4d03 (review fixes).

v2 shipped with the VITE STARTER robots.txt - allow everything, no sitemap named - no sitemap at all, no OpenGraph image, and NO description meta tag on any route. Every v2 page had no snippet for a search result or a link preview.

THE MOST DURABLE THING BUILT: a test asserting every path in routeTree.gen.ts is either advertised in the sitemap, disallowed in robots.txt, or in a NEITHER map with a written reason. Reproduced by review by actually creating src/routes/branding.tsx: the test failed naming /branding and stating the three remedies. robots.txt and the sitemap can no longer drift apart or silently omit a route, which is how sitemaps rot everywhere else.

REVIEW FOUND INSTANCE TWELVE OF THE PHASE'S RECURRING DEFECT, and it was the highest-consequence one yet for users. The test helper flattened meta tags' name= and property= attributes into a single key, so THREE separate mutations survived all four gates AND the e2e suite: og:image as name=, description as property=, twitter:card as property=. Production's split is exact - all eleven og:* use property, description and all eight twitter:* use name. <meta name="og:image"> is ignored by the OpenGraph parsers in Facebook, LinkedIn, Slack and Discord, so a shared link silently loses its card image - exactly the failure the test's own comment said nobody notices until someone shares a link. The e2e could not catch it either: its locator matched both attributes by construction. Now asserted as ordered attribute/key PAIRS; verified independently by the controller.

TWO v1 DEFECTS CONFIRMED, both independently:
  - v1's production robots.txt says 'Disallow: /me/' with a trailing slash. Rules are PREFIX matches, so /me is uncovered and v1's dashboard has been crawlable for the life of the project. v2 writes /me; pinned two ways.
  - v1 ships the OpenGraph image TWICE - opengraph-image.png and twitter-image.png are byte-identical (md5 0bc403bf3db8f765efcdbf65592369dd), 196KB of the same picture from two URLs. v2 ships one.

lastmod DROPPED rather than stamped with the build date. v1 stamps an identical always-now timestamp on all seven entries, which is the pattern that disqualifies a site's lastmod from being trusted; a build date is the same mistake more slowly, claiming /privacy changed because someone adjusted a colour token. Review added a stronger argument the implementer had not made: three entries declare changefreq yearly, so a per-deploy timestamp would contradict its own document.

REVIEW ALSO IMPROVED AN ARGUMENT RATHER THAN ACCEPTING IT. Keeping /maintenance in the sitemap was defended with 'v1 has published it for the project's life with no observed consequence' - evidence only if someone was looking, and nothing cited a Search Console check. The better argument: /maintenance answers 200 with no noindex, so it is indexable whether the sitemap lists it or not. Removing the entry would not address the objection; only noindex would. That makes keeping it free AND identifies the real fix - filed as wt-ksh.8.58.

Also filed: wt-ksh.8.54 (beta has no noindex at all - Vercel supplied X-Robots-Tag on previews automatically and Cloudflare supplies nothing, and beta now serves the full marketing surface on a real hostname), wt-ksh.8.55 (og:url is the apex on every route; / and /home render the same component and are both advertised with no rel=canonical), wt-ksh.8.57 (the served robots.txt carries two User-agent:* groups because Cloudflare prepends a managed block - repo should NOT compensate).

NOTE FOR THE RECORD: a P1 was filed during this task claiming Cloudflare OVERRIDES our robots.txt. That was WRONG and is withdrawn - Cloudflare prepends and serves our file in full beneath. The wrong conclusion came from piping a fetch through 'grep | head -20', which truncated before our section. Same defect class, committed by the controller while filing a P1 about it.

Tests 1055 / 68 files. e2e 59 (2 known flakes, wt-ksh.8.51, passing in isolation). All four gates green.
close_reason: Closed

title: Task 6: /login-error, and a decision on wordle-teams-vjh
description:
Port the copy verbatim from src/app/login-error/page.tsx: the two asterisked notes explain real failure modes to a user who has just hit one. v1 calls clearAllCookies() on mount; do NOT port that unexamined, since v2's auth is Better Auth on Convex rather than Supabase and clearing every cookie would also drop the theme preference. THE VJH DECISION MUST BE MADE HERE: v1's callback discards the provider's ?error= param so a Google access-denied looks identical to an expired OTP. Port as-is or carry the param through. Either is acceptable; leaving it undecided is not.

## Context
Phase 7 of the v2 re-platform (T6). Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit-design.md  Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit.md
acceptance_criteria: The route renders with a way back to sign in, and wordle-teams-vjh carries the decision and its reason.
notes:
CLOSED 2026-09-01. Commits 498a313 (the route + the vjh decision), ede61de (review fixes).

THE ISSUE WAS NOT WHAT IT SAID, AND v2 HAD A WORSE BUG THAN v1. vjh was filed against v1's callback discarding the provider's ?error=. Better Auth 1.6.23 already parses error and error_description, so nothing in this repo was discarding it - but v2 threw it away one step later and more damagingly. With no error URL configured, resolvedErrorURL fell back to Better Auth's own /error page, which per dist/api/routes/error.mjs:371-380 does NOT render when isProduction and no customizeDefaultErrorPage is set: it 302s to / with the code in the query string. The redirect is relative and resolves against the APP origin, so on beta and production a declined Microsoft consent landed the user SILENTLY ON THE MARKETING LANDING with no message anywhere. Verified line by line in node_modules by review.

Fixed with two config lines that are NOT redundant, and dist/oauth2/state.mjs:34 is what settles it: errorCallbackURL lives INSIDE the OAuth state, so it cannot cover the case where parsing the state is itself what failed - a missing or mismatched state cookie, which is exactly the first asterisked note's own failure mode. onAPIError.errorURL in convex/auth.ts is read before the state is parsed and covers it.

A VERBATIM PORT WOULD HAVE LIED TO THE READER. v1's page says the passcode expires after 1 hour; this deployment sets it to 300 seconds and the code email says 5 minutes from the same constant. The page now interpolates it, so it cannot contradict the email in the reader's inbox.

clearAllCookies() dropped, and the reasoning was checked rather than assumed: v2's session cookies are httpOnly and invisible to document.cookie where v1's Supabase cookies were readable, the theme is localStorage not a cookie, and signOut() on mount would be worse - reaching this page does not imply a session exists, and it would destroy one the user still holds in another tab.

XSS: none reachable. Review probed 11 payloads; any code outside the allowlist produces a 307 that strips the param entirely, and error_description - provider-written free text - is never read. The allowlist is a Map rather than an object literal, so ?error=constructor is not a hit; mutation-proven.

REVIEW FOUND TWO ASSERTIONS SCOPED WIDER THAN THEIR NAMES, instances 9 and 10 this phase. Detaching errorCallbackURL from the signIn.social() call while leaving the identical literal in a dead const passed ALL FOUR GATES AND ALL 54 E2E TESTS - silently un-wiring the whole feature. And the copy suite pinned the React element tree rather than visibility, so adding a hidden class made both failure notes vanish with everything green; the realistic version of that is not malice but a responsive tweak like 'hidden sm:flex'.

Both now pinned at GATE level, verified independently by the controller. The config fix uses the TypeScript compiler API rather than a regex: it parses the CallExpression and asserts the option is a property of THAT object literal, so a detached literal fails at any indentation and reformatting changes nothing.

Also: OTP_EXPIRY_SEC moved to convex/lib/ (every other cross-boundary import respects that directory), and a humanDuration() helper replaces Math.round arithmetic that was duplicated in the page and the email and wrong in both below 120s - 90 seconds now renders '90 seconds' rather than a false '2 minutes'.

Filed wt-ksh.8.51: an e2e flake at routes.spec.ts:146, same SHAPE as wordle-teams-1cd but not the same root cause - 1cd's fix still holds; the unguarded hop is one step later, at the profile submit.

Tests 996 / 64 files (was 964/62). e2e 54. All four gates green.
close_reason: Closed

title: The timezone picker offers 27 zones; production players span 57
description:
Measured 2026-08-28 during Phase 6 task 6 review.

  picker offers:            27 zones (src/lib/time-zones.ts, ported verbatim from v1's user-dialog.tsx:50-103)
  production players span:  57 distinct timezones (convex/schema.ts:186, measured in Phase 2)

A copied player whose stored zone is not one of the 27 opens the Notifications tab and sees the placeholder 'Select a time zone' — as though nothing were configured — even though a zone IS set and the reminder sweep resolves it correctly. Worse, the placeholder invites them to pick, and picking CHANGES their zone to a neighbouring one, silently shifting when their reminder fires.

INHERITED FROM v1, not introduced by v2: v1's picker is the same 27-zone list with the same behaviour. So this is a faithful port and not a Phase 7 parity divergence. What changed is that it now matters more — Phase 6 makes the stored zone decide when a daily email arrives, where in v1 the setting was largely decorative for anyone who never opened the dialog.

NOT the same issue as the Postgres-spelling aliases, which task 6 fixed via canonicalTimeZone(). That fix is real but narrower than first described: of the five aliased pairs, only Asia/Calcutta -> Asia/Kolkata is actually in the picker. Asia/Katmandu, Asia/Rangoon, Europe/Kyiv and Pacific/Kanton normalise correctly through the table and STILL hit the placeholder, because the picker never offered those zones in either version. Credit to the task 6 implementer for narrowing that claim rather than letting it overclaim.

OPTIONS, none obviously right:
  - Render the stored zone as a disabled/extra option when it is not in the list, so it displays truthfully and is not silently replaced. Smallest fix, keeps the curated list.
  - Widen the list toward the full IANA set, or make it searchable. Better, bigger, and a design decision.
  - Group by UTC offset rather than by named city, which collapses 57 into ~24 without a searchable combobox.

Whichever, the display must never claim 'unset' for a player who has a zone.
acceptance_criteria: A player whose stored timezone is outside the offered list sees their actual zone rather than the 'Select a time zone' placeholder, and cannot have it silently changed by opening the dialog.
close_reason: unlistedZoneOption renders a stored zone the curated list omits, both as the trigger's text and as a selectable option under 'Your time zone', so it displays truthfully and cannot be silently replaced by opening the dialog. Label derived from the IANA identifier plus Intl offset rather than approximated by a nearby curated zone. Five mutations killed.

title: Task 4: pushSubscriptions table, pruned with its player
description: New table keyed by playerId and endpoint. No legacyId — v1 never stored a subscription, so there is nothing for the copy to match. e2ePrune must delete these with their player from the start, rather than after a snapshot finds thousands of orphans, which is how the other five tables got their coverage. Plan task 4.
acceptance_criteria: Schema pushes to beta; a prune test deletes one player's subscription and leaves another's; all four gates green.
close_reason:
pushSubscriptions table + prune coverage. Landed across e19c9f7 and 7173d4f, deployed to beta green — and a green "Deploy Convex" step is what proves a schema change is real. 705 tests / 43 files; all four gates verified independently by the controller.

SHIPPED: pushSubscriptions (playerId, endpoint, p256dh, auth) with by_player and by_endpoint. No legacyId — v1 never stored a subscription, so the copy has nothing to match, same rationale scoringSystems gives. No queries, mutations or delivery code; those are task 11.

VERIFIED BY MUTATION, not by report: moving the counter inside `if (execute)` kills the dry-run parity test. The counter is genuinely correct when PREVIEWING as well as when writing — which is the property e2ePrune.ts has been bitten on twice.

Spec review settled the open question: by_player IS sufficient. cascadeDeleteTeam (teams.ts:272-288) deletes only monthlyWinners, scoringSystems and the team doc — it never touches pushSubscriptions and never deletes a player. That is the structural difference from monthlyWinners, which needs winnersAlreadyCounted precisely BECAUSE the team cascade is a second route. Nothing else points at this table.

THE CRITICAL FINDING WAS ONE FILE AWAY FROM THE REVIEW SCOPE. scripts/prune-e2e-data.mjs keeps TOTAL_KEYS, a hand-maintained duplicate of the report's numeric fields, and the new counter was not in it. A missing key is not an error there — it is absent from both the summing loop and the operator's table. The DRY RUN read before typing --execute would not have mentioned push subscriptions, nor would the summary after. Rows destroyed from a real deployment, never previewed, never reported. Third instance of the exact failure that file records twice in its own comments.

Nothing caught it: tsconfig includes only .ts/.tsx so the .mjs is never typechecked, no test references TOTAL_KEYS, and all four gates were green with it present. Mutation-testing e2ePrune.ts could never have reached it. Fixed with the key AND a guard that fails the run on any unprinted numeric counter; the two sets verified to match exactly at 14 each, so it cannot misfire.

createdAt dropped after the review argued it out: unread, duplicating _creationTime for a rationale that only applies to COPIED tables, absent from scoringSystems, and destined to lie once task 11's endpoint-keyed upsert migrates a subscription between accounts on a shared device.

PROCESS NOTE: I told the implementer to amend a commit I had already pushed. Rather than force-push over published history that a deploy had already run against, the fixes became a follow-up commit. Do not instruct an amend without checking whether the target is pushed.

title: v2 has ONE upgrade entry point and it is gated behind already being at the team cap
description:
FOUND 2026-08-27 while the owner tried to run Phase 5's sandbox pass.

v2's only route to createProCheckout is team-picker.tsx:78, rendered when atFreeLimit (team-picker.tsx:48):

  const atFreeLimit = !isPro && teams.length >= FREE_TEAM_LIMIT

So a free player with ONE team has no way to pay. v1 had THREE upgrade buttons - src/lib/polar/checkout.ts's own comment says 'the three upgrade buttons in the app stay identical', which is why it passes both products to one checkout and lets the customer choose the interval on Polar's page.

NOT A PORT DEFECT. The Phase 5 spec never said v2 must match v1's entry points, and nobody decided to drop them - Task 11 wired the CTA that already existed, which was the right call for that task. This is the gap that leaves.

WHY IT MATTERS: it is a funnel question, and this project already has two open funnel bugs (wordle-teams-390, ~7% of /login visitors complete auth; wordle-teams-456, 87% of prod signups never enter a board). An upgrade path reachable only by users who have already created two teams is reachable by very few of them.

IT ALSO BLOCKS TESTING. The owner's account is comped pro (Phase 5 spec, 'correct by construction'), so isPro is true and the CTA never renders for them - they cannot reach checkout as themselves at all. Running the sandbox pass needs a fresh non-pro account with two teams created first.

DECIDE BEFORE CUTOVER: match v1's three entry points, add one somewhere always-reachable (Header sits beside the Billing button), or accept the single gated CTA deliberately. Any of those is fine; leaving it undecided is not.
notes:
RESOLVED 2026-09-01, Phase 7 Task 12.

DECISION TAKEN: option 2 of the three this issue listed — ONE always-reachable entry point, in the header, beside where the Billing button was. Not v1's three; three is a funnel experiment and this is a parity phase.

WHAT SHIPPED:
- src/components/Header.tsx: the billing slot is now a SWAP. showBilling = isPro === true renders Billing; showUpgrade = isPro === false renders Upgrade (Sparkles, aria-label "Upgrade", same ghost/sm shape so the slot does not resize). isPro === undefined — amIPro still in flight — renders NEITHER, matching the pending-invite badge one line above and for the same reason: `!isPro` is true for undefined, so the loose spelling would flash "Upgrade" at a paying subscriber on every cold load. This mirrors v1's user-dropdown.tsx, which gates Billing on hasBillingAccount and Upgrade on !proMember so nobody sees both.
- src/lib/use-start-upgrade.ts: routes/app.tsx's startUpgrade lifted whole, so both call sites share one copy. The outcome branching stays in billing-copy.ts's checkoutOutcome where a test can see it. Adds a `pending` flag for the header's button; app.tsx's dropdown item ignores it.
- team-picker.tsx's gated "Upgrade for more" STAYS. Two entry points to one action.

COVERAGE (gate level — CI runs test:once, never Playwright, wt-ksh.8.49):
- src/components/Header.hook.test.ts (new, 8 tests, jsdom): all three isPro states asserted as the exact SET of buttons in the bar; the signed-out case; Upgrade reaches createProCheckout and Billing reaches getCustomerPortalUrl; each reports its own not-configured sentence; the disabled window.
- src/lib/use-start-upgrade.hook.test.ts (new, 11 tests, jsdom): navigate, not-configured, error, a transport throw, a typed ConvexError, and the pending flag on all three exits.

MUTATIONS KILLED (full suite each time): showUpgrade `=== false` -> `!isPro`; showInviteBadge `=== false` -> `!isPro`; the hook's action ref -> getCustomerPortalUrl; the header's Upgrade onClick -> manageBilling; the whole Upgrade block deleted; showBilling -> true (both buttons at once); mutationErrorMessage dropped from the catch.

VERIFIED END TO END: e2e/billing.spec.ts run in isolation, 2/2 passed. It mints a fresh FREE account with ONE team, and that account now sees Upgrade in the header (and no Billing), clicks it, and reaches createProCheckout — which is exactly the state that could not pay before.

UNBLOCKS wordle-teams-02c / wt-ksh.8.41 (Task 18's sandbox pass): the owner is comped pro, so he sees Billing, not Upgrade. He still cannot reach checkout AS HIMSELF — but any fresh non-pro account can now reach it with zero teams created, which is what the pass needed.

FILED: wordle-teams-dyvt — the swap means no e2e account can reach the Billing button any more, so PORTAL_NOT_CONFIGURED loses its end-to-end proof. Gate-level coverage of it is new and better; the join to a real action is what is lost.

CORRECTION 2026-09-01, Task 12 REVIEW (finding C1). The "WHAT SHIPPED" note above rests on a FALSE reading of v1 and shipped a regression. Fixed in the same phase; recording both halves here so the claim is not repeated.

WHAT WAS WRONG: the note says the billing slot is a SWAP and that "This mirrors v1's user-dropdown.tsx, which gates Billing on hasBillingAccount and Upgrade on !proMember so nobody sees both." v1 does the opposite. src/components/app-bar/user-dropdown.tsx:55-59 computes hasBillingAccount as ['pro','cancelled','expired'].includes(user.memberStatus) and proMember as memberStatus === 'pro'; the two entries render at :168 and :175. For 'cancelled' and 'expired' BOTH conditions are true and BOTH render, deliberately - v1's own comment says why: "Anyone who has ever subscribed has a Polar customer record worth linking to, even once the subscription has lapsed. A lapsed player sees both entries."

THE LIVE CONSEQUENCE: convex/schema.ts carries 'cancelled' and 'expired'; convex/lib/polarEvents.ts maps subscription.revoked to 'expired', so every lapse lands there; convex/access.ts's isProFor answers membershipStatus === 'pro', so amIPro is FALSE for both; convex/migrate.ts copies both statuses out of Supabase, so real users arrive in this state at cutover. Header.tsx is the ONLY getCustomerPortalUrl call site in all of v2. Gating Billing on isPro === true therefore left a player whose subscription had lapsed - a real Polar customer with real invoices and possibly an expiring card - with no route to the portal anywhere in the app. It also stranded PortalResult's no-customer branch and "You do not have a billing account yet.", which exist precisely to answer a non-subscriber who reaches the portal.

THE FIX: Billing is UNCONDITIONAL for an authenticated player and Upgrade renders beside it when isPro === false. showBilling is gone; showUpgrade keeps its strict === false spelling, as does showInviteBadge. In-flight (isPro undefined) now renders Billing and no Upgrade: nothing wrong, nothing flashing.

STILL A DIVERGENCE FROM v1, AND NOW RECORDED AS ONE: amIPro is a boolean with no hasBillingAccount equivalent, so v2 shows Billing to EVERY authenticated player where v1 shows it only to someone who has ever subscribed. Deliberate widening - the alternative was a second Convex query and a second subscription on every page, in a parity phase, purely to hide a button whose no-customer branch already answers that reader honestly. V2-ADDENDUM.md section 7a row 39.

THE OWNER BLOCK IS STILL NOT FIXED, AND THE NOTE ABOVE IMPLIED IT WAS. His account is comped pro, so isPro is true and Upgrade does not render for him; he still cannot reach checkout as himself. That is correct behaviour, not a gap, and it is why Task 18's sandbox pass needs a fresh non-pro account. What Task 12 actually fixed is that ANY fresh non-pro account reaches checkout with zero teams created.

COVERAGE ADDED BY THE REVIEW FIX:
- src/components/Header.hook.test.ts: the free player now expects the exact set ['Billing','Upgrade']; the in-flight state expects ['Billing']; the portal click test runs at isPro === false (the lapsed player's state), so putting the gate back cannot even find the button. New: the portal's throw branch (a transport error and a typed ConvexError), the no-customer INFO level, the wordle-teams-9fm reason-collapse guard the diff had deleted from e2e, and both button icons (below sm the icon is the only difference between them).
- src/routes.test.ts: team-picker's CTA had zero gate cover - making it dead (onUpgrade={() => {}}) and repointing it at getCustomerPortalUrl both passed lint, typecheck and 1192/1192. Now pinned through a new jsxPropsOf helper in src/test-support/source-ast.ts.
- e2e/billing.spec.ts: the portal block is back, reached by the same free account, with the deleted "You do not have a billing account yet." guard restored.

TRIMMED AS VACUOUS: two bare constant comparisons duplicating billing-copy.test.ts, three assertions about a string the preceding toEqual had already pinned, and one throw test strictly weaker than its neighbour.

MUTATIONS RE-RUN AFTER THE FIX: showBilling back to isPro === true (now RED), the header Upgrade onClick to manageBilling, the header portal catch emptied, toast[outcome.level] to toast.error in manageBilling, Sparkles to CreditCard on Upgrade, and the two team-picker CTA mutations.
