Phase 7 of the v2 re-platform (T19). Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit-design.md  Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-31-v2-phase7-parity-audit.md
acceptance_criteria: Each of the four is closed, with p37 either fixed or carrying a written decision to keep the exception.
notes:
DONE. All four P3s closed, one at a time, each committed and gated separately as the plan asked.

wordle-teams-dpi - the dashboard loader's three ensureQueryData calls are one Promise.all. MEASURED as the done-when required: medians 156/133/140ms sequential against 109/112/111ms together, three runs each way, twelve document requests per run. About a fifth, and said to be modest - an earlier draft of the code comment claimed 'a third off' with figures invented before the measurement was taken, which is exactly the thing this phase keeps catching. Note the issue cited src/routes/index.tsx, correct when filed; Task 1 moved the dashboard to app.tsx.

wordle-teams-069 - fixed server-side, which is what the issue asked for rather than a tighter client. setReminderMethodFor reads and composes inside one mutation; api.settings.updateReminderMethods is replaced by setReminderMethod. The from-scratch hazard both toggles guarded by hand is now unrepresentable - there is no array to build. applyPushToggle's contract shrank with it: currentMethods gone, setMethods(array) becomes setMethod(enabled). Idempotency moved from the client's Set() to the server's includes() and both ends are tested. Five mutations, all killed.

wordle-teams-p37 - DOCUMENTED, not converted, which the plan sanctioned as an outcome. Both throws are 'SITE_URL is not set', an operator misconfiguration with no user-actionable remedy: the logs get the real message, production redacts it, and Header.hook.test.ts already pins that the UI toasts, naming an unset SITE_URL as its case. The teams.ts throw is load-bearing beyond its message - VERIFIED that invitePlayerFor patches teams.invited before the check inside the same mutation, so throwing rolls the invite back; answering gracefully would leave the row written, no mail sent, and success reported.

wordle-teams-uhx - fixed ahead of the feature. Confirmed unreachable first (nothing in src/ calls signOut), armed anyway because the failure is silent and permanent and whoever adds sign-out has no reason to look inside this hook. Three mutations, two killed, one an equivalent mutant recorded as such rather than papered over.

Four gates green throughout, ending at 1257 tests / 78 files, e2e 60/60.
close_reason: Closed

title: Two user-facing Convex paths throw a plain Error when SITE_URL is unset
description:
Found during Phase 6 Task 14's acceptance-criteria walk while checking criterion 12.

The phase spec's criterion 12 says "No Convex function throws a plain Error; every thrown failure is a ConvexError via accessError." That is false as written -- there are eleven plain Error throws in non-test convex modules, most predating Phase 6, and nearly all are correctly operator-facing.

The REAL rule the codebase follows is: anything a CALLER sees must be a ConvexError via accessError, because a plain Error's message is redacted in production while convex-test never redacts, so no test can catch the mistake. Operator-facing failures with no user-facing caller correctly use a plain Error so they fail loudly in the logs.

Two paths violate that real rule, both conditioned on exactly one thing -- SITE_URL missing from a LIVE deployment:

1. convex/teams.ts:686, inside the invitePlayer mutation. The check sits at the top level of the handler, so the plain Error propagates to the client.

2. convex/polar.ts:270 via getCustomerPortalUrl -- the returnUrl = siteUrl() call at polar.ts:653 is OUTSIDE every try in that handler. Note createProCheckout is safe only by accident of placement: its siteUrl() call at polar.ts:431 is INSIDE the try, so the failure is caught and returned as a not-configured/error result instead.

Neither is triggerable by user input. Both require an operator to remove SITE_URL from a running deployment, which convex deploy itself will not ship into (auth.ts:18 throws at module scope). In that state the user sees a redacted server error and the operator sees the real message in the logs -- arguably the intended outcome. But it is an undocumented exception to the stated rule.

Options, for Phase 7 to decide:
- Leave it and write the real rule down (the acceptance walk now does).
- Give getCustomerPortalUrl the same treatment createProCheckout got by accident: move siteUrl() inside the try, or return a not-configured reason.
- Add SITE_URL to a startup-config check so a live deployment cannot lose it silently.

Full analysis: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-27-v2-phase6-reminders-pwa-design.md, section "Criterion 12 is false as written, and the real rule is narrower".
notes:
DECIDED: DOCUMENT THE EXCEPTION, do not convert either throw. Phase 7 owns this call and the plan sanctions either outcome.

BOTH SITES THROW THE SAME THING - 'SITE_URL is not set on this deployment' - and that is an OPERATOR misconfiguration, not a state a user can be in or act on. The rule this codebase follows ('anything a caller sees must be a ConvexError via accessError') exists so a user meets copy that helps them. There is no copy that helps here.

WHAT THE THREE OUTCOMES ACTUALLY ARE, which is why redaction is right rather than a gap:
  - the logs get the real message, loudly, which is who needs it;
  - production redacts it to a generic server error, so a deployment's internal configuration is not handed to a browser;
  - the UI already says something, and it is already pinned. Header.hook.test.ts's 'the portal handler says something when the action THROWS' names an unset SITE_URL as the case it covers, and was added by the Task 12 review after emptying that catch passed lint, tsc, build and the whole suite.

Giving either an accessError code would invent user-facing copy for a state no user can resolve, and would make a deployment fault QUIETER in the one place it has to be loud.

THE TEAMS.TS THROW IS LOAD-BEARING BEYOND ITS MESSAGE, and this is the part that decided it. VERIFIED rather than assumed: invitePlayer is a mutation, invitePlayerFor patches teams.invited at :603 and :647, and the SITE_URL check runs after that in the same Convex transaction. So throwing ROLLS THE INVITE BACK. Answering gracefully instead would leave the row written and no mail sent - the invite exists, the person never hears about it, and invitePlayer reported success. That is the one outcome worse than failing.

ON polar.ts's siteUrl() SITTING OUTSIDE EVERY try, which this issue flagged: deliberate, and now stated in the file. A missing POLAR credential is answered as { url: null, reason: 'not-configured' } because a credential can only be found wrong by ASKING Polar. A missing SITE_URL is knowable up front and is not a Polar outcome, so folding it into that branch would report a local configuration error as a vendor one.

NO TEST CAN REGRESS THIS EITHER WAY - convex-test never redacts, so a plain Error and a ConvexError are indistinguishable to the suite. It is a review-only invariant, so the reasoning is written at both sites rather than left in beads where the next reader of the code will not meet it.

Four gates green: 1254 tests / 78 files. No behaviour changed.
close_reason: Closed

title: Delivery-method writes lose updates across a slow browser prompt
description:
notifications-tab.tsx captures reminderDeliveryMethods at the render where a switch was clicked, then writes a value derived from it after the whole browser flow completes. The push permission prompt is MODAL and can stay open for minutes.

So if Email is toggled in another tab during that window, the push write resurrects or drops it — a lost update. handleEmailToggle has the same shape, so this is a pre-existing read-modify-write pattern rather than something Task 12 introduced, and the blast radius is one boolean in one array.

The real fix is server-side: a mutation that adds or removes a single method against the current row, rather than the client sending a whole array it computed from a stale read. That would also remove the from-scratch-array hazard both handlers currently guard against by hand.

Surfaced by the Task 12 code-quality review, 2026-08-30.
notes:
FIXED SERVER-SIDE, which is what this issue asked for rather than a tighter client.

convex/settings.ts gains setReminderMethodFor(ctx, playerId, method, enabled): it READS the row and composes the array inside the same mutation, so the client sends only its own intent. Same shape as markCelebrationSeen for hasSeenCelebration, and for the same reason. api.settings.updateReminderMethods is REPLACED by api.settings.setReminderMethod - the array mutation had exactly one caller, the settings tab, so nothing else had to move.

THE FROM-SCRATCH HAZARD IS NOW UNREPRESENTABLE, not merely avoided. Both toggles carried a hand-written comment warning that constructing the array from scratch would drop a player's push method the first time they touched the Email switch - subscription still stored, switch still showing on, nothing ever sent. There is no array to build any more, so that comment is gone rather than restated.

applyPushToggle's contract changed with it: PushToggleEffects loses currentMethods and its setMethods(array) becomes setMethod(enabled). That is a simplification - the function no longer needs to know what the other methods are - and it keeps the ordering rule the extraction exists for (subscribe, save, THEN the method write).

A RULE MOVED, AND BOTH ENDS ARE TESTED. Idempotency used to be the client's Set(...) and is now the server's includes() guard: convex/settings.test.ts pins 'enabling twice is idempotent rather than a duplicate', and the tab test that used to assert the composed array now asserts the intent. Five mutations against setReminderMethodFor, ALL KILLED: composing from an empty array, dropping the method validation, dropping the duplicate guard, inverting the disable filter, and swapping the branches.

VALIDATED ON THE METHOD, not only on the resulting array - a point worth keeping. Disabling an unknown method yields an array that is itself valid, because the filter matches nothing, so delegating to updateReminderMethodsFor alone would accept a typo in exactly one direction and answer with a silent no-op. Pinned in both directions with test.each.

ONE TEST-QUALITY FIX FOUND ALONG THE WAY: the new tests originally leaned on aPlayer()'s default of ['email'] without saying so, which made 'adds a method' pass while its email half was a no-op against a value already there. Starting state is now always explicit.

Four gates green: 1254 tests / 78 files. e2e 60/60.
close_reason: Closed

title: useLocalCapture refs outlive the account once sign-out exists
description:
src/lib/use-local-capture.ts guards its two writes with useRef flags. Header mounts once in __root.tsx and never unmounts, so those refs live as long as the tab.

There is no sign-out in v2 yet (grep -rn signOut src/ returns nothing), so this is NOT reachable today. When sign-out lands, signing out and back in as a DIFFERENT account without a full page reload leaves wroteZone.current === true, and the second brand-new account never gets a timeZone. The reminder sweep then skips that player forever with nothing indicating why — the same silent-inertness failure Task 7 exists to prevent, arriving through a different door.

mySettings returns no player identity (convex/settings.ts), so the hook currently cannot detect the switch on its own. Cheapest fix at the time: reset both refs in an effect keyed on isAuthenticated going false.

Surfaced by the Task 7 code-quality review, 2026-08-28. Whoever introduces sign-out owns this.
notes:
FIXED, ahead of the feature that would make it reachable.

src/lib/use-local-capture.ts now resets both refs in an effect keyed on isAuthenticated going false - the cheapest fix this issue itself proposed. Confirmed still unreachable first: nothing in src/ calls signOut (the only textual hit is a comment in login-error.tsx explaining why signing out on mount would be wrong).

ARMED NOW RATHER THAN LEFT FOR WHOEVER ADDS SIGN-OUT, which is what this issue suggested. The reason is the failure's shape, not its likelihood: convex/reminders.ts skips any player with no timeZone, so the second account is never reminded, FOREVER, with nothing logged and nothing in the UI to suggest why. And the person adding sign-out has no reason to look inside a local-capture hook and every reason to assume a hook resets itself. A note in beads would have been read after the bug, not before it.

KEYED ON isAuthenticated, NOT ON A PLAYER IDENTITY, and the issue is right that the hook cannot see an account swap directly - mySettings returns no identity. It does not need to: the sign-out that must sit between two sessions is observable, and every switch passes through it.

THREE MUTATIONS, TWO KILLED, ONE SURVIVED - and the survivor is an EQUIVALENT MUTANT rather than a coverage gap, which is worth stating plainly instead of contriving a test to kill it:
  killed    the reset effect removed entirely
  killed    only attemptedZone resets, not attemptedPwa
  SURVIVED  guard inverted to `if (!isAuthenticated) return`
The inverted form resets on sign-IN instead of sign-OUT. The refs are still false by the time the second account's settings arrive, so the zone is still written and the behaviour this issue describes is still fixed. Both forms are equally exposed to an isAuthenticated flicker mid-session. There is no scenario distinguishing them, so no test should claim to.

TESTS also pin that the guard STILL HOLDS within one session - a new settings object with no sign-out writes only once. Without that, a reset that simply disabled the guard would look like a fix.

Four gates green: 1257 tests / 78 files. e2e 60/60.
close_reason: Closed

title: removePushSubscription authenticates but does not authorize
description:
convex/push.ts removePushSubscription calls requirePlayer(ctx) and DISCARDS the result, then deletes by endpoint alone. So any signed-in player can delete any other player's subscription row if they hold the endpoint.

Impact is bounded: the endpoint is itself a secret capability URL, so an attacker who has it can already push to the device. This is a defence-in-depth gap, not an open door.

NOT AN ACCIDENT — this is the behaviour Phase 6 Task 11's plan specified, and the comment there accurately describes the case it was written for (blocking an UNAUTHENTICATED caller). It just does not cover the authenticated case.

The obvious fix (scope the delete to player._id) interacts with saveSubscriptionFor, which deliberately re-points an existing endpoint row at a new playerId so a shared device can migrate between accounts. Decide whether removal should follow the same ownership rule before changing it.

Surfaced by the Task 11 spec-compliance review, 2026-08-28.
close_reason:
Fixed in 79bda50. removeByEndpointFor now takes the playerId and deletes only on a match; removePushSubscription passes requirePlayer's _id instead of discarding it; the removeByEndpoint internal mutation carries playerId, supplied by deliverTo, which already holds the id subscriptionsFor used to fetch the row.

Absent and "present but not yours" are both silent no-ops rather than throws. A throw on "not yours" would let a caller distinguish a non-existent endpoint from someone else's, one call at a time, which is a probe for other players' endpoints.

saveSubscriptionFor's reassignment is untouched, so the shared-device migration still works — that path goes through save, not remove.

Mutation-checked: making the delete unconditional again turns the new test red.

title: Email dark-mode: bgcolor + inline background-color is best-effort, not guaranteed
description:
Raised by the Phase 6 task 8 implementer, unprompted, rather than presenting the fix as airtight — recording it so the limitation is known rather than assumed away.

The reminder email wraps both branding images in a panel carrying BOTH the bgcolor HTML attribute and an inline background-color on the same td. That is the standard technique and is what most clients use to decide "this element has an explicit colour, leave it alone". It is not a guarantee: there is no cross-client contract that an inverting dark-mode client will respect an explicitly-dark td rather than flattening it toward white.

If it does flatten, the failure is the one the panel exists to prevent — the images become the only dark elements again and effectively vanish.

The extra layer, deliberately NOT done because it reaches past this task's scope: vendor-specific dark-mode targeting, e.g. [data-ogsc] selectors for Outlook.com/Yahoo, and a prefers-color-scheme block for clients that honour it.

WHY IT IS P3: affects appearance only, in a subset of clients, on an email nobody receives yet — the cron that sends it is not built, and reminders ship OFF by default behind REMINDERS_ENABLED. Worth doing before the first real send, not before the next commit.

Best verified by actually sending one to a few clients rather than by reasoning — the phase's done-when already requires a real reminder to arrive, so check it then.
acceptance_criteria: A real reminder email rendered in at least one inverting dark-mode client (Outlook.com or Yahoo) keeps its dark image panels, or the vendor-specific overrides are added and the result re-checked.

title: pnpm build copies .dev.vars, with secret VALUES, into dist/server
description:
FOUND 2026-08-27 while measuring the bundle for wordle-teams-9fm (grep -ro 'POLAR_[A-Z_]*' dist).

After 'pnpm build', dist/server/.dev.vars exists and contains POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN and POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET with their VALUES - it is a copy of the wrangler dev-secrets file.

NOT A REPO LEAK: v2/.gitignore line 3 ignores dist, verified with git check-ignore. Nothing is committed. And dist/client is clean - the substring POLAR_ appears nowhere under it, which is the property billing-copy.ts's note and billing-copy.test.ts care about.

WHAT IS UNVERIFIED IS THE DEPLOY. 'pnpm deploy' is 'pnpm run build && wrangler deploy'. dist/client is the assets directory and dist/server is the worker, so a file under dist/server should not be served - but that was reasoned, not measured, and the cost of being wrong is two live secrets on a public URL.

DONE WHEN: someone has confirmed against a real deployment that dist/server/.dev.vars is not fetchable, or the build stops copying it.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-09-01 (Task 14 Step 5). ANSWER: exclude-going-forward at most; NO ROTATION IS REQUIRED. The file is real, the secrets in it are real, and it has never left this machine.

WHAT IS THERE. dist/server/.dev.vars, 496 bytes, written by @cloudflare/vite-plugin on every build. Nine keys; three are live secrets - CONVEX_MIGRATION_KEY, POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN, POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET. The rest are Convex/site URLs and the Sentry DSN, all public by design.

WHY IT IS NOT A DEPLOYED SECRET, four independent checks:
1. wrangler uploads dist/client, not dist/server. dist/server/wrangler.json says assets.directory = "../client".
2. The worker module graph cannot reach it: main = index.js and rules glob **/*.js and **/*.mjs only.
3. .dev.vars is a wrangler LOCAL DEV convention. wrangler deploy does not read or upload it at all.
4. Scanned every file under dist/ for each value: none of the three secrets appears in any bundle, client or server. Only in .dev.vars itself.

AND IT IS A LOCAL-MACHINE ARTIFACT, NOT A CI ONE. The secret values come from v2/.env.local, which is gitignored and absent from a clean checkout - so the .dev.vars produced by the CI build holds only v2/.env.production, every value of which is public and documented as such in that file's header. The secret-bearing version has only ever existed here.

Confirmed dist/ is gitignored (v2/.gitignore:3) and .dev.vars has never been tracked on any branch. Beta answers 404 for /.dev.vars and /server/.dev.vars.

RECOMMENDATION, NOT YET APPLIED - this needs a decision. Deleting the file in a post-build step would break 'pnpm preview', which runs the worker locally and needs exactly those vars. Given it is never uploaded, never committed, and CI never even produces the secret-bearing version, removing it would break a working local workflow to mitigate a risk that does not exist. Suggest closing as measured-and-not-exploitable rather than changing the build. Owner's call.

title: The dashboard SSR loader awaits three independent Convex queries in sequence
description:
src/routes/index.tsx's loader awaits api.teams.getMyTeams, then api.teams.amIPro, then api.scores.getMyPlayerId, one after the other. They are independent of each other, so the SSR of '/' pays the sum of three round-trips where it could pay the max of them via Promise.all.

FOUND WHILE MEASURING wordle-teams-1cd. Not the cause of that flake and not fixed there, deliberately: the flake was fixed in the e2e helper and touching product code for a test's benefit was out of scope. But this is the reason a cold full-document load of the dashboard is the slowest navigation in the app, and it is on the path every OTP sign-in and every OAuth callback takes.

MEASURED CONTEXT (local backend, 6 concurrent sign-ins driven straight through /api/auth with no browser): the SSR leg that only runs beforeLoad's needsProfile and then 307s to /complete-profile took 320-590ms. The dashboard leg adds these three on top of that.

DONE WHEN: the three ensureQueryData calls are issued together (Promise.all or equivalent) and the dashboard still renders identically, with the measured before/after SSR time recorded here.
notes:
FIXED. The three ensureQueryData calls are now one Promise.all in src/routes/app.tsx's loader.

NOTE THE PATH: this issue says src/routes/index.tsx, which was correct when it was filed. Phase 7 Task 1 moved the dashboard to /app, so the loader is in src/routes/app.tsx now.

MEASURED, as the done-when requires. Local backend, three runs each way, twelve document requests per run, one warm-up discarded. Timed with page.request.get('/app') against a signed-in context, which reuses the cookies but renders nothing - so what is timed is the document response (beforeLoad plus loader) and not hydration:

  sequential   medians 156, 133, 140 ms   (min 120-134, max 399-529)
  Promise.all  medians 109, 112, 111 ms   (min  99-106, max 324-484)

Roughly 140ms -> 111ms, about a fifth. STATED AS MODEST ON PURPOSE: three round-trips to a LOCAL backend are cheap, and an earlier draft of the code comment claimed "a third off" with invented figures before the measurement was taken. The win is proportionally larger wherever the backend is further away than localhost, which is every real deployment.

WHAT WAS NOT DONE, and why: the three are not hoisted into beforeLoad beside needsProfile. needsProfile has to be awaited alone there - its whole purpose is to decide whether this route renders at all, so starting three more queries beside it would issue them for a page that is about to 307 to /complete-profile.

__root.tsx's comment about deliberately NOT prefetching the Header's two queries does not apply here, and the plan flagged that correctly: that reasoning is about useQuery versus useSuspenseQuery, and these three feed useSuspenseQuery - the component suspends on them whether or not the loader warmed them.

Four gates green, e2e 60/60. The measurement harness was a throwaway spec, deleted in the same change.
close_reason: Closed

title: e2e: the pending-invite badge above zero is uncovered
description:
Task 11 (wordle-teams-ksh) shipped the non-pro 'N Invites Pending' badge in v2/src/components/Header.tsx. e2e/billing.spec.ts asserts the ZERO case (the badge is absent, so it can never render '0 Invites Pending') but not the above-zero case.

Reaching count > 0 needs a SECOND account that owns a team: the count only rises when someone else's invite is parked - a non-pro invitee already on FREE_TEAM_LIMIT teams (teams.ts invitePlayerFor) or an address invited to more teams than completeProfileFor claims at signup. That is two OTP sign-ins and two browser contexts.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE: measured during Task 11. At 15 e2e tests the suite passed 3 runs of 3. Adding 4 tests / 3 sign-ins took it to 0 clean runs of 5, always the same shape - the first 5s-default assertion after an OTP sign-in timing out on 'waiting for navigation to finish', spread across invites.spec.ts:119, invites.spec.ts:254, teams.spec.ts:85 and teams.spec.ts:145, never in billing.spec.ts. Folded back to 17 tests / 1 sign-in it passed 4 of 5, the exception being the known flake wordle-teams-1cd. Parallel OTP sign-ins are the scarce resource, not tests.

So this is blocked on the suite having headroom - either a seed mutation on convex/e2eSeed.ts that parks an invite directly (one sign-in instead of two), or pinning workers in playwright.config.ts, or fixing wordle-teams-1cd. A seed mutation is the cheapest and needs a Convex push, which Task 11 was not permitted to make.

The arithmetic itself IS covered: pendingInviteCountFor in convex/billing.test.ts, and the pluralisation in src/lib/billing-copy.test.ts.

DONE WHEN: an e2e test observes '1 Invite Pending' in the header for a non-pro player with a parked invite, and the suite still passes at the rate it does today.

title: copy-from-supabase.mjs and verify-parity.mjs silently ignore unknown flags
description:
Found 2026-08-26 during Phase 5 Task 0 review, and the review's premise was BACKWARDS - worth recording so it is not 'fixed' the wrong way round.

A code reviewer asserted that both scripts exit 1 on an unrecognised flag and that backfill-team-owner.mjs should conform. MEASURED: they do not. copy-from-supabase.mjs:56 and verify-parity.mjs:37 validate only the VALUE of --scope=; neither has a general unknown-argument check.

So 'node scripts/copy-from-supabase.mjs --dryrun' (typo for --dry-run) SILENTLY WRITES to the deployment, because has('--dry-run') is false. That is the dangerous direction: the typo turns a dry run into a real one against production data.

backfill-team-owner.mjs now rejects unknown args and is the FIRST script in the repo to do so - deliberate asymmetry, documented in its header, not precedent.

DONE WHEN: both scripts reject unrecognised arguments with exit 1, or a decision is recorded that they should not.

NOT PHASE 5's PROBLEM. Filed so the asymmetry is a choice rather than an accident.

title: Three more sites carry the stale 533 or the false 'no membership row' claim
description:
Found by the wt-ksh.13.11 review, 2026-08-24. All three verified by direct read, not inferred. Parent: wt-ksh (set separately).

wt-ksh.13.11 corrected the Phase 4 DESIGN doc and V2-ADDENDUM row 7. It did not cover these, and two of them were cleared on a partial grep during that task.

1. v2/convex/players.ts:25 - UNDATED 533 IN SHIPPED SOURCE:
     'afterwards - leaving 151 of production's 533 players permanently nameless.'
   The only undated 533 in shipped source. Its sibling v2/convex/schema.ts:55-56 carries '(measured 2026-08-20)' on the next line, and v2/scripts/lib/copy-filters.mjs:39 dates its own. This one rots silently. NOTE: source comment, so the four gates apply (pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test:once && pnpm build from v2/).

2. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites.md:528 - UNDATED 533:
     '// the name in later at /complete-profile - so 151 of production's 533'
   The same file's line 243 IS dated, which is why a grep that stopped at the first hit cleared the file. Line 528 is a code block reproducing what schema.ts should say, and the SHIPPED schema.ts did get the date - so this is the plan's copy drifting from what actually shipped. Plans are historical artifacts in this repo; decide whether to correct it or annotate it as superseded rather than retro-editing silently.

3. wt-ksh.5's EPIC BODY (Phase 4) still carries the false claim verbatim, at line 49 of its description:
     'teams.creator. They can be left out of the copy without orphaning anything real.'
   preceded by 'Nameless players are referenced by nothing except teams.player_ids and...'.
   This is the LAST surviving instance of the claim wt-ksh.13.8 disproved - grep -rn 'orphaning anything' now returns only this and the design doc line that 13.11 fixed.

   THERE IS PRECEDENT REQUIRING THIS ONE. wt-ksh.5's own notes record that when divergence 8's false claim was found, it was fixed in V2-ADDENDUM 7a row 8, in the Phase 4 design spec, AND in 'this epic's decision 4'. The same three-place discipline applies here and only two of the three were done.

THE FACT TO STATE, from the production query recorded on wt-ksh.13.8 (2026-08-24): players_total 535, players_nameless 151, memberships_total 535, memberships_of_nameless 151, memberships_orphaned 0. Every nameless player DOES carry a player_customer row.

DO NOT WRITE THAT THE 1:1 HOLDS 'BY CONSTRUCTION'. The wt-ksh.13.11 review checked the schema: supabase/migrations/20240319201543_move_columns_to_playercustomer.sql:8-19 declares only an FK on player_customer.player_id and a unique index on id - there is NO uniqueness on player_id. The 1:1 is a behavioural artifact of handle_new_user inserting one row per signup, i.e. a measured property that can drift. v2/scripts/lib/verify-filters.mjs's header is the canonical statement of what a future divergence would mean; point at it rather than restating it.

title: Epic wt-ksh's design names the copy script as .ts; it is copy-from-supabase.mjs
description:
The epic description's Data Model & Migration section says **Copy script** (`v2/scripts/copy-from-supabase.ts`). The file is v2/scripts/copy-from-supabase.mjs — verified by ls v2/scripts/, and the sibling helpers are .mjs too (lib/copy-tallies.mjs, lib/copy-filters.mjs).

Cosmetic, but the paragraph immediately below it (added by wt-ksh.13.6) is what a cutover reader is sent to, and a wrong filename one line above the discard decision is the kind of thing that makes a reader distrust the rest. Left unfixed by 13.6 on purpose: that task's diff was required to be an insertion only, so the surrounding text was not touched.

DONE WHEN: the epic description names the .mjs file. Same body-file round-trip discipline as 13.6 (jq out, edit, diff, bd update --body-file, export, diff again).

title: The clobber banner's headline and footer are neither wrapped nor length-asserted
description:
Found by the code-quality review of wt-ksh.13.5 (Task 2), 2026-08-24. LATENT: not reachable today.

formatClobberReport wraps its DETAIL lines to the 80-column frame and pins that with a boundary test and a mutation test. The HEADLINE (copy-tallies.mjs, 'OVERWROTE STORED VALUES: <labels>') and the FOOTER notes ('Overwrote nothing: ...' / 'Not diffed: ...') are built from the same variable-length label lists and are simply emitted, unwrapped and unasserted.

MEASURED by the reviewer, sweeping every assignment of the six tables across {absent, clean, overwritten}:
  - today, with three tables reporting clobbered:        longest framed non-detail line = 80. Safe.
  - with playerMembership also reporting (Phase 5 Polar): 80. Still safe.
  - with dailyScores ALSO reporting:                      90 - the headline escapes its own frame.

WHY THIS IS WORTH FILING RATHER THAN SHRUGGING AT. The trigger is not hypothetical the way 'all six diff' is. convex/migrate.ts classifies upsertDailyScores as MERELY UNWIRED - it already has the same clobber shape and is left out only pending a dual-running decision. That is wordle-teams-r9d. dailyScores is the most likely next table to start reporting, and it is exactly the one that trips this.

The failure is the same defect class Task 2 already fixed for the detail lines: a continuation line loses the '##' gutter and reads as unrelated output escaping the block, which undercuts the acceptance criterion ('visually distinct from the routine output around it').

DONE WHEN: a report whose headline and footer carry the widest label list they can produce stays inside the 80-column frame, and a test pins it.

APPROACH NOTES from the review and the implementer:
  - The fix likely belongs in the same place as detailLines' wrapping (headline could wrap through it with an empty label column).
  - ALTERNATIVE, possibly better: drop the label list from the headline entirely. The detail lines below already name every table, so the headline list is redundant.
  - The existing 'stays inside its 80-column frame' describe block in scripts/lib/copy-tallies.test.mjs is where the guard slots in. It currently only exercises detail lines: its fixture has two overwritten tables and no clean/notDiffed entries, so it never renders a wide headline or any footer at all. Widening that fixture to five overwritten tables plus a clean and a not-diffed one makes it fail, which is the point.

BLOCKS NOTHING TODAY. Whoever wires dailyScores (wordle-teams-r9d) should do this in the same change.

title: The 533-player figure in the Phase 4 design and V2-ADDENDUM is now 535
description:
Measured against production 2026-08-24 while answering wt-ksh.13.8: players_total is 535, not the 533 stated in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites-design.md and in V2-ADDENDUM.md 7a row 7. Two signups since the 2026-08-20 measurement.

NO CONCLUSION MOVES. The 151 nameless figure both documents rest on is unchanged, verified in the same query, so the copy filter's premise and divergence 7's reasoning stand exactly as written.

Filed because this project treats a stated measurement as a claim, and the Phase 7 parity audit will compare against these totals. A reader who finds 535 where the document says 533 should be able to see that it was noticed and dated rather than wonder which number is stale.

FIX: state the figure with its measurement date, or express it as '151 of the then-533' so it cannot rot again. Also worth recording that player_customer is exactly 1:1 with players (535/535, 0 orphans), which is load-bearing for wt-ksh.13.7's membership narrowing and is not written down anywhere today.
notes:
SCOPE WIDENED 2026-08-24 by the wt-ksh.13.7 review. The same Phase 4 design doc carries a SECOND now-false measurement, in the same table.

docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites-design.md (around line 47) states that nameless players are referenced by 'no board, no winner row, no membership row'. wt-ksh.13.8 disproved the last clause against production on 2026-08-24: all 151 nameless players carry a player_customer row, memberships_total == players_total == 535, and memberships_orphaned = 0. player_customer is exactly 1:1 with players.

This matters more than the 533/535 drift does, because that line is the cited justification for leaving memberships to the upsert's own orphan tally - and it is the claim wt-ksh.13.7 had to work around by narrowing memberships verifier-side. A reader trusting it would conclude the membership narrowing in scripts/lib/verify-filters.mjs is unnecessary.

Fix both in the same pass: 533 -> 535, and correct the membership clause.
close_reason:
Shipped in 804ccbe..92c497e (two commits). Documentation only.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY STALE, which is not what the bead said. The bead claimed the 533 figure appeared in BOTH the Phase 4 design doc AND V2-ADDENDUM 7a row 7. Verified by grep against both files and their pre-images: V2-ADDENDUM contains no 533 and no 535 at all, and row 7 made no membership claim. The bead's file attribution was simply wrong. No 533 edit was invented there.

FIXED IN docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites-design.md:
  - Line 30, dated PER-ROW rather than at the table header: '151 of 533' now carries 'Re-measured 2026-08-24 (wt-ksh.13.8): still 151, now of 535 - two signups since.' Per-row because the header's 'Run against production on 2026-08-20' stays true for the four rows that were only ever measured then; rewriting it to name two dates would have implied all five were re-run.
  - Lines 44-47, the false clause. 'no board, no winner row, no membership row points at one' - the last third is false. All 151 nameless players carry a player_customer row.
  - A THIRD instance the bead did not name, found by grep: the design's own divergence-7 row restated 'nothing but player_ids/creator refers to them' 275 lines later.

FIXED IN docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md 7a row 7: not false, but SILENT on memberships - and 7a is the parity audit's reference list, read by the same person who will watch verify-parity.mjs narrow memberships by 151. One clause, in-cell so a reader who only opens the table still gets it. Table still has its 11 rows and the 'Eleven known differences' header is untouched.

THE DEFECT REVIEW CAUGHT, and it is the one worth remembering. The first draft wrote that player_customer is '1:1 with players ... BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by coincidence' - and then pointed the reader at scripts/lib/verify-filters.mjs, which says the opposite, deliberately, because wt-ksh.13.7 had just fixed exactly that misdirection. There is no construction: 20240319201543_move_columns_to_playercustomer.sql declares an FK on player_id and a unique index on id, and NO uniqueness on player_id. Review swept all 20 migrations touching player_customer and confirmed no later one adds it. The 1:1 is a behavioural artifact of handle_new_user inserting one row per signup - verified as the current definition, 20240321210006 being the latest of five. So the property is measured and can drift, exactly as the 533 did. Now stated as a measurement with the migration cited, in both documents - the same rule-framing had appeared in V2-ADDENDUM row 7 too.

NO CONCLUSION MOVED, as the bead required: the copy filter's premise, the 'Not copied' decision row and divergence 7's reasoning are byte-identical.

FOLLOW-UP FILED: wordle-teams-9vq (P3) - three sites still carrying a stale or false form of these claims. Two undated 533s (v2/convex/players.ts:25, the only one in shipped source, and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-21-v2-phase4-invites.md:528), plus wt-ksh.5's EPIC BODY, which still carries the false 'orphaning anything real' claim verbatim - and wt-ksh.5's own notes record the three-place precedent that requires fixing it there too.

title: Add a no-restricted-imports rule so Resend cannot be imported outside email.ts
description:
The last third of wordle-teams-sga. The choke point is in place - convex/email.ts exports only a guarded sendEmail and keeps the Resend client module-private - but nothing MECHANICALLY stops a new module doing 'import { Resend } from @convex-dev/resend' and constructing its own.

That is a convention held by a comment, and this exact guard has now had to be added after the fact twice (see wordle-teams-96l).

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINER: v2 has no ESLint config of its own. The only config in the repo is v1's root .eslintrc.json (next/core-web-vitals), which does not cover v2/. So this needs a v2 config before it needs a rule.

Shape once there is one:

  'no-restricted-imports': ['error', { paths: [{
    name: '@convex-dev/resend',
    message: 'Send mail through convex/email.ts sendEmail, which applies the e2e guard.',
  }]}]

with an override allowing it in convex/email.ts and convex/convex.config.ts only.
close_reason:
Fixed. v2 now has ESLint (flat config), a lint script with --max-warnings 0, and a CI step ahead of the unit tests in deploy-v2.yml. The substantive rule: nothing but convex/email.ts may reach the Resend client.

THREE IMPORT VECTORS BLOCKED, each verified by probe with the tree restored after: a static import from convex/ or src/; a DYNAMIC import(), which core no-restricted-imports cannot see at all because it only inspects ImportDeclaration - that needed no-restricted-syntax on ImportExpression; and .tsx under convex/, which the original file glob missed and which is exactly where Phase 6's React Email templates would land.

NOT CLOSED, and stated in the config rather than implied otherwise: createRequire, and reaching the component through the generated components.resend handle (convex/_generated/api.d.ts exposes it as a typed ComponentApi, so a convex module can call ctx.runMutation(components.resend...) without importing anything restricted). 'Structural' here means the obvious path is blocked, not that every path is.

Kept deliberately narrow - the recommended sets and nothing more, so it passes clean rather than importing a style backlog. no-console left off and filed as wordle-teams-61x. rules-of-hooks turned ON (a conditional hook call is a crash, not a preference; the tree already satisfied it). --max-warnings 0 because without it the severities pointed the wrong way: an unused disable directive is an error and would fail the deploy, while a genuine missing hook dependency was a warning and shipped green.

Three pre-existing findings fixed rather than silenced: migrate.ts's chunkNote is a live @see {@link} target (proved with tsc - noUnusedLocals does NOT fire while the tag exists, and DOES when it is removed), and two disable directives that suppressed nothing.

SEPARATE FINDING, fixed here: the pre-commit hook is not a beads stager, it is scripts/check-no-pii.mjs. Committing --no-verify - which every Phase 4 commit did - skipped the PII guard on a public repo for an entire phase. It failed on 40 addresses, all RFC 2606 reserved .test names, which is why it would keep being bypassed; ALLOWED_EMAILS now covers the .test TLD alongside example.com/org/net. Clean over 471 tracked files, and a real address is still blocked.

Filed alongside: wordle-teams-61x (no-console decision), and the CI-never-typechecks gap.

title: accessError('UNAUTHENTICATED') is dead code - getAuthUser throws before it is reached
description:
Found by the Phase 4 Task 8 review, 2026-08-22.

v2/convex/players.ts:247 and :291 both do:

  const user = await authComponent.getAuthUser(ctx)
  if (!user?.email) throw accessError('UNAUTHENTICATED')

The guard is unreachable. getAuthUser throws new ConvexError('Unauthenticated') rather than returning null (@convex-dev/better-auth/dist/client/create-client.js:74). Because that payload is a bare string, convexErrorCode (src/lib/convex-error.ts:12-32) returns null and the UI renders its GENERIC fallback ('Could not save your profile, please try again') instead of the typed 'Your session expired'.

THIS IS THE ROOT OF A REAL DEBUGGING COST. Two separate attempts to diagnose a flaky e2e spec chased this: the failure presented as a mystery precisely because the typed path was dead. Had UNAUTHENTICATED been live, the spec's failure would have been self-describing.

FIX: use safeGetAuthUser (or catch and re-throw as accessError) so the typed code is live. Check every other authed wrapper for the same pattern - the ...For helpers are unaffected, this is wrapper-only, which is the exposure wordle-teams-obw already tracks.

Note this is the SAME class as the ConvexError-vs-Error rule the phase already follows: an error a human reads must carry a code the client can map.

title: Extract PendingInvites so the creator-only query boundary is structural, not a comment
description:
Raised by the Phase 4 Task 7 quality review.

current-team-card.tsx now holds 6 useState, 3 mutations and 1 query in ~330 lines. The Pending block is cleanly separable: it needs only teamId, owns openEmail / pendingEmail / the cancel mutation / the getTeamInvites query / the dedupe, and renders its own Separator + h3 + ul. Nothing else in the card reads any of it.

THE ARGUMENT IS NOT LINE COUNT. Conditional mounting makes the 'skip' subtlety structurally unnecessary:

  {isCreator && <PendingInvites teamId={teamId} />}

A non-creator never calls the hook, so no query-cache entry is created and subscribeInner never sees an 'added' event. That replaces ~13 lines of comment explaining a library internal with a guarantee the render tree enforces - and, crucially, one that survives a future contributor 'simplifying' convexQuery(..., 'skip') back to enabled: isCreator, which is exactly the regression Task 7 had to measure at the websocket to disprove.

A comment is the weakest possible protection for a security-adjacent boundary over real email addresses. See the memory note on enabled-vs-skip.

Not done in Task 7 because the plan specifies the inline shape and the shipped code is correct; changing it there would have been uninstructed refactoring.

title: ConfirmPopover loses focus to <body> when its trigger unmounts
description:
Measured during Phase 4 Task 7 review. After a successful destructive confirm, Radix restores focus to the trigger on close - but the handler sets the popover closed AFTER the await, by which point the Convex subscription has already re-pushed the list without that row, so the trigger is gone and there is nothing to restore to.

Measured: focus with popover open = BUTTON 'Cancel invite'; immediately after the toast = BODY; at 300ms, 1000ms and 2500ms = still BODY, never recovers. The next Tab lands on the site logo at the top of the document, then Home, About, theme switcher.

PRE-EXISTING SHAPE, NOT INTRODUCED BY TASK 7. The untouched remove-member path does the same thing (focus after remove = BODY). Radix Dialog's Escape restore is also BODY for both the new invite dialog and the pre-existing settings dialog.

WHY IT IS WORSE ON PENDING INVITES. Removing a member or deleting a team is a one-off. The pending list exists so a creator can clear out SEVERAL bad addresses in a row - and after each one a keyboard user must Tab past the header, theme switcher, team picker, month picker, board-entry button and the whole scores table to reach the next row.

FIX BELONGS IN src/components/confirm-popover.tsx, once, covering cancel-invite, remove-member and delete-team: give PopoverContent an onCloseAutoFocus that redirects when the trigger is detached, or have callers move focus deliberately after a successful destructive action (e.g. tabIndex={-1} on the list wrapper, focused on success).

title: Extract the needsProfile route guard once a third authed route needs it
description:
index.tsx and complete-profile.tsx now run near-identical mirror-image beforeLoad logic: check context.isAuthenticated, redirect to /login if not, read needsProfile via ensureQueryData, then redirect in opposite directions.

BOTH Task 6 reviewers independently recommended LEAVING the duplication for now. It is four lines, two call sites, and a shared helper would need a direction parameter and end up longer than what it replaces.

THE RISK IS OMISSION, NOT DUPLICATION. Nothing forces a new authed route to carry the guard. A route that skips it puts a playerless account in front of queries that assume a player exists - which is exactly wt-ksh.5.1's dead end, where the dashboard rendered NO_PLAYER as 'Your session expired' and signing in again could not fix it.

Phase 4/5's invite-acceptance route is the likely third. Extract then, and at that point make the guard the default rather than something each route opts into.

title: Extract the normalise-on-read invite comparison into lib/invite.ts
description:
The trim().toLowerCase() comparison over teams.invited is now restated FIVE times across two modules: teams.ts (invitePlayerFor's filter and its some() scan, and cancelInviteFor's filter) and players.ts (completeProfileFor's some() scan and its filter). Each site carries a long comment re-deriving the same reasoning.

lib/invite.ts's own header states the principle this violates: 'the rules live here, once, rather than being restated at each call site where they could drift apart.'

Suggested shape:

  export function isSameInvite(entry: string, normalisedEmail: string): boolean
  export function withoutInvite(invited: Array<string>, normalisedEmail: string): Array<string>

THE TRAP THE EXTRACTION MUST NOT FALL INTO. The obvious simplification of these five lines is normaliseInviteEmail(entry) === email. That is WRONG: normaliseInviteEmail returns null for an entry that fails EMAIL_SHAPE, so a malformed stored entry would never match and could never be cancelled - resurrecting exactly the uncancellable-invite bug this surface exists to remove. The helper must compare entry.trim().toLowerCase(), not re-run the write-side normaliser over stored data. Write a test that pins this: a stored entry failing EMAIL_SHAPE must still be cancellable by an address that normalises to the same string.

Deferred out of Phase 4 Task 4 deliberately: the extraction touches invitePlayerFor and completeProfileFor, both already shipped, tested and reviewed, while Task 4 was scoped to a new surface. Raised by the Task 4 code-quality review.

title: isNamed and isCompleteName disagree on whitespace-only names
description:
Found by the Phase 4 Task 0c/0d joint review, 2026-08-21.

scripts/lib/copy-filters.mjs's isNamed is a plain falsy test, so a name of ' '
(a single space) is treated as NAMED and copied across.

convex/lib/invite.ts's isCompleteName trims before testing, so the same value is
treated as INCOMPLETE and rejected by the profile flow.

So v2 will refuse a name that its own copy accepts. Nobody has written that
asymmetry down, and a mutant that makes isNamed trim survives the copy-filter
suite — the rule is unpinned in the direction that would fix it.

Not a regression: the retired deleteNamelessPlayers used the same falsy test, so
the two have always disagreed. Low priority because a whitespace-only name in
Supabase is unlikely and unmeasured.

Worth doing together with wordle-teams-9lt, since both are about the copy's
selection rules being exactly right before the Phase 7 audit. If the answer is
"make isNamed trim", add the pinning test at the same time.
acceptance_criteria: A whitespace-only name is treated the same by the copy filter and the profile flow, or the divergence is documented as deliberate.

title: A profile-incomplete member is invisible and unremovable
description:
Found by the whole-phase review of Phase 3, 2026-08-19. A known constraint for Phase 4 to design around, not a bug to fix now.

getMyTeamsFor filters profile-incomplete members out of the payload, so CurrentTeamCard renders no row for them and the creator never receives their id. removeMember would happily remove them — there is simply no path in the UI to call it with that id.

So an invitee who accepts but never completes their profile is INVISIBLE AND UNREMOVABLE. They sit in the team's playerIds forever, counting against nothing visible, with no way for the creator to clear them out.

Phase 4 owns invites and onboarding and is where this becomes reachable. Worth knowing going in rather than discovering it: the fix is probably a pending-members section on the team card rather than relaxing the filter, since relaxing it would put a nameless row on the scoreboard, which is the thing the filter exists to prevent.
acceptance_criteria: A creator can see and remove a member who accepted an invite but never completed their profile.
close_reason:
Closed by Phase 4, though not in the shape this issue anticipated. The premise - a member who accepted an invite but never completed their profile - is now UNREPRESENTABLE: decision 2 of the epic made firstName/lastName required and a players row is born only on profile completion, so such a person has no player row and never enters teams.playerIds. They remain an address in teams.invited.

So the remedy is the one this issue asks for, reached differently: Task 4 (wt-ksh.5.16) added getTeamInvites and cancelInvite, creator-only, with the refusal in the QUERY rather than a hidden button; Task 7 (wt-ksh.5.19) added the Pending invites section with a per-address cancel. The creator can now SEE them - v1 showed pending invites nowhere - and remove them. Case- and whitespace-insensitive, because copied rows predate v1's own case fix. Divergence 6.

Note the query is gated with convexQuery(..., 'skip'), not enabled:, because enabled does not gate a Convex query at all - see wt-ksh.5.19 and the bd memory note. These are real email addresses.

title: Month dropdown lists oldest first; most recent should be on top
description:
Reported by the owner: the month dropdown lists the oldest month at the top and the most recent at the bottom. It should be the other way round — most recent first.

CAUSE: monthOptions in v2/src/components/month-picker.tsx returns ascending:

  return [addMonths(currentMonth, -2), addMonths(currentMonth, -1), currentMonth]

and MonthPicker renders them in array order.

FIX is small: reverse the order so the current month is first. Two other things must move with it or the change is incomplete:

 1. v2/src/components/month-picker.test.ts pins the ascending order in both its tests (monthOptions('2026-08') -> ['2026-06','2026-07','2026-08'] and the year-boundary case). Update them to the new expectation rather than deleting them — the year-boundary case is the one worth keeping.
 2. This DIVERGES FROM v1. Prod builds the same list ascending (getMonthsFromScoreDate in src/lib/utils.ts appends forward from the earliest month) and renders in array order, so prod also shows oldest-first. Record the change in docs/design-system/V2-ADDENDUM.md section 7a so Phase 7's parity audit expects it.

RELATED: wordle-teams-rzu (MonthPicker does not validate its value against the offered months) is in the same component, and the deferred pro-gate expansion — which widens this list to every month back to the team's earliest score — will touch this ordering too. Worth doing together; a long ascending list makes the wrong-end problem considerably worse than a three-item one.
acceptance_criteria: The current month is the top entry and older months descend below it, with the tests and the divergence record updated.

title: Pin the invariant that N/A weekend days never affect the month total
description:
Confirmed correct, needs a test pinning it.

A weekend day on a team with playWeekends off renders N/A and contributes NOTHING to the month total — monthTotal skips it before consulting any score. That is the intended behaviour and matches v1.

The scoring for a 0 day is also correct and is NOT changing: a past day with no board scores the team's own "0 attempts" value from its scoring system (the nA field, default 0). The owner initially asked for a 0 day to score like an X, then withdrew it on realising the default system already scores a 0 day as 0 and the scoring system was being honoured correctly. No parity divergence results.

scoring.test.ts already covers "weekends are skipped entirely when the team does not play them". Add an explicit companion asserting a weekend contributes nothing even when the team's nA value is NON-ZERO — the existing test uses nA:-2 and would catch a regression, but nothing states the invariant in terms a reader would recognise as "N/A must never score".

Small, and it stops a future change to the missed-day rule from silently sweeping weekends in with it.
acceptance_criteria: A test fails if a weekend day on a playWeekends-off team ever contributes to the total.
close_reason: Closed

title: MonthPicker does not validate its value against the offered months
description:
MonthPicker takes `value` straight from the URL search param and does not check it against monthOptions(currentMonth), which is a fixed three-month window (current month and the two before it).

A bookmarked or hand-edited URL for a month outside that window renders the trigger label for that month while no radio item in the dropdown shows as selected. Not a data or access problem — getTeamMonth serves any month to a team member by design, and the window is a UI affordance rather than access control in both v1 and v2 — just an inconsistent control.

Cheapest to fold into whatever work expands the window for pro accounts, since that phase has to reason about exactly this logic anyway and will decide whether the window becomes server-enforced.

Raised in the Phase 2 whole-phase review.
acceptance_criteria: A month outside the offered window either redirects to a valid one or is shown as selected.

title: e2e login spec asserted removed Phase 1 debug-view testids
description:
Task 6 (2df6872, 'launch url, open to dashboard') rewrote v2/src/routes/index.tsx
into the real dashboard, dropping the Phase 1 debug view that rendered
data-testid="signed-in-email" / "copied-data" / "no-player". e2e/login.spec.ts
still asserted against those testids and was silently broken (pnpm e2e failed)
from that commit onward -- nothing in the normal quality gates (test:once,
tsc, build) runs Playwright, so it went unnoticed until Task 9 ran the e2e
suite directly.

Found and fixed while extracting the sign-in helper for Task 9
(wt-ksh.3.11): updated login.spec.ts's post-verify assertions to check the
CURRENT dashboard behavior (URL is '/' and the 'You are not on a team yet'
empty state renders) instead of the removed testids. Filing this so the
regression and root cause are on record, separate from the Task 9 work
itself.
close_reason: Fixed in the same commit that files this issue: e2e/login.spec.ts's assertions updated to match the current dashboard (part of Task 9 / wt-ksh.3.11).

title: form.tsx duplicates board-input.tsx's keystroke interception
description:
board-entry/form.tsx's handleAnswerKeyDown re-implements the same keystroke interception as board-entry/board-input.tsx's handleKeyDown: the letter regex, backspace handling, Tab passthrough, preventDefault-everything-else. No shared helper.

Two costs. It is a DRY violation on logic that must stay in lockstep — both fields are contentEditable and both depend on identical guarantees about which events can reach the DOM (see the beforeinput/paste hardening added in task 8). And it means BoardEntryForm is simultaneously a data-orchestration layer and a raw keystroke interceptor, so the capture logic cannot be reasoned about or tested apart from the form.

Suggested by code review: an AnswerInput component mirroring BoardInput's shape, or a shared module exporting the key classification and the apply helpers.

Raised during Phase 2 task 8 review, deliberately deferred to avoid widening that commit further.
acceptance_criteria: One shared implementation of contentEditable key capture, testable without mounting the form.

title: Extract the dashboard search-param sync into a hook
description:
src/routes/index.tsx now holds the route definition (loader, validateSearch, beforeLoad), three independent useEffects (login-funnel arrival tracking, URL/localStorage search-param sync with a redirect, team-selection persistence) and the dashboard layout.

Phase 3 adds team management to this same screen.

The search-param sync effect is the piece worth extracting: it is the highest-risk code in the Phase 2 UI (an effect that navigates to fill in URL state while racing hydration — the classic infinite-redirect shape), it is the piece Phase 3 is most likely to touch, and pulling it into a useDashboardSearchSync hook would also make it testable independently, which wordle-teams-pow wants.

DashboardError was already extracted during Phase 2 task 8 review. This covers the remainder.
acceptance_criteria: index.tsx holds the route and layout; the search-param sync lives in its own tested hook.
close_reason: Closed by wt-ksh.4.19. index.tsx holds the route and layout (143 -> 115 lines); the decision lives in the pure resolveDashboardSearch with 7 tests including an idempotency round-trip that encodes the termination property as an assertion rather than a comment.

title: The dashboard redirect effect has no targeted test
description:
The dashboard route resolves team and month from URL search params, filling in missing ones via a useEffect that navigates with replace:true and reads localStorage for the last team. That effect is the highest-risk code in the Phase 2 UI: it is the classic shape for infinite redirect loops (an effect depending on unstable-identity values that navigates to fill in URL state, racing hydration).

It currently has no test. The Phase 2 spec ruled out a component-test suite on the grounds that Phase 2 is a 1:1 port — but this code is NOT a port. v1 used a React context backed by localStorage; search params are a deliberate v2 divergence chosen because v1's approach needed three hydration guards and still shipped a production hydration crash (wordle-teams-uc5). So the no-component-tests rationale does not cover it.

Loop-safety was verified by hand during code review and holds today. Nothing would catch a regression — for instance someone adding a dependency to the effect, or reordering the early-return guard.

The Playwright smoke test does exercise the path incidentally (it must resolve params to reach the board), so this is not uncovered end to end; what is missing is a targeted test that fails fast and points at the cause.

v2 already has jsdom and @testing-library/react installed. vitest's global environment is edge-runtime, so a component test needs a per-file `// @vitest-environment jsdom` pragma.
acceptance_criteria: A test fails when the redirect effect loops, double-fires, or stops filling in missing params.

title: INVALID_BOARD does double duty for a rejected today
description:
upsertBoardFor throws INVALID_BOARD for two distinct failure classes:
  - the board itself is malformed (boardIsValid failed)
  - the board is fine but the client-supplied today is outside +/-1 day of the server date

Inert today because nothing on the client branches on AccessCode yet. It stops being inert as soon as an error-message mapping keys off INVALID_BOARD to say something like "your board is incomplete" — a clock-skew rejection would then show a misleading message to someone whose board was perfectly good.

Wants a distinct code (INVALID_TODAY or similar) before the client starts consuming these. Note the Phase 2 plan specified INVALID_BOARD here explicitly, so this is a plan choice to revisit rather than an implementation slip.

Related: wordle-teams-3ht (AccessCode carrying non-access concerns).
acceptance_criteria: A clock-skew rejection is distinguishable from a malformed board by its error code.

title: Extract recomputeWinners from scores.ts before Phase 3 needs it
description:
recomputeWinners is an unexported function inside convex/scores.ts, reachable only through upsertBoardFor. Its five distinct behaviours (a row per team, tie-break by team order, no-winner deletes, preserve hasSeenCelebration on unchanged, reset on changed) can only be exercised by first constructing a valid board submission and passing the whole validity/upsert machinery.

Compare lib/scoring.ts, whose monthTotal and winnerOf get direct dependency-free unit tests.

The forward-looking cost is the bigger one: Phase 3 changes team membership, and a member leaving mid-month plausibly needs the same recompute triggered from a DIFFERENT mutation. Today there is no way to call it without either exporting it or duplicating ~70 lines.

Suggested by code review: extract to convex/winners.ts, typed against the same narrow WriterCtx scores.ts already uses. Decouples winner tests from board-validity setup and gives Phase 3 an entry point.

Also noted: scores.ts is now 349 lines holding reads, the write, team listing, player-id lookup and winner recomputation. Not unreadable, but the split is cheapest before Phase 3 needs it.

Not blocking Phase 2.
acceptance_criteria: Winner recomputation is callable and unit-testable independently of a board submission.
close_reason: Closed by wt-ksh.4.18. recomputeWinners now lives in convex/winners.ts as recomputeTeamMonth / recomputeTeamMonths / monthsWithWinners / recomputePlayerMonth, unit-tested directly without constructing a board submission — which was this issue's acceptance criterion. Phase 3 tasks 6/7/8 call it from removeMember, updateTeam and setScoringSystem.

title: Today's answer is visible to teammates who have not played yet
description:
PRODUCT QUESTION, not a defect. Needs an owner decision.

getTeamMonth returns every team member's scores for the month, each row carrying its own answer. Wordle has one global puzzle per day, so once any teammate submits today's board, today's correct answer is present in the wire payload sent to every other member of that team — including those who have not played yet. Opening devtools reveals the day's answer.

The showLetters team setting does not prevent this. Per the comment in wordle-board.tsx, showLetters only hides LETTERS; the client still needs the raw answer to compute tile colours, so it must cross the wire regardless.

v1 has the same architecture (client-side tileStates(answer, guess)), so this is inherited rather than introduced by the re-platform, and strict parity argues for leaving it. Worth an explicit "yes, we know" rather than silent inheritance across a re-platform.

If it is ever deemed undesirable the fix is not small: tile states would have to be computed server-side for boards other than your own, so the answer never leaves the server until you have submitted.

Raised in Phase 2 task 3 review.
acceptance_criteria: Owner decision recorded: accepted as v1 parity, or a follow-up filed to compute tile states server-side.

title: getTeamMonth collapses a missing answer into an empty string
description:
getTeamMonthFor returns answer: score.answer ?? '', collapsing a genuinely-absent answer into an empty string. dailyScores.answer is v.optional(v.string()) for a real reason — legacy Supabase rows can lack one — and "no answer on record" is distinguishable from "the answer was empty".

For SCORING the coalesce is correct and deliberately harmonised with scoring.ts, which does attemptsFor(guesses, answer ?? '') itself.

For DISPLAY it loses something. WordleBoard feeds answer straight into tileStates(answer, guess) to colour tiles. A legacy row with no answer renders every tile as absent/grey — indistinguishable from a real answer sharing no letters with the guesses — rather than letting the UI say "no answer on record". Because the query collapses the type before it reaches a component, that distinction cannot be recovered downstream.

Not biting yet: no client consumes getTeamMonth as of task 3. Decide when the board history view is built — either keep answer optional through the query and let the presentational layer choose, or keep the coalesce only on the path feeding attemptsFor/monthTotal.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded on whether the absent-answer state survives to the presentational layer.

title: ReaderCtx is duplicated with a comment-only guarantee
description:
convex/access.ts and convex/scores.ts each define an identical private type:

  type ReaderCtx = { db: GenericDatabaseReader<DataModel> }

scores.ts carries a comment saying it mirrors access.ts's exactly. Nothing enforces that. If access.ts later widens its version (say it needs ctx.storage), the comment in scores.ts silently becomes false with no compiler signal.

Two options: promote it to a shared export once a third consumer appears, or make the claim self-verifying now with a type-level equality assertion. Near-zero cost either way.

Raised in Phase 2 task 3 review, deliberately deferred rather than widening that commit.
acceptance_criteria: Either one shared definition, or a type-level assertion that fails when the two drift.

title: SITE_URL guard checks presence, not scheme
description:
convex/auth.ts guards startup with:

  const siteUrl = process.env.SITE_URL
  if (!siteUrl) throw new Error('SITE_URL is not set on this deployment')

That checks PRESENCE only. The bug it exists to prevent (amendment A2, commit fe81c46) was a redirect origin built from a scheme-LESS deployment hostname, which Supabase then silently replaced with its own Site URL. A bare hostname with no https:// satisfies this guard completely, so the guard is narrower than the comment framing around it suggests.

Also: there is no regression test asserting auth.ts throws when SITE_URL is unset. Phase 2 added env.SITE_URL to vitest.config.ts so tests could import auth.ts transitively; that dummy is never dereferenced, so it hides nothing that was previously covered, but it does mean the guard itself stays untested.

Consider validating the shape (parses as a URL with an http/https protocol) rather than mere presence, and adding a test.

Found during Phase 2 task 2 review. Not blocking.
acceptance_criteria: SITE_URL is validated as a URL with an http/https scheme, with a test covering the rejection.

title: AccessCode carries INVALID_BOARD, a non-access concern
description:
AccessCode in convex/access.ts is the union UNAUTHENTICATED | NO_PLAYER | NOT_A_MEMBER | INVALID_BOARD. The first three are access concerns. INVALID_BOARD is board-shape validation, which is not, and the file's own header describes itself as "the access checks that replace Supabase's RLS policies".

The consequence: scores.ts imports access.ts partly just to borrow an error-code union and factory unrelated to membership or authentication. Every future domain wanting a typed ConvexError faces the same choice — pile onto AccessCode, or fork the pattern.

Suggested by code review: a shared errors.ts owning a generic factory (appError<T extends string>(code: T): never), with access.ts importing only the codes it actually throws and each domain declaring its own literal union.

Cheap now, more annoying after a third domain reaches for AccessCode. Not blocking Phase 2 — flagged during task 2 review and deliberately deferred to avoid widening that commit.
acceptance_criteria: Typed ConvexError codes are organised so a new domain can declare its own without touching AccessCode.

title: me.ts duplicates access.ts playerForEmail instead of calling it
description:
convex/me.ts myData looks a player up inline: same by_email index, same .toLowerCase(), same .first()-not-.unique() choice, same justifying comment. convex/access.ts playerForEmail is now the canonical version of exactly that lookup.

Two hand-synced copies of the player-resolution rule. It is the join the whole migration rests on (copied players carry a Supabase uuid with nothing tying them to a Better Auth user id, so email IS the join), which makes drift between the copies expensive rather than cosmetic.

Point me.ts at playerForEmail. Small and safe; deliberately left out of Phase 2 task 2 to keep that commit to its stated file list.
acceptance_criteria: me.ts myData resolves its player through playerForEmail; one definition of the email join remains.

title: public/sw.js is a tracked build artifact that dirties the tree on every build
description:
next.config.js:46 has serwist write the service worker to swDest: 'public/sw.js', and both public/sw.js and public/sw.js.map are tracked by git. Every 'pnpm build' rewrites them (Sentry debug IDs and the workbox precache manifest change with the chunk hashes), so the working tree comes back dirty after any build.

git log shows they are only actually committed occasionally — 543d4f0, 24732bf, e2d9ee0 — while recent app changes that certainly altered the bundle (391a065, touching src/app/login/actions.ts) left them untouched. So the committed copy is already stale relative to main, and the churn is pure noise that has to be reverted by hand before every commit. It is also an easy way to accidentally commit an unrelated 2-line binary-ish diff.

Either gitignore them and let the build produce them (they are regenerated on every deploy anyway), or regenerate and commit them deliberately as a release step. The first is almost certainly right — nothing reads the committed copy.
acceptance_criteria: A clean checkout plus 'pnpm build' leaves 'git status' clean.
notes:
FIXED on fix/untrack-sw-artifact. .gitignore entries for /public/sw.js and /public/sw.js.map, plus git rm --cached on both.

VERIFIED THE ARTIFACT IS ACTUALLY REGENERATED BEFORE UNTRACKING IT, because the failure mode of getting this wrong is a production PWA with no service worker:
  deleted both files, ran pnpm build -> serwist logs 'Bundling the service worker script with the URL /sw.js' and both files reappear (49302 and 192923 bytes)
  pnpm start -> GET /sw.js returns 200, application/javascript, size 49302; GET /sw.js.map returns 200
Same build pipeline Vercel runs, so nothing depends on the checked-in copy.

ACCEPTANCE MET: with the change applied, pnpm build leaves git status showing only the intentional edits — no sw.js churn at all.

The committed copy was stale regardless: git log shows public/sw.js last updated in 543d4f0 / 24732bf / e2d9ee0, while recent app changes that certainly altered the bundle (391a065, touching login/actions.ts) left it untouched. So the tracked file had not matched the built output for some time.

Cost before fixing: it dirtied the tree on every build, got swept into unrelated commits, and blocked the #157 rebase outright ('cannot rebase: You have unstaged changes').

title: Drop the two instant-based dailyScores indexes once a key can
description:
dailyScores still carries by_player_and_date and by_date, which index the raw instant. Nothing should use them — grouping by an instant across 57 player timezones is the bug puzzleDay exists to fix — and the schema says DO NOT USE in as many words.

They survive only because REMOVING a Convex index requires deployment:data:view, which neither the CI key (deployment:deploy only) nor the local-cli key carries. Adding indexes is permitted; dropping them is not. Isolated by experiment: the identical deploy succeeds with the two indexes present and fails with them absent, and Convex's own error names CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY as the cause.

TO FIX: add deployment:data:view to the github-actions deploy key (and local-cli if local deploys are wanted), then delete the two .index() lines and the DO NOT USE comment block from v2/convex/schema.ts.

Low priority — they cost a little storage and are correctly labelled — but worth doing before Phase 2 builds scoreboard queries, so nobody reaches for the wrong index.
acceptance_criteria: Both indexes gone from schema.ts and from the deployment, with CI green.
notes: Reparented from wt-ksh.2 to the top-level epic on 2026-08-18 when Phase 1 closed. This is not Phase 1 work and must not hold a phase open: it is blocked indefinitely on a Convex key carrying deployment:data:view, which neither the CI key nor the local key has. Adding an index is permitted; removing one is not. The two indexes are harmless while unused and carry a DO NOT USE comment in the schema explaining that grouping by the raw instant is the v1 timezone bug puzzleDay exists to fix.

title: Root package.json pins pnpm 11.13.0, which pnpm has marked a broken release
description:
Root package.json has packageManager: pnpm@11.13.0, added in 16af819 to make Vercel corepack deterministic. pnpm now refuses that version outright:

  [ERR_PNPM_BROKEN_PNPM_RELEASE] pnpm v11.13.0 is a broken release and cannot be installed
  Its "@pnpm/exe" build shipped without a binary and does not run.

Observed in GitHub Actions on 2026-08-03: pnpm/action-setup read the root manifest and its self-installer failed hard. Run 30853583666.

NOT CURRENTLY BREAKING v1. Vercel production builds are green — the most recent Production deployment succeeded 2h before this was filed, and .env.production.local sets ENABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_COREPACK. The break is specific to the @pnpm/exe artifact that pnpm's own self-installer pulls; Vercel's corepack path evidently fetches the ordinary npm tarball and is unaffected.

So this is a latent risk, not an incident: the pin names a version its own maintainers say cannot be installed, and any change to how Vercel resolves corepack would turn a green build red with an error that looks nothing like an app problem.

v2 is already insulated — v2/package.json pins pnpm@11.20.0 independently (c8bb3ea), per the island rule.

FIX: bump the root pin to a current 11.x (latest-11 was 11.20.0 on 2026-08-03) and confirm one Vercel preview build goes green before merging. Deliberately not done as a drive-by during v2 CI work, since it touches the production build of the live app.
acceptance_criteria: Root packageManager names a pnpm version that installs cleanly, proven by a green Vercel preview build and a successful pnpm install --frozen-lockfile at the repo root.

title: Close the Lemon Squeezy store once the final payout clears
description:
Last remaining step of the Lemon Squeezy decommission (split out of wordle-teams-k6a so that issue could close).

Everything else in the decommission is done: no LEMONSQUEEZY_* env var remains in any Vercel scope, all LS webhooks are deleted, @lemonsqueezy/lemonsqueezy.js is absent from package.json and the lockfile, and README.md documents Polar.

DO NOT close the store yet. Two things must clear first:
  1. The final payout must land. Closing the store early can strand funds.
  2. Subscription 370720 (owner's annual, cancelled at period end) runs to 2027-05-17.

Subscription 1676073 (the real paying customer) was cancelled at period end and ends 2026-08-05, so it is no longer a blocker.

The LS API key is no longer in Vercel but is retained in the gitignored local .env files, which is what to use for any further GET /v1/subscriptions checks against the store.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: the final Lemon Squeezy payout has cleared, subscription 370720 has ended (2027-05-17), and the store is closed in the Lemon Squeezy dashboard.

title: custom_access_token_hook is declared IMMUTABLE but reads tables
description:
public.custom_access_token_hook is declared 'immutable' while performing a SELECT against public.players and public.player_customer. Postgres defines IMMUTABLE as 'cannot modify the database and always returns the same result for the same arguments', which permits the planner to pre-evaluate or cache calls. A function that reads mutable tables should be STABLE at most.

In practice the risk is low - Supabase's auth service invokes the hook directly per token issuance rather than inside a query the planner would fold - which is presumably why it has never visibly misbehaved. But the declaration is incorrect and could produce stale membership claims.

Pre-existing since 20240313202756_custom_claims.sql and carried through every subsequent redefinition, including the Polar migration (20260731120000). That migration deliberately preserved 'immutable' rather than changing it, to keep the riskiest migration in the project scoped to exactly one concern - see wordle-teams-j8c.

Changing it is a one-word migration but alters planner behavior for the function that gates every login, so it deserves its own change with its own verification.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: the volatility is either corrected to STABLE with login verified on dev and prod, or a comment in the migration documents why IMMUTABLE is deliberate.

title: public/sw.js churns on every build, dirtying the working tree
description:
public/sw.js and public/sw.js.map are tracked build artifacts regenerated by serwist on every 'pnpm build'. The only delta between builds is a rerolled Sentry debug ID inside the minified bundle, so every build leaves ~96KB of meaningless diff in the working tree that has to be reverted by hand before committing anything unrelated.

Discovered while building for the Polar migration (wordle-teams-9he), where the artifact churn had to be discarded to keep the commit readable.

Options: gitignore them and generate at build time on Vercel; or configure the Sentry plugin to emit a stable debug ID; or leave as-is and keep reverting. Low priority - it is a papercut, not a defect.
acceptance_criteria: Done when: a clean 'pnpm build' either leaves the working tree clean, or the churn is documented as intentional so future sessions stop reverting it.

title: Triage 'Error: Rejected' on /home in production
description:
